# Spin-offs and demergers — NiftyTotalMarket

*Run 2026-11-24 · filings window 2024-06-13 → 2026-11-15 · 4652 restructuring filings across 556 companies · 33 confirmed demergers, 17 partial spin-offs (subsidiary IPOs), 11 completed demergers, 0 probable, 11 indicated, 470 rights / preferential offerings, 889 other restructurings · judge: claude-opus-5 read the schemes, three years of calls and the segment pages.*

**The method, in one paragraph.** Spin-offs are where the notes say the bargains hide: the new stock is sold by holders who never chose it for about a year, the parent is often the better buy before the split, insiders tell you what they think through the stock and options they take in the new entity, and a pro-forma statement plus the peer P/E prices what the market is ignoring. This report puts the CONFIRMED demergers first — a demerger scheme on the exchange record — each with when the new entity lists, why management is doing it (three years of calls, with the transcript each point came from), the parent's last three years with charts, P/E and cash flows, and the separated business's own numbers from the annual reports and presentations, page-cited. Probable and indicated cases follow, then every other restructuring on file.

**How each company is written up.** Nine parts, in this order: (1) the company and what its situation is; (2) stages and dates — filings, record date and every entity's listing; (3) the size of the separated business beside the parent, and whether institutional selling is likely; (4) insider ownership — share swap, promoters' holding, management incentives; (5) why, point by point; (6) the management calls, verbatim; (7) the parent's financial statements; (8) the separated business's financial statements; (9) other financial differences — working capital, margins, returns, debt. In this report part 6 is a table of calls; **the complete text of every question and answer is in the company's own file under `companies/`**, which carries all nine parts.

# Confirmed demergers — in full

## UPL — UPL Ltd.

### 1. UPL Ltd. — CONFIRMED DEMERGER

**CONFIRMED** (a demerger scheme is on the exchange record) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 7.1/10 · spin-off · 9 filing(s) from CALLS, NSE · first 2026-01-19, latest 2026-08-01

**The separated entities — every one the documents name:**

| **UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions Limited** (earlier UPL Agri Science Limited) | 2026 Composite Scheme of Arrangement — Demerger of India Cr… | Dedicated pure-play crop protection platform housing UPL's India Crop Protection Business (ex UPL SAS) and th… | to be listed | Mike Frank, CEO of UPL Global ("Mike Frank, who h… |
| **Advanta Enterprises Limited** (earlier Advanta Enterprises Private Limited) | 2026 initial public offering of Advanta Enterprises Limited… | Seeds and post-harvest platform; seeds across 40 crops with 900+ hybrid varieties, plus the DECCO post-harves… | to be listed | Bhupen Dubey, Chief Executive Officer, Advanta |

**The other parties to the scheme(s)** — not separated entities: UPL Sustainable Agri Solutions Limited — merged in — no shares for the parent's holders; UPL Crop Protection Holdings Limited — merged in — no shares for the parent's holders

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** India Crop Protection Business demerged into UPL 2, then combined with UPL's international (global) crop protection business — class `value_unlocking`.

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

Management's stated reason is that UPL is a conglomerate whose crop protection business is trapped inside a diversified holding structure and is therefore mis-valued: Bikash Prasad said on the May 2026 Capital Markets Day that "even today market is valuing us using a single conglomerate multiple" and that UPL carries "a huge conglomerate discount," so separation would make "the sum of the parts... much, much clearer." The Scheme (board-approved 20 Feb 2026) is a three-step composite arrangement: amalgamate UPL Sustainable Agri Solutions (UPL SAS, India crop protection, 90.91% owned, FY25 turnover INR 24,120 Mn or 31.15% of UPL's turnover) into UPL Limited; demerge that India crop protection undertaking into UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions (UPL 2) on a 1:1 share entitlement; then amalgamate UPL Crop Protection Holdings Ltd., Cayman (UPL Cayman, the 77.78%-held international crop protection vehicle, FY25 turnover USD 4,187 Mn, net worth USD 1,599 Mn) into UPL 2 at 1,000 UPL 2 shares for every 213 UPL Cayman shares, with UPL SAS holders getting 1,000 UPL shares per 48 UPL SAS shares. The problems it is said to solve: a split holding structure created by the 2022 platform carve-out that left India and international crop protection in separate vehicles; a single conglomerate multiple and no value visibility per platform; crop protection's cash-flow and capital-allocation needs being, as COO Toshan Tamhane put it in Feb 2026, "very different from that of the seeds business" (he cited Corteva's own crop protection/seeds split); and inability to raise capital or set governance per platform — the filing says the Scheme lets UPL 1 and UPL 2 "raise capital independently" and "optimize its capital structure," and Prasad said platforms with "independent capital structure, independent governance structure... will grow much faster." The demand came from several directions: analysts and investors gave five pieces of feedback that Prasad catalogued (reporting consistency, the four below-EBITDA items worth ~INR 5,000 crore or 60% of FY25 EBITDA, and debt/liquidity), rating agencies and lenders drove the deleveraging that Jai Shroff said had removed the leverage drag on the multiple, and private investors needed exits — KKR (which wrote a "$300-plus million check" into Advanta) and Alpha Wave (USD 350 Mn for ~12.44%, of which USD 250 Mn secondary from UPL Limited), plus The Upswing Trust, the UPL SAS investor that swapped into UPL Cayman and ends with 16.78% of UPL 2 as a public shareholder with one board nomination right. The result is two listed entities: UPL Limited as a diversified agri and specialty-chemicals platform keeping SUPERFORM as its manufacturing arm and incubating new verticals, and UPL Global as what Mike Frank (its CEO-designate) called "the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform" in 140+ countries with 9 R&D centres, 25 formulation facilities and a 14% innovation rate. Shroff framed it as each business needing "a kind of independent life" and said the plan went through advisors and "at least 10 different structures," expected to complete in 12-15 months.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. Pre-history: value was being unlocked privately, not structurally — Alpha Wave bought ~12.44% of Advanta for USD 350 Mn, USD 250 Mn of it secondary from UPL Limited, the second global investor into Advanta in two years, with proceeds earmarked for debt repayment. “We have signed a definitive agreement with Alpha Wave Global under which they will invest US$350 million, US$100 million as primary investment in the company, and US$250 million as secondary through purchase of shares from UPL Limited for an approximate 12.44% stake in the company.” — *[Jan 2025](https://www.upl-ltd.com/financial_result_and_report_pdfs/9DyAsm9UB52Kn6Za4Ryuqpae2kOB58CLDfHR4eh4/UPL---Q3FY25---Concall-Transcript.pdf)*
2. First mention of structural work: advisors newly engaged to explore unlocking value across all platforms, with no decided structure and no timeline; Prasad tied it to a focus on significantly deleveraging the balance sheet over the next year or two. “The idea behind engaging advisors is to explore unlocking value across all platforms.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.upl-ltd.com/financial_result_and_report_pdfs/r3nhTBqvvaJwil4Yfw2svFbm3ssp7pXGaXZJVwLM/UPL---Q1FY26---Earnings-call-transcript.pdf)*
3. The option set was named for the first time — restructuring, strategic fundraising or an IPO — after the DECCO post-harvest business was folded into Advanta in September 2025. “I think we had indicated in our Q1 press release and subsequently also during the earnings call that UPL continues to evaluate various strategic opportunities to unlock shareholders' value across platforms, including restructuring or strategic fundraising, potential liquidity events like IPO.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.upl-ltd.com/financial_result_and_report_pdfs/UPL-Q2FY26-Earnings-call-transcript.pdf)*
4. Prasad linked the value-unlock options directly to the debt problem, in the context of USD 500 Mn due March 2026 and ~USD 900 Mn of Q3/Q4 FY27 maturities. “We had indicated during Q1 earnings call and press release that we are looking at various options to unlock shareholders' value. And if some of those we decide to take, that would also help in terms of deleveraging the balance sheet.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.upl-ltd.com/financial_result_and_report_pdfs/UPL-Q2FY26-Earnings-call-transcript.pdf)*
5. Advanta's DRHP (filed 19 January 2026) was presented as the first concrete step, within a stated 1-to-3-year window of corporate actions covering every platform. “As we have communicated earlier, we remain focused in evaluating various corporate actions for all our platforms, including IPO and restructuring within a period of 1 to 3 years.” — *Feb 2026*
6. The Advanta IPO was an offer for sale, not a primary raise — KKR selling 2.2% and UPL Limited 7.8% — with proceeds going to the group, principally to cut debt rather than to fund Advanta. “This transaction is offer for sale. It's not a primary transaction. So the cash is not going to Advanta. It is coming to the selling shareholders, which are KKR and UPL Limited in this case.” — *Feb 2026*
7. The clearest business logic given for separating platforms: crop protection and seeds have fundamentally different cash-flow and capital-allocation profiles, with Corteva's own split cited as precedent and Advanta called the eighth-largest global seeds player. “As you would have seen globally, Corteva has also announced a split between crop protection and seeds because just those two businesses are fundamentally different, and we believe Advanta as the eighth largest seeds player globally has a journey and destiny of its own.” — *Feb 2026*
8. Tamhane conceded the trigger was partly that private-round valuations (KKR, then Alpha Wave) were not being reflected in UPL Limited's own price, so public-market separation was needed to capture it. “Because, if you look at the valuation that KKR and subsequently Alpha Wave came in at, at least we feel that the full value of that is not flowing through to UPL Limited.” — *Feb 2026*
9. The 20 Feb 2026 board-approved Composite Scheme consolidates UPL SAS (India crop protection) and UPL Cayman (global crop protection) into UPL Global, to be listed; UPL Limited stays listed as a diversified agri and specialty-chemicals platform. “The Scheme proposes to consolidate the India Crop Protection Business held in UPL SAS and Global Crop Protection Business held in UPL Cayman, under a single entity, creating a focused, pure-play crop protection platform.” — *Scheme*
10. Independent capital raising and capital-structure optimisation for each entity is given as a core benefit, alongside simplification of the group structure created by the 2022 platform carve-out and enhanced managerial and board focus. “The Scheme will allow UPL 1 and UPL 2 to raise capital independently, allowing each entity to optimize its capital structure and pursue business opportunities more efficiently and effectively.” — *Scheme*
11. Scale claim for the new entity, with Mike Frank named CEO of UPL Global; promoters hold 71.56% of UPL 2 post-Scheme versus 28.44% public (The Upswing Trust alone 16.78%), and UPL promoters agreed to an 18-month voluntary lock-in from listing. “Bringing our crop protection businesses under one platform creates the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform.” — *Scheme*
12. The valuation argument stated most bluntly: a single conglomerate multiple is being applied to UPL, and separation is meant to make the sum of the parts visible once each platform has its own capital and governance structure. “You know that even today market is valuing us using a single conglomerate multiple, they are applying on us.” — *[May 2026](https://www.upl-ltd.com/financial_pdfs/cmd-2025-transcript.pdf)*
13. Shroff's framing: brand- and IP-led businesses growing 3x-4x peers need autonomy, and the structure was chosen after extensive tax and structuring advice ahead of the announcement; SUPERFORM stays inside UPL Limited as the manufacturing platform. “All these businesses need long-term need a kind of independent life, right?” — *[May 2026](https://www.upl-ltd.com/financial_pdfs/cmd-2025-transcript.pdf)*
14. Shroff said the historic leverage overhang that had suppressed UPL's multiple is gone — gross debt down 40% from USD 3.8 bn (FY24) to USD 2.3 bn and net debt down 48% to USD 1.6 bn, gearing from 4.6x to below 1.6x — clearing the way for the separation to be read as value unlock. “We've also made sure that the as in the past leverage was an issue for which kept the multiple of the company.” — *[May 2026](https://www.upl-ltd.com/financial_pdfs/cmd-2025-transcript.pdf)*
15. An existing shareholder (Old Bridge Asset Management) objected that the announced structure would trigger a HoldCo discount and dilute existing holders, and pressed management on alternate structures; Shroff offered a meeting. “But the challenge is that the manner in which that the current structure has been announced, it's likely to trigger a significant HoldCo discount.” — *[May 2026](https://www.upl-ltd.com/financial_pdfs/cmd-2025-transcript.pdf)*
16. Management said it had run a two-month investor consultation with a tracker of feedback that would go unfiltered to the board within a month or two, and that at least ten structures had been reviewed with advisors before this one was chosen. “And very shortly, we will be presenting that unfiltered to the board.” — *[May 2026](https://www.upl-ltd.com/financial_pdfs/cmd-2025-transcript.pdf)*

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced as an unspecified value-unlock exercise on the 1 Aug 2025 Q1FY26 call, where Prasad said advisors had just been engaged to "explore unlocking value across all platforms" with "no firm decision on any structure," after Jai Shroff's press-release comment on restructuring; before that, on 31 Jan 2025, the only visible step was private monetization of Advanta (Alpha Wave's USD 350 Mn) and a net-debt/EBITDA target of ~2x. On 6 Nov 2025 it broadened to "restructuring or strategic fundraising, potential liquidity events like IPO," explicitly linked to deleveraging, alongside the DECCO-into-Advanta integration. By 2 Feb 2026 it had a timetable and a first concrete step — Advanta's DRHP filed 19 Jan 2026, described as "the first such step in this direction," with corporate actions for all platforms "within a period of 1 to 3 years" — and management argued seeds and crop protection are fundamentally different businesses. The crop protection scheme itself was announced 20 Feb 2026 (CCI clearance 2-3 Jun 2026, exchange observation letters and the Upswing swap completed 29-31 Jul 2026), and by the 11 May 2026 Capital Markets Day the debate had shifted to the structure's fairness, with Old Bridge calling it "fairly detrimental to the current shareholders," Shroff defending it and Prasad promising to take investor feedback "unfiltered to the board" within a month or two.

**What management expects from it:** UPL Global: pure-play crop protection across 140+ countries, independent capital structure and governance, faster growth, wider investor and lender base. UPL Limited: diversified agri and specialty-chemicals platform retaining SUPERFORM, incubating new ventures, deleveraged with net debt/EBITDA below 1.6x. Both: independent fundraising, clearer sum-of-parts valuation removing the conglomerate discount, sharper board and managerial focus.

*Not explained on the calls:* No debt split between UPL 1 and UPL 2, no UPL 2 standalone financials or guidance, no answer to the HoldCo-discount objection, no word on Advanta's IPO post-Scheme.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Unlock shareholder value by consolidating India and international crop protection into one focused pure-play platform; simplify group structure, enable clearer value discovery, independent capital raising, sharper board/managerial focus, synergies
- *What it reveals:* Crop protection is the bulk of UPL: segment revenue Rs 42,399 cr of Rs 51,839 cr FY26. UPL Cayman alone: USD 4,187 Mn turnover, USD 1,599 Mn net worth; demerged India undertaking 31.15% of UPL 1 turnover. CFO frames it as deleveraging and balance-sheet strengthening
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *Read next:* The Composite Scheme of Arrangement with Joint Valuation Report and J.P. Morgan fairness opinion, on the company's scheme-of-arrangement webpage
- *In their words:* “UPL 2, which shall be listed pursuant to the Scheme would be a dedicated crop protection platform.”

**What the documents themselves say about the differences:**

- **other** — parent / remaining: UPL 1 remains an existing listed company operating as a diversified platform encompassing agriculture and specialty chemical businesses while incubating and developing new businesses and verticals; separated business: UPL 2 will be a dedicated pure-play crop protection platform consolidating the India Crop Protection Business (UPL SAS) and the Global Crop Protection Business (UPL Cayman), with independent management “The Scheme proposes to consolidate the India Crop Protection Business held in UPL SAS and Global Crop Protection Business held in UPL Cayman, under a single entity, creating a focused, pure- play crop protection platform. This integrated business will benefit from a strong manufacturing base, advanced research capabilities, a broad portfolio of registered products and brands across multiple geo graphies and independent management.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: Turnover of UPL 1 for the year ended March 31, 2025 was INR 53,313 Mn with net worth of INR 120,210 Mn (audited standalone); separated business: The Demerged Undertaking (India Crop Protection Business) had turnover of INR 24,120 Mn, being 31.15% of UPL 1's turnover; UPL Cayman had turnover of USD 4,187 Mn and net worth of USD 1,599 Mn “Turnover of the Demerged Undertaking (as defined in the Scheme) (INR Mn) % of Turnover of UPL 1* 24,120 31.15%”
- **capex and capital intensity** — parent / remaining: The Scheme will allow UPL 1 to raise capital independently and optimize its capital structure; separated business: The Scheme will allow UPL 2 to raise capital independently, build a wider capital and financial base and attract a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and stakeholders “The Scheme will allow UPL 1 and UPL 2 to raise capital independently, allowing each entity to optimize its capital structure and pursue business opportunities more efficiently and effectively.”
- **debt and leverage** — parent / remaining: Group CFO states the structural simplification drives deleveraging, reinforces balance sheet strength and improves return metrics; FY26 gross debt down $850 million to $2.3 billion, net debt $1.6 billion, net debt/EBITDA below 1.6x versus 4.6x in FY24; separated business: not stated “Bikash Prasad, Group CFO of UPL, said, "This structural simpliﬁcation strengthens our ﬁnancial foundation and accelerates our journey towards a more eﬃcient an d resilient UPL. By driving deleveraging, reinforcing balance sheet strength, and improving return metrics, we are creating a sharper, more focused organization designed to deliver sustainable long- term value for all shareholders ."”
- **growth** — parent / remaining: UPL Limited consolidated revenue from operations of INR 51,839 crore and EBITDA growth of 18% in FY26; segment revenue FY26 — Crop protection INR 42,399 crore, Seeds & Post harvest INR 6,830 crore, Non agro INR 2,803 crore; separated business: UPL Corp (global crop protection) FY26 revenue growth 11% with contribution margin up more than 250 basis points to 31.5% and EBITDA growth of 20%; UPL SAS India crop protection revenue flat with contribution up 19% and EBITDA up 24% “For the full year, we delivered 11% revenue growth year -on-year, driven by industry-leading volume growth across herbicides and fungicides. Contribution margins grew by more than 250 basis points to 31.5% versus FY25.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: Separation is expected to enable clearer value discovery and give investors flexibility to choose between the diversified platform and the pure-play platform; separated business: UPL Global is described as creating the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform with a presence in more than 140 countries “Mik e Fr ank, CE O of UPL Global, added , "Bringing our crop protection businesses under one platform creates the world's second largest listed pure- play crop protection platform.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: An investor at the Capital Markets Day objected that the announced reorganization is detrimental to existing UPL shareholders and could trigger a holding-company discount; management said feedback will be presented to the Board; separated business: Management stated at least 10 different structures were reviewed before arriving at this structure, and that the purpose is to unlock value at each platform level “By going to a structure, and before we come to conclusion on this structure, it has been discussed, reviewed by our advisors, and we have looked at least 10 different structures to come up to this structure.”

After the Scheme has been effected, the issued shares shall be listed on BSE and NSE." Also: "There is no cash consideration being discharged under the Scheme." The entire pre-scheme paid up share capital of ASTPL held by AMPL "shall stand cancelled and reduced".
- **Management incentives:** No stock option, RSU or SAR plan is mentioned in the documents, and no treatment of existing grants in the Scheme is stated. Convertible warrants: "The Board of the Directors of the Company at its meeting held on May 20, 2025 and the shareholders of the company at Extraordinary General Meeting held on June13, 2025 has approved the allotment of up to 20,13,885 convertible warrants each convertible into, or exchangeable for, one fully paid up equity share of the Company, having a face value of Rs. 2, within the period of eighteen months in accordance with the applicable laws at a price of Rs. 864 aggregating up to Rs. 173.99 crores ("issue proceeds"). During the previous year ended March 31, 2026, the Company has received 25% of the issue proceeds i.e., Rs. 43.50 crores (Upfront monies) on June 23, 2025 and June 24, 2025." Managerial performance bonus is linked to restructuring: for Dr. M. V. Reddy and Mr. Atim Kabra the performance criteria include "Other intiatives of corporate restructuring like merger/demerger 10.0%" weightage. Cash compensation on exit of the outgoing MD: "the consent of the Members of the Company be and is hereby accorded for payment of Rs.1,35,00,000/- (Rupees One Crore Thirty-Five Lakhs only) to Mr. S. Gurunatha Reddy (DIN: 00003828) in the nature of cash" (Explanatory Statement: recommended "payment of a cash compensation of Rs.1,35,68,889/-" representing "the remuneration payable for the unexpired portion of his tenure as Managing Director"). Director shareholding in AMPL: Mr. P. A. Chitrakar "32,40,830 Equity Shares.", Mr. Atim Kabra "33,56,074 Equity Shares.", Dr. M. V. Reddy "Holds 63,570 equity shares." Insider holdings in the JV: "Mr. S. Gurunatha Reddy is holding 0.20% shareholding in ARC", "Dr. M.V. Reddy is holding 0.20% shareholding in ARC", "Mr. Atim Kabra is holding 0.10% Shareholding in ARC", "Mr. Suresh Kumar Somani is holding 0.10% Shareholding in ARC", "Mr. P. A. Chitrakar is holding 0.20% Shareholding in ARC."
- **Insider actions around the separation:** No promoter or management buying, selling or pledging of shares is stated. Stated intent around the separation: "Mr. S. Gurunatha Reddy, Managing Director of AMPL has agreed to take on the additional responsibility of overseeing the ongoing demerger of the Space and Meteorology business and thereafter shall join Astra Space Technologies Private Limited (ASTPL) as a Director subject to the approval of the Board." Gurunatha Reddy will join ASTPL as Director; MD/WTD bonus weights "merger/demerger" 10%. · *option pricing date:* not stated

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

Astra Microwave is splitting itself into two sector-focused listed companies: the parent (AMPL) keeps Radar Electronics, Electronic Warfare and Telemetry, while the Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business is demerged on a going-concern basis into its wholly-owned subsidiary Astra Space Technologies Pvt Ltd (ASTPL), which will itself be listed on BSE and NSE. On the May 27, 2026 call MD S.G. Reddy said the board had given in-principle approval and framed the objective as creating 'sharper strategic and operational focus,' enabling dedicated management teams to chase sector-specific opportunities, enhancing governance and accountability, simplifying the corporate structure and creating 'clearer investment propositions to shareholders,' with focused growth, better capital allocation and improved operational efficiency over the medium to long term. The sizing numbers management gave: FY26 standalone turnover INR1,157 crore of which radar was ~60% and space plus meteorology ~16%; the scheme puts the demerged undertaking's FY26 turnover at ~INR157 crore, i.e. 13.58% of standalone turnover; the Dec-2025 order book of INR2,226 crore contained INR249 crore of space and INR369 crore of meteorology/hydrology orders. The scheme's stated reasoning is that space/met/hydro has 'distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile' needing a differentiated strategy, and that a standalone entity would be 'better positioned to attract investors, strategic partners, lenders, and other stakeholders with sector-specific interests,' thereby unlocking the value of that undertaking for shareholders. Mechanically there is no cash consideration: shareholders get 1 ASTPL share of Rs 2 for every 1 AMPL share of Rs 2, ASTPL's existing promoter-held capital is cancelled, and post-scheme ASTPL mirrors AMPL (promoters 6.45%, public 93.55%). No investor, lender or partner is identified anywhere as having demanded the separation — it is presented as management/board-initiated strategic re-alignment, though Atim Kabra had repeatedly argued on earlier calls that the embedded space business was worth far more than the market credited (Aug 2025: 'very, very valuable'; Nov 2025: peers raising at $750-800m valuations with almost no revenue, close to Astra's whole market cap). The move is also backed with people: MD S. Gurunatha Reddy took on oversight of the demerger, stepped down as AMPL MD and director from close of September 30, 2026 to join ASTPL as a director, and Joint MD Dr M.V. Reddy became AMPL's MD from October 1, 2026. As of the last filings, BSE gave 'no adverse observations' and NSE 'no objection' on October 29, 2026, SEBI/NCLT approvals are still pending, and no effect of the scheme has been taken into the Q2 FY27 accounts.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. First disclosure on a call: the board has in-principle approved demerging the space, meteorology and hydrology business, with the formal scheme to follow within weeks. “On a strategic front, the Board of Directors have in-principle approved demerger of our space, meteorology, and hydrology business.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78f3aacc-b7ef-4d51-b1e1-d6e5863786b8.pdf)*
2. The stated objective is focus, not cash or deleveraging. “The objective of this move is to create sharper strategic and operational focus for business segments.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78f3aacc-b7ef-4d51-b1e1-d6e5863786b8.pdf)*
3. The specific problems named: management bandwidth, governance/accountability, a complicated corporate structure and an unclear investment case for shareholders. “The proposed structure will enable dedicated management teams to pursue sector-specific growth opportunities, enhance governance and accountability, simplify the corporate structure, and create clearer investment propositions to shareholders.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78f3aacc-b7ef-4d51-b1e1-d6e5863786b8.pdf)*
4. Expected outcome framed over the medium to long term, including capital allocation. “Over the medium to long term, we believe this initiative will support focused growth, better capital allocation, and improved operational efficiency.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78f3aacc-b7ef-4d51-b1e1-d6e5863786b8.pdf)*
5. Scale of the business being separated, as management described FY26 revenue mix: space and meteorology ~16% versus radar ~60%. “Our radar business continued to be a primary growth driver, contributing nearly 60% of our revenue, while space and meteorology segment contributed around 16%, demonstrating our expanding footprint in strategic and high-technology domains.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78f3aacc-b7ef-4d51-b1e1-d6e5863786b8.pdf)*
6. The June 10, 2026 scheme disclosure states the purpose as creating two separately listed sector-focused companies — radar/EW/telemetry on one side, space/met/hydro on the other. “The proposed demerger is intended to create two sector-focused listed entities, namely: (a) Radar Electronics, Electronic Warfare and Telemetry business focused entity; and (b) Space, Meteorology and Hydrology focused entity;” — *Scheme*
7. Core argument: the two businesses face different industry, competitive, regulatory and risk conditions and therefore need different strategies. “The Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business operates in a sector with distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile, necessitating a differentiated growth strategy aligned with its specific market opportunities.” — *Scheme*
8. Capital-access rationale — the only place any outside constituency (investors, partners, lenders) is invoked, and as a prospective benefit rather than as a party that asked for the split. “A standalone Space, Meteorology and Hydrology entity would be better positioned to attract investors, strategic partners, lenders, and other stakeholders with sector-specific interests.” — *Scheme*
9. Explicit value-unlock objective for AMPL shareholders. “unlocking the value of the Demerged Undertaking for the shareholders of the Demerged Company.” — *Scheme*
10. Size of the carve-out quantified in the filing: ~INR157 crore of FY26 turnover, 13.58% of the parent's total. “The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking of the Company for the financial year ended 31st March 2026 was approximately INR. 157 Crores , representing 13.58% of the total turnover of the Demerged Company for the said year.” — *Scheme*
11. No cash changes hands; a 1:1 share entitlement mirrors AMPL's register into ASTPL (promoters 6.45%, public 93.55% post-scheme), and ASTPL shares will be listed on BSE and NSE. “For the purpose of the demerger of Demerged Undertaking ( as defined in the Scheme ) of Demerged Company into Resulting Company, the Resulting Company shall issue 1 fully paid-up equity share of INR 2 (Indian Rupees 2/- only) each for every 1 fully paid-up equity share of INR 2 (Indian Rupees 2/- only) each held in the Demerged Company ("Share Entitlement Ratio").” — *Scheme*
12. Leadership is being split alongside the businesses: MD S. Gurunatha Reddy was given the demerger and will move to ASTPL, with Dr M.V. Reddy taking over as AMPL MD from October 1, 2026 (April 3, 2026 press release; confirmed in the August 10, 2026 board outcome). “In this role, he will lead the adoption of tailored growth strategies and capital allocation frameworks suited to the Space, Meteorology and Hydrology sector, thereby enabling focused management attention, enhanced operational efficiency and the unlocking of value for the shareholders of the Company.” — *Scheme*
13. Status as of the latest filings: exchange clearances in hand on October 29, 2026; SEBI/NCLT and other approvals still pending, with no accounting effect taken in Q2 FY27. “AMPL has received observation letter with "no adverse observations" from BSE Limited on 29th October 2026 and observation letter with "no objection" from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited on 29th October 2026 in relation to the Scheme of Arrangement.” — *Scheme*
14. Pre-announcement value framing: Kabra argued the embedded space business alone could justify something close to Astra's entire market capitalisation, versus peers raising at high valuations with little revenue. “Companies are raising money at like $750 million, $800 million valuation with hardly any revenue numbers to their credit. If I extrapolate these numbers, actually, I got close to my current market capitalization.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8920e2b3-bd77-473a-94ef-a0dba0be3236.pdf)*
15. Earliest hint of the value-unlock logic, alongside disclosure that Astra Space Technologies had been set up as a wholly-owned subsidiary with a ~INR230 crore space order book. “So our order book, as SG mentioned, is in excess of INR230 crores over there. And given where companies with very limited indigenous capabilities are valued, you might find that our space business is actually very, very valuable.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8665322a-8313-49d9-b271-c9f46183b085.pdf)*
16. Two weeks before the in-principle board approval, Kabra flagged a need for creative financing for development projects and told investors to watch for options crystallising — the closest the calls come to foreshadowing the restructuring. “But as you know, balance sheet for efficiently -- for them to efficiently function, especially when our sales volumes are projected to go significantly higher, we need to be creative as well as ensure that there is enough financing is there so that our NCNC projects, the products being developed and the large blue sky thinking driven projects do not suffer due to inadequate financing.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=82557eb2-8eb5-49c4-b6db-4fe6f8761102.pdf)*

**How it evolved:** Through the Aug 14, 2025 and Nov 13, 2025 calls there was no demerger talk at all, but the groundwork was visible: Astra Space Technologies had been incorporated as a wholly-owned subsidiary with Bangalore clean rooms and a ~INR230-239 crore space order book, and Atim Kabra argued the space business was being carried inside Astra at far less than standalone peers' valuations. On the Feb 13, 2026 call there was still no mention of a demerger, only Kabra's hint about needing to 'be creative' on financing and 'watch the space.' The board granted in-principle approval on Feb 27, 2026, which surfaced publicly in the April 3, 2026 press release (tied to the MD succession) and was first spoken to investors on the May 27, 2026 (Jun 2026) call, where the detailed scheme was promised 'over the next few weeks.' The board approved the full Scheme of Arrangement on June 10, 2026, and the stock exchanges issued their observation/no-objection letters on October 29, 2026; notably, not a single analyst asked a question about the demerger on the May 27, 2026 call.

**What management expects from it:** AMPL becomes a radar/EW/telemetry-focused listed company; space/met/hydro becomes a separately listed entity with its own management team, tailored growth strategy and capital allocation, sharper focus, better governance and accountability, a simpler structure, improved operational efficiency, easier access to sector-specific investors, partners and lenders, a clearer investment proposition and unlocked shareholder value. No margin, EBITDA or valuation targets were quantified.

*Not explained on the calls:* No segment margins/EBITDA, asset-debt-employee split, ASTPL standalone financials, listing timeline, transaction costs, or where ARC/MMIC sit; no analyst questioned it; no requesting party named.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Strategic re-alignment to create two sector-focused listed entities; Space/Meteorology/Hydrology has distinct industry characteristics, enabling focused management, tailored growth and capital allocation, sector-specific investors, and "unlocking the value of the Demerged Undertaking for the shareholders".
- *What it reveals:* Demerged undertaking turnover INR 157 crores, 13.58% of FY26 total; management says "the space margins are better compared to even defence also"; Dec-2025 order book INR 249 crores space plus INR 369 crores met/hydrology. Parent keeps radar/EW/telemetry with QRSAM, Uttam, Su-30 programs.
- *Parent or spin:* both · *Read next:* ASTPL abridged-prospectus disclosure in the NCLT shareholders' notice: demerged undertaking assets, liabilities, net worth, PAT, EBITDA.
- *In their words:* “Yes, all new shares of ASTPL will be listed and will be admitted for trading on the NSE and BSE, subject to receipt of requisite approvals from the Stock Exchanges.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

Management framed the demerger as splitting one company that had been doing two businesses with two different investor bases: an asset-heavy business that designs, develops, finances and owns hotels (pension funds, insurance companies betting on inflation, repricing and annuity yield) and an asset-light business that monetises brand, management, loyalty, distribution and technology with almost no capital intensity. Keswani said Lemon Tree had only built hotels in 2004-2007 because owners would not hand their hotels to an unknown brand, and that with the brand now widely recognised (MakeMyTrip's CEO told him 20-25% of occupancy comes from them the moment a Lemon Tree opens) there was no reason to keep owning assets rather than monetise the brand — explicitly the Marriott/Host Hotels and Hilton/Park Hotels playbook. Mechanically (Composite Scheme approved 9 Jan 2026, appointed date 1 April 2026): Carnation Hotels and Hamstede Living merge into LTH; Oriole Dr. Fresh, Canary, Sukhsagar and Manakin merge into Fleur against shares to LTH; and the Demerged Undertaking — 11 operating hotels plus Aurika Shimla under construction, the investment in Arum (Aurika Shillong, 165 rooms) and the entire development capability/team with exclusivity on all future ownership, leasing and development — demerges into Fleur, with 20 Fleur shares for every 311 LTH shares (demerged division turnover Rs 23,037.34 lakh, 59.90% of LTH standalone turnover; 1,563 operating rooms across 15 hotels per the presentation, 1,820 keys/17 hotels per the press release). A second stated problem was conflict of interest: development capability was moved to Fleur with 'Chinese firewalls' so Fleur shareholders could never feel Lemon Tree was cherry-picking the best assets for itself, and Lemon Tree must refer new acquisition/development opportunities to Fleur. All group debt (about Rs 1,300 crore at demerger, Rs 1,500 crore total borrowings at FY26-end, cost of debt 7.42%) goes to Fleur, leaving Lemon Tree debt-free with only technology and marketing spend, forcing the Board to frame a dividend/shareholder-reward policy. Warburg Pincus (Coastal Cedar Investments B.V.) bought APG's entire 41.09% of Fleur and committed up to Rs 960 crore of primary equity, giving Fleur roughly Rs 3,000 crore of deployable capital at 1:1 debt-equity against 2,500+ rooms under active discussion and Aurika Nehru Place (572 rooms, ~Rs 700 crore); post-scheme LTH shareholders own ~74% of Fleur (32.96% direct plus ~41% through LTH) versus the 59% LTH owns today, and Fleur lists separately for 'transparent price discovery and market-driven valuation of the asset-heavy business'.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. Asked directly by Kunal Lakhan (CLSA) what was wrong with the old structure, Keswani said the hotel business has two subsets with two different investor types — developers/owners wanting chunky yield and inflation-linked annuity returns versus asset-light investors betting on brand and management — and Lemon Tree was a combination of both. “We have actually separated 2 types of businesses. One is asset heavy, long -term appreciating asset, capital intensive. It has a different kind of investor, and this business has a very different kind of investor, and we wanted to actually attract both types of investors.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)*
2. He explained the historical accident being corrected: hotels were built only to establish the brand, and with the brand now established the company should monetise it instead of owning assets. “We were forced to build hotels to build our brand. But once we build our brand, technically, we do not need hotels because now it is time for Lemon Tree to monetize its brand, which is enormous recall.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)*
3. The transfer of the development capability and exclusive development mandate to Fleur was driven by a conflict-of-interest problem — Fleur minorities fearing Lemon Tree would keep the best projects for itself — and was solved with firewalls. “Development capability was an issue which was raised in order to maximize Fleur's growth, we did not want shareholders of Fleur to ever feel that Lemon Tree when it recommends any assets was cherry -picking, which means Lemon Tree would say, I have got this very nice asset in Delhi, why should I offer it to Fleur.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)*
4. All of Lemon Tree's debt moves to Fleur: Fleur carries roughly Rs 1,300 crore of debt against a ~Rs 900 crore net EBITDA and can borrow another ~Rs 1,300 crore, while Lemon Tree goes to zero debt. “Firstly, when this demerger happens, all the debt, including the Lemon Tree's debt, after adjustment is being transferred to Fleur. Fleur will have 100% of our debt and Lemon Tree will have zero debt.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)*
5. Keswani justified keeping a ~41% indirect stake in Fleur (challenged by Jinesh Joshi on hold-co discount) as Lemon Tree retaining 'skin in the game' as Fleur's manager, with natural dilution as Fleur raises capital; he quantified that Rs 1,000 crore deployed by Fleur generates ~Rs 350 crore of turnover, Rs 170-180 crore EBITDA and ~Rs 30 crore of fees for Lemon Tree. “We felt it was prudent to have significant skin in the game at this stage, which means that going forward, it is very possible that Lemon Tree may dilute or even increase its stake over time; this will obviously be a Board decision .” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)*
6. Warburg's Rs 960 crore primary commitment plus Fleur's own cash and 1:1 debt gives roughly Rs 3,000 crore to deploy pre-listing against 2,500 rooms in active discussion; Keswani guided Fleur to over Rs 1,000 crore net EBITDA by FY28 and Lemon Tree to 80% EBITDA margin / 60% PAT margin. “We have potentially about Rs 3,000 crores available to deploy in this growth before we list.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=098527b9-fd65-4aa9-9c6d-1ac184b2eda0.pdf)*
7. Opening the call with pro forma financials for both entities, Keswani described the transaction as simple — Warburg has bought APG's Fleur stake, Lemon Tree transfers 17 hotels and development capabilities in exchange for Fleur shares to LTH shareholders, and Fleur lists. “This scheme will result in 2 distinct financially sound businesses.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a03e8364-4037-407c-8929-d956c0976b96.pdf)*
8. He restated the economic outcome for each entity: Lemon Tree debt-free, high-margin, high-ROCE and fee/brand-driven; Fleur the consolidated owner of a fully renovated portfolio, post-scheme India's largest hotel platform by inventory at 5,600 rooms and 39 operational hotels. “Post the reorganization , Lemon Tree will emerge as a debt -free, high-margin, high ROCE company generating strong free cash flows from fees and brand -related income.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a03e8364-4037-407c-8929-d956c0976b96.pdf)*
9. Shareholder arithmetic: LTH shareholders end up with close to 74% of Fleur (33% direct, ~41% through Lemon Tree) versus the 59% Lemon Tree directly owns in Fleur today, before Warburg's primary infusion; Keswani also said he will cease to be executive at Lemon Tree from March 2027 and focus on Fleur as Executive Chair. “Post reorganization , Lemon Tree shareholders will effectively own close to 74% of Fleur Hotels, 33% directly and about 41% indirectly through Lemon Tree.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a03e8364-4037-407c-8929-d956c0976b96.pdf)*
10. Answering Achal Kumar, Keswani confirmed Fleur will be brand-agnostic post-demerger and may hand assets to other operators — Lemon Tree has no automatic right to Fleur's hotels and must earn them on results. “Yes. But Lemon Tree must be able to deliver best results to get it . Just because Lemon Tree has skin in the game with Fleur does not mean that it has an automatic right to any asset that Fleur develops.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a03e8364-4037-407c-8929-d956c0976b96.pdf)*
11. On capital allocation after the split, Lemon Tree is expected to need almost no capital and move to distributing profits, while Fleur will retain capital for growth rather than pay dividends. “Lemon Tree will not need any significant capital other than potentially investments in technology or in marketing and so on. It will be essentially a zero -debt cash accretive company.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a03e8364-4037-407c-8929-d956c0976b96.pdf)*
12. Keswani confirmed the scheme is effective from 1 April and that Lemon Tree becomes debt-free from next year, with all assets and debt going to Fleur and fee income becoming free cash; the Board must decide a dividend policy within six months. “What will happen is in the scheme of demerger, all the assets of Lemon Tree, including its debt will be transferred to Fleur. Lemon Tree will immediately effectively be a debt -free company from next year.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b0215f7f-3372-4231-8b2f-7f433eb77faf.pdf)*
13. Investors pushed for separate reporting: Ashish Kumar of Infinity Alternatives asked for pro forma financials of both businesses while awaiting the listing, and management agreed to publish them from the next quarter. “Now that we have decided on the split of the 2 businesses, what might be helpful is if we can add pro forma financials for both of the assets as they look like so that while we are waiting for the l isting, we do get a good sense of what the numbers are looking like.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b0215f7f-3372-4231-8b2f-7f433eb77faf.pdf)*
14. Keswani positioned the asset-light entity as a first in India, with fee income from hotels signed three years earlier only now flowing, and Fleur guided to ~Rs 1,000 crore EBITDA by FY28, its first year as a listed company. “And keep in mind that Lemon Tree will be the first fully asset -light brand owning tech and distribution and management company in India, the first.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b0215f7f-3372-4231-8b2f-7f433eb77faf.pdf)*
15. The demerger was still with Board subcommittees of both Lemon Tree and Fleur, with management hinting that more than the demerger was being negotiated (the Warburg/APG transactions announced two months later). “It is not only the demerger of Fleur, but some other even more exciting stuff, but we will talk about it when the time is right.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=5a3cfc96-c662-414a-bc34-4635bef2415b.pdf)*
16. First formal disclosure of the structure: committees of directors in both companies to evaluate transferring LTH's assets into Fleur via demerger and then list Fleur, with Lemon Tree becoming asset-light and focused on management, brand and technology — described as the global trend in the space. “You may have also seen that we have said that a committee of directors has been set up in Lemon Tree and in Fleur to evaluate how we can possibly look at a transfer of assets from Lemon Tree into Fleur through a demerger scheme and then automatically look at how we can list Fleur.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c30ba016-9c4b-4e13-8b0d-a5fb02eb43b7.pdf)*
17. The separation of management was done first and explicitly for this purpose — Neelendra Singh to run asset-light Lemon Tree from 1 October and Saurabh Shatdal to drive Fleur's asset-heavy growth, with Keswani handholding and moving to strategic oversight. “The intent of the leadership change was to get 2 very good people who would then run these two companies independently on a day -to-day basis.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c30ba016-9c4b-4e13-8b0d-a5fb02eb43b7.pdf)*
18. Keswani drew a hard line on mandates — Fleur builds, buys and leases, Lemon Tree only manages or franchises — and noted that the more Fleur dilutes and raises capital, the more Lemon Tree's economic interest rises via fees (Rs 100+ crore this year, potentially Rs 300-400 crore from Fleur in three years). “Fleur's mandate will be to focus on, at the right value, building, buying, or leasing hotels. Lemon Tree's will only be to manage or franchise. Lemon Tree will not lease hotels once the Fleur demerger happens.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c30ba016-9c4b-4e13-8b0d-a5fb02eb43b7.pdf)*
19. The earliest trace in these calls: a Fleur listing was already seen as the accelerator of deleveraging, with Keswani putting an IPO within 2-3 years at most when asked by Prashant Biyani. “I think we are sticking to our guidance that in the next 3 - 3.5 years, we should be debt free , but if we list Fleur before that then we will be debt free that much earlier.” — *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3c895122-81f1-4b3e-be92-d1bf92b7945a.pdf)*
20. The 9 Jan 2026 filing states the Board reviewed the business with a view to segregating the asset-heavy ownership/development undertaking from the asset-light management/brand platform, and that the demerged business is self-sustaining and better housed in Fleur; the demerged division's turnover was Rs 23,037.34 lakh, 59.90% of LTH standalone turnover. “Therefore, to achieve operational focus, greater flexibility for capital deployment, and clearer alignment of business objectives, it is proposed under this Scheme to (i) amalgamate Transferor Company 3, Transferor Company 4, Transferor Company 5 and Transferor Company 6 with the Transferee Company; and (ii) demerge and vest the Demerged Undertaking (comprising the Demerged Hotel Properties and the Development Capabilities together with the related undertakings, as defined hereinafter) into the Transferee C ompany, while the Company will continue to focus on the asset -light hotel management support, brand and operations including management support of the hotels transferred to the Transferee Company and other properties.” — *Scheme*
21. A stated purpose is market-driven valuation: Fleur ceases to be LTH's subsidiary and lists, so LTH shareholders participate directly in the asset-heavy business through listed shares rather than through a subsidiary. “Following the implementation of the Scheme, the Transferee Company will cease to be a subsidiary of the Company , and its shares will be listed on the Stock Exchanges, enabling transparent price discovery and market -driven valuation of the asset -heavy business.” — *Scheme*
22. The filing also sets out structural clean-up and partner-flexibility objectives: merging two wholly owned subsidiaries into LTH to remove layering and cost, and creating a structure that lets Fleur bring in investors or co-development partners per project without touching LTH's brand operations. “To create a flexible structure enabling the Transferee Company to attract investors or co -development partners for specific hotel projects, without affecting Company's brand operations or control over strategic decisions.” — *Scheme*
23. Continuity is contractually locked: every hotel amalgamated into or demerged to Fleur stays under Lemon Tree Hotel Operating Agreements (existing ones amended/restated and extended from the Appointed Date), and LTH must refer new acquisition/development opportunities to Fleur and drop them if Fleur declines. “Further, all the hotels amalgamated with or demerged into the Transferee Company will continue to be managed and operated by the Company under Hotel Operating Agreements and, the existing Hotel Operating Agreements with the Transferee Company and its subsidiaries shall be amended and/or restated, inter alia, to reflect the revised terms as detailed in the Scheme, and the Company shall refer new hotel acquisition or development opportunities to the Transferee Company and shall not pursue them if declined, except for hotel operations/franchise arran gements through third parties.” — *Scheme*
24. The Shareholders' Agreement with Warburg gives Fleur the exclusive global right to own, lease and develop hospitality assets, Investor/LTH affirmative consent on reserved matters, up to 3 Investor and 3 LTH directors with Keswani as non-retiring executive chairman, and the right to inject up to Rs 960 crore of primary capital. “The Agreement provides Fleur t he exclusive right to own, lease and develop hospitality assets globally, with LTHL being entitled to undertake key money arrangements, in the manner as mutually agreed.” — *Scheme*
25. The 22 Sept 2026 filing records receipt of NSE 'no objection' and BSE 'no adverse observation' letters under Regulation 37, valid six months, with NCLT, shareholder and creditor approvals still pending — the gating item management had flagged as the timing risk. “In this regard, we wish to inform you that the Company has received the Observation Letter s with 'no objection ' from the NSE and 'no adverse observations' from the BSE on September 22, 2026 vide their respective letters , pursuant to Regulation 37 of the Listing Regulations , in relation to the Scheme .” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** The idea was first visible as a Fleur listing aspiration in the Nov 2024 call, where Keswani said debt-freedom would come sooner 'if we list Fleur before that' and put an IPO 'within the next 2-3 years at most'; in the Aug 2025 call he disclosed that committees of directors had been set up in both Lemon Tree and Fleur to evaluate transferring LTH's assets into Fleur via a demerger and listing it, alongside splitting the management teams (Neelendra Singh for LTH from 1 October, Saurabh Shatdal for Fleur), with listing hoped for end-CY2026. In the Nov 2025 call it was 'in process' with a Board subcommittee and a promise of 'some other even more exciting stuff' within three months; the scheme, the Warburg/APG transactions and the 74%/26% shareholding math were announced in the Jan 2026 (15 January) dedicated call with a 12-15 month path to listing. By the Feb 2026 call Keswani confirmed the scheme was effective from 1 April and, responding to Ashish Kumar's request, promised pro forma financials for both entities; those pro formas appeared with the Jun 2026 (29 May) results, where CCI approval (April 2026), Warburg's completed purchase of APG's stake and a longer 12-18 month NCLT-dependent timeline were given, followed by NSE/BSE observation letters on 22 September 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Lemon Tree: debt-free, fee/brand/tech-only, EBITDA margin from ~60% pro forma to 70-80% steady state, ~60% PAT margin, high ROCE, free cash funding dividends. Fleur: India's largest owner (5,600 rooms, 39 hotels), net EBITDA Rs 850 crore FY27 and Rs 1,000+ crore FY28, ~48%+ post-fee margins, Warburg-backed capital for 2,500+ rooms, capital growth not dividends, and separately listed for market valuation.

*Not explained on the calls:* Absolute valuation of the demerged undertaking and Warburg's price for APG's stake, Fleur's issue price, hold-co discount size, post-demerger ROE, and fate of the two retained leases.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Segregate asset-heavy hotel ownership/development from the asset-light hotel management and brand platform, to achieve operational focus, greater flexibility for capital deployment, clearer alignment of business objectives and unlock long-term shareholder value
- *What it reveals:* Fleur becomes India's largest hotel owner by rooms (5,556 rooms, 39 hotels; FY25 revenue Rs 1,189 cr, net EBITDA Rs 509 cr), carries all group debt, and gets Warburg's Rs 960 crore; Lemon Tree is left debt-free, 80% EBITDA-margin fee business
- *Parent or spin:* both · *Read next:* Fleur's pro-forma financials in the Q4 FY26 presentation (FY27 net EBITDA ~Rs 850 crore) and Fleur's Information Memorandum
- *In their words:* “This structure ensures that the shareholders of the Company directly participate in the economic value of the hotel-ownership and development undertaking through listed shares of the Transferee Company.”

**What the documents themselves say about the differences:**

- **operating margin** — parent / remaining: Pro forma Lemon Tree EBITDA margin of 60% currently, guided to a 70%+ steady-state flow-through (hopefully 75%, possibly 75%-80%); "70%+ EBITDA margins" shown for the fee business; PAT then ~60% of revenue after 22%-25% tax.; separated business: Fleur net EBITDA post renovation and management fees of Rs. 359 cr (44.4%) FY2023, Rs. 423 cr (42.7%) FY2024, Rs. 509 cr (42.8%) FY2025; guided to "north of 48%" of revenue post-renovation, with pre-fees same-store margins "in the late 50s" and gross EBITDA margin expectation of 60% for FY28. “Our expectation is what we have said as guidance is that our steady state flow-through will be 70% +. We are currently at 60% for a very simple reason.”
- **debt and leverage** — parent / remaining: Becomes debt-free: all of the Company's debt is transferred to Fleur under the Scheme; "Debt Free" and "zero-debt company" in the investor presentation.; separated business: Carries the entire group debt — about Rs. 1,300 crore at demerger against ~Rs. 900 crore net EBITDA; could borrow a further ~Rs. 1,300 crore, taking debt to roughly Rs. 2,500-3,000 crore; group debt-to-EBITDA ~2.25x at the time of the FY26 call, total borrowings Rs. 1,500 crore versus Rs. 1,699 crore a year ago at a 7.42% cost of debt. “What will happen is in the scheme of demerger, all the assets of Lemon Tree, including its debt will be transferred to Fleur. Lemon Tree will immediately effectively be a debt-free company from next year.”
- **capex and capital intensity** — parent / remaining: Asset-light with minimal capital required for growth; only technology, marketing and branding spend; renovation/GST/tech cost heads falling from 5.8% of revenue in FY26 to 4.8% in FY27 and 3.7% in FY28; normal renovation 1.2%-1.4% of revenue.; separated business: Capital intensive: holds all owned/leased hotels and the development pipeline; up to ~Rs. 3,000 crore deployable in 12-18 months, Aurika Nehru Place alone requiring about Rs. 700 crore, Aurika Shillong about Rs. 200 crore, and ~Rs. 1 crore a room for the 2,500 rooms under discussion. “Rapidly growing and highly capital efficient business model – ~11,700 rooms operationalised in 20+ years, 70%+ EBITDA margins , and minimal capital required for growth”
- **growth** — parent / remaining: Fee income (Total Income, assuming all assets pay fees) Rs. 112 cr FY2023, Rs. 144 cr FY2024, Rs. 171 cr FY2025 — 23.5% CAGR; inventory 8,382 → 11,769 rooms FY2023 to 9M FY2026 (1.4x); FY26 total management fees Rs. 169.7 cr, up 14%, with third-party fees up 23% to Rs. 73.9 cr and Fleur fees up 8% to Rs. 95.8 cr; managed/franchised pipeline of 9,414 rooms.; separated business: Fleur total revenue Rs. 810 cr FY2023, Rs. 991 cr FY2024, Rs. 1,189 cr FY2025 — 21.2% CAGR; net EBITDA Rs. 359 → 509 cr (19.1% CAGR); net EBITDA guided to Rs. 850 crore or more in FY27 and above Rs. 1,000 crore by FY28; owned portfolio from 3,993 keys / 24 hotels to 5,813 keys / 41 hotels. “Okay. If you look at FY23 to FY26, our fee income of the managed portfolio grew at 27% a year.”
- **cash** — parent / remaining: "Lemon Tree will not need any significant capital other than potentially investments in technology or in marketing and so on. It will be essentially a zero-debt cash accretive company."; post-approval Lemon Tree will define a dividend distribution policy to reward shareholders annually.; separated business: Receives primary equity capital of up to INR 960 crore from Warburg Pincus in tranches, plus a few hundred crore (Rs. 300-350 crore) of its own equity cash; "Fleur is not currently seen as a dividend distributing company". “Fleur Hotels will receive primary investment of up to INR 960 crores of equity capital (in tranches when required) which will provide further capital to fast track its growth”
- **return on capital** — parent / remaining: High RoCE, zero debt, high cash-flow conversion — "Leading to High RoCE"; "Post the reorganization, Lemon Tree will emerge as a debt-free, high-margin, high ROCE company generating strong free cash flows from fees and brand-related income."; separated business: Asset-heavy platform underwritten to hurdle rates — IRR expectation "north of 15%" on the Nehru Place project; acquisitions available "anywhere from 8x of EBITDA to 16x of EBITDA"; "We are not very rigid on structures, but we are very disciplined on returns." “Unlocking intrinsic value of the asset-light hotel management business housed in Lemon Tree; distinct visibility of high quality and rapidly growing fee income. High growth , high RoCE and zero-debt company leading to likely re-rating”
- **tax** — parent / remaining: On a steady-state basis an ~75%-80% EBITDA margin with no depreciation and no interest, taxed at 22%-25%, giving a PAT of about 60% of revenue.; separated business: not stated “This is including technology . Then 75% flow -through means that if you take tax at 22%, then you have a 60% PAT.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: Keeps only two owned/leased hotels with 202 rooms (Indore and Aurangabad, not transferred due to limited remaining lease tenure), and manages/franchises 89 operational hotels with 6,011 rooms plus 127 hotels and 9,414 rooms in the pipeline owned by third parties.; separated business: Owns/leases 39 hotels with 5,556 rooms and 2 under-construction hotels with 256 rooms; highest number of operational rooms among all asset owners (5,556 vs SAMHI 4,862, Chalet 3,359, Ventive 2,140, Juniper 2,130). “Owns/leases and operates 2 hotels with 202 rooms (not transferred due to limited remaining lease tenure)”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

NATCO is demerging its Crop Health Sciences (Agrochemicals) division into Natco Crop Health Sciences Limited, leaving the listed parent as a pure pharmaceutical company (FDFs, APIs, oncology-led branded/complex generics). Management's stated reason is that the two verticals carry different risk-reward profiles and serve entirely different customers — Rajesh Chebiyam said the demerger "gives a more focused approach because the business, ultimately, the customers are quite different" — so a dedicated management, channel and product strategy (differentiated, patent-controlled, limited-competition molecules like the fungicide GLANZ and CTPR combinations) can be run without competing for attention inside a much larger pharma P&L. The second reason is valuation and capital: agro turnover was only INR 60.62 crore in FY25, i.e. 1.48% of total turnover, against FY25 group revenue of INR 4,784 crore and PAT of INR 1,883.4 crore, and Rajeev Nannapaneni said shareholders "will get another business which is not being valued in our system because it is of a very tiny business and a very large business in pharma"; separately listed, "it can raise its own capital and grow by itself." The timing was deliberately set after the division approached breakeven — segment loss of about INR 150 crore in FY25 (including a INR 50 crore non-cash PP&E impairment taken in Q4 FY25), narrowing to a INR 3.2 crore loss in Q1 FY26 on INR 34.7 crore of sales, EBITDA-positive at INR 52.4 crore of sales in Q2 FY26, and roughly INR 140 crore of FY26 sales versus INR 60 crore the prior year, against the INR 150–170 crore management had said was needed for EBITDA breakeven. The Scheme adds the corporate-finance logic: focused growth, operational rationalisation, optimum use of resources, and the ability for each business to "address independent business opportunities, pursue efficient capital allocation and attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders," plus unlocking the value of the verticals. Shareholders get 1 share of the resulting company for every 1 NATCO share, with NATCO retaining 20% of the post-listing equity to keep supporting a business "still at its early growth stages" — so holders retain 100% of the ultimate economic interest (80% direct, 20% through NATCO). The push came from public-market shareholders, not lenders or partners: an investor on the Nov 14, 2025 call asked directly about "value unlocking for the shareholders," and management separately cited shareholder feedback that NATCO's profit base was too concentrated. Agro is almost entirely domestic ("predominantly domestic" sales, with 25–30% input cost inflation flagged in 2026), which management contrasts with the export-weighted pharma business.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. First public confirmation of the plan: demerge Crop Health Sciences out of the parent and list it separately, targeted for 2026, disclosed alongside the division reaching roughly EBITDA breakeven at INR 52.4 crore of quarterly sales. “I think we have announced earlier that we will demerge this business from the main company and list it separately and we are targeting that for the year 2026.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac8f848f-8703-4403-9ae3-cb2d420d47da.pdf)*
2. Rajeev defines the value-unlock logic in response to an investor question: separate listing gives the business special focus and the ability to raise its own capital and grow independently, now that it is breaking even. “Value unlocking means I think what we see is this business now is about breaking even now. So, we will list it separately and then we will have special focus on this and it can raise its own capital and grow by itself.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac8f848f-8703-4403-9ae3-cb2d420d47da.pdf)*
3. The core valuation argument: the agro business is too small to be valued inside a pharma company of NATCO's size, and shareholders will get a complete see-through into both businesses. “I think you will get another business which is not being valued in our system because it is of a very tiny business and a very large business in pharma.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac8f848f-8703-4403-9ae3-cb2d420d47da.pdf)*
4. Timeline guidance: the process has started, with an internal goal of completing in the next 8–9 months (around October–November 2026), but no firm date committed. “I think we have started the process. So , I think roughly, we're thinking by October, November, but I don't want to say any definite time lines, but this is our, what should I say, goal to do.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7ea4dc21-a77e-4e6d-967e-2da2d51bc890.pdf)*
5. Management's clearest operating rationale, from the head of Crop Health Sciences: a focused approach is needed because the agro customer base is entirely different from pharma, with FY26 agro sales of about INR 140 crore versus INR 60 crore the year before. “So, as you're aware, so we're in the process of demerging the business. And one of the primary reasons we felt also it gives a more focused approach because the business, ultimately, the customers are quite different.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=230327e4-9a77-4095-b46d-b9c836cc9b96.pdf)*
6. Growth plans — new differentiated, patent-controlled, limited-competition products, more channel partners and more people — are tied directly back to the demerger as the reason for sharper focus. “So I think we're fairly confident going forward. And that's also one of the main reasons for demerging and having more focus on the business.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=230327e4-9a77-4095-b46d-b9c836cc9b96.pdf)*
7. The Mar 24, 2026 Scheme of Arrangement grounds the demerger in differing risk-reward profiles of the pharmaceutical and agrochemicals verticals; agro turnover was INR 60.62 crore in FY25, 1.48% of total company turnover. “The Board of Directors of the Demerged Company believe that the risk and reward associated with each of the aforesaid business verticals are different.” — *Scheme*
8. The Scheme's capital-markets rationale: each business can chase its own opportunities, allocate capital efficiently and attract its own investor and lender base, alongside focused growth, operational rationalisation and value unlocking. “Each business would be able to address independent business opportunities, pursue efficient capital allocation and attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.” — *Scheme*
9. NATCO keeps 20% of the post-listing equity of the resulting company so it can keep funding and strategically supporting an early-stage business; shareholders get 1 new share for every 1 NATCO share, retaining 100% of the ultimate economic interest (80% direct plus 20% indirect). “Further, the Demerged Company intends to retain the current shareholding in the Resulting Company (20% of post listing shareholding) in order to continue to offer support to the Agrochemicals Business which is still at its early growth stages and help in monitoring the progress and providing strategic support.” — *Scheme*
10. The Nov 14, 2025 board filing states the purpose as unlocking value in the core pharmaceutical business while giving each entity operational flexibility, dedicated management and separate brand positioning. “To demerge the Agro business of the Company into a separate entity, the move shall enable value unlocking of the core business (pharmaceuticals) and enhance long -term growth.” — *Scheme*
11. Pre-demerger baseline for why the division was a drag: a INR 50 crore non-cash impairment on agro property, plant and machinery in Q4 FY25, FY25 agro revenue of about INR 60 crore, and INR 160–170 crore needed just to be EBITDA positive. “So, I think this year, we feel we are going to hit that critical mass where we'll start breaking even. We are doing about INR60 crores net revenue last year. So, I think we need to hit about INR160 crores to INR170 crores at least to have that EBITDA positive.” — *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d43e2593-6819-4d99-b9a6-c3019c901490.pdf)*
12. The Sep 9, 2026 board update: the Scheme had received observation letters from both exchanges but was not filed with the NCLT because the INR 1,300 crore rights issue changes the capital structure, so the Scheme will be amended and re-filed post-issue with the swap ratio unchanged. “The fund raising by way of a Rights Issue proposed at the meeting of the board of directors held on September 09, 2026 is expected to result in change to the Company's capital structure and shareholding pattern and consequently would require necessary changes to the Scheme.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** On the Feb 13, 2025 and May 29, 2025 calls there was no demerger talk — only agro losses, the INR 50 crore impairment and a INR 120–170 crore breakeven target; the Aug 13, 2025 call reported the loss down to INR 3.2 crore with still no mention. The board gave in-principle approval to evaluate the demerger on Sep 25, 2025, and Rajeev first discussed it publicly on the Nov 14, 2025 call ("demerge this business from the main company and list it separately... targeting that for the year 2026"), framing it as value unlocking plus the ability to raise its own capital; the board approved incorporating the wholly-owned resulting company on Nov 14, 2025. On Feb 12, 2026 the timeline was guided to "October, November" 2026 (8–9 months), and the Scheme itself was approved on Mar 24, 2026 with a 1:1 share entitlement, appointed date Oct 1, 2026 and 20% retained by NATCO; the May 29, 2026 call reiterated focus and different customers as the primary reason. By Sep 9, 2026 the Scheme had stock-exchange observation letters but had not been filed with the NCLT, because the INR 1,279.36 crore rights issue at INR 750/share (allotted Oct 23, 2026) changes the capital structure — the board decided to re-cut and re-file the Scheme after the rights issue while keeping the same swap ratio.

**What management expects from it:** Agro: dedicated management focus, its own capital raising, differentiated limited-competition products, growth past breakeven from roughly INR 140 crore sales. Pharma: a cleaner, focused oncology/complex-generics entity. For shareholders: value unlocked in a business "not being valued in our system," a complete see-through into both, operational efficiency, efficient capital allocation, and distinct investor/lender bases.

*Not explained on the calls:* No standalone agro financials, debt/asset split, valuation or swap-ratio basis; no post-demerger profitability, capital needs, board/management, listing date, or revised Scheme terms.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Risk and reward of the pharmaceutical and agrochemicals verticals differ; segregation enables focused growth, operational efficiency, independent capital allocation, different investor sets, and is expected to unlock the value of the business verticals.
- *What it reveals:* Demerged turnover was only ₹60.62 crore, 1.48% of total; FY25 agro segment result was a ₹1,458 million loss. Management says it reached ~₹140 crore sales and roughly EBITDA breakeven. Separation removes a loss-maker from pharma and exposes an early-growth agro business.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* The revised Scheme to be filed with Stock Exchanges post Rights Issue — check the share swap ratio and agro segment numbers.
- *In their words:* “The segregation is also expected to unlock the value of the business verticals of the Demerged Company.”

**What the documents themselves say about the differences:**

- **growth** — parent / remaining: Pharmaceutical business declining as Lenalidomide/Revlimid exclusivity ends: consolidated revenue INR4,375.9 crores in FY26 vs INR4,784 crores in FY25; FY27 guidance of INR3,400–3,500 crores revenue and INR700–750 crores PAT, with 15%–25% compounding only from FY28.; separated business: Agrochemicals growing from a small base — roughly ₹60 crore in FY25 to about ₹140 crore in FY26, driven by product launches, channel expansion and people additions; commercial presence of only 3–4 years. “So yes. So in terms of sale, let's say, this year, we ended up close to INR140 crores, right? And as opposed to a declared number for last year was about INR60 crores.”
- **operating margin** — parent / remaining: Pharmaceuticals segment result ₹6,334 million for the quarter ended 30-09-2025 and ₹24,611 million for the year ended 31-03-2025; consolidated EBITDA margin 46.4% in Q2FY26 and 30.7% in Q3FY26.; separated business: Agro chemicals segment result negative: ₹(66) million for the quarter ended 30-09-2025, ₹(98) million for the half year, and ₹(1,458) million for the year ended 31-03-2025; around break-even at EBITDA level by Q2FY26. “And if you look at the business, now it has grown to about 52 crores this quarter. So, we are at least close to EBITDA positive now. Earlier, we were losing money.”
- **cash** — parent / remaining: Group net cash of about INR2,400 crores (Q4 FY26), reserved for acquisitions rather than a buyback; a further Rights Issue of ₹1,279.36 crore was allotted on 23 October 2026 at ₹750 per share.; separated business: The Resulting Company is expected to raise its own capital after listing, with the Demerged Company retaining about 20% to support it. “So, we will list it separately and then we will have special focus on this and it can raise its own capital and grow by itself.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: Pharmaceutical Undertaking is the mature, cash-generating core with robust R&D capabilities and a US/Brazil/Canada/India/South Africa footprint; R&D spend guided at 7%–9% of sales.; separated business: Agrochemicals is described as still at its early growth stages, with the Demerged Company retaining about 20% post-listing to provide support, monitoring and strategic input; business is predominantly domestic and so more exposed to the 25%–30% rise in input raw material costs. “Further, the Demerged Company intends to retain the current shareholding in the Resulting Company (20% of post listing sh arehold ing) in order to continue to offer support to the Agrochemicals Business which is still at its early growth stages and help in monitoring the progress and providing strategic support.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: Risk and reward profile of the Pharmaceutical vertical differs from the Agrochemicals vertical; demerger intended to unlock value and allow focused capital allocation and different investor sets for each.; separated business: Separate legal entity with dedicated management, different customers and different brand positioning; expected to attract different sets of investors, strategic partners and lenders. “The Board of Directors of the Demerged Company believe that the risk and reward associated with each of the aforesaid business verticals are different.”
