### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

Management presented the separation as the heart of "Vedanta 2.0": dismantling one diversified holding company into five sector-specific pure-play entities — Vedanta Aluminium Metal Ltd, Vedanta Power (renamed from Talwandi Sabo Power), Vedanta Oil & Gas (renamed from Malco Energy), Vedanta Iron & Steel Ltd, and a residual Vedanta Limited holding Zinc India (60.71% of HZL), Zinc International, Copper (Silvassa/Fujairah/KSA), FACOR ferrochrome and nickel/semiconductor assets — on the stated logic that each would "chart out their own growth trajectory and attract respective thematic investors," with sharper accountability and separate dividend policies set by five independent boards. The first problem they said it solves is valuation: one monolithic entity buried the parts, and after listing on 15 June 2026 the company itself claimed the combined value of VEDL plus the four new shares went from ₹225.50 at announcement (29 Sep 2023) to ₹932.05, ">300% upside". The second is capital structure: the ~$5.5bn group net debt (earlier quoted as $6.7bn) was re-architected "aligning debt with earning strength and growth stage of each resulting company" — ~$3.5bn to Aluminium (1.3x EBITDA), Power at 4.7x but on long-dated 7–10 year PFC/REC paper, residual Vedanta Ltd ~$1bn at 0.4x, and Oil & Gas nil / Iron & Steel ≤$0.2bn net debt — against group leverage of 0.95x. Third, it removed rigid cash rules: the prescriptive policy requiring at least 30% of profit as dividend and upstreaming of Hindustan Zinc dividends within six months became "principle-based," giving each board flexibility. Fourth, it repriced intra-group charges: copper's brand fee falls from 3% to 0.75% (~$65mn on $3.1–3.2bn revenue, +2.25% EBITDA), which management expects to lift that near-trading business from ~1% to at least 5% margin in FY27, while the blended group brand fee stays ~$400–450mn and the 3% rate stands to FY29. Fifth, it opens dedicated capital pools — "differentiated capital structure" means "many anchor investors domestically and globally are very keen to come in the cap table," an extra deleveraging avenue for Vedanta Resources' remaining ~$4.7bn debt serviced out of ~$400mn brand fee plus 4–5% dividend. Third parties shaped it: lenders made debt allocation "a precondition for granting NOC"; the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas objected at NCLT over disputed Cairn arbitration dues (~$512mn) and was satisfied only by a Vedanta corporate guarantee ring-fencing the demerged oil & gas entity; and a ₹660 crore full-and-final SEPCO settlement was booked as an exceptional item "paving the way for a proposed demerger process." A second, separate demerger followed on 30 July 2026: ~2,264 acres and ~53,185 sq ft across 22 non-core real estate assets (FY26 turnover ₹1.26 crore, 0.001% of standalone revenue) go to Vedanta Property Platforms Ltd at 1 share per 20 VEDL shares, because the portfolio sat "embedded within the operating business" with "sub-optimal visibility" and a claimed ₹30,000 crore+ of latent value.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. Ajay Goel positioned the demerger purely as value unlock while it was at the shareholder/creditor-approval stage, with the meeting scheduled for 18 February 2025. “This transformative step is poised to unlock significant value for our investors.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/VedantaEarnings-transcript-Jan31-2025.pdf)*
2. Naidoo, in her first call as Group CEO, tied the demerger to the "Vedanta 2.0" ambition of a $100 billion critical minerals, energy and technology powerhouse, with completion then guided for September 2025. “We are making good progress with our demerger plan, aiming to create pure-play entities that will enhance strategic focus and operational flexibility.” — *[Apr 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/Vedanta-CallTranscript-Apr30-2025_v2.pdf)*
3. An investor (Ashish Kejriwal) flagged that mining leases for the Sijimali bauxite and coal blocks had to be transferred to Vedanta Aluminium before the split could close; management confirmed a parallel approvals plan. “But the team has a detailed approvals plan, including all of the mining licenses that will start being approved, in fact, have already started the process.” — *[Apr 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/Vedanta-CallTranscript-Apr30-2025_v2.pdf)*
4. Delays were attributed to two external forums — the NCLT second-motion hearing and an NCLAT stay on the TSPL power order — yet the split was named a top corporate priority. “The execution of the demerger remains a top priority for Vedanta.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta_Transcript_Jul31_2025.pdf)*
5. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, a key counterparty in the oil and gas business, objected at NCLT that the demerged Cairn entity might not be able to pay disputed arbitration dues. “And in the last NCLT hearing, they did express concern about the payments of any of the disputed dues that may become payable by Cairn in case the ongoing arbitration ruling, as we have all learned now, comes in their favor.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta_Transcript_Jul31_2025.pdf)*
6. A long-standing creditor dispute was bought out with a ₹660 crore exceptional charge explicitly to clear the demerger path; MoPNG's objection was neutralised by a Vedanta corporate guarantee covering the full extent of the alleged claims (~$520mn). “As part of demerger proceedings, a full and final settlement of Rs. 660 Cr has been done with SEPCO, thereby resolving a long-standing dispute, paving the way for a proposed demerger process.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/VEDL_Q2FY26_Transcript.pdf)*
7. Goel framed the end state as five separately valued verticals and listed all five demerged entities for the end of FY26, ahead of the final NCLT hearing on 12 November. “On the demerger, we are at the final stage. We remain confident of completing our demerger by end of this fiscal, unlocking focused value across our five verticals.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/VEDL_Q2FY26_Transcript.pdf)*
8. With NCLT approval in hand (16 Dec 2025 for four businesses, 9 Jan 2026 for power), Naidoo gave the fullest statement of purpose — strategy focus, balance-sheet strength and growth — and targeted 1 April as effective date. “This marks a defining moment in our journey, one that empowers our businesses to sharpen the strategies, strengthen the balance sheets and accelerate growth with the aim of unlocking shareholder value.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Transcript_29Jan2026.pdf)*
9. Lenders were an active party: debt allocation across entities had to be agreed with bankers before they would release no-objection certificates, with the $6.7bn consolidated net debt apportioned by assets and each entity's debt-servicing capability. “When we went to the banker seeking NOC, in that case, debt allocation was broadly aligned with the bankers as a precondition for granting NOC for demerger approval.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Transcript_29Jan2026.pdf)*
10. Goel also framed the restructuring as a tax and structuring opportunity (accumulated losses, unabsorbed depreciation) and said it would be used to make oil and gas and iron and steel debt-free, part-funded by a 1.1% HZL OFS worth ~₹3,000 crore. “One thing I can confirm to the entire audience and to the stakeholders at large, that demerger in fact, becomes an opportunity across the areas.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Transcript_29Jan2026.pdf)*
11. The power CEO used the demerger to justify a standalone growth mandate: from 4.2 GW today to ~4.8 GW by H1FY27 and a plan for an additional 10–12 GW over five to seven years. “And as we demerge, we really want to be a growth company and ride the India's growth story on energy.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Transcript_29Jan2026.pdf)*
12. On the final pre-demerger call Goel set out the structural logic: five pure-plays, each attracting its own investor base, effective 1 May 2026 with one VEDL share earning four additional shares and trading expected by mid-June. “This will entail creation of five independent sector-specific pure-play companies, allowing each company to chart out their own growth trajectory and attract respective thematic investors.” — *[Apr 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta-Transcript-Apr29-2026.pdf)*
13. Capital structure was deliberately engineered per entity — Oil & Gas nil debt, Iron & Steel ≤$0.2bn, Aluminium ~$3.5bn at 1.3x, Power 4.7x on 7–10 year PFC/REC maturities, Vedanta Ltd ~$1bn at 0.4x — against group leverage of 0.95x. “The de-merger has been architected with precision on capital structure, aligning debt with earning strength and growth stage of each resulting company.” — *[Apr 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta-Transcript-Apr29-2026.pdf)*
14. The split removed prescriptive cash rules: the mandatory 30% profit payout and the six-month Hindustan Zinc dividend upstreaming requirement give way to board discretion at each of the five companies. “Currently, Vedanta's policy on dividend is more prescriptive; it will become more descriptive.” — *[Apr 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta-Transcript-Apr29-2026.pdf)*
15. Unbundling also repriced the brand fee for the thin-margin copper business, which management expects to lift copper margins from ~1% to at least 5% in FY27 (~$65mn benefit), while blended group brand fee stays flat and the 3% rate holds to FY29. “So the brand fee for copper from the current 3% will go down to 0.75% and that alone from India's viewpoint means higher EBITDA by 2.25%.” — *[Apr 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta-Transcript-Apr29-2026.pdf)*
16. Separate cap tables were pitched as a new deleveraging channel for Vedanta Resources, which still carries $4.7bn of debt against ~$400mn brand fee plus a 4–5% dividend. “Now as we de-merge all the five companies, additionally we'll have the optionality of a differentiated capital structure and in that case, many anchor investors domestically and globally are very keen to come in the cap table, and that will be additional avenue for de-leveraging.” — *[Apr 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta-Transcript-Apr29-2026.pdf)*
17. Asked whether the entities could still acquire outside their sector, Naidoo said business CEOs are mandated to grow organically on their own 2x/3x plans while cross-sector M&A sits at a holdco with its own team and the Chairman. “Holdco will be set up to make sure there is some visibility of capital allocation across all 5 businesses, but also with its own M&A team to start looking at some of these opportunities.” — *[Apr 2026](https://www.vedantalimited.com/uploads/investor-overview/financial-results/2026/Vedanta-Transcript-Apr29-2026.pdf)*
18. The 30 July 2026 real-estate scheme (VEDL into Vedanta Property Platforms Ltd, 1 share for every 20) rests on the claim that ~2,264 acres and ~53,185 sq ft across 22 assets were trapped inside the operating business — FY26 turnover of just ₹1.26 crore, 0.001% of standalone revenue — with a claimed ₹30,000 crore+ of latent value. “The real estate business is currently embedded within the operating business and the real estate portfolio has been historically subject to limited focused utilisation, resulting in sub-optimal visibility of the real estate business segment and value realization.” — *Scheme*
19. The stated benefits mirror the five-way split — dedicated management and governance, sector-specific investors, lenders and strategic partners, and separate financial disclosure enabling clearer valuation; VPPL may also absorb real estate from Meenakshi Energy and Incab Industries. “enabling focused and sharper capital market access and thereby unlocking the value of the Demerged Undertaking and creating enhanced value for shareholders.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** By the Feb 2025 (Q3FY25) call the scheme was already in execution with shareholder/creditor meetings set for 18 Feb 2025, and in Apr 2025 (Q4FY25) new Group CEO Deshnee Naidoo folded it into "Vedanta 2.0" with completion guided for September 2025. It then slipped repeatedly through regulatory friction: Aug 2025 (Q1FY26) disclosed the NCLT second-motion part-hearing of 2 July with the next date 20 August, an NCLAT interim stay on the TSPL power order (₹1,248 crore bank guarantee posted) and MoPNG objections; Nov 2025 (Q2FY26) set final hearing for 12 November, settled SEPCO for ₹660 crore and gave MoPNG a Vedanta corporate guarantee; Jan 2026 (Q3FY26) reported NCLT approval on 16 Dec 2025 for four businesses and 9 Jan 2026 for power, Ind AS 105 discontinued-operations accounting, and a 1 April effective-date target. Apr 2026 (Q4FY26) was the final pre-demerger call: effective and record date 1 May 2026, one VEDL share earning four additional shares, listing by mid-June, plus newly disclosed mechanics — the copper brand-fee cut, the principle-based dividend policy and holdco-level M&A. After listing, the 30 July 2026 board meeting opened a further leg by approving the real-estate demerger into VPPL, targeted for completion in FY28.

**What management expects from it:** Each pure-play sets its own strategy, dividend policy and capital structure: Aluminium 1.3x levered on strong cash flow, Power a 10–12 GW growth story, Oil & Gas and Iron & Steel debt-free, residual Vedanta Ltd 0.4x with HZL dividends optional and copper margins rising 1%-to-5% on a 0.75% brand fee. Thematic investors and anchor capital per cap table; simpler structures, sharper accountability, value unlock (claimed >300%).

*Not explained on the calls:* No explanation of why these five groupings, no SOTP targets, separation costs, dis-synergies, duplicated corporate overhead, or who originally proposed the split.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Creation of five independent sector-specific pure-play companies, allowing each to chart its own growth trajectory and attract thematic investors; 'simpler structures, sharper accountability, and focused platforms to drive growth and value creation.'
- *What it reveals:* Separation exposes Zinc India's 56-57% margins and residual VEDL at 0.30x net debt/EBITDA with AA+ upgrade, versus Vedanta Power's 4.7x pro-forma leverage; combined market cap of resulting companies grew over ₹71,000 crore in Q1FY27.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* Vedanta Power Limited's own first standalone results/production release — TSPL plant availability, Athena restart and its 4.7x leverage
- *In their words:* “The Scheme has come into effect on May 01, 2026, being the Effective Date (as defined under the Scheme).”

**What the documents themselves say about the differences:**

- **debt and leverage** — parent / remaining: Vedanta Limited (remaining) keeps about $1 billion of net debt at 0.4x net debt/EBITDA, serviceable "through FACOR, through Zinc International, and the Copper" plus Zinc India dividends; Q1FY27 net debt ₹8,299 crore and net debt/EBITDA 0.30x, gross debt ₹28,291 crore; separated business: Of $5.5 billion group net debt, Vedanta Aluminium takes $3.5 billion (1.3x); Vedanta Power's leverage 4.7x with mostly long-term PFC/REC debt of 7 to 10 years; Vedanta Oil and Gas debt-free; Vedanta Iron and Steel no more than $0.2 billion “So out of 5.5, 3.5 goes to Vedanta Aluminum, and looking at the EBITDA of that business, their leverage will be still 1.3.”
- **debt and leverage** — parent / remaining: Continuing operations carried ₹10,522 crore of net debt as on 31 March 2026, reduced to ₹8,299 crore by 30 June 2026; separated business: ₹42,732 crore of the ₹53,254 crore group net debt as on 31 March 2026 went out with the discontinued (demerged) operations “At Vedanta group level pre-de-merger, our leverage stands at 0.95x, reflecting resilient EBITDA and disciplined financial structuring.”
- **operating margin** — parent / remaining: Remaining Vedanta Limited: Q1FY27 EBITDA ₹8,469 crore on revenue ₹23,456 crore, EBITDA margin 57% (excludes copper business), up 985 bps YoY; separated business: Pre-demerger combined group: Q4FY26 EBITDA margin ~44% (record) and FY26 ~39%; Aluminium FY26 margin 38%, Zinc India 56%, Cairn Oil and Gas ~44% “EBITDA margin# of 57%, up by 985 bps YoY and 225 bps QoQ”
- **return on capital** — parent / remaining: Remaining Vedanta Limited: ROCE c.29% in Q1FY27 ("ROCE is EBIT net of tax outflow divided by average capital employed"); separated business: Pre-demerger combined group: "Record Return on Capital Employed at ~32%, improved by 539 bps YoY" in Q4FY26; 27% in Q3FY26 and ~26% in Q2FY26 “Strong Return on Capital Employed at 29%, reflecting disciplined capital allocation”
- **capex and capital intensity** — parent / remaining: Remaining Vedanta Limited: growth capex ₹1,148 crore in Q1FY27 (project capex ₹1,181 crore and sustaining capex ₹1,390 crore in the net debt walk); separated business: Pre-demerger combined group: "Total capital expenditure in the year stood at ₹ 14,918 crores" in FY26 (c.$1.7 billion), deployed across aluminium, zinc, oil and gas and power; Saudi rod mill and Gamsberg Phase 3 plans of $2 billion and $4 billion discussed for the separated/retained international businesses “Invested Growth Capex of ₹1,148 crore in Q1 FY27”
- **cash** — parent / remaining: Remaining Vedanta Limited: cash and cash equivalents ₹19,992 crore at 30 June 2026 (Zinc India ₹12,892 crore of it), FCF pre-capex ₹4,412 crore in Q1FY27; separated business: Pre-demerger combined group: "Cash and Cash Equivalent stood at ₹28,485, improving by 38% YoY on the back of Free cash flow (pre-capex) of ₹ 26,013 crore" in FY26 “Cash and cash equivalents position remains strong at ₹ 19,992 crore .”
- **growth** — parent / remaining: Remaining Vedanta Limited: Q1FY27 PAT ₹5,294 crore, up 152% YoY, on continuing operations; credit rating upgraded to AA+/Stable by both ICRA and CRISIL (highest since 2014); separated business: Market value created by the separated entities after listing: combined market capitalisation of the resulting companies up over ₹71,000 crore in Q1FY27 “Vedanta’s demerger is unlocking significant shareholder value, with combined market cap of resulting companies growing by over ₹71,000 crore in the 1st quarter .”
- **tax** — parent / remaining: Remaining Vedanta Limited: normalized effective tax rate 26% in Q1FY27 versus 28% in Q1FY26, with a tax charge of ₹1,895 crore; separated business: not stated; the cost-of-acquisition apportionment was made "in accordance with Sections 73 of the Income-tax, Act, 2025" and the resulting-company share issue was "in accordance with the provisions of Section 2(35) of the Income-tax Act, 2025" “Normalized ETR is 26% vs 28% in Q1’ FY26, lower due to reduced losses in subsidiaries wherein DTA is not recognized .”
- **other** — parent / remaining: Remaining Vedanta Limited revenue: ₹23,456 crore in Q1FY27 (continuing operations only); separated business: Pre-demerger combined group revenue: ₹51,524 crore in Q4FY26 and ₹1,74,075 crore in FY26 — i.e. the continuing business is well under half the former group's quarterly revenue “Achieved C onsolidated Revenue of ₹23,456 crore, up 51% YoY and down 1% QoQ”

**Reading: VERY LIKELY — the piece is under a tenth of the whole; index funds and large holders who receive it without choosing it tend to sell.**

| Apollo Healthtech Limited | "The turnover of the Identified Business Undertaking I deme… | 0.86% | 42.8% (FY2026) | — | — | not listed |

**In the documents' words:** “The turnover of the Identified Business Undertaking I demerged division for the year ended March 31, 2025 was INR 70.13 Crores representing 0.86% of the total standalone turnover of the Company for the year ended March 31, 2025.”

**The judge's read of selling pressure:** likely — Shares distributed to all 1.75 lakh AHEL holders in a different industry (pharmacy distribution/digital health) than the hospital parent they own

Under the 2026 Cloudnine transaction: not stated (consideration of cash and a 9.9% stake goes to AHLL, not to AHEL shareholders).
- **Management incentives:** Treatment of existing grants in the Scheme is not stated; no new plan of the new entity is described. The documents state: "In addition, an agreement dated June 30, 2025 has been executed between Rasmeli Limited (an existing shareholder of Transferor Company I) ('Rasmeli') and Ms. Shobana Kamineni (the promoter of Transferor Company I) ('AHL Promoter'), in terms of which Rasmeli has agreed to share an agreed portion of the upside received by it pursuant to its investment into Transferor Company I with the AHL Promoter and designated employees, in order to incentivise the management of such companies. Upon the effectiveness of the Scheme, the obligation of Rasmeli to provide upside as described above would stand automatically linked to the shareholding of Rasmeli in Resultant Company." Further: "No minimum amount is guaranteed, with a maximum of 9% of the upside delivered to Rasmeli for achieving at least 4x MOIC." and "Ms. Shobana Kamineni (the proposed Executive Chairperson of Apollo Healthtech) has been given flexibility to identify the relevant employees who will be the beneficiaries of the Upside Agreement so that the contributions of the employees who drive value creation over time is recognised and rewarded. Any such identification of beneficiaries will be done by Ms. Shobana Kamineni, in consultation with the Board of Apollo Healthtech (and the relevant committees thereof)." Exercise price or pricing date: not stated.

The stated promoter/management actions around the separation are: the Upside Agreement dated June 30, 2025 under which Rasmeli Limited shares an agreed portion of its investment upside with Ms. Shobana Kamineni (the promoter of Apollo Healthco) and designated employees; Ms. Shobana Kamineni's proposed appointment as Executive Chairperson of Apollo Healthtech "pursuant to and upon sanction of the Scheme by the Hon'ble NCLT and consequent effectiveness of the Scheme"; and the promoter and promoter group's commitments to waive board nomination rights below the stated 10% aggregate and 5% individual shareholding thresholds, with the Articles of Association of Apollo Healthtech "to be suitably amended, after the Scheme becomes effective, to give effect to these waivers." Shobana Kamineni to be Executive Chairperson of Resultant Company; Rasmeli-funded upside share agreement (max 9% of upside at 4x MOIC) to her and identified employees; new ESOP to be established · *option pricing date:* not stated

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The business being separated is AHEL's omnichannel pharmacy and digital health vertical — Apollo HealthCo, comprising the ~7,500-store Apollo Pharmacy retail/front-end network and the Apollo 24/7 digital platform (46mn users, INR 528 cr quarterly platform GMV) — which is being demerged into Apollo Healthtech Ltd, with Apollo Healthco Ltd and the promoter-linked distributor Keimed Private Limited (which supplies ~60,000 pharmacy stores) amalgamated into the same vehicle, which is then renamed Apollo Healthco Limited and listed; hospital-based pharmacies stay inside Healthcare Services, since as A. Krishnan put it in Aug 2025, 'what we are spinning out is only the retail pharmacies and the online.' The Scheme's own rationale states the problem plainly: the Identified Business Undertaking is 'distinct from other businesses undertaken by the Demerged Company' and 'necessitates a differentiated strategy aligned to its industry specific risks, market dynamics, and growth trajectory', so separation lets hospitals and retail/digital each focus on 'their respective businesses, efficient management, and control', consolidates HealthCo's and Keimed's distribution 'in an independent company focusing exclusively on digital health and pharmacy distribution', and lets the new entity 'build a wider capital and financial base, by attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and stakeholders' — plus supply-chain integration, wider assortment, 'improved transparency in the supply chain preventing the entry of counterfeit or substandard medicines', administrative efficiency, board/managerial rationalisation and economies of scale. The financial case management repeated for six straight quarters is scale plus margin convergence: pro-forma combined revenue of INR 4,430 cr in Q1 FY26 (~INR 17,000 cr run-rate, INR 19,000 cr for FY26) becoming a INR 25,000 cr run-rate at 7% EBITDA by Q4 FY27; Sanjiv Gupta's arithmetic was that a 3.2% blended FY25 margin is already 6.4% once Apollo 24/7's losses and the accelerated ESOP charge are stripped out, with offline pharmacy going 7.4%→8-9% on private label (15.5% of pharmacy sales) and Keimed 3.1%→3.5%. The loss drag has in fact collapsed — digital cash losses fell from INR 111 cr (Q4 FY24) and INR 101 cr (Q2 FY25) to INR 29 cr in Q3 FY26 and INR 16 cr in Q4 FY26, with breakeven ex-ESOP guided to Q1 FY27 and including ESOP (~INR 50 cr FY27) by Q3 FY27 — and Apollo HealthCo crossed INR 10,000 cr of annual revenue in FY26, making it listable on its own. Keimed's merger was justified on concrete synergies: shared technology, data, people and product categories, cheaper dark stores (22 today) to push beyond the top six metros to the next ten cities, and private-label penetration across Keimed's franchise base. The push is not purely internal: Rasmeli Limited, the investor holding Class A/B compulsorily convertible preference shares in Apollo Healthco, receives a nominee director in the Resultant Company and signed a June 30, 2025 Upside Agreement sharing up to 9% of its own upside (only above 4x MOIC) with Ms. Shobana Kamineni — proposed Executive Chairperson — and identified employees; after shareholder and proxy-adviser pushback the Company issued clarifications on June 15 and June 19, 2026 adding 10% fall-away thresholds on nomination rights, tiered caps on promoter nominees, an individual 5% waiver, six independent directors and a Lead Independent Director. A second, separate separation was announced in May 2026: AHLL's Apollo Cradle and fertility verticals (INR 450 cr FY26 revenue, INR 45 cr IGAAP EBITDA) were combined with Cloudnine at INR 1,550 cr — 35x EBITDA — for cash plus a 9.9% stake, with the INR 750 cr of cash redeployed into primary care and diagnostics, which management called the funnel into Apollo.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. Earliest reference in the window: integration of the acquired distribution business plus offline pharmacy growth is framed as the path to HealthCo's 'strategic intent' over three years, before any demerger language appears. “Transaction integration and healthy growth in offline pharmacy distribution revenues will drive Apollo HealthCo towards its stated strategic intent in the next 3 years.” — *[Aug 2024](https://www.apollohospitals.com/apollo_pdf/Transcript-of-Apollo-Hospitals-Q1-FY25.pdf)*
2. The restructuring is still presented as a merger-plus-breakeven story, with Sanjiv Gupta quantifying the FY27 target for the combined entity at INR 25,000 crore of revenue and 6-7% EBITDA, against a then run-rate of ~INR 17,000 crore at 6.5% excluding digital losses. “So, we are looking at about INR 25,000 crore of revenue and about 6% to 7% of EBITDA in FY 27.” — *[Feb 2025](https://cdn.apollohospitals.com/apollohospitals/apollo_pdf/Transcript-of-Apollo-Hospitals-Q3-FY25.pdf)*
3. Suneeta Reddy's closing remarks on the Q4 FY25 call tie the Keimed merger explicitly to scale and margin durability in pharmacy, not to a listing. “The Keimed merger process is also progressing well, which will further enhance scale and margin resilience in our Pharmacy business.” — *[Jun 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-06/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q4-fy25-earnings-call---1-.pdf)*
4. Sanjiv Gupta gave the margin bridge that underpins the 7% target: removing Apollo 24/7's operating losses and the ESOP charge (INR 100 cr in FY26, falling to a third thereafter) lifts the blended 3.2% to 6.4% even on then-current numbers. “If I remove these two things, if I assume these two things even today and remove these losses and the ESOP cost, the new number that comes for the EBITDA percentage is 6.4%.” — *[Jun 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-06/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q4-fy25-earnings-call---1-.pdf)*
5. First explicit statement on a call of the demerger and separate listing, with the 18-21 month timetable and the INR 25,000 crore / 7% EBITDA end-state for the scheme concluding by FY27. “The strategic reorganization of our omni -channel pharmacy and digital health business is proceeding as planned , and we expect to complete all steps within 18 to 21 months, a timeline that we had earlier announced.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-08/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q1-fy26-earnings-call---13-august-2025.pdf)*
6. A. Krishnan confirmed the mechanics in answer to an investor: HealthCo in its current form is the entity being demerged and listed by Q4 FY27, by which time Keimed's NCLT merger will also have happened. “What will happen is Apollo HealthCo., as you are seeing in the current form, is what is going to be demerged and will be listed separately by Q4 of FY27.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-08/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q1-fy26-earnings-call---13-august-2025.pdf)*
7. Scope limit made explicit — hospital-based pharmacies stay with Healthcare Services; only the ~6,500-store retail chain and the online business leave, alongside Keimed, which supplies about 60,000 third-party pharmacy stores. “The hospital -based pharmacies continues as part of hospitals, which I am sure you know, but it is something that , remember, what we are spinning out is only the retail pharmacies and the online out of that.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-08/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q1-fy26-earnings-call---13-august-2025.pdf)*
8. Madhivanan Balakrishnan listed the Keimed synergies: shared technology, data and people, cheaper dark stores (22 at the time) enabling expansion from the top 6 cities to the next 10 and beyond, and private label (then 14.6% of sales) pushed across Keimed's franchises. “So , technology, data, people, and product categories , all the four synergies should start playing out as this merger comes in place.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2025-08/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q1-fy26-earnings-call---13-august-2025.pdf)*
9. Process update framing the combination as the way to capture scale benefits inside HealthCo; separately Madhivanan said merging Keimed, Apollo Pharmacy and the digital business would release further cost synergies from the next financial year. “The statutory processes for the restructuring within Apollo HealthCo and the Keimed merger continue to proceed as per plan, and we remain well positioned to capture the full benefit of scale within Apollo HealthCo.” — *[Nov 2025](https://drupal-cdn-hfaeddcdbng5hfbg.a01.azurefd.net/sites/default/files/2025-11/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q2-fy26-earnings-call---7-november-2025....pdf)*
10. Regulatory progress is reported and the combined-entity target is restated verbatim as INR 25,000 crore run-rate revenue with 7% EBITDA. “We have also made progress with respect to the regulatory integration process for the com posite scheme of Keimed merger and demerger of Apollo HealthCo and remain well positioned to capture the full benefits of scale with the combined entity to achieve a run rate of INR 25,000 crore in combined revenues with 7% EBITDA.” — *[Feb 2026](https://drupal-cdn-hfaeddcdbng5hfbg.a01.azurefd.net/sites/default/files/2026-02/transcript-of-ahel-q3fy26-concall_11feb2026.pdf)*
11. Obul Reddy itemised the approvals obtained (CCI, SEBI) and the NCLT filing, and confirmed Keimed had been cleaned up so that its subsidiaries are 100% owned before the merger. “We have obtained Competition Commission approval and SEBI approval. We have filed with NCLT.” — *[Feb 2026](https://drupal-cdn-hfaeddcdbng5hfbg.a01.azurefd.net/sites/default/files/2026-02/transcript-of-ahel-q3fy26-concall_11feb2026.pdf)*
12. The purpose is stated in value terms for the first time in opening remarks — sharpening focus and unlocking long-term value across the integrated platform — in the same breath as HealthCo crossing INR 10,000 crore of annual revenue. “During the year, we also announced a strategic restructuring of the omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business, an important step towards sharpening focus on unlocking long -term value across our integrated health care platform.” — *[May 2026](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q4-fy26-earnings-call.pdf)*
13. Timeline and end-state confirmed: NCLT-convened shareholder meeting on June 24, 2026, listing of Apollo Healthtech around end-December/early Q4 FY27, annualised revenue of INR 25,000 crore at listing. “And hopefully, by Q4 FY27, end of December or early Q4 FY27 is when Apollo Healthtech should get demerged and listed.” — *[May 2026](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q4-fy26-earnings-call.pdf)*
14. A second, separate disposal: AHLL's Cradle and fertility verticals (INR 450 cr revenue, INR 45 cr EBITDA) go into a Cloudnine-combined platform at INR 1,550 crore — 35x EBITDA — for cash plus a 9.9% stake, with INR 750 crore of cash redeployed into primary care and diagnostics. “One is the valuation, which is clearly key to get a valuation of INR 1,500 for EBITDA at a multiple of 35 in this market is something that you cannot ignore.” — *[May 2026](https://www.apollohospitals.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/transcript-of-apollo-hospitals---q4-fy26-earnings-call.pdf)*
15. The Scheme's stated core problem: the pharmacy/digital undertaking is a different business from hospitals and needs its own strategy, risk posture and growth path; separation gives each side focus, management and control. “The Scheme would enable carving-out of the Identified Business Undertaking, which is distinct from other businesses undertaken by the Demerged Company, necessitates a differentiated strategy aligned to its industry specific risks, market dynamics, and growth trajectory.” — *Scheme*
16. Capital-markets rationale: the separated entity is expected to attract its own investors, partners and lenders — i.e. a funding base hospitals cannot supply. “The Scheme is expected to enable Resultant Company to build a wider capital and financial base, by attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and stakeholders, as well as promoting overall business growth;” — *Scheme*
17. The Keimed leg is justified as consolidating pharmacy distribution into a single pure-play vehicle, with the Scheme also citing supply-chain integration, wider assortment, counterfeit prevention, administrative efficiency and board rationalisation. “The Scheme would also result in consolidation of pharmacy distribution business of Transferor Company 1 and Transferor Company 2, in an independent company focusing exclusively on digital health and pharmacy distribution, enabling synergies;” — *Scheme*
18. Governance package embedded in the Scheme: a 12-member board with 6 independents, the AHL Promoter as Executive Chairperson, three promoter nominees, one AHEL nominee and one nominee for investor Rasmeli Limited, plus the Rasmeli-funded upside-sharing arrangement with Ms. Shobana Kamineni and identified employees. “reconstitution of the board of directors of Resultant Company as follows: (i) AHL Promoter (as defined in the Scheme); (ii) 3 (three) directors nominated by the Resultant Company Promoters (as defined in the Scheme); (iii) 1 (one) director nominated by the Demerged Company; (iv) 1 (one) director nominated by Rasmeli Limited; and (v) 6 (six) independent directors;” — *Scheme*
19. June 15, 2026 clarification issued in response to shareholder feedback: the Upside Agreement is investor-funded with no cash outflow from Apollo Healthtech, capped and conditional on a 4x MOIC hurdle, and Rasmeli plus the promoter group will waive nomination rights below 10% shareholding. “No minimum amount is guaranteed, with a maximum of 9% of the upside delivered to Rasmeli for achievin g at least 4x MOIC.” — *Scheme*
20. June 19, 2026 follow-up added a sliding scale of promoter nominee caps (nil below 10%, up to 5 at 35%+), an individual 5% waiver per promoter entity, half the board independent while there is an executive chairperson, and a Lead Independent Director. “Apollo Hospitals now further clarifies that the promoter and promoter gro up are committ ed to waiving their rights to nominate directors in excess of the maximum numbers set out below, by reference to their aggregate shareholding.” — *Scheme*
21. Shareholder vote on June 24, 2026 passed the Scheme (90.44% of votes polled in favour; 85.71% of public votes), but institutional public shareholders split 85.69% for / 14.31% against — the clearest sign of residual investor discomfort, which no earnings call addressed. “the public shareholders of the Demerged Company have approved the Scheme the votes cast in favour of the Scheme are more than the votes cast against the Scheme.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced before this window as the 'strategic intent' for Apollo HealthCo (Aug 14, 2024 call) and was tracked through Feb 11, 2025 and the May 31, 2025 (Jun 2025) call purely as the Keimed merger 'progressing well', with a ~15-month timeline and Sanjiv Gupta's 3.2%→7% FY27 margin bridge; the composite Scheme itself was board-approved and filed on June 30, 2025. On the Aug 13, 2025 call management first spelled out the full shape — Apollo HealthCo as it stands gets demerged and separately listed by Q4 FY27, all steps within 18-21 months, only retail plus online moving out, Keimed folded in for technology/data/people/product synergies. Nov 7, 2025 and Feb 11, 2026 were process updates (statutory steps on track; CCI and SEBI approvals obtained, NSE no-objection Dec 23, 2025, NCLT filed and hearings begun, Keimed's subsidiaries consolidated to 100%), and the May 21, 2026 call set the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting for June 24, 2026 with completion still Q4 FY27. In the final stretch the plan changed on governance rather than structure: clarifications dated June 15 and June 19, 2026 added nomination-right fall-away thresholds in response to shareholder feedback, and on June 24, 2026 the Scheme passed with 90.44% of all votes and 85.71% of public votes in favour, but 14.31% of institutional votes against.

**What management expects from it:** Apollo Healthtech becomes a pure-play pharmacy and digital health company: INR 25,000 cr run-rate revenue at 6.5-7% EBITDA by Q4 FY27 (FY26 exit 4.3%), digital at breakeven, Keimed 3.1%-to-3.5%, offline pharmacy 8-9% on private label, its own investors, lenders and board. AHEL keeps hospitals and AHLL at 25.4% ROCE, redeploying cash into beds, primary care and diagnostics.

*Not explained on the calls:* Calls never discussed the share entitlement ratio, debt/cash split, AHEL's residual stake, Keimed's purchase valuation or related-party pricing, the 14.31% institutional dissent, or the Upside Agreement.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Value unlocking via separation and independent listing: sharper strategic focus, operational flexibility, enhanced capital allocation, clearer investor visibility, plus consolidation of pharmacy distribution and a wider capital base
- *What it reveals:* A pharmacy/digital platform at ~INR 25,000 crore run-rate revenue with 6.5-7% targeted EBITDA margin, digital losses near breakeven, Keimed distribution consolidated; promoter and investor incentives concentrated in the spin, not the hospital parent
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *Read next:* The Scheme's Demerger Share Entitlement Ratio and the Part E abridged-prospectus disclosures for Apollo Healthtech
- *In their words:* “During the year, we also announced a strategic restructuring of the omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business, an important step towards sharpening focus on unlocking long-term value across our integrated health care platform.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The business being separated is HUL's Ice Cream business — brands Kwality Wall's, Cornetto and Magnum — demerged into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited (KWIL) under a Sections 230-232 scheme sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 30th October 2025 (rectified 6th November 2025), effective (and appointed) 1st December 2025. The stated commercial logic in the scheme is creation of a leading listed Indian ice cream company with focused management having 'greater flexibility to deploy strategies suited to the Ice Cream businesses' distinctive operating model and market dynamics, to realise its full potential'; on the Feb 2026 call Priya Nair framed the same point as 'a dedicated management team and singular focus' letting KWIL capitalise on a growing India market. The financial problem it solves for HUL is dilution: management sized Ice Cream at 'roughly 3-odd percentage of our business' earning 'low single-digit margin' — below HUL average, and even below that in FY26 because of monsoon and investment impacts — so removing it adds 50-60 bps to reported EBITDA margin, which is exactly how the band moved from 22-23% to an implied 22.5-23.5% (confirmed by Niranjan Gupta as 'the implied number' and restated as the mid-term guide in May 2026). The business was also volatile and seasonal: September quarter 2025 Ice Cream 'declined year on year, impacted by extended monsoon in addition to GST transition', while March quarter 2025 had double-digit volume-led growth. Execution was a deliberate two-step: demerge and report Ice Cream as a discontinued business from the December 2025 quarter, then list — KWIL allotted 2,34,95,91,262 equity shares of Re. 1 on a 1:1 entitlement to HUL holders of record 5th December 2025, listing and trading from 16th February 2026, with cost of acquisition apportioned 98.09% HUL / 1.91% KWIL based on HUL net worth versus Ice Cream net assets at 30th November 2025. Accounting consequences disclosed were a one-time non-cash gain inside reported PAT of Rs 6,603 crores (+121% y-o-y) in the December 2025 quarter, and loss of PLI benefit accruals that had flowed through other operating income. Strategically it is presented as one leg of continuous portfolio rotation toward 'fewer, bigger bets' — alongside Pureit divestment (circa Rs 600 crores), Minimalist (90.5%), OZiva (remaining 49% for Rs 824 crores) and the Nutritionalab exit (Rs 307 crores) — with May 2026 citing the Ice Cream demerger as already 'enhancing the growth mix of the portfolio'.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The scheme's own stated benefit is a focused, separately listed Indian ice cream company whose management can run strategies fitted to ice cream's different operating model and market dynamics. “Creation of a leading listed ice cream company in India with focused management having greater flexibility to deploy strategies suited to the Ice Cream businesses’ distinctive operating model and market dynamics, to realise its full potential” — *Scheme*
2. First mention in the window is purely a status update on regulatory progress and completion timing, listed alongside Pureit divestment and the Minimalist/OZiva portfolio moves. “The demerger of Ice cream business is progressing on track with regulatory requirements, and we expect it to be completed by the end of financial year 2026.” — *[Apr 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=57aad284-8283-4c21-8035-99627387a92d.pdf)*
3. Ritesh Tiwari quantified the margin rationale: Ice Cream runs below HUL's average margin, so its exit lifts reported EBITDA margin by 50-60 bps over the 22-23% guided band. “Coming to EBITDA margin, Ice Cream demerger is expected to result in an improvement of 50-60 bps to the reported margin as Ice Cream business operates at a margin lower than HUL average.” — *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2eb875fe-ef79-4b40-88b8-228ccc8be17e.pdf)*
4. He sized the business being removed — about 3% of HUL turnover earning low single-digit margins, and even lower in FY26 because of monsoon and investment impacts. “Ice Cream, as we had called out even earlier, it's roughly 3-odd percentage of our business. and the business makes low single-digit margin.” — *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2eb875fe-ef79-4b40-88b8-228ccc8be17e.pdf)*
5. The plan was explicitly sequenced in two steps — demerge and report Ice Cream as a discontinued business from the December quarter, then list the entity in the March quarter. “So, this is two-step process, demerger, reporting discontinued business for December quarter and then listing the business in March quarter.” — *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2eb875fe-ef79-4b40-88b8-228ccc8be17e.pdf)*
6. The segment's in-quarter weakness underlined its seasonality and volatility: it declined year-on-year on extended monsoon plus GST transition, and its PLI benefit would stop flowing into HUL's P&L. “Ice Cream business declined year on year, impacted by extended monsoon in addition to GST transition.” — *[Oct 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2eb875fe-ef79-4b40-88b8-228ccc8be17e.pdf)*
7. Priya Nair stated the completion and gave the focus argument for KWIL — a dedicated management team with singular focus to pursue India's growing ice cream opportunity; listing set for 16th February. “With a dedicated management team and singular focus, we are confident that KWIL is well positioned to capitalise on the growing market opportunity in India and deliver sustained performance.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=38a5c0b9-6eee-4de5-bdd8-98ac200204cc.pdf)*
8. The guidance band was formally rebased for the demerger — 22-23% plus roughly 50 bps, which Niranjan Gupta confirmed as an implied 22.5-23.5%; December quarter EBITDA margin of 23.3% was reported excluding Ice Cream. “We also outlined that the range, therefore, you will see a benefit of the ice cream demerger to the extent of 50 basis points.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=38a5c0b9-6eee-4de5-bdd8-98ac200204cc.pdf)*
9. Accounting effect disclosed: reported PAT of Rs 6,603 crores (+121% y-o-y) included a one-time non-cash gain from the Ice Cream demerger recognised per the approved scheme. “And the second item is one- time non -cash gain arising from I ce Cream demerger accounted for in accordance with the approved scheme of demerger and applicable accounting standards.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=38a5c0b9-6eee-4de5-bdd8-98ac200204cc.pdf)*
10. The demerger is retrospectively grouped with the OZiva and Minimalist investments as portfolio rotation that has already improved the quality and growth profile of what remains. “Strategic actions such as the demerger of Ice Cream, along with the investments at OZiva and Minimalist, are already enhancing the growth mix of the portfolio.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=55988411-440d-4801-8c08-90a5908c4a04.pdf)*
11. On perimeter: asked why HUL is doubling down on Foods while Unilever globally exits foods, Priya Nair said HUL's Foods (Tea, Coffee, Lifestyle Nutrition, Kissan) was deliberately left out of the Unilever transaction. “So therefore that, combined with the opportunities that exist in India in Foods, is the reason why Foods is outside the perimeter of the Unilever transaction that we have done, and Foods continues to be a very important area and focus of strategy for HUL.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=55988411-440d-4801-8c08-90a5908c4a04.pdf)*
12. Mechanics and shareholder economics: 1:1 entitlement, 2,34,95,91,262 KWIL shares of Re. 1 allotted to HUL holders of record 5th December 2025, trading from 16th February 2026, with cost of acquisition split 98.09% HUL / 1.91% KWIL based on net worth versus Ice Cream net assets at 30th November 2025. “In accordance with the provisions of the Scheme, KWIL has allotted 2,34,95,91,262 (Two Hundred Thirty -Four Crore Ninety -Five Lakh Ninety -One Thousand Two Hundred Sixty -Two Only) Equity Shares of  Re. 1 /- each to the shareholders of HUL” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** On the Apr 2025 call (24th April 2025, March quarter FY25) it was only a progress line — on track with regulatory requirements, completion expected by end of FY26 — bundled with Pureit, Minimalist and OZiva as portfolio rotation. By the Oct 2025 call (23rd October 2025) Ritesh Tiwari hardened both timing and economics: demerger in the December quarter with listing in Q4 FY26, a two-step 'demerger then listing' sequence, Ice Cream at ~3% of business on low single-digit margin, and a quantified 50-60 bps uplift to reported EBITDA margin on top of the 22-23% guidance. Filings then closed the mechanics: NCLT sanction 30th October 2025, effective 1st December 2025, record date 5th December 2025, 1:1 allotment of 2,34,95,91,262 shares, 98.09%/1.91% cost apportionment, listing from 16th February 2026 — and on the Feb 2026 call (12th February 2026) Priya Nair declared the demerger complete, reported the continuing business ex-Ice Cream, attributed part of the Rs 6,603 crores reported PAT to a one-time non-cash demerger gain, and reset margin guidance to an implied 22.5-23.5%. By the May 2026 call (30th April 2026) it was retrospective justification — a completed action improving portfolio growth mix, with Foods explicitly kept 'outside the perimeter of the Unilever transaction'.

**What management expects from it:** HUL: reported EBITDA margin up ~50-60 bps (guidance rebased 22-23% to an implied 22.5-23.5%), a better growth mix, and capital redeployed into bigger bets (Rs 3,500 crores acquisitions, Rs 2,000 crores premium-format capex). KWIL: dedicated management, singular focus and flexibility for ice cream's distinct operating model to capture a growing India market. Shareholders: direct 1:1 listed exposure.

*Not explained on the calls:* No KWIL standalone financials, cold-chain capex or stranded costs; no Unilever brand-licensing/royalty terms; no named investor, lender or partner demand; no demerger-versus-sale comparison or valuation target.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* "Creation of a leading listed ice cream company in India with focused management having greater flexibility to deploy strategies suited to the Ice Cream businesses' distinctive operating model and market dynamics, to realise its full potential"
- *What it reveals:* Cost-of-acquisition split allots only 1.91% to KWIL vs 98.09% to HUL (based on HUL net worth and Ice Cream net assets at 30 Nov 2025), so a very small, cold-chain business carrying Kwality Wall's, Cornetto and Magnum is separated from a 23.6% EBITDA-margin FMCG parent.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *Read next:* KWIL's first standalone results, and the net assets of the Ice Cream Business Undertaking at 30 November 2025 underlying the 1.91% allocation.
- *In their words:* “The aforesaid ratio has been determined based on the net worth of HUL and the net assets of the Ice Cream Business Undertaking, as at 30 November 2025, in accordance with Sections 49(2C) and 49(2D) of the Act.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The separation Quess management describes is a completed three-way demerger of the old Quess Corp, effected from 1 April 2024 under a Composite Scheme of Arrangement in which Quess Corp was the Demerged Company and Digitide Solutions Limited (Resulting Company 1, holding the Global Technology Solutions/BPM, platform, foundit and Brainhunter businesses) and Bluspring Enterprises Limited (Resulting Company 2, holding Operating Asset Maintenance — IFM, food & beverage, security, Vedang telecom infra, and the Golden Star facility-management contracts) were carved out, leaving Quess Corp as a pure-play workforce/staffing company in General Staffing, Professional (IT) Staffing, Overseas staffing and the Hamara digital platforms. The stated reason was focus and value unlocking: management repeatedly said the demerger gives each entity 'its own focus and its own management', a 'sharper strategic identity', agility and the ability to unlock value for shareholders, with Quess itself able to concentrate on 'high-margin, high-growth core segments'. The separation was explicitly used as the trigger for portfolio cleaning: in the run-up, Digitide's service lines were rationalised for low-margin/low-efficiency contracts, and at Quess, the Board and management decided to exit non-core, outcome-based projects in skilling and utilities, booking INR158 crore of Q4 FY25 exceptionals (INR119 crore accelerated expected credit loss on discontinued projects, INR26 crore goodwill impairment — INR7 crore Stellarslog and INR19 crore Quess International Services — and INR13 crore of demerger costs, mainly stamp duty), after INR22 crore of demerger expenses in Q3 FY25; skilling alone had been roughly INR300 crore of revenue at ~20% EBITDA margin. Management conceded the cost: standalone workforce margins of 2.4–2.5% pre-demerger became 1.8% post-demerger because of newly allocated corporate overheads, and the old 4–4.5% consolidated margin is 'noncomparable' since skilling was discontinued and Brainhunter (US/Canada) moved to Digitide — so the goalpost was reset to 2% exit margin. The quid pro quo was balance-sheet and capital-allocation discipline: net cash of INR255 crore and gross debt of only INR12 crore at 31 March 2025, consolidated DSO cut from 44 to 37 days, a new dividend policy returning up to 75% of free cash flow over a rolling three-year block, FY25 dividend of INR10 per share, adjusted ROE moving from high teens to above 20%, and no acquisitions planned — investment to go into AI/sourcing technology instead. Strategically, the separated Quess was to tilt its mix from volume to value: profitability from General Staffing fell from 59% (FY25) to 50%, with Professional Staffing (~30%) plus Overseas (~20%) now half of operating profit (42% a year earlier), Professional Staffing margins rising from ~4.5–4.7% in FY20–21 to 12.7% by Q4 FY26, and 'Quess 2.0' targeting 65% of profit from Professional Staffing plus Overseas and dollar-linked revenue from 7% to over 20% in three to four years. By the AGM, Ajit Isaac framed the outcome as value created from the INR1,270 crore of IPO/IPP capital reinvested, with the three listed companies together generating about INR500 crore of EBITDA and employing over 600,000 people, while Quess remained debt-free with FY26 revenue of INR15,305 crore, EBITDA of INR312 crore (up 19%) and 20% ROE. No call attributes the decision to a demand from investors, lenders or partners — only to the Board and management.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. With the first NCLT approval done and shareholder/creditor approvals obtained on 9 December 2024, Guruprasad framed the pending three-way split as a value-unlocking and positioning exercise for each entity. “This transition marks an important step in unlocking shareholder value and positioning each entity for its future success.” — *CALL Feb 2025*
2. CFO Kamal Pal Hoda described the internal work — internal controls, process streamlining and separate leadership teams — as aimed at creating agile, independently focused entities; demerger-related expenses of INR22 crore were booked in the quarter and more were flagged for Q4. “Our aim is to create independent entities that are agile, strategically focused and well positioned to unlock value for all stakeholders in the long term.” — *CALL Feb 2025*
3. The separation was already being used to clean the portfolio of the entity going into Digitide, by exiting low-margin, low-efficiency service lines to lift long-run operating margins. “As a run-up to demerger, with a new entity, Digitide, we are examining our existing service lines and rationalizing low-margin low-efficiency contracts, which would give a sustainable upside to our long-term operating margins.” — *CALL Feb 2025*
4. First call as a standalone company: the completed three-way demerger was presented as delivering sharper focus, value unlocking and strategic transformation, alongside net cash of INR255 crore, gross debt of INR12 crore and DSO improved by 7 days to 37. “This important milestone leads to a sharper focus and unlocking value, strategic transformation, and delivering sustained growth.” — *CALL May 2025*
5. Guruprasad tied portfolio streamlining post-separation directly to profitability, capital efficiency and long-term value creation for the remaining staffing core. “Moving forward as we streamline our business portfolios, it will enable a sharper focus on high-margin, high-growth core segments.” — *CALL May 2025*
6. The demerger triggered a comprehensive business review and Board-approved exit of non-core outcome-based projects in skilling and utilities — INR158 crore of exceptionals (INR119 crore accelerated ECL, INR26 crore goodwill impairment in Stellarslog and Quess International Services, INR13 crore demerger/stamp-duty costs); skilling had been ~INR300 crore of revenue at ~20% EBITDA margin. “As part of the demerger transformation, we revisited some of our businesses through a comprehensive review, and we will be exiting certain non-core projects in line with the position taken by the management and the Board to discontinue such projects.” — *CALL May 2025*
7. Asked about new geographies, management said the point of the separation was to go deeper in existing core businesses rather than expand, with no acquisitions planned and investment redirected to AI-led sourcing productivity. “See, as part of this demerger, Siddharth, our focus is going to be on the core businesses and how much more we can do and bring in more efficiency and stay profitable.” — *CALL May 2025*
8. The identity after separation was stated plainly in the closing remarks — a pure-play staffing company with a simplified structure, zero gross debt at quarter-end, and 53%/29%/21% profitability contribution from General Staffing, Professional Staffing and Overseas. “So, as we strengthen our position as a pure-play staffing leader, we remain deeply committed to operational excellence, innovation and continuously evolving our offerings to meet the dynamic needs of our clients.” — *CALL Aug 2025*
9. The post-separation design goal was restated as a 50/50 profit split between scale (General Staffing) and the higher-margin Professional Staffing (11–12%) and Overseas (6%+) businesses — a point management said it had set out two or three quarters earlier and had now reached. “I think we had made one point about 2 or 3 quarters ago where we said we would like to have a healthy state where General Staffing on a growing base contributes 50% of the profitability of that company.” — *CALL Nov 2025*
10. Answering why margins are ~2% versus 4–4.5% historically, new CFO Neeraj Jain explained the pre-demerger comparison is invalid: the high-margin skill development business was discontinued and Brainhunter (US/Canada operations) went to Digitide; Kushal added the demerged balance sheet applies from 1 April 2024. “With all of those business with high EBITDA margins, we were averaging around 4%, 4.5%, but that businesses have been discontinued and Brainhunter as part of demerger has moved into Digitide.” — *CALL Feb 2026*
11. On the INR120 crore expected credit loss taken in Q4 FY25, Guruprasad confirmed it related to the government skilling receivables of the businesses discontinued as part of the demerger, with collections still being pursued (delayed into Q4 by a new RBI escrow process) and any recovery to be a write-back. “If you recollect, in Q4, these were the discontinued businesses as part of the demerger that we had announced to the Street, and we had taken an exceptional credit loss on that.” — *CALL Feb 2026*
12. One year after the demerger, the same exit test was applied again: a 7,000-headcount milestone-based project was closed down, costing about INR200 crore or 1.3% of revenue, with no further such events known. “As you would remember, closer to our demerger timeline, we had said any business which does not meet the financial metrics of the company and does not yield us the cash realization, we will exit and discontinue such businesses.” — *CALL May 2026*
13. AGM (August 2026): Chairman Ajit Isaac described the FY25 three-way demerger as turning one company into three separately listed ones, with the value creation enabled by INR1,270 crore of IPO/IPP capital reinvested; the three now generate about INR500 crore of EBITDA and employ over 600,000 people. “Where there was one company, there are now three separately listed companies: Quess Corp, Bluspring Enterprises and Digitide Solutions, each with its own focus and its own management.” — *Scheme*
14. What shareholders retain in Quess Corp was defined as a debt-free, single-mandate workforce company — FY26 revenue INR15,305 crore, EBITDA INR312 crore (up 19%), net cash INR271 crore, 20% ROE, INR11 per share dividend — with Professional Staffing plus Overseas now half of operating profit versus 42% in FY25, targeted at ~65%. “What remains with you is Quess Corp, an independent workforce, talent and technology company, with no debt on its books.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** In the Feb 2025 (Q3 FY25) call the demerger was still in flight — first NCLT approval received, shareholder and creditor approvals on 9 December 2024, second-motion NCLT pending, INR22 crore of demerger costs booked, listing of all three companies guided for Q1 FY26 — and Digitide's low-margin contracts were already being rationalised 'as a run-up to demerger'. By the May 2025 (Q4 FY25) call it was done ahead of timeline and framed as Quess's 'first earnings call as an independent entity', with INR158 crore of exceptionals for exiting non-core skilling and utilities projects, a new 75%-of-FCF dividend policy, and a reset margin goalpost of 1.8% to 2%. The Aug 2025 and Nov 2025 calls shifted entirely to execution of the 'pure-play staffing leader' model and the 50/50 profit-mix target, while Feb 2026 used the demerger retrospectively to explain why margins are 2% rather than the old 4–4.5% (skilling discontinued, Brainhunter moved to Digitide) and why the INR120 crore ECL related to demerger-era discontinued businesses. The May 2026 call, 'one year post our demerger', applied the same demerger-era test to exit a further 7,000-headcount, milestone-based project worth about INR200 crore (1.3% of revenue), and the August 2026 AGM closed the arc with the three-company outcome and the 'Quess 2.0' mix targets.

**What management expects from it:** For Quess: a pure-play, zero-debt staffing company with sharper focus on high-margin segments — margins rebuilt from 1.8% to 2%+ (2.4% medium term), Professional Staffing 11–12% and Overseas 6%+ lifting their profit share from 50% to 65%, dollar-linked revenue 7% to 20%, ROE above 20%, 80% EBITDA-to-cash conversion and up to 75% of free cash flow returned. Digitide and Bluspring get independent focus, management and technology/industrial platforms.

*Not explained on the calls:* Who initiated or demanded it; sum-of-parts or valuation math; how assets, debt and corporate costs were allocated between the three; Digitide/Bluspring economics or listing details.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Three-way split so each company has "its own focus and its own management"; Quess left "deliberately a pure play business with a single mandate" in workforce management
- *What it reveals:* Reveals parent as a thin-margin volume business: FY26 EBITDA margin 2.0% versus ~4–4.5% pre-demerger, since higher-margin skilling and Brainhunter left. Offset by zero debt, ₹271 crore net cash, 20% ROE, ₹11 dividend
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* Digitide Solutions and Bluspring Enterprises standalone results — the EBITDA and debt that left Quess
- *In their words:* “Where there was one company, there are now three separately listed companies: Quess Corp, Bluspring Enterprises and Digitide Solutions, each with its own focus and its own management.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

Siemens Ltd. has separated two businesses, and the one management explained in the most detail is the Low Voltage Motors (LVM, plus geared motors and related customer service) business, sold as a going concern on a slump-sale basis to Innomotics India Private Limited for an enterprise value of INR 22 billion (INR 2,200 crore), cash-free/debt-free. The trigger was not Indian: on 1 October 2024 Siemens AG sold the global Innomotics business — and all of its intellectual property — to KPS Capital Partners, leaving the Indian unit as, in Sunil Mathur's words, a licensed sales organisation with no IP, no manufacturing (contract-manufactured to Innomotics design, ~97% of the Business's revenue) and survival dependent on an Agency & Distributorship Agreement and a Technical Cooperation & License Agreement with an entity now controlled by a private-equity owner. So the counterparty, not investors or lenders, effectively forced the decision: the Board stated the Business could not be sold to anyone else because Innomotics owns the IP, making the only alternatives selling to Innomotics India or restructuring the Business and bearing those costs. The numbers management cited were small and deteriorating: for the 12 months to 30 September 2025, revenue from operations of INR 9.67 billion (INR 967 crore) and profit from operations of INR 0.35 billion (INR 35 crore) — 6% of the company's revenue and ~2.2% of its profit from operations ex-Energy — with net capital employed of negative INR 1.38 billion, orders down 6.9% y/y in Q2 FY25, H1 EBITDA of 7.8% (down 130bps on lower price realisation and higher royalties paid to Innomotics), volumes that 'have not increased', cyclicality tied to private-sector capex and copper, and only 89 sales employees; the filing also recorded negative net worth of INR 1,175.66 million and 4.53% of revenue in FY24. Management said synergies with the rest of Siemens Ltd. were 'very limited' and framed the exit as portfolio optimisation that creates value and cash while giving customers and employees continuity. Price was set after negotiation using two independent valuations (Grant Thornton Bharat LLP and KPMG Valuation Services LLP) as at 30 September 2025, and Mathur stressed INR 22 billion was 'the same price that had been offered earlier on by the parent company' despite volumes having since declined. The earlier, larger separation was the Energy demerger into Siemens Energy India Limited (appointed date 1 March 2025, effective 25 March 2025), justified as creating two independent pure-play companies focused on their relevant markets, each with a large backlog; it transferred net assets of INR 37,846 million including INR 25,478 million of cash, cost INR 1.0 billion of demerger expenses in FY25 versus INR 0.1 billion in FY24, and under the November 2023 disclosure the promoters agreed procedures to let Siemens Energy AG acquire a majority in the new listed entity.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. CFO Wrumnig first links LVM's fate to the parent's global divestment of Innomotics to KPS Capital Partners and to the Indian unit's technical dependence on that business, announcing an options review. “In view of this sale and the dependency on the global Innomotics business, we will now explore options for the future of the Low Voltage Motors business.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2ae69c31-b96b-4781-9858-035146160df1.pdf)*
2. The economics were already visibly impaired: weak orders, price pressure and royalties payable to the new KPS-owned owner of the IP compressing margins. “Year-to-date, the business reported an EbitDA margin of 7.8%, down by 130bps due to lower price realization and higher royalties paid to Innomotics, the former global Siemens business, now owned by KPS Capital Partners.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2ae69c31-b96b-4781-9858-035146160df1.pdf)*
3. Mathur describes what Siemens Ltd. actually owned in LVM — a licence to sell someone else's product, with outsourced manufacturing and no IP rights in India. “It is within Siemens Limited. It is outsourced manufacturing. Revenues are cyclical, as you know, for motors.” — *[Dec 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=82783258-f887-444b-a6f1-cbeaf34f0b62.pdf)*
4. The volume thesis that justified keeping the business had failed, tied to muted private-sector capex and copper prices. “The expectation was that the volumes will increase. Those volumes have not increased in the country.” — *[Dec 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=82783258-f887-444b-a6f1-cbeaf34f0b62.pdf)*
5. Board approval of the slump sale to Innomotics India at INR 22 billion, explicitly the same price the parent had offered earlier, with closing guided to mid-2026. “And this was then finally approved by the board of Siemens Limited in terms of a sale and transfer on a slump sale basis to Innomotics India at a purchase price of 22 billion, which I will remind you was the same price that had been offered earlier on by the parent company.” — *[Dec 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=82783258-f887-444b-a6f1-cbeaf34f0b62.pdf)*
6. Materiality and shareholder-interest framing: the business had shrunk to 6% of volumes and 2% of profits. “Considering the fact that the volumes have declined, in the meantime, it is only 6% of the overall volume of Siemens and only 2% of Siemens profits in the meantime.” — *[Dec 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=82783258-f887-444b-a6f1-cbeaf34f0b62.pdf)*
7. The prior, bigger separation is presented as completed and successful — Energy is now a separately listed pure-play, leaving Siemens Ltd. with DI, SI and Mobility. “A major development during this period has been the demerger of Siemens Energy India Limited, which is now a separately listed pure play energy company.” — *[Dec 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=82783258-f887-444b-a6f1-cbeaf34f0b62.pdf)*
8. Rationale originally given for the Energy demerger: two focused, independently capitalised companies each with large backlogs. “Both companies are very well prepared for the future growth, focusing on their relevant markets.” — *[Dec 2024](https://assets.new.siemens.com/siemens/assets/api/uuid:dc7b02ca-736c-4db6-8118-da2b47754aa6/Analyst-Call-Transcript-website.pdf)*
9. Final status update before closing; the quarter also shows demerger-related expenses falling by INR 500 million as separation costs roll off. “And third, on the portfolio topic, the sale of the low-voltage motors business is on track for completion in June 2026.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f8a31e42-7fdf-46ab-8ac9-a4540a097f8b.pdf)*
10. Filing of 8 Dec 2025 states the hard constraint: without Innomotics/KPS support Siemens Ltd. cannot run the business, which is why the only buyer was the counterparty itself. “The Company itself does not have the requisite intellectual property or other capabilities to service the Business without support from Innomotics GmbH which is now owned by KPS.” — *Scheme*
11. Strategic-fit argument plus the stated financial benefit of exiting — portfolio optimisation generating value and cash. “Synergies between the Business and the rest of the Company’s businesses are very limited.” — *Scheme*
12. Price discovery and process: negotiated against two independent valuations as at 30 September 2025, outside any scheme of arrangement and not a related-party transaction. “The consideration for the sale and transfer of the Business has been determined after negotiation between the Company and the Buyer, taking into account two separate independent valuation reports of the Business as at 30th September 2025 pursuant to independent valuation exercises conducted by each of Grant Thornton Bharat LLP and                 KPMG Valuation Services LLP .” — *Scheme*
13. Completion on 1 June 2026 at INR 22 billion enterprise value, booking a provisional one-time gain of INR 20,990 million (INR 2,099 crore) in discontinued operations. “Basis the preliminary sale consideration, a provisional gain of Rs. 20,990 million is recognized during the quarter ended 30 June 2026 and six months period ended 30 September 2026.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** Dec 2024 call (20 Dec 2024): only the Energy demerger is discussed as a separation — 'on track', creating two independent companies, with LVM not yet flagged as a portfolio issue. May 2025 call (20 May 2025): after the Siemens AG–KPS Innomotics deal of October 2024 and visible margin pressure from royalties paid to Innomotics, management formally said it would 'explore options for the future' of LVM. Dec 2025 (board 8 Dec 2025; analyst meet 12 Dec 2025): the option became a signed slump-sale agreement with Innomotics India at INR 22 billion, justified by lost IP, no local manufacturing, declining volumes (6% of revenue, 2% of profit) and shareholder interest, with closing guided to mid-2026. Jun 2026 call (28 May 2026) reconfirmed completion 'on track for June 2026'; the sale closed 1 June 2026 with a provisional gain of INR 20,990 million, while in the opposite direction the Board approved amalgamating subsidiary Siemens Rail Automation into the parent (26 May 2026) and took C&S Electric to 100% via capital reduction (NCLT order 24 September 2026).

**What management expects from it:** For Siemens Ltd.: a cleaner three-business technology portfolio (DI, SI, Mobility), removal of a sub-scale, negative-capital-employed, royalty-burdened unit worth 6% of revenue but only 2% of profit, INR 22 billion of cash plus an INR 2,099 crore gain, and portfolio optimisation 'creating value and cash'. For Innomotics India: ownership aligned with the IP it already holds, continuity for LVM customers and the 89 sales staff. For Energy: an independent pure-play.

*Not explained on the calls:* No post-sale margin, ROCE or capital-deployment guidance; no bridge from the 2024 parent offer to INR 22 billion; silent on employee transfer terms, ADA/TCLA wind-down, and buyer-selection alternatives.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* not stated — the filings give no rationale; the Dec 2025 analyst meet only describes SEIL as 'now a separately listed pure play energy company'
- *What it reveals:* Energy left with net assets of Rs 37,846 million including Rs 25,478 million cash; it earned Rs 9,418 million PBT on Rs 61,580 million revenue in FY2024. Parent remains cash-rich (Rs 77,905 million cash and bank, 30 Sep 2026) with a Rs 47,034 crore backlog.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* Siemens Energy India Limited's own results and the Scheme, for the Rs 37,846 million net assets and Rs 25,478 million cash transferred
- *In their words:* “Pursuant to receipt of necessary statutory approvals and in accordance with the Scheme, the Company has demerged the Energy business effective 25 March 2025, with appointed date being 1 March 2025, as per the Scheme.”
