- **growth** — parent / remaining: Continuing operations (Siemens Limited excluding Energy business) in Q1 FY 2025: New Orders up 20% at INR 4,258 crore, Revenue 3% lower at INR 3,587 crore, Profit after Tax lower by 10% at INR 372 crore; separated business: Energy business (discontinued operations) in Q1 FY 2025: Revenue INR 1,431 crore (up 28%) and Profit after Tax INR 243 crore (up 158%), on continued strong demand for Transmission products and solutions, including a favorable one-time impact of INR 98 crore on profitability “Revenue and Profit after Tax for discontinued operations for Q1 FY 2025 was INR 1,431 crore (up 28%) and INR 243 crore (up 158%), respectively .”
- **operating margin** — parent / remaining: Standalone continuing operations for the year ended 30 September 2024: revenue from operations Rs. 143,386 million with profit before tax of Rs. 25,759 million; for the eighteen months ended 31 March 2026, revenue Rs. 220,254 million with profit before tax Rs. 27,375 million; separated business: Energy business as discontinued operations for the year ended 30 September 2024: revenue from operations Rs. 61,580 million, total income Rs. 61,622 million, total expenses Rs. 52,204 million and profit before tax Rs. 9,418 million; profit for the year from discontinued operations Rs. 6,980 million “Revenue from operations 14,308 20,041 11,157 61,580 Other income 15 38 23 42 Total income 14,323 20,079 11,180 61,622 Total expenses 11,077 15,926 9,912 52,204 Profit before tax for the period/ year 3,246 4,153 1,268 9,418”
- **debt and leverage** — parent / remaining: No secured creditors and no preference shareholders in Siemens Limited; 4,342 unsecured creditors with an outstanding amount of INR 34,31,68,90,458 as on 31 August 2024; fund and non-fund based working capital facilities availed from State Bank of India with no dues owed at the date of filing the Company Scheme Application; separated business: No secured creditors and no preference shareholders in Siemens Energy India Limited; 2 unsecured creditors having an outstanding amount of INR 20,92,540 as on 31 August 2024 “It is further submitted that since there are no (i) Secured Creditors in Siemens Limited and Siemens Energy India Limited; and (ii) Preference Shareholders in Siemens Limited and Siemens Energy India Limited, this Tribunal had dispensed with the holding and convening of the meetings of Secured Creditors of Siemens Limited and Siemens Energy India Limited and Preference Shareholders of Siemens Limited and Siemens Energy India Limited.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: Cost of acquisition apportionment for the parent after the demerger: 76.18% of the total cost of acquisition of shares of the Company; separated business: Cost of acquisition apportionment for the resulting company: 23.82% of the total cost of acquisition of shares of the Company “Sr. No. Name of the Entity % of Total Cost of Acquisition of Shares of the Company 1 Siemens Limited 76.18 2 Siemens Energy India Limited 23.82”
- **other** — parent / remaining: Demerger related expenses charged in the parent: Rs. 148 million in the quarter ended 31 December 2024 and Rs. 110 million in the year ended 30 September 2024; Rs. 1,092 million in the eighteen months ended 31 March 2026 (Rs. 31 million in the quarter ended 30 June 2026). The CFO stated it was 0.1 billion in FY24 and 1 billion in FY25; separated business: not stated “And the second one : we had energy demerger -related e xpenses . In ’24 it was just 0.1 billion. In ’25 it was 1 billion.”
- **capex and capital intensity** — parent / remaining: Parent retains 25 factories and continues to invest in local manufacturing (vacuum interrupter and gas-insulated switchgear factories in Goa, Mobility factories in Nashik, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and Dahod); roughly 65-75% localisation in Smart Infrastructure; separated business: Low Voltage Motors business sold in 2025 has no manufacturing: the Company largely functions as a sales organisation with outsourced contract manufacturing constituting approximately 97% of the revenue of the Business, a sales team of 89 employees, and negative net capital employed of Rs. 1.38 billion “The Company largely functions as a sales organisation in respect of the Business and does not have manufacturing facilities to manufacture the low voltage motors and follows a contract  manufacturing model with Innomotics  design and with stringent quality controls across the supply chain and manufacturing, which constitute approximately 97% of the revenue of the Business.”
- **working capital** — parent / remaining: Remaining business is investing heavily in working capital, chiefly for Mobility: inventory levels raised and trade receivables and contract assets up with the revenue ramp, so operating cash flow is below prior periods; over dues stable and not at a critical level; separated business: not stated “On one hand, of course, we have CapEx with regards to our investments in manufacturing. Then , also we have OpEx related to th ese investments. And one big portion is also we invest a lot in working capital right now for the Mobility business.”

*Stated figures are the documents' own (a turnover share, or the cost-of-acquisition split the company publishes for tax, which reflects relative value); the segment share is this business's revenue over the parent's sales, and the market-cap share is the entity's value over the entity plus the parent (parent ₹7,246 cr, NSE bhavcopy of 2026-11-13), both computed here.*

**In the documents' words:** “The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking of the Company for the financial year ended 31st March 2024 was approximately Rs. 28,978.7 Million, representing 63% of the total turnover of the Company for the said year.”

**The judge's read of selling pressure:** likely — 1:1 mirror allotment pushed industrial shares onto holders of what is now a pure-play automotive company — a different industry.

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

SKF India separated its Industrial bearings business out of the listed company into SKF India (Industrial) Limited, leaving SKF India Ltd as a pure-play Automotive bearings company (management called it a "reverse carve-out" mirroring SKF AB's global split of Automotive, ~30% of group revenue versus 34-35% in India). Management's stated logic rested on three pillars: fundamentally different macro drivers (Automotive: EV/CAFE and BS-VII emission norms, 30% EV penetration target by 2030, premiumization/SUVs, last-mile commercial vehicles; Industrial: infrastructure spend, Make in India/NIP/PLI, China-Plus-One, railways/metro/Vande Bharat, wind and renewables doubling by 2030); different customer needs (a few large auto OEMs needing application-specific, longer-cycle engineered products — 60-65% engineered order in Auto versus ~25-30% in Industrial — against hundreds of industrial verticals wanting uptime, condition monitoring and remanufacturing); and a different manufacturing philosophy (Auto = large batch, small/medium bearings, automation and cycle-time efficiency; Industrial = wide assortment, small/large sizes, flexible lines with fast changeover plus a large traded component). The problems they said this solves: management attention split across two unlike businesses, capital allocation that could not be tailored (Auto was short of capacity, Industrial needed a brand-new Pune plant and localization from ~30-35% toward 70%), slow decision-making and launches, mismatched innovation cycles, and poor financial visibility for investors in a combined P&L. Operationally the split was defined down to the line: Bangalore 10 lines (7 Auto, 3 Industrial, with those 3 moving to Pune so Bangalore becomes 100% Auto), Pune 22 lines (12 Auto, 10 Industrial), Haridwar 4 lines all Auto; land 85:15 in Bangalore, 52:48 in Pune, 100% Auto in Haridwar; manpower 55-60% Auto versus 40-45% Industrial; cash allocated on the two businesses' last three years of profits. Shareholders received one SKF Industrial share of Rs 10 for every SKF India share held (PwC Business Consulting share entitlement report dated 24 December 2024; Saffron Capital fairness opinion 25 December 2024), with pre-demerger cost of acquisition apportioned 46.88% to SKF India and 53.12% to SKF Industrial. Pro forma FY24 economics shown to investors were Auto ~18% EBITDA and Industrial ~17%, both ~16% PBT, off a combined FY24 revenue of INR 45.7 billion; FY25 combined revenue was INR 4,919.9 crore (+7.65%) with PBT INR 763.1 crore (+3.71%). Nobody external demanded the separation — it was a group-level decision, with investors on the calls supportive (one explicitly "wholeheartedly supported" it) while pressing for structural clarity given SKF would still have three Indian entities including the unlisted SKF Engineering & Lubrication (Ahmedabad plant, global technical centre, lubrication and sealing factories); no lender or partner requirement was ever cited.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The stated purpose: two independent, fit-for-purpose companies that each accelerate growth and profitability, driven by three differences — industry dynamics, customer needs and manufacturing philosophy. “The intention of this demerger is to create 2 fit-for-purposes independent companies, which will accelerate both growth and profitability of both companies.” — *Apr 2025*
2. Management summarised the rationale as three separate axes of difference, with manufacturing efficiency and customer service as the payoff. “So to summarize, macro drivers are different. Customer drivers and innovation is different; and third, the manufacturing itself, the process of manufacturing itself is very different, what will make us most efficient and help us serve the customer needs.” — *Apr 2025*
3. Manufacturing philosophy was the concrete operating problem: Auto runs large batches of small/medium bearings for few OEMs with automation and economies of scale, while Industrial needs flexible lines, customised solutions and a large traded/regional component. “Automotive has a large batch sizes with small and medium-sized bearings.” — *Apr 2025*
4. Margin ambition attached to the separation: 2-3 percentage points of EBITDA upside in both businesses, from more efficient manufacturing, procurement and value-based pricing of premium products such as ceramic and energy-efficient bearings. “So I would say while the margins are typically relatively thin, we would hope that we can get at least 2 to 3 more points on our EBITDA going forward.” — *Apr 2025*
5. Shareholders were told the split was economically neutral — a mirror shareholding with a 1:1 share issue and listing of SKF Industrial on both exchanges. “The new company will mirror the shareholding of the existing listed company with each shareholder of SKF India receiving one share of SKF Industrial as a consideration of the demerger.” — *Apr 2025*
6. Investor visibility into the two businesses' separate performance was explicitly listed as one of the demerger benefits, alongside tailored capital deployment and two different manufacturing philosophies. “and finally, just more visibility for the -- our investors, all of you, to be able to see the performance of the 2 entities independently.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78b3fd3b-6609-4f9b-ac56-5ec9fc26a320.pdf)*
7. Pro forma FY24 carve-out economics given to investors: Automotive ~18% EBITDA, Industrial ~17%, both around 16% PBT, with capex set to double from INR 130-150 crore as a new Industrial plant is built next to the existing Pune site. “So if you look at FY '24, our EBITDA margins for automotive was around 18%. And industrial was around 17%.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78b3fd3b-6609-4f9b-ac56-5ec9fc26a320.pdf)*
8. The asset split was disclosed line by line — Bangalore 10 lines 70:30 with three lines moving to Pune so Bangalore becomes 100% Automotive, Pune 52:48 land, Haridwar 100% Automotive, manpower roughly 55:45. “There are three main plants, as we said, Bangalore, Pune and Haridwar. Bangalore, today there are 10 lines that will be split in the ratio of 70 to 30.” — *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3d94636c-b87c-4f11-91b6-556b4efcce20.pdf)*
9. Three-year guidance for the two entities: Automotive 10-12% growth, Industrial 8-10% (held back until the new Pune plant and localization land in FY27-28), with margins maintained at 17-19% and upside beyond FY28. “Next 3 years till '28, we expect growth in automotive to be in the 10 % to 12% range, industrial to be a little lower, 8% to 10% range.” — *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3d94636c-b87c-4f11-91b6-556b4efcce20.pdf)*
10. Capital allocation was the hard constraint being fixed: a brand-new Industrial-only Pune plant (DGBB, TRB, unitised bearings) costing INR 450-500 crore by 2028 plus INR 350-450 crore of additional lines, on top of INR 500-600 crore of Automotive capex to 2030. “Pune, we will be setting up a new plant, fully industrial, for industrial, making primarily DGBBs, which are deep groove ball bearings, tapered roller bearings, and unitized bearings, which are UCs.” — *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3d94636c-b87c-4f11-91b6-556b4efcce20.pdf)*
11. At the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting, management conceded the separation was complex precisely because the two businesses were deeply intertwined, and said the total demerger cost was still being accumulated. “As you know, it's a complex project primarily because the businesses both automotive and industrial, they are so deeply integrated that having two independent businesses is a complex process.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6801dc1e-769f-42ac-9ea4-5ada85787e74.pdf)*
12. An existing institutional shareholder (Ravi Purohit) publicly backed the demerger while asking why India would still be left with three SKF entities when the group was simplifying structures; management said no merger of entities was contemplated until the demerger completed. “And first of all, we'd like to congratulate and have wholeheartedly supported this demerger initiative that SKF Group is undertaking.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6801dc1e-769f-42ac-9ea4-5ada85787e74.pdf)*
13. First quantification of the cost: INR 184 million in Q1 FY26, mainly SAP and separate data infrastructure plus compliance consultants, with a 1.5-2% margin drag expected to run to H1 FY27 and extra stamp duty/registration cost on asset transfer in the Industrial entity. “So if you look at our current quarter, cost of demerger was around INR184 million.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6801dc1e-769f-42ac-9ea4-5ada85787e74.pdf)*
14. At the FY25 AGM the Chairman framed the demerger as strategic repositioning to sharpen focus, improve execution agility and deepen customer alignment, with manufacturing roadmaps diverging (Automotive automation-led high throughput; Industrial modular and demand-responsive). “The announcement of our demerger, which is separating the automotive and industrial businesses into two focused publicly listed entities was a significant milestone.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6801dc1e-769f-42ac-9ea4-5ada85787e74.pdf)*
15. Post-demerger, management clarified the direction of the carve-out — Industrial was hived off and the listed SKF India Limited is the automotive division, a reverse of the group-level split. “But in India, it is a reverse carve -out where industrial has gone out. So SKF India Limited remains as automotive division.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=fa739605-3c56-43bc-8950-6cc1db2e700e.pdf)*
16. The promised margin uplift did not appear: FY26 PBT fell 694 bps, EBITDA was 15.3%, and guidance was reset to 11-12% PBT, with Auto still buying medium DGBB and tapered roller bearings from SKF Industrial because of its own capacity shortage. “Now talking about the sustainable margin, we could be looking at 11 -12% kind of margin in the near future, while obviously in long term, the focus would be on improving it further, but the sustainable margin will be that.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=fa739605-3c56-43bc-8950-6cc1db2e700e.pdf)*
17. A long-term shareholder attacked the post-demerger communication gap, noting pre-demerger guidance of 16-19% (even 18-19%) EBITDA for a 95%-localised Auto business and a 50-70% valuation discount to Schaeffler and Timken; management replied royalty was unchanged and there is now no pure-play comparable. “Increasingly, our post demerger, what we are realizing is that the investor communication and the disclosures have dropped substantially.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=fa739605-3c56-43bc-8950-6cc1db2e700e.pdf)*
18. Management's closing framing still rested on focus and agility as the value-unlock, with restructuring costs described as a temporary hit. “The demerger positions us to unlock greater value by enabling sharper focus and agility in our business.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=fa739605-3c56-43bc-8950-6cc1db2e700e.pdf)*
19. The scheme transferred the Industrial business as a going concern into SKF India (Industrial) Limited under Sections 230-232, effective 1 October 2025 (NCLT order 26 September 2025, record date 15 October 2025), with pre-demerger cost of acquisition apportioned 46.88% to SKF India and 53.12% to SKF Industrial — i.e. Industrial was the larger half. “The Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench, vide its Order dated 26th September, 2025, sanctioned the Scheme of Arrangement between SKF India Limited ("the Company" or "Demerged Company") and SKF India (Industrial) Limited ("SKF Industrial" or "Resulting Company") and their respective shareholders and creditors under Sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 ("Scheme"), providing for the demerger of the Company's Industrial Business (Demerged Undertaking as defined in the Scheme ) into SKF Industrial on a going concern basis” — *Scheme*
20. The post-completion press release restated the purpose as two focused entities with independent boards and governance, and attached separate investment plans — Industrial INR 8,000-9,500 million by 2030 including a new Pune facility by 2028, Automotive INR 4,100-5,100 million by 2030 across EV, two-wheeler and wheel-end capacity in Haridwar, Pune and Bangalore. “The demerger, sanctioned by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) and approved by shareholders earlier this year, has formally separated SKF India's business into two focused entities — SKF Industrial and SKF Automotive — each equipped with independent boards and governance structures.” — *Scheme*
21. The FY26 AGM presentation codified the five official reasons for the separation and rebranded the automotive entity as SKF Vertevo, reporting FY26 revenue of INR 21,295 million, 15% EBITDA margin and EPS of INR 23.7. “Why the Demerger? Different Market Dynamics Distinct Customer Needs Focused Capital Allocation Faster Decision Making Independent Growth Strategies” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** The demerger was announced in Q4 CY2024 and first explained in detail on a dedicated update call on 9 April 2025, which laid out the three macro/customer/manufacturing drivers, the six enablers (management focus, manufacturing efficiency, tailored capital, agility, innovation, investor visibility), pro forma FY24 carve-out financials and a 12-15 month timeline, plus an aspiration of "2 to 3 more points" of EBITDA. By the 19 May 2025 Q4 call the plant allocation had firmed up (Haridwar 100% Auto, Bangalore ~80-85% Auto, a new Industrial factory beside the Pune plant), and the 30 June 2025 investor meet added line-by-line, land and manpower splits, segment revenue mixes from FY22-FY25, three-year guidance (Auto 10-12%, Industrial 8-10% to FY28, margins held at 17-19%) and a step-up in capex from ~INR 150 crore to roughly INR 350-400 crore a year (INR 450-500 crore Pune industrial plant by 2028, INR 500-600 crore Auto capex to 2030); the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting on 14 July 2025 approved the 1:1 scheme, and the 6-7 August 2025 AGM and Q1 FY26 call quantified the cost for the first time (INR 184 million in Q1, mostly SAP/IT separation and consultants, 1.5-2% margin drag running into H1 FY27, plus stamp duty on asset transfer) while conceding the businesses were "so deeply integrated" that separation was complex. After NCLT sanction on 26 September 2025, effectiveness on 1 October 2025 and a 15 October 2025 record date, the story changed tone: the 21 May 2026 call presented SKF India as a standalone automotive company guiding to only 11-12% PBT margin (FY26 EBITDA 15.3%) with investors complaining that disclosure had "dropped substantially" post-demerger and that margins were far below what was promised in the run-up to the demerger vote, management answering that royalty was unchanged and this was a transition.

**What management expects from it:** Two fit-for-purpose entities growing faster and more profitably: automotive 10-12% and industrial 8-10% growth to FY28, both holding 17-19% EBITDA with 2-3 points of upside later; sharper management focus, tailored capital deployment and manufacturing efficiency, plus separate financial visibility attracting more aligned investors.

*Not explained on the calls:* Never quantified: total demerger cost, dis-synergies, inter-entity trading/rent/service charges, or why post-demerger margins (11-12% PBT) fall far below the 16-19% promised pre-demerger.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Different market dynamics, distinct customer needs, focused capital allocation, faster decision making and independent growth strategies for the two businesses; strategic clarity to unlock greater value.
- *What it reveals:* Cost of acquisition apportioned 46.88% to SKF India (automotive) vs 53.12% to SKF Industrial — the industrial half carries more value. Parent's margins fell to ~15.3% EBITDA / 11-12% PBT guidance versus 16-19% pre-demerger commentary, blamed on one-offs.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* SKF India (Industrial) Limited's Information Memorandum and its standalone results — margins behind the 53.12% cost allocation.
- *In their words:* “The demerger gives us the strategic clarity to sharpen our priorities, accelerate growth, and unlock greater value for all stakeholders.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The business being separated is the Commercial Vehicles (CV) business of the erstwhile Tata Motors Limited, carved out under a Composite Scheme of Arrangement into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (since renamed Tata Motors Limited), while the listed parent was renamed Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (TMPV) and simultaneously absorbed its wholly-owned subsidiary Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited by amalgamation — the Scheme's stated purpose there being 'consolidating the Passenger Vehicles Business with TML'. The net effect, as the Scheme describes it, is that 'the Commercial Vehicle and Passenger Vehicle businesses of the Company are housed in two separate entities' from October 1, 2025, leaving TMPV with India PV, EV (Tata Passenger Electric Mobility) and JLR, plus Tata Technologies and Tata Motors Holdings Singapore in 'others'; segment reporting was recast accordingly and prior-period balance sheets declared non-comparable. Critically, across all six transcripts management never articulates a strategic reason for the split — no dis-synergy, focus, capital-allocation or value-unlock argument is given; the demerger appears only as a corporate action with dates, approvals, accounting and costs. The economics disclosed are: CV was valued at about Rs 94,000 Cr by third-party agencies against a transferred book value of about Rs 11,000 Cr, producing a Rs 83,000 Cr accounting profit on disposal of the CV undertaking that is 'only a notional gain' because of an equal contra deemed-dividend entry, so there is 'absolutely no impact on either distributable reserves or on our net worth'. Shareholders got one CV share for every one share held (1:1), the split is Section 2(19AA)-compliant so it is not a transfer in shareholders' hands, and cost of acquisition was apportioned 31.15% to CV and 68.85% to TMPV. Costs cited were a Rs 400 Cr stamp duty provision in Q3 FY26 (within Rs 1,600 Cr of exceptionals) rolling into the Rs 4,100 Cr of FY26 exceptionals alongside cyber and labour-code charges. Governance was split too — separate boards and KMP, Shailesh Chandra as MD & CEO of TMPV, P B Balaji moving to CEO of JLR — and capital structures now report separately (India PV net cash ~Rs 5,000 Cr at Q3 FY26 and ~Rs 7,000 Cr at year-end versus JLR net debt of ~Rs 33,000–39,000 Cr). No investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for the separation; the only constituency cited is shareholders, who approved it with 'overwhelming votes in our favor', plus SEBI/stock exchange NOCs and NCLT sanction.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The demerger is reported purely as a process milestone: regulatory no-objections from the exchanges and SEBI awaited, operational separation work advanced, appointed date July 1 and effective date around October 1, 2025. “We are expecting the NOC from the Stock Exchange and SEBI any time now, all filed and done.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=28345af3-7271-4146-8cf3-8da0f9c73222.pdf)*
2. Shareholder approval is confirmed as emphatic and the timetable reaffirmed; the only related substantive disclosure is that the Tata Capital stake goes with the CV business. “The demerger update: we had overwhelming votes in our favor and therefore we are on track for an appointed date of July 1st and an effective date of October 1st 2025.” — *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=80350d5e-9578-469f-bf9f-31610098f897.pdf)*
3. The NCLT final hearing concluded on the day of the call with judgment reserved, and management still guided to an October 1 effective date, expecting completion within the quarter. “We had the NCLT final hearing today and it has been concluded and the judgment is reserved.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2a91a004-4cbd-440e-93d3-2ca8967ff37b.pdf)*
4. First results as the post-demerger listed entity: CV is out of segment reporting, the automotive segment is now JLR plus Tata Passenger Vehicles, others is mainly Tata Technologies and Tata Motors Holdings Singapore, and prior-period balance sheets still include CV so are not comparable. “It's a pleasure speaking to you as we report our first quarterly earnings as a listed entity.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e6684a03-5a4d-4c7a-8da0-d5b2c52ec7d1.pdf)*
5. The accounting: CV was independently valued at about Rs 94,000 Cr versus about Rs 11,000 Cr of net assets transferred, giving a Rs 83,000 Cr disposal profit that is purely notional because of an offsetting Rs 83,000 Cr deemed dividend. “As part of demerger accounting entries, we have recorded a profit of ~Rs. 83,000 Cr on disposal of the CV undertaking, which is essentially the fair value of the CV assets, less the book value of net assets transferred.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e6684a03-5a4d-4c7a-8da0-d5b2c52ec7d1.pdf)*
6. Capital structures are now shown standalone — auto net debt moved from net cash to ~Rs 20,000 Cr (all at JLR) while India PV is net cash, which is the one place management links the standalone balance sheet to funding its product cycle. “Domestic India business is net cash which gives a lot of flex to fund the rich product investment cycle that will be coming through in the years.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e6684a03-5a4d-4c7a-8da0-d5b2c52ec7d1.pdf)*
7. The demerger is now only a reporting and cost item: CV permanently out of segments, and a Rs 400 Cr stamp duty provision taken within Rs 1,600 Cr of quarterly exceptionals alongside Rs 800 Cr of cyber costs and a Rs 400 Cr wage-bill charge. “I would like to call out that this excludes exceptional for Rs. 1,600 Cr: Rs. 800 Cr at JLR - additional impact because of the cyber incident, Rs. 400 Cr one-time Wage bill impact for India business, and another Rs.400 Cr provision we have taken for the stamp duty impact.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7907e958-7953-4b49-b831-aab03d6e2746.pdf)*
8. FY26 PBT of Rs 2,500 Cr is stated before Rs 4,100 Cr of exceptionals that include the demerger stamp duty, and the two entities' dividends are presented together as evidence shareholders are better off post-split. “So this actually represents a total dividend of Rs. 7 in the year when the demerger was undertaken and an increase over the Rs. 6 that we have paid for the last two years.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b4d386d7-de53-4409-8e90-187e08cb4a91.pdf)*
9. The Scheme has two legs: the CV undertaking demerges out of Tata Motors into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited on a going-concern basis, and the PV subsidiary amalgamates into the parent so that the passenger business is consolidated in one listed company, with the subsidiary dissolved. “Amalgamation of TMLPV with TML with an objective of consolidating the Passenger Vehicles Business with TML and consequent dissolution of TMLPV without being wound up.” — *Scheme*
10. Shareholders received 1 CV share for every 1 share held, the demerger is Section 2(19AA)-compliant so not a transfer in their hands, and cost of acquisition splits 31.15% to the new Tata Motors (CV) and 68.85% to TMPV; separate boards and KMP were constituted for both entities, with CV shares listed from November 12, 2025. “the Commercial Vehicle and Passenger Vehicle businesses of the Company are housed in two separate entities” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** In the Feb 2025 (Jan 29, 2025) call the demerger appears only as a corporate-action status item — filings done, NOC from the exchanges and SEBI awaited, appointed date July 1 and effective date around October 1, 2025 — and by the Jun 2025 (May 13, 2025) call management reports 'overwhelming votes' from shareholders and reaffirms those dates. In the Aug 2025 (Aug 8, 2025) call the NCLT final hearing had concluded that same day with judgment reserved, with the October 1 effective date still 'on plan'; the Nov 2025 (Nov 14, 2025) call is the first reported as a post-demerger listed entity, dominated by mechanics: segment recast, non-comparable balance sheets, and the Rs 83,000 Cr notional disposal gain against the Rs 94,000 Cr valuation and Rs 11,000 Cr book value. Thereafter it shrinks to a cost line — a Rs 400 Cr stamp duty provision in Feb 2026 (Feb 5, 2026) and stamp duty inside Rs 4,100 Cr of FY26 exceptionals in Jun 2026 (May 14, 2026), where the only forward-looking framing offered is that TMPV's Rs 3 dividend plus TMLCV's Rs 4 equals Rs 7 against Rs 6 paid by erstwhile Tata Motors. At no point in that sequence does the stated rationale evolve, because none is ever stated.

**What management expects from it:** Little quantified. Post-separation TMPV holds PV, EV and JLR only; segments recast to automotive plus others. India PV stays net cash (~Rs 5,000–7,000 Cr), giving 'flex' to fund its product cycle toward double-digit EBITDA; CV lists separately with its own board and dividend. Combined dividend rose to Rs 7 from Rs 6; net worth unchanged.

*Not explained on the calls:* Calls never state the strategic rationale, value-unlock or synergy numbers, who asked for the split, total transaction costs beyond stamp duty, or post-demerger capital-allocation, margin and valuation targets.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Scheme housed CV and PV businesses in two separate entities; stated objective of the amalgamation limb was "consolidating the Passenger Vehicles Business with TML". No further rationale stated.
- *What it reveals:* Cost apportionment implies 68.85% of value in TMPV versus 31.15% in CV. Parent keeps JLR plus India PV/EV: FY26 consolidated net debt Rs 30,000 Cr sits almost entirely at JLR (Rs 33,000 Cr) while India PV is cash positive Rs 7,000 Cr.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* Tata Motors Limited (formerly TML Commercial Vehicles) standalone results and its Rs 4 dividend — the spin's own profitability.
- *In their words:* “In this regard, we wish to inform that TMCV has intimated the Company today that it has received approval from BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited for listing and trading of its equity shares, effective November 12, 2025.”

**What the documents themselves say about the differences:**

- **other** — parent / remaining: Passenger Vehicles Business retained in the listed entity; Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (the amalgamating wholly owned subsidiary carrying the PV business) had total income of ₹51,206.32 crore for the year ended March 31, 2024; separated business: Commercial Vehicles Business demerged into TMLCV with total income of ₹73,116.64 crore, ~99% of TML's standalone total income for FY 2023-24 “As per audited standalone financial statements as at March 31, 2024, Tata Motors Limited's ("the Company"/ "TML") total income relating to Commercial Vehicles Business was ₹ 73,116.64 crore, representing ~99% of the total income for FY 2023-24.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: 68.85% of a shareholder's total cost of acquisition of Ordinary Shares is apportioned to Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (formerly Tata Motors Limited); separated business: 31.15% of a shareholder's total cost of acquisition of Ordinary Shares is apportioned to Tata Motors Limited (formerly TML Commercial Vehicles Limited), being the proportion the net book value of assets transferred bears to the net worth of the demerged company “The total cost of acquisition of INR 4,00,000/- would be apportioned in the aforesaid ratio - INR 1,24,600/- (31.15% of INR 4,00,000/-) being the total cost of acquisition of 1,000 Resulting Company shares and INR 2,75,400/- (INR 4,00,000/- less INR 1,24,600) being the total cost of acquisition of 1000 original shares of Demerged Company.”
- **debt and leverage** — parent / remaining: TMPV group net debt of Rs. 30,000 Cr for the year ending March 2026; net auto debt had moved from a net cash position at end FY25 to ~Rs. 20,000 Cr at Q2 FY26; separated business: Identified Rated, Listed, Unsecured, Redeemable NCDs aggregating ₹2,300 crore transferred from the Demerged Company to the Resulting Company (NCD record date October 10, 2025) “The net debt for the year ending March 2026 was Rs. 30,000 Cr, largely representing the Rs. 25,000 Cr of consol cash burn and the Rs. 2,200 Cr of dividends that we paid last year.”
- **cash** — parent / remaining: PV remains cash positive at about Rs. 7,000 Cr while JLR net debt stood at Rs. 33,000 Cr (FY26); India business was net cash ~Rs. 5,000 Cr at Q2 FY26; separated business: not stated “PV remains cash positive at about Rs. 7,000 Cr, while the net debt at JLR stood at Rs. 33,000 Cr.”
- **growth** — parent / remaining: Passenger Vehicles sales in Q2 FY26 of 144,397 units vs 130,753 units in Q2 FY25, robust double-digit year-on-year growth of more than 10%; separated business: Commercial Vehicles sales in Q2 FY26 of 94,681 units vs 84,281 units in Q2 FY25, growth of 12% “Overall, in Q2 FY26, Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles delivered sales of 94,681 units, registering a growth of 12% over the same period last year.”
- **operating margin** — parent / remaining: TMPV India business ended FY26 with 9.4% EBITDA margin for the quarter and 4.7% EBIT margin; PBT before extraordinary expenses in Q4 of Rs. 1,100 Cr; separated business: not stated “We ended the year with 9.4% EBITDA margin for the quarter and 4.7% EBIT margin.”
- **capex and capital intensity** — parent / remaining: TMPV India capex for FY26 of about Rs. 4,300 Cr, about 7.5% of revenues (combined PV and EV); JLR full-year investment of GBP 3.57 billion, of which GBP 2.6 billion engineering; separated business: not stated “Capex for the year stood at about Rs. 4,300 Cr that translated to about 7.5% of revenues, well within the guidance range that we gave from the combined Capex for PV and EV.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: TMPV Board approved a dividend of Rs. 3 per share for FY26, cash outflow about Rs. 1,100 Cr; erstwhile Tata Motors paid Rs. 6 in dividends for the last two years; separated business: TMLCV announced Rs. 4 of dividend for FY26 “The TMLCV has announced Rs. 4 of dividend in the results meeting yesterday.”
- **tax** — parent / remaining: Cost of acquisition of original shares in the demerged company deemed reduced under Section 49(2D); amalgamation of TMPV complies with Section 2(1B) of the Income-tax Act, 1961; separated business: Demerger complies with Section 2(19AA) of the Income-tax Act, 1961; issue of shares by the Resulting Company is not regarded as transfer under Section 47(vid), and holding period of the demerged company's shares carries over “Therefore, the Demerger is not treated as a transfer in the hands of the shareholders.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: Reporting boundary split: "Passenger Vehicles (PV) businesses for the period 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026"; the Chinchwad facility in Pune became part of the Company from October 2025; separated business: "Commercial Vehicles (CV) business for the period 1 April 2025 to 30 June 2025", disclosed in Annexure I to the BRSR “As per the Demerger Scheme, the CV business was transferred and vested into a separate entity with effect from the appointed date, being July 1, 2025, while the Passenger Vehicle (PV) business continued to remain with Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (formerly Tata Motors Limited) (Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles or 'TMPVL' or 'Company').”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

Management says Anant Raj Ltd today runs two unlike businesses under one roof — the legacy real estate/infrastructure business (residential townships, luxury housing, commercial leasing, hospitality) and a data centre & cloud services business — and that the Data Centre Business is itself split across two entities, Anant Raj Limited and its wholly owned Anant Raj Cloud Private Limited (ARCPL), with assets, employees, investments and operations housed in both. The Composite Scheme therefore first amalgamates ARCPL into ARL and then demerges the whole Data Centre Business out of ARL into Ashok Cloud Private Limited (ACPL), so all of it sits in one dedicated, separately listed company. The stated problems it solves: the two verticals differ 'significantly in their nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics, and capital requirements', and the Board recorded on May 11, 2026 that keeping both in one company 'does not adequately reflect the true potential and intrinsic value of each business segment, thereby impacting stakeholder returns'; the split is meant to give independent market-driven valuation of a pure-play digital infrastructure asset, dedicated management focus, a simpler ownership structure with intra-group arrangements cancelled/rationalised, and the ability to attract sector-specific capital, strategic investors and partnerships. The numbers cited: the Demerged Undertaking did ₹145.90 cr turnover in FY26 versus ₹1,627.72 cr aggregated (8.96%); ARCPL turnover ₹136.20 cr and net worth ₹49.45 cr versus ARL's ₹1,491.52 cr turnover and ₹4,471.64 cr net worth; ACPL had nil turnover and ₹0.04 cr net worth and was capitalised days earlier via a ₹74.86 cr rights issue (37,43,22,553 shares at ₹2). Scale is the driver: the Board noted an MOU with the Govt. of Andhra Pradesh for 50 MW IT load taking total planned capacity to 357 MW IT load, requiring about ₹20,000 cr of investment — against a real estate business management repeatedly said should carry as little debt as possible. Mechanically, ARL shareholders get 1 ACPL share of ₹2 for every 1 ARL share of ₹2, giving them 49% of ACPL directly (promoters 28.14%, public 20.86%) while ARL retains 51%, so ACPL stays a subsidiary and ARL holders keep 100% of the ultimate economic interest; ACPL will be listed on BSE and NSE under the Rule 19(7) exemption. The ask came from the equity market side — an investor asked about a demerger as early as the Apr 2024 call, and analysts kept pressing for separate real estate vs data centre reporting — not from lenders or partners, who are never cited as requesting it.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. An investor (Arpit Shah, Stallion Asset) directly asked about demerging the data centre business; management declined to engage, calling the business too young and prioritising execution toward the 300 MW mark in four years. “We are too soon to say anything on that. Let's focus on execution, Arpit.” — *[Apr 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=03aa7997-f0a0-4f9b-8373-f4a4684da92d.pdf)*
2. Management set out the different capital philosophies that later justify separation: real estate was to be net debt-free by December 2024 and the only debt acceptable would be lease rental discounting, including against long 10-15 year data centre leases. “And the only debt which Anant Raj is open to taking is LRD and this is one of the best items for LRD because you have long-term leases and good clients.” — *[Apr 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=03aa7997-f0a0-4f9b-8373-f4a4684da92d.pdf)*
3. Management began describing the group as two separate divisions — the historic real estate 'bread and butter' and a new technology division of colocation and cloud — the same two-vertical framing the Scheme later uses. “So Anant Raj Limited will now have two full-fledged divisions. Real estate division which is the historical, the division of the company, the bread and butter of the company as of now and plus the technology division, in which we will be data center, co-location infrastructure and cloud.” — *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=27b8b856-615a-44a5-8be4-157fd1831d5c.pdf)*
4. The ₹2,100 cr fundraise (₹100 cr promoters, ₹2,000 cr market) was ring-fenced entirely for the data centre/cloud build-out, with real estate funded from internal accruals — distinct funding requirements per vertical, with cloud capex cited at ~₹100 cr per MW on top of ₹26 cr colocation capex. “This is purely data center, sir. This fund is going to be purely for data centers. For our real estate, we are completely funded with our internal sources.” — *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=27b8b856-615a-44a5-8be4-157fd1831d5c.pdf)*
5. An analyst (Raj Sarraf of Finvestors) asked for data centre revenue to be reported separately from real estate because it would become the major contributor; management conceded the point. “Sir, both the revenues are going to be substantial and we will be breaking them up, sir . We will do that definitely.” — *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=27b8b856-615a-44a5-8be4-157fd1831d5c.pdf)*
6. The CFO positioned the company at an 'inflection point' with a legacy real estate business and a separate future-ready data centre/cloud platform — H1 FY26 revenue ₹1,223.2 cr of which data centre only ₹58.42 cr, ₹1,100 cr QIP completed, net cash positive, ~₹700 cr capital employed in data centres at 75% EBITDA margin. “Our legacy real estate business continues to deliver a consistent growth and strengthen our leadership in high demanding markets. At the same time, our Data Center and Cloud initiatives are shaping up the future ready platform that positions us as a diversified resilient enterprise s.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3ac557ff-2c8f-4014-b2d4-e7e582aa0e59.pdf)*
7. Investors (Sri Gopal of StockHifi, Ashwani Sharma of Emkay) again pressed for separate real estate vs data centre revenue and EBITDA reporting; management said formal segment disclosure was not yet triggered because data centre revenue was under 10% of the total. “In this, you have to give segmental breakup once you do 10%.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3ac557ff-2c8f-4014-b2d4-e7e582aa0e59.pdf)*
8. Asked whether the company should lever up to scale data centres faster, management refused on the grounds that real estate is the backbone and must stay low-debt — a tension a separately funded data centre entity resolves. Capacity plans were 63 MW by Dec 2026, 117 MW by FY28 and 307 MW by FY31-32. “And as it is, we feel that our backbone is still real estate, which will always be. And we feel that real estate should be as low on debt as possible.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3ac557ff-2c8f-4014-b2d4-e7e582aa0e59.pdf)*
9. The May 11, 2026 board note first records the need for a merger/demerger, citing differing nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics and capital requirements, plus the 357 MW IT load plan (after the 50 MW Andhra Pradesh MOU) needing about ₹20,000 cr; a committee of Amit Sarin, Ashim Sarin, Manoj Goyal and Pankaj Gupta was formed to design it. “The Board of Directors have considered that the Company is presently engaged in two distinct business undertakings, namely Real Estate Development and Data Center Services, which differ significantly in their nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics, and capital requirements and continuing both businesses under a single corporate does not adequately reflect the true potential and intrinsic value of each business segment, thereby impacting stakeholder returns.” — *Scheme*
10. The July 21, 2026 Scheme explains the data centre business is split across ARL and ARCPL, so ARCPL is first merged into ARL and the combined Data Centre Business then demerged into Ashok Cloud — consolidating it in one entity and creating two focused listed companies. “The Data Centre Business is presently conducted through ARL and ARCPL, with various assets, employees, investments and business operations pertaining to the Data Centre Business being housed across both entities.” — *Scheme*
11. Stated benefit one: independent market recognition and valuation of the data centre business given its distinct operating profile, growth trajectory, risk-return characteristics and funding needs; demerged undertaking turnover was ₹145.90 cr, 8.96% of ₹1,627.72 cr for FY26. “the segregation of the Data Centre Business into a separately listed company would facilitate independent market recognition and valuation of the Data Centre Business, having regard to its distinct operating profile, growth trajectory, risk-return characteristics and funding requirements;” — *Scheme*
12. Stated benefit two: a distinct legal entity lets Ashok Cloud attract sector-specific capital, investors, acquisitions and partnerships, with simpler ownership and intra-group arrangements cancelled or rationalised. “the separation of the Data Centre Business into a distinct legal entity will enable Ashok Cloud to effectively attract sector specific resources for its growth requirements and pursue strategic investments, partnerships, thereby unlocking greater value for its shareholders;” — *Scheme*
13. Consideration is 1 ACPL share of ₹2 for every 1 ARL share of ₹2; ARL holders get 49% of ACPL directly (promoters 28.14%, public 20.86%) while ARL keeps 51%, so ACPL remains a subsidiary and ARL holders retain 100% of the ultimate economic interest; listing on BSE and NSE via the Rule 19(7) exemption. “Overall, the shareholders of ARL will hold 100% of the ultimate beneficial economic interest in the Resultant Company, ACPL ( direct holding of 49% and indirect holding of 51% throughARL).” — *Scheme*
14. Days before the Scheme, the Finance and Investment Committee funded the shell resultant company: a ₹74,86,45,106 rights issue of 37,43,22,553 ₹2 shares in ACPL (incorporated Oct 11, 2021; nil turnover in FY24, FY25 and FY26) to meet data centre and cloud development funding. “ACPL proposes to raise the fund to meet the funding requirement for development of its data centres and cloud business.” — *Scheme*
15. The press release frames the outcome as two independent platforms — ARL in real estate/infrastructure and Ashok Cloud in data centres, sovereign public cloud, AI-ready cloud infrastructure and DC/DR services — citing separate growth trajectories, operational priorities and capital needs. “"Our real estate, infrastructure business and Data Centre & Cloud Services Business have evolved into two distinct platforms, each with its own growth trajectory, operational priorities, and capital needs.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** On the Apr 25, 2024 call Arpit Shah of Stallion Asset asked outright whether there were plans to demerge the business and Amit Sarin refused — 'too soon', focus on execution — while describing the cloud venture as a half-megawatt pilot with TCIL. By the Oct 30, 2024 call (Q2 FY25) management was framing the group as 'two full-fledged divisions' (real estate plus a technology division) with a ₹2,100 cr fundraise earmarked purely for data centre/cloud, and Raj Sarraf pushed for separate data centre revenue disclosure; on the Nov 12, 2025 call (Q2/H1 FY26) the CFO called the company 'at an important inflection point' with a 'legacy real estate business' alongside the data centre/cloud 'future ready platform', the ₹1,100 cr QIP was done, and analysts again asked for a separate segment/EBITDA breakup, which management declined on the 10%-of-revenue threshold. The demerger itself was never discussed on any of the three calls: it surfaced in the May 11, 2026 board note (which recorded the need for merger/demerger and set up a committee of Amit Sarin, Ashim Sarin, Manoj Goyal and Pankaj Gupta to frame a scheme), then was executed as the ACPL rights-issue funding on July 20, 2026 and the Composite Scheme approved on July 21, 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Ashok Cloud: pure-play digital-infrastructure valuation and independent market recognition, sector-specific growth capital, partnerships and acquisitions, dedicated leadership, consolidated ownership (75% EBITDA-margin colocation/cloud, 357 MW plan, ~₹20,000 cr capex). Anant Raj: sharper focus on real estate, infrastructure and hospitality, low debt, continued execution. Both: operational efficiency, agility, faster decision-making, transparency, unlocked shareholder value, with holders participating directly in each.

*Not explained on the calls:* Calls never mention the demerger; no appointed date, debt/cash/asset split, valuation or swap basis, why ARL keeps 51%, how ₹20,000 cr capex gets funded, or listing timeline.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Consolidate the entire Data Centre Business in one entity and create two dedicated listed companies, enabling independent market recognition and valuation, dedicated management focus and sector-specific funding.
- *What it reveals:* Demerged Undertaking turnover Rs 145.90 cr is only 8.96% of Rs 1,627.72 cr; management cites ~75% data-centre EBITDA margin, 357 MW planned capacity, Rs 20,000 cr capex, net-cash parent with Rs 4,471.64 cr net worth.
- *Parent or spin:* both · *Read next:* The full Composite Scheme: asset/liability split and valuation of the Demerged Undertaking versus ACPL's Rs 74.86 cr rights issue.
- *In their words:* “The Data Centre Business has evolved significantly over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity focused on the rapidly growing Data Centre Business whilst continuing to leverage ARL's institutional strengths, strong brand equity and goodwill.”

- **capex and capital intensity** — parent / remaining: Real estate launches planned of about 2.6 million square feet for FY26; company states real estate "should be as low on debt as possible"; separated business: Data Centre capacity to reach 357 MW IT Load with planned investment of about Rs. 20,000 crore; incremental build cost stated at Rs. 26 crore per MW on existing buildings (versus Rs. 50 crore per MW earlier guided) “With this plan, the total planned Data Center capacity will reach to 357 MW IT Load, mix of Colocation and Cloud Services. The company will be investing about Rs. 20,000 Cr to reach total planned capacity.”
- **operating margin** — parent / remaining: Consolidated EBITDA margin for Q2 FY26 stood at 27.76%, up year-on-year from 23.62%; separated business: Data Center business EBITDA margin of 75% on Q2 FY26 revenue of INR 35.47 crore “So, sir, we have generated the revenue from Data Center business in this quarter is INR 35.47 crore and the EBITDA margin is 75%.”
- **debt and leverage** — parent / remaining: Net debt below INR 50 crores for five quarters in a row; net cash positive after a INR 1,100 crore QIP and prepayment of INR 125 crore of debt; outstanding qualified borrowings down from INR 388.47 crore to INR 297.92 crore in FY26; separated business: Data Centre build stated to be fully funded without debt; the demerger is intended to let Ashok Cloud attract sector-specific resources and growth capital of its own “One main highlight which we are very proud of is that the fifth quarter in a row, even prior to the QIP which the company has successfully done, fifth quarter in a row, the net debt of the company has been below 50 crores.”
- **growth** — parent / remaining: Consolidated revenue from operations grew from Rs. 2,059.97 crore (FY25) to Rs. 2,511.60 crore (FY26); H1 FY26 revenue up 24.22% year-on-year; separated business: Data Centre revenue of INR 58.42 crore in H1 FY26, scaling from 28 MW to 63 MW by December 2026 and to 117 MW by FY28, with INR 1,200 crore of revenue targeted from 63 MW “The Data Centre Business has evolved significantly over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity focused on the rapidly growing Data Centre Business whilst continuing to leverage ARL's institutional strengths, strong brand equity and goodwill.”
- **cash** — parent / remaining: Standalone cash and cash equivalents Rs. 806.90 crore and consolidated Rs. 899.46 crore as at March 31, 2026; of the INR 1,099.99 crore QIP, "an amount of Rs. 750 crores remains unutilized as on March 31, 2026"; separated business: Ashok Cloud had net worth of Rs. 0.04 crore and nil turnover before being funded with Rs. 74,86,45,106 of fresh equity by ARL ahead of the scheme “ACPL proposes to raise the fund to meet the funding requirement for development of its data centres and cloud business.”
- **tax** — parent / remaining: not stated; separated business: A taxation benefit for the data centre business was described on the call as proposed by the government and not yet in effect, applicable to both Colocation and Cloud “It is a very welcome step, sir. It is going to be really encouraging. And it is applicable to both, sir, Colocation as well as Cloud.”
- **working capital** — parent / remaining: Standalone inventories fell from Rs. 720.15 crore to Rs. 552.68 crore; consolidated cash used from operations of Rs. (326.49) crore in FY26 against Rs. 322.33 crore generated in FY25; separated business: Colocation power cost is a pass-through to customers while in Cloud the power cost is borne and recovered in pricing “Sir, for Colocation , we will always do the netting of electricity pass through expenses . And for Cloud we charge for that.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

No earnings-call transcripts are on file, so the reasoning below is reconstructed only from the filings. The separation is the demerger of Valor Estate Ltd's (formerly D B Realty Ltd) hospitality business into Advent Hotels International Limited (formerly Shiva Realtors Suburban Private Limited) under a Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement that also amalgamated Esteem Properties Private Limited into Valor; the Explanatory Statement to the 12th December 2025 EGM says the Scheme was entered into 'mainly with aim to demerge hospitality business of the Company into Resulting Company and thus unlock overall value for the shareholders.' NCLT Mumbai sanctioned it on 12 June 2025, it became effective 1 July 2025 (demerger appointed date 1 April 2025; Esteem amalgamation appointed date 1 April 2024), and shareholders on the 18 July 2025 record date received 1 AHIL share of Rs. 10 for every 10 Valor shares. The carve-out moved consolidated net assets of Rs. 1,02,194.65 lakhs (standalone Rs. 1,01,512.91 lakhs) out of Valor — Rs. 1,49,386.00 lakhs of property, plant and equipment, Rs. 54,858.00 lakhs of goodwill, Rs. 29,117.12 lakhs of intangibles, against Rs. 46,196.17 lakhs non-current and Rs. 16,028.03 lakhs current borrowings, Rs. 2,01,956.25 lakhs of other non-current financial liabilities and Rs. 28,951.71 lakhs of deferred tax liability — and took out a business that had FY25 revenue of Rs. 36,650.21 lakhs and PAT of Rs. 4,468.06 lakhs, now shown as discontinued operations. Management's stated problems solved are focus and structure: Valor 'is now engaged solely in the real estate business, which constitutes its only reportable segment,' so segment reporting ceased, while Advent gets 'its own Board and Management team,' NSE/BSE listing on 13 November 2025 for 'enhanced market visibility, liquidity for existing shareholders, and a strengthened capital structure,' and an asset-heavy growth path (five projects, 3,100 keys, EBITDA from under Rs. 200 crore to over Rs. 1,200 crore by FY32, targeted mid-teens compounded ROE) that a combined entity would have had to fund alongside real estate. The second, smaller separation/consolidation strand is non-core cleanup: Sahyadri Agro and Dairy Private Limited (dairy farming, milk procurement and trading), taken to 76.63% via enforcement of security and then to 100% 'as the transaction relates to the liquidation of non-core assets,' sold its entire dairy business under a Business Transfer Agreement at a gain of Rs. 6,901.20 lakhs with Rs. 1,697.63 lakhs of non-compete fees booked as an exceptional item, is now 'evaluating opportunities to engage in the business of real estate development,' and was amalgamated into Horizontal Ventures Private Limited for structural simplification, synergies, avoidance of duplication and lower compliance and overhead costs. Running alongside is balance-sheet repair the filings tie to the same strategy: consolidated secured debt down to Rs. 730 crore, full redemption of Rs. 235 crore of NCDs out of the Rs. 262 crore Dahisar/Aradhya Park development-rights conveyance, and the Scheme-driven reduction and consolidation of the 8% RPS (Clause 32: Rs. 10 face value cut to Rs. 9, then 10 consolidated into 9) plus Clause 20's 1:10 allotment of AHIL preference shares, followed by the November 2025 proposal to convert KRPL's 6,45,75,000 RPS into 0.0001% CCPS converting into 32,02,330 equity shares at Rs. 201.65 'with a view to conserve the financial resources of the Company.' No filing names any investor, lender or partner as having demanded the separation; the only named partner is Prestige Group, which sits on Advent's side as a 50:50 JV partner in the Sahar project and co-developer at Aerocity.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The Composite Scheme's stated purpose, as put to shareholders in the EGM explanatory statement, was to demerge the hospitality business into Advent Hotels International Limited and unlock shareholder value; it simultaneously amalgamated Esteem Properties Private Limited into Valor. “mainly with aim to demerge hospitality business of the Company into Resulting Company and thus unlock overall value for the shareholders” — *Scheme*
2. Post-demerger Valor is a pure-play real estate company with a single reportable segment, and prior-period hospitality results are reclassified as discontinued operations under Ind AS 105. “Consequent to the demerger, the Company is now engaged solely in the real estate business, which constitutes its only reportable segment.” — *Scheme*
3. Management framed the separation as letting each business pursue its own growth path: Chairman Vinod Goenka tied Q2FY26 progress to completing the demerger and listing of hospitality. “We successfully completed the demerger and listing of our Hospitality business, an important milestone that enables each platform to pursue its independent growth path.” — *Scheme*
4. The Q2FY26 press release states the problems the split solves on Valor's side: targeted independent strategies for each business, sharper operational focus, and unlocked long-term value. “This development enables each business to pursue a targeted, independent growth strategy, strengthens operational focus, and positions the Group to unlock enhanced long-term value for shareholders.” — *Scheme*
5. Advent's 13 November 2025 NSE/BSE listing was justified on visibility, shareholder liquidity and capital structure, with Advent carved out of Valor and run by its own board and management. “The listing will mark a significant milestone in Advent's journey as a dedicated hospitality platform, enabling enhanced market visibility, liquidity for existing shareholders, and a strengthened capital structure to support future growth.” — *Scheme*
6. Advent now has independent governance: two operating hotels (313-key Grand Hyatt Bambolim Goa plus 113 keys under development, and a 171-key Hilton in Andheri East, Mumbai). “The Company is governed by its own Board and Management team following the demerger.” — *Scheme*
7. Advent quantified the growth the standalone platform is meant to fund: five projects under development including St. Regis and Marriott Marquis at Aerocity Delhi with Prestige Group (FY27), Waldorf Astoria and Hilton at Worli, and a 1,175-key BKC hotel. “With five projects under development, the company is on track to expand to 3,100 keys. EBITDA, currently under ₹200 crore, is projected to surpass ₹1,200 crore as these projects mature by FY32, reflecting the company's robust growth and institutional approach.” — *Scheme*
8. Advent's MD & CEO Rahul Pandit cast the separation and listing as a governance and financing fix for an asset-heavy hospitality business; Promoter Director Arshad Balwa targeted mid-teens compounded ROE over the next decade. “This listing enhances our financial flexibility, strengthens governance, and enables sustainable value generation for all stakeholders.” — *Scheme*
9. Vice Chairman & MD Shahid Balwa linked the demerger and non-core divestments to deleveraging — consolidated secured debt of ₹730 crore, full redemption of ₹235 crore of NCDs from the ₹262 crore Dahisar/Aradhya Park development-rights conveyance. “The rationalisation of our project portfolio, combined with selective monetisation initiatives, including the divestment of non-core assets, has enabled us to reduce debt levels, bringing us closer to our medium-term objective of a leaner and more efficient capital structure.” — *Scheme*
10. Sahyadri Agro and Dairy was treated explicitly as a non-core asset being liquidated: the Group went to 76.63% through enforcement of security, then to 100%, and SADPL sold its dairy assets under a Business Transfer Agreement at a gain of Rs. 6,901.20 lakhs with Rs. 1,697.63 lakhs of non-compete fees as an exceptional item. “As the transaction relates to the liquidation of non-core assets, SADPL has not been consolidated.” — *Scheme*
11. The NCLT order of 29 January 2026 records the benefits claimed for folding dairy-turned-real-estate SADPL into Horizontal Ventures Private Limited, a wholly-owned-subsidiary merger inside the group with appointed date 1 April 2025, effective 12 March 2026. “Simplification  and rationalisation  of corporate  struct ure through consolidation;” — *Scheme*
12. The same order lists compliance and overhead reduction as the operating rationale for the SADPL-HVPL consolidation, with the petitioners undertaking not to claim Section 72A tax-loss benefits after the Income-tax Officer objected. “Reduction in multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances,  reduction in overheads, including administrative, managerial and other administrative costs.” — *Scheme*
13. The Scheme itself restructured Valor's preference capital: Clause 32 cut RPS face value from Rs. 10 to Rs. 9 and consolidated 10 into 9 (KRPL's 7,17,50,000 becoming 6,45,75,000), and Clause 20 allotted 1 AHIL preference share for every 10 Valor RPS (71,75,000 to KRPL). “which were reduced and consolidated as per the recent Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement sanctioned by the Hon’ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench on 12th	June,	2025	(effecting	 the	demerger	 of	Company’s	 hospitality	 business,” — *Scheme*
14. Building on the Scheme, the Board on 14 November 2025 proposed converting KRPL's 6,45,75,000 8% RPS into 0.0001% CCPS convertible into 32,02,330 equity shares at Rs. 201.65 (premium Rs. 191.65), to avoid the redemption cash outflow and lift net worth. “The conversion of RPS into CCPS is expected to reduce the future cash outflows otherwise required for the redemption of RPS, thereby improving liquidity, conserving cash resources, and enabling the Company to channel funds towards its operational and growth requirements.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** There are no transcripts on file, so the idea cannot be traced call by call; the paper trail runs through filings and the Scheme itself. The Composite Scheme was sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 12 June 2025, became effective 1 July 2025 with demerger appointed date 1 April 2025, and the 1:10 entitlement was fixed on the 18 July 2025 record date; the SADPL-into-HVPL amalgamation was approved by both boards on 18 August 2025 with appointed date 1 April 2025. The plan then became visible in public filings in quick succession: Advent's listing press release (12 November 2025), Valor's Q2FY26 results and press release (14-15 November 2025) which first framed the demerger as completed and as the basis for debt reduction, the EGM notice and corrigendum (20 November and 8 December 2025) which disclosed the Scheme's preference-share reduction, consolidation and 1:10 AHIL allotment and layered the RPS-to-CCPS conversion on top, and finally the NCLT order of 29 January 2026 and effective date of 12 March 2026 completing the SADPL consolidation. The shape of the plan therefore widened over time from a single hospitality demerger into a package: demerger plus listing, plus non-core dairy liquidation and merger, plus capital-structure conversion.

**What management expects from it:** Valor: pure-play real estate, single reportable segment, leaner and more efficient capital structure, lower debt (secured debt ₹730 crore), greater financial flexibility, unlocked value. Advent: independent board and management, focused hospitality platform, better visibility, shareholder liquidity, stronger capital structure, 3,100 keys and EBITDA above ₹1,200 crore by FY32, mid-teens compounded ROE.

*Not explained on the calls:* No call transcripts supplied; filings never name investors, lenders or partners who asked for it, nor give swap-ratio valuation basis, cost savings, or Advent fundraising plans.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* "mainly with aim to demerge hospitality business of the Company into Resulting Company and thus unlock overall value for the shareholders"; listing enables each platform to pursue independent growth, focus and financial flexibility.
- *What it reveals:* Spin holds 313-key Grand Hyatt Goa and 171-key Hilton Mumbai, five projects under development, EBITDA under Rs.200 crore targeted above Rs.1,200 crore by FY32 (3,100+ keys). Parent left as pure real estate; consolidated borrowings fell sharply post-demerger.
- *Parent or spin:* both · *Read next:* AHIL's own balance sheet: the Rs. 2,01,956.25 lakhs other non-current financial liabilities transferred with the demerged undertaking
- *In their words:* “A Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement was entered into between the Company ("Amalgamated Company" and "Demerged Company") and Esteem Properties Private Limited ("Amalgamating Company"/"EPPL") and Advent Hotels International Limited (formerly known as Shiva Realtors Suburban Private Limited) ("Resulting Company"/"AHIL) ("Scheme") mainly with aim to demerge hospitality business of the Company into Resulting Company and thus unlock overall value for the shareholders.”
