### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

Management's case, as set out in the 27 June 2026 board filing, press note and demerger presentation, is that Pricol had become two structurally different companies inside one shell: the Driver Information & Connected Vehicle Solutions (DICVS) business — instrument clusters (mechanical, electro-mechanical, LCD/TFT), integrated infotainment, e-cockpit, telematics, battery management systems and some sensors — versus the Actuation, Control & Fluid Management Systems (ACFMS) business and the polymer/precision business held in wholly owned Pricol Precision Products (P3L). DICVS was the bigger half, at INR 2,424.63 crore of FY26 revenue, or 61.17% of consolidated turnover (the press release rounds it to ~INR 2,400 crore and ~60%), against FY26 consolidated revenue of INR 3,963.85 crore and total income of INR 40,523.70 million. The problem they said this solves is divergence: the two now operate with "differing customer needs, competitive dynamics, capital allocation and risk profiles" — DICVS innovation-led (display, electrification, connectivity, e-cockpit, ADAS, software-defined vehicles; risk = technology disruption and the semiconductor ecosystem; partners = display, chip-design and semiconductor firms; talent = embedded software, system architects, cyber-security and functional-safety experts) while ACFMS/P3L is scale-led (manufacturing excellence, cost competitiveness, lightweighting, exports; risk = automotive cyclicality and commodity costs; partners = Tier-2/3 suppliers). Capital deployment priorities were said to be incompatible in one entity: DICVS money goes to talent, software, global R&D centres, technology investments and overseas acquisitions, Pricol Limited's to manufacturing capacity, automation, productivity and domestic acquisitions. Other stated benefits: financial flexibility for each entity, reduced operational complexity and faster decision-making, independent and dedicated management teams, the ability to tailor processes, policies, systems and governance, improved visibility of each business's value and growth prospects, better ability to attract strategic and financial investors, and "appropriate valuation benchmarks for each business, free from conglomerate discount." Consideration is non-cash: 1 Pricol Autotech share of INR 1 for every 1 Pricol Limited share, so Autotech's register mirrors Pricol's (promoters 38.51%, public 61.49%), with listing sought on NSE and BSE; SSPA & Co. gave the share-entitlement report and Saffron Capital the fairness opinion. The 13 November 2026 filing revealed the commercial endpoint the June rationale did not mention: the promoters (Vijay, Vikram and Vanitha Mohan plus family and Pricol Holdings, Pricol Engineering Industries, Shrimay Enterprises and Pricol Logistics) will sell their entire 38.51% — 4,69,34,833 shares — of Pricol Autotech to Topaz Terrace Investments B.V., a Warburg Pincus affiliate, for up to INR 1,663.07 crore, followed by a mandatory open offer for up to a further 26%, after which Warburg controls Autotech and the family keeps ACFMS and polymer with no change in shareholding; no investor, lender or customer is named as having asked for any of this, and the only disclosed initiators are the board and the promoters, who used Veda Corporate Advisors as exclusive financial advisor.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The 27 June 2026 board filing frames the DICVS demerger as creating a simpler, faster entity matched to fast-changing technology, because the two halves already ran on different customer, competitive, capital and risk logic. “The demerger of the DICVS Business is a strategic decision to create a simpler, sharper and more agile corporate entity, to meet the fast changing needs and technologies related to this business and its dynamic market realities.” — *Scheme*
2. The demerged undertaking is the majority of the company: DICVS turnover of INR 2,424.63 crore in FY26, 61.17% of consolidated turnover (press note: ~INR 2,400 crore, ~60%), against consolidated FY26 revenue from operations of INR 3,963.85 crore. “The turnover of the DICVS Business for the financial year ending March 31, 2026, stood at INR 2,424.63 crores. This represents 61.17% of the total consolidated turnover of the Company for the financial year ending March 31, 2026.” — *Scheme*
3. Consideration is a mirror 1:1 share entitlement with no cash, so Pricol Autotech starts with promoters at 38.51% and public at 61.49%, and is to be listed on NSE and BSE; Pricol Limited receives nothing and retains no shares. “1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of the Resulting Company having face value of INR 1 (Rupee One only) each for every 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of INR 1 (Rupee One only) each of the Company.” — *Scheme*
4. The presentation makes valuation an explicit objective — separate frameworks for two structurally different businesses, removing the holding-company drag of one blended multiple. “Clear market recognition and appropriate valuation benchmarks for each business, free from conglomerate discount” — *Scheme*
5. The side-by-side table splits the two on capital deployment (software, global R&D centres and overseas acquisitions for Autotech versus capacity, automation and domestic acquisitions for Pricol), talent, partners and risk (technology disruption versus automotive cyclicality and commodity costs). “Talent, product development, software, global R&D centres, tech investments & overseas acquisitions” — *Scheme*
6. The 13 November 2026 share purchase agreement discloses the endpoint: Warburg Pincus affiliate Topaz Terrace Investments B.V. buys the promoters' entire 4,69,34,833 shares (38.51%) of Pricol Autotech for up to INR 1,663.07 crore, plus a mandatory open offer for up to 26% more. “For completeness, the aggregate consideration payable for the sale by the Sellers of their entire stake of Pricol Autotech of 38.51% (to be issued to the Sellers pursuant to the Scheme) is up to INR 1,663.07 Crores (Indian Rupees One Thousand Six Hundred and Sixty Three Crores and Seven Lakhs) subject to the terms of the Share Purchase Agreement.” — *Scheme*
7. Control of the demerged business passes to Warburg and the Mohan family seeks reclassification out of Autotech's promoter group, while the agreement imposes non-compete obligations on the sellers and on Pricol Limited itself; ACFMS and polymer stay with the family with no shareholding change. “Amongst other things, the Share Purchase Agreement contains customary stand still provisions, warranties and indemnities being provided by the Sellers, subject to customary limitations and caps, and certain non-compete obligations on the Sellers and the Company for a specified period.” — *Scheme*
8. Vikram Mohan ties the separation rationale directly to handing the business to Warburg, describing DICVS as having been "at the heart" of Pricol's five-decade journey and Warburg as its next owner-custodian. “The proposed demerger will give Pricol Autotech the focus and independence to realise its full potential.” — *Scheme*
9. Asked on the 30 January 2026 call why a new subsidiary had been incorporated, Siddharth Manoharan attributed it to technology-partnership flexibility and the BOE MOU, not to any restructuring; Pricol Autotech Limited was incorporated on 21 February 2026. “But whenever the plan materializes, we will talk about that in detail later.” — *CALL Feb 2026*
10. Management's own segment guidance showed the margin and growth divergence later used as rationale — DICVS at INR 2,100–2,200 crore and 12.5–13% EBITDA, ACFMS at INR 600 crore growing 30–35%, polymer at INR 850–900 crore on 9.5% — though no separation was suggested. “This year, the plastics, the Polymer business will be about INR 850 crores to INR 900 crores with a steady-state margin of 9.5%.” — *CALL Nov 2025*
11. A year earlier Vikram Mohan had conceded that consolidating the lower-margin plastics business pulled the group's blended EBITDA down even as rupee profit rose — the conglomerate-mix problem the 2026 presentation addresses via separate valuation frameworks. “Overall margin of Pricol will be maintained, but when Sundaram consolidates, it is going to come down lower because plastics is a single digit margin and not a double digit EBITDA product.” — *CALL Feb 2025*
12. Six weeks before the board approved the scheme, the Q4 FY26 call described a unified group starting a fresh INR 680–700 crore capex cycle across all three divisions, with no hint of a demerger; Ganesh put DICVS at ~60%, ACFMS ~20% and P3L ~20% of revenue. “In fact, this year, in itself, we have planned for about between INR 680 crore to INR 700 crores of CAPEX to cater to all of our new businesses that we have won, new plants, new machines, so on and so forth, which will keep propelling us forward and to maintain this growth momentum.” — *CALL May 2026*
13. The same call disclosed the governance handover that preceded the restructuring: Vanitha Mohan stepped back from Pricol to chair Pricol Holdings and Vikram Mohan became Chairman and Managing Director — the signatory of both the June scheme and the November stake sale. “Mrs. Vanita Mohan has stepped down as an active role from PRICOL, and I have taken over as the Chairman of the company.” — *CALL May 2026*

**How it evolved:** The idea is entirely absent from the eleven earnings calls (Nov 2023 through the 15 May 2026 Q4 FY26 call), where management instead talked up a single integrated group — a FY31 INR 8,000 crore target, INR 680–700 crore of FY27 group capex across DICVS, ACFMS and polymer, and converting polymer "from a component maker to a value-added polymer player." The nearest hint is the 30 January 2026 (Feb 2026) call, where Siddharth Manoharan confirmed a newly incorporated subsidiary but attributed it to technology-partnership flexibility and the BOE MOU, saying the plan would be discussed "later"; Pricol Autotech Limited was in fact incorporated on 21 February 2026. The board then approved the scheme on 27 June 2026 — six weeks after a call that never raised it — and the purpose sharpened on 13 November 2026, when the promoters' entire 38.51% of the demerged entity was agreed for sale to Warburg Pincus for up to INR 1,663.07 crore plus a 26% open offer, converting a stated "focus and agility" restructuring into a control exit from the group's largest business.

**What management expects from it:** Pricol Autotech: a focused automotive-electronics platform — innovation-led growth, higher content per vehicle, global R&D, IP-led acquisitions, Warburg's capital and sector network. Pricol Limited: scale-led precision engineering — ACFMS exports, disc brakes, a polymer centre of excellence, domestic acquisitions. Both: dedicated management, tailored capital allocation, faster decisions, separate valuation benchmarks free of conglomerate discount, easier access to strategic and financial investors.

*Not explained on the calls:* No call ever mentioned it. Filings omit stranded corporate costs, debt/asset and employee/IP allocation, tax, the INR 1,663.07 crore valuation basis, and why promoters exited DICVS.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Clear segregation so each company concentrates on its core activities; strategic decision to create a simpler, sharper, more agile entity meeting fast-changing technology needs and dynamic market realities; unlocking shareholder value.
- *What it reveals:* DICVS is the bigger, faster business — INR 2,424.63 crores, 61.17% of FY26 consolidated turnover — yet presented as a "4.5%" small share; Warburg Pincus pays INR 1,663.07 crores for 38.51%, implying ~INR 4,318 crores equity value, plus a 26% open offer.
- *Parent or spin:* both · *Read next:* The Scheme of Arrangement on pricol.com/investors — DICVS asset, liability and debt allocation to Pricol Autotech.
- *In their words:* “The turnover of the DICVS Business for the financial year ending March 31, 2026, stood at INR 2,424.63 crores. This represents 61.17% of the total consolidated turnover of the Company for the financial year ending March 31, 2026.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

Religare is demerging its entire financial services business — SME/MSME lending (Religare Finvest), retail broking plus e-governance (Religare Broking and its subsidiary Religare Digital Solutions), affordable housing finance (Religare Housing Development Finance, already an RFL subsidiary), and the related investment and ancillary/support activities — out of the listed holdco REL into RFL, which will itself be listed, leaving REL as a pure-play holder of its 63.2% stake in Care Health Insurance; REL shareholders get 1 RFL share for every REL share, and RFL's pre-scheme capital held by REL is cancelled so RFL's shareholding mirrors REL's. Management framed it as three converging conditions rather than a reaction to distress: the Burman Group's completed takeover as promoters (open offer concluded Feb 2025, board reconstituted July 2025, promoters at 29.75% fully diluted in Feb 2026 and ~30.3% by May 2026 after ~4% of open-market buying, heading to ~34% on warrant conversion), the INR1,500 crore preferential warrant raise subscribed 50:50 by the Burmans and marquee investors (earmarked INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking, INR75 crore to repay REL's own debt and INR375 crore general corporate purpose), and the fact that the businesses had reached an inflection point where "each business also operates with different capital requirements, risk frameworks, manpower talent and growth trajectories." The stated problems it solves are a conglomerate structure in which insurance (FY26 GWP INR11,417 crore, PBT INR539 crore on 'n' basis, 19.7% retail SAHI share) drowns out a tiny financial services segment (FY25 demerged-undertaking turnover of only INR457.29 crore, 6.2% of consolidated revenue), investors who cannot value the two halves, and management bandwidth: the scheme's four pillars are streamlined focus/simplified structure, value unlocking plus targeted capital raising through a separate RFL listing, dedicated leadership with sector-specific talent and performance-linked rewards, and risk/compliance frameworks tailored to each segment. The financial services side is being restarted from a cleaned-up base — RFL is debt-free with all legacy promoter-era diversion issues provided or written off (including the full INR750 crore Lakshmi Vilas Bank FD), RBI's Corrective Action Plan lifted in July 2025 and bank fraud tags removed, leaving ~INR591 crore cash, ~INR900 crore net worth, 261% CRAR, NOF of INR821 crore and only a ~INR60 crore core SME book — so Arjun Lamba tied the demerger directly to scaling: "Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this." Who asked for it: shareholders and analysts had been pressing since the first call back in Nov 2025 (Vikas Shrivastav on demerging Care and removing the holdco discount, Dixit Doshi on IPO vs demerger of Care), and after the announcement nearly every questioner — Umang Shah, Adarsh, Hitaindra Pradhan, Ravi Purohit, Niharika Karnani, Sarvesh Gupta — argued the value sits in Care and demanded a reverse merger giving direct Care shares, citing the Max Financial precedent. Management conceded the point but said IRDAI's 25–26% promoter requirement cannot be met while the Burmans' look-through stake in Care is only ~18–19%, so this was "the first step in that direction," done after evaluating structural alternatives with leading advisors; Lamba refused to amend the scheme and would not commit to a timeline for a second one. Execution has since run into the regulator: exchanges gave no-objection/no-adverse-observation letters on 7 July 2026, but on 6–7 August 2026 RBI informed REL and RFL that their application for no-objection/prior approval "has not been acceded to," and the companies said they would engage further with the regulator.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. Asked outright about demerging Care and the other subsidiaries from the holdco and about removing the holdco discount, Pratul Gupta said nothing was decided — the board was weighing options and wanted to strengthen the businesses first, after the INR1,500 crore raise, before any capital-market action. “On the second question about how the structure will look like in some future time, what I can very clearly assure you is that the management and the Board is evaluating various options which can add value to the shareholders.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=25fe79a7-8023-4efc-9cd6-43c8dee47d4f.pdf)*
2. Investors were already framing the choice as Care IPO versus demerger; Dixit Doshi asked it explicitly alongside questions on NBFC yields, showing the separation idea originated with shareholders rather than management. “And in terms of your initial comments on the value unlocking, if you can just touch upon whether we will be looking for an IPO for the care health business or we will be better off with the de -merger of the business?” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=25fe79a7-8023-4efc-9cd6-43c8dee47d4f.pdf)*
3. Gupta presented the demerger as a strategic imperative rather than a housekeeping exercise, announced two days after the REL and RFL boards approved it on 14 Feb 2026. “It is a strategic imperati ve step designed to unlock shareholder value, create business clarity and position the resulting entities for sustained long -term growth.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b273d588-fe12-446c-bee6-b5d6269b6a44.pdf)*
4. The trigger was three converging conditions — the Burman takeover as promoters, the INR1,500 crore warrant raise covering funding needs for the foreseeable future, and the businesses reaching a scale that demands specialised focus. “Each business also operates with different capital requirements, risk frameworks, manpower talent and growth trajectories.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b273d588-fe12-446c-bee6-b5d6269b6a44.pdf)*

Mechanics: lending, broking and ancillary support services move from REL to RFL on a going-concern basis, the Care stake stays in REL, RFL issues one share per REL share and then lists, with a 15–18 month process ending in Q1 FY28. “The lending, broking and ancillary support services held under REL shall be demer ged into RFL on a going concern basis. The investment in CARE shall continue to be retained in REL.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b273d588-fe12-446c-bee6-b5d6269b6a44.pdf)*

A separate RFL listing is meant to unlock value, widen investor participation and let that business raise its own capital — the second of four stated pillars. “The independent listing of RFL is expected to unlock shareholder value and enhance investor participation.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b273d588-fe12-446c-bee6-b5d6269b6a44.pdf)*
7. Analysts attacked the design immediately: Umang Shah argued demerging Care directly would have removed the holdco discount on the asset that carries most of the value. “I'm a bit puzzled why we chose to demerge financial services and not CARE directly?” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b273d588-fe12-446c-bee6-b5d6269b6a44.pdf)*
8. Gupta positioned this as stage one of a longer restructuring, with a Care reverse merger possible later once unspecified milestones and minimum-shareholding thresholds are met. “Well, I think this is -- as I mentioned, this is the first step in that direction.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b273d588-fe12-446c-bee6-b5d6269b6a44.pdf)*
9. The binding constraint on a Care reverse merger is the IRDAI promoter-shareholding rule against a Burman look-through stake in Care of only ~18–19%, which Gupta confirmed when Vikas Srivastava spelled out the law. “So you are right in terms of the fact that the look - through shareholding of the promoter group today in CARE is at around 18% to 19%.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b273d588-fe12-446c-bee6-b5d6269b6a44.pdf)*
10. Management said the structure was chosen after a full review of alternatives with external advisors, and promised no operational, customer or employee disruption during implementation. “This has resulted after comprehensive evalu ation of various structural alternatives which were discussed with leading advisors.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b273d588-fe12-446c-bee6-b5d6269b6a44.pdf)*
11. Arjun Lamba restated the core purpose as separating financial services from insurance to give shareholders a clean, understandable structure and management a single focus, while acknowledging the holdco-discount complaint. “And for us, number one has been to separate the FS business from the insurance business and to provide a clean structure so that the shareholders can understand, th e management can be very focused in doing what they have to do.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=87938b4d-578d-40b0-89a8-7803462a6057.pdf)*

Lamba linked the demerger to the capital allocation plan — INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking, ~INR375 crore general corporate purpose, with RFL needing none given ~INR900–1,000 crore net worth and ~INR600 crore cash. “Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=87938b4d-578d-40b0-89a8-7803462a6057.pdf)*

We don't want to amend the scheme.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=87938b4d-578d-40b0-89a8-7803462a6057.pdf)*

Lamba conceded the value is concentrated in Care and said the separation is intended to create value in the other entity too, as promoters moved from ~26% toward ~34% diluted. “Yes, we understand that the value is in Care. We are cognizant of that. That's why we are separating the entities, creating clear paths, and we hope to create value in the other entity as well” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=87938b4d-578d-40b0-89a8-7803462a6057.pdf)*
15. The 14 Feb 2026 filing states the demerged undertaking is all of REL's financial services activity — lending, broking, investment and ancillary/support services — explicitly excluding the retained insurance business, i.e. the Care Health shareholding. “Provided that, the Demerged Undertaking shall exclude the Remaining Business ( as defined in the Scheme ) compris ing of all the units, divisions, undertakings, assets and liabilities in relation to the Demerged Company’s insurance business, comprising of its investment and shareholding in Care Health Insurance Limited .” — *Scheme*
16. The scheme quantifies how small the demerged half is: FY25 turnover of INR457.29 crore on a consolidated basis, just 6.2% of REL's consolidated turnover. “The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended 31  March , 202 5 was INR 457.29 Crores on a consolidated basis  representing 6.2% of the total consolidated turnover of the Company for the year ended 31 March , 202 5.” — *Scheme*
17. Stated rationale includes that the two businesses face different competition and attract different investors, partners and lenders, and that a separately listed vehicle enables sector-focused talent and growth opportunities. “The nature and competition involved in the businesses comprising of the Demerged Undertaking is distinct from the other businesses and it is capable of attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.” — *Scheme*
18. The press release lists four objectives — streamlining businesses, listing financial services, focused management with performance mapped to each business, and segment-tailored risk and compliance frameworks — with 1:1 mirror shareholding in RFL and listing targeted for Q1 FY28. “Focused management attention:  Enable mapping of employee p erformance and rewards to respective business outcomes, and facilitate attraction and retention of sector -specific talent and resources.” — *Scheme*
19. SEBI's comments routed through the NSE observation letter of 7 July 2026 require REL to disclose the need for the demerger, cost-benefit analysis, risks and the RBI approval position to shareholders — i.e. the rationale was not yet fully documented for them. “Need for demerger, rationale of the scheme, synergies of  business of the entities involved in the scheme, impact of the scheme on the shareholders and cost benefit analysis of the s cheme.” — *Scheme*
20. Execution setback: after exchange no-objections on 7 July 2026, RBI declined the no-objection/prior-approval applications of both REL and RFL in letters dated 6 and 7 August 2026, and the companies said they would go back to the regulator. “The Company has received a letter dated August 6, 2026 , from the RBI, conveying that the application has been examined and that the request has not been acceded to .” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** On the Nov 2025 call (Q2/H1 FY26, the first investor call after the Burman takeover) there was no plan — Vikas Shrivastav asked directly what the structure would look like in two years and whether Care would be demerged from the holdco, and CFO Pratul Gupta would only say the board was evaluating options and wanted to make the businesses "larger, better, stronger" before any capital-market action, while Dixit Doshi asked whether Care would be IPO'd or demerged. A Moneycontrol report on 3 Feb 2026 that REL would demerge and list Care drew an exchange query, which REL denied as a disclosable event; eleven days later, on 14 Feb 2026, the REL and RFL boards approved the scheme — and the Feb 2026 call (16 Feb) was where Gupta laid out the full rationale, the four pillars, the 1:1 ratio, the 15–18 month timetable and a Q1 FY28 RFL listing, while every analyst pushed back that Care, not financial services, should have been separated. By the May 2026 call (13 May, Q4/FY26) the framing had shifted from Gupta's structural logic to Executive Director Arjun Lamba's: separating FS from insurance was "number one," the promoters had bought ~4% more stock toward the IRDAI threshold, and he declined to amend the scheme while leaving a later reverse merger of Care open "at an appropriate stage." The 7 July 2026 exchange observation letters cleared the way, but the 7 Aug 2026 filings disclosed RBI had refused to accede to the application, leaving the scheme stalled pending further engagement.

**What management expects from it:** REL becomes a pure-play health insurance holdco around Care (GWP INR11,417 crore, PBT INR539 crore 'n' basis, combined ratio heading from 101.4% to ~100% in two years on operating leverage, 18–24% growth). RFL becomes an integrated, separately listed financial services platform — debt-free, ~INR900 crore net worth, ~INR591 crore cash, 261% CRAR — able to leverage to industry norms, raise targeted capital, hire sector-specific leadership on performance-linked rewards, run tailored risk frameworks, and unlock value via mirror 1:1 listing.

*Not explained on the calls:* No cost-benefit or synergy quantification, no RFL valuation or AUM/ROE targets, no holdco-discount fix or Care reverse-merger timeline, no stated path to IRDAI's 26%, and no RBI-rejection reasoning.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Growth needs differentiated strategy; business is distinct and attracts different investors, lenders and partners; focused management, targeted regulatory compliance and risk frameworks; separate listing to unlock value for REL shareholders
- *What it reveals:* RFL is debt-free with ₹898.8 crore net worth, 261.9% CRAR and ~₹591 crore cash, yet the demerged undertaking was only 6.2% of FY25 consolidated turnover; REL retains Care Health, where management says the value is
- *Parent or spin:* both · *Read next:* The next intimation on RBI no-objection after its August 6, 2026 refusal — the scheme's gating approval
- *In their words:* “The Company has received a letter dated August 6, 2026, from the RBI, conveying that the application has been examined and that the request has not been acceded to.”

**What the documents themselves say about the differences:**

- **operating margin** — parent / remaining: Insurance segment reported a loss of approximately ₹46.8 crore at PBT level for FY26 (segment revenue ₹7,969 crore); Care's combined ratio under Ind AS improved 120 bps to 101.4%; separated business: Financial Services segment reported PBT of ₹152.3 crore for FY26 on segment revenue of about ₹537 crore “The profitability for the insurance segment is at INR41 crores for the last quarter, while it reported a loss of approximately INR46.8 crores at PBT level for FY26. For the Financial Services segment, PBT of INR127.5 crores was reported for the last quarter and INR152.3 crores on the annual basis.”
- **growth** — parent / remaining: Health insurance GWP up 24% YoY to ₹11,417 crore in FY26; retail market share up from 18.8% to 19.7% in SAHI; expected growth "anything between 18% to 24%"; separated business: Broking operating income down 2% to ₹373.4 crore in FY26 with PBT down 31%; RFL core SME book down to about ₹60 crore; RHDFCL AUM down to ₹243 crore from ₹250 crore “Consolidated Revenue grew 14.7% YoY to ₹8,493.84 crore in FY26 led by the health insurance business”
- **debt and leverage** — parent / remaining: REL repaid its ₹75 crore loan and "REL today is debt free"; Care raised sub debt of ₹100 crore in FY26 and runs investment leverage of 4.07x; separated business: RFL is debt-free with no subsisting default, no cumulative ALM mismatches, CRAR 261.9% and NOF ₹821 crore; RHDFCL managed gearing 0.3 times with 130% CRAR “Debt-free; strong liquidity profile with cash balance, including liquid investment of ~₹591 crore as of 31st March 2026”
- **cash** — parent / remaining: Capital raise of ₹1,500 crore via convertible warrants at REL, of which ₹600 crore earmarked for Care (₹256 crore infused in September '25); separated business: RFL holds cash including liquid investments of over ₹591 crore, entirely unlevered; ₹250 crore earmarked for RHDFCL and ₹200 crore for broking “RFL reported a profit of INR89 crores in quarter 4 on account of improved recoveries and has a cash balance including liquid investments of over INR591 crores currently.”
- **return on capital** — parent / remaining: Care: "Return on equity based on profit before tax increased to 19.9% from 17.7% in the previous year"; mid-teens ROE for the fourth consecutive financial year; separated business: Broking ROE in single digits (6%-7%) with no pathway number worked out; RHDFCL PAT and RoMA of Rs. -18.4 crore and -6.7% in FY2026 “So basically, we are having 6%, 7% ROE, right? So I wanted to understand, is there a pathway and how quickly can we go to a normal ROE for a broker, which is in the vicinity of 25%, 30%?”
- **capex and capital intensity** — parent / remaining: ₹600 crore of the ₹1,500 crore warrant proceeds allocated to Care Health Insurance to support solvency and business growth; separated business: ₹250 crore to housing finance, ₹200 crore to broking, ₹375 crore general corporate purpose; RFL needs no capital infusion; IT platforms being refurbished across RFL, RBL and RHDFCL “Out of the INR1,500 crores, INR600 crores is going to Care, INR250 crores is going to the housing finance company, INR200 crores is going to the broking entity. And there's about INR375-odd crores, which is a general corporate purpose fund, which can be allocated depends on the need of these businesses.”
- **tax** — parent / remaining: Scheme framed to comply with Section 2(19AA) of the Income Tax Act; details of accounting method to be certified by the Statutory Auditor per SEBI comments; separated business: Scheme framed to comply with Section 2(19AA) of the Income Tax Act “in compliance with the provisions of the SEBI Scheme Circular – Equity (as defined in the Scheme) and the Income Tax Act (as defined in the Scheme), including Section 2(19AA) thereof.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: REL continues to be barred from declaring dividends as per RBI letter issued in December, 2019; REL retains a single asset (Care) with a stated holding-company discount concern; separated business: RFL's RBI Corrective Action Plan and the banks' fraud classification have been removed; the NBFC business is set to restart operations “Strengthened balance sheet with net worth of ₹898.8 crore and 261.9% CRAR as of 31st March 2026 following RBI's removal of the Corrective Action Plan (CAP) restrictions and withdrawal of fraud classification by banks”

**The checklist:**

| Item | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Why the spin-off | yes | value unlocking for shareholders; unrelated businesses separated; regulatory / strategic knot; attracting different investors / capital; a weak or capital-heavy business carved away — “…broad understanding on that NBFC business, that will be helpful. And in terms of your initial comments on the value unlocking, if you can j ust touch upon whether we will be looking for an IPO for the care health busine” |
| Institutional selling likely (small / different business) | partly | the businesses are described as distinct |
| Insider ownership and incentives aligned | unknown | no promoter-continuity or option-pricing language found *(next: the date the management options are priced; promoter holding in the resulting company)* |
| A hidden value revealed (pro-forma, leverage, comparables) | unknown | no pro-forma or market data on file *(next: pro-forma P&L of each piece × the peer P/E of its own industry)* |
| Parent before the spin (clean parent, takeover prelude) | partly | stage exchange_noc — the spin has not happened; the parent can still be bought whole |
| Timing (first year sells, second year gains) | partly | not yet listed — 294 days since the first filing, stage exchange_noc |
| Management discussing it on the calls | yes | 16 mention(s) in the last 12 months of calls — “…his. If Kedaara is a long term -- as there are some legal issues, which the previous person asked, can we amend -- is it possible legal ly to amend the current demerger in case you are able, for example, to either get A” |

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The separation is the demerger of the Industrial undertaking of SKF India Limited (automotive remaining with SKF India Ltd.) into SKF India (Industrial) Limited, a company incorporated 17 December 2024 purely to receive it, sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 26 September 2025 with appointed/effective date 1 October 2025, a 1:1 share exchange (49,437,963 shares to SKF India holders on the 15 October 2025 record date) and listing on BSE/NSE from 5 December 2025. Management's stated reason is sector focus: the Q3 FY25-26 release frames it as 'SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders,' a 'pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey,' with the industrial entity 'more agile and focused,' able to 'respond faster to market needs' and 'tailor it's manufacturing capabilities' for manufacturing, railways, renewables, cement and heavy engineering. On the 13 May 2026 call the operating logic is spelled out as the ACES strategy to 2028 (accelerate localization, commercial excellence, disciplined execution, one SKF) plus the point that industrial economics differ structurally from automotive — 'industrial business is all about flexibility in the channels... because the lot size, unlike automotive, is smaller' — and that localization lets it re-enter segments it had exited (wind, freight railways, agricultural tractors). Dedicated capacity is the second half of the logic: the Board approved a new Pune factory on 3 February 2026, part of INR 800 crore+ capex to FY29-30 (including INR 350-400 crore of DGBB/TRB channel additions), commissioning end-CY2028, because the business is 'running out of capacity' and currently relies on SKF India job work. The cost of separating was explicit: INR 1,800.8 million of exceptional demerger charges in Q3 FY26 (IT, professional fees, large stamp duty/transfer premium on the land transferred from SKF India), INR 1,961 million for nine months, and a further INR 183 million of demerger IT cost in Q4, which turned reported Q3 PBT to negative INR 671.4 million against INR 1,129.4 million before exceptionals. Management's payoff case is margin recovery to ~13% once demerger costs lapse by end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 and an aspiration of 16-18%, on 8%+ growth; interim performance cited was Q4 FY26 sales INR 9,457.2 million (+9.8% QoQ, +31% YoY), PBT 9.5% reported and 11.5% ex-one-offs, net working capital down 2.8% to 18.7% of sales, then Q1 FY27 revenue INR 9,707.7 million (+18.3% YoY) at 9.0% PBT.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The Scheme of Arrangement between SKF India Limited (Demerged Company) and SKF India (Industrial) Limited (Resulting Company) transferred the Industrial Undertaking on a going-concern basis at carrying values, with the difference credited to Capital Reserve; NCLT order dated 26 September 2025, appointed and effective date 1 October 2025. “The Scheme, among other provisions, entails the demerger of the Demerged Undertaking from the Demerged Company into the Resulting Company on a going concern basis.” — *Scheme*
2. The only explicit statement of purpose in the filings: two sector-focused, independent organizations for sharper market orientation, faster decision-making and shareholder value, after 102 years of SKF in India. “The results come against the backdrop of SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders, marking a pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey.” — *Scheme*
3. MD Mukund Vasudevan's rationale in the 4 February 2026 Q3 FY25-26 release: agility, speed of response and manufacturing tailored to industrial customers, serving manufacturing, railways, renewables, cement and heavy engineering. “As a more agile and focused industrial entity, SKF India (Industrial) is well-positioned to respond faster to market needs, tailor it's manufacturing capabilities, and support India's accelerating infrastructure and manufacturing build-out.” — *Scheme*
4. Separation cost quantified as exceptional items: INR 1,800.8 million in Q3 FY26 and INR 1,961 million for nine months for IT cost, professional services and stamp duty including transfer premium on land acquired under the Scheme — which pushed reported Q3 PBT to negative INR 671.4 million versus INR 1,129.4 million before exceptionals. “During the quarter and nine months ended 31 December 2025, the Company accounted certain demerger expenses for IT Cost, professional services and stamp duty, including estimated transfer premium payable to statutory authorities to effect transfer of registration of land acquired under the Scheme, aggregating to Rs. 1,800.8 million and Rs. 1,961 million, respectively, which have been included under "Exceptional items".” — *Scheme*
5. The Board meeting of 3 February 2026 — the same meeting that approved the first post-demerger results — approved a new standalone factory at Pune, the capacity leg of the separation. “We wish to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today, i.e. on February 03, 2026, has approved the setting up of a new factory /plant at Pune, Maharashtra.” — *Scheme*
6. Management re-stated the ACES strategy (accelerate localization, commercial excellence, disciplined execution, one SKF, defined through 2028) explicitly because the company is now separately listed and needs its own growth and profitability narrative. “I thought it's important to reiterate our strategy as we are now a separate listed entity as SKF India (Industrial) and I think it helps to kind of say what are we trying to do and how are we trying to grow and make our business more profitable.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1289a753-236a-4201-9367-4432f4270674.pdf)*
7. The structural case for separate industrial management: industrial runs on small lot sizes and channel flexibility unlike automotive — the Pune TRB example raised capacity from 600,000 to 886,000 pieces, cut cost ~18% and improved changeover/flexibility 20% and new-product lead time 35%. “Flexibility, which is key, which is industrial business is all about flexibility in the channels, which means we can switch between one product and another because the lot size, unlike automotive, is smaller.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1289a753-236a-4201-9367-4432f4270674.pdf)*
8. A concrete problem the focused, localized entity solves: segments previously abandoned on cost/margin grounds — wind, freight railways, agricultural tractors — are being re-entered via localization, including a 32.5 crore tractor OEM win and ZF/Suzlon wind orders that drove 91% QoQ wind growth. “The reason you are right, we did exit wind business . Because of localization we are now getting back into it.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1289a753-236a-4201-9367-4432f4270674.pdf)*
9. Residual entanglement with the automotive entity persists: SKF India (Industrial) manufactures for SKF India Automotive (~4% of FY26 sales), pays royalty/trademark (up ~INR 60 million QoQ) and a transfer-pricing margin on services, and SKF India job-works for it until the new plant starts. “We are , till that new plant comes up , comes about, we are continuing to do some our SKF India entity is continuing to manufacture some for us on a job work basis.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1289a753-236a-4201-9367-4432f4270674.pdf)*
10. The one-off separation charges continued into Q4 FY26 at INR 183 million, so reported PBT of 9.5% was 11.5% adjusted (versus 13.1% adjusted in Q3), with the remaining gap blamed on OEM mix (OEM up from 46% to 50%) and full bonus accrual. “In this quarter, we again had demerger -related IT costs, primarily that, totalling up to INR 183 million.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1289a753-236a-4201-9367-4432f4270674.pdf)*
11. Margin roadmap post-separation: back to ~13% once demerger costs end around end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 through localization, operational efficiency and S&A leverage, with 16-18% only an aspiration held back by OEM mix, competition and depreciation from the new plant. “So given the recent demerger expenses, right, by we would say towards the end of this calendar year, we see that mostly normalizing. We should get back to a little more around 13%.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1289a753-236a-4201-9367-4432f4270674.pdf)*
12. Standalone capital plan: INR 800 crore+ capex FY26-27 to FY29-30, a large part for the new Pune plant plus DGBB and TRB channel additions (the INR 350-400 crore earlier flagged), operational mid-2028 and fully ramped by end-CY2028, with growth of ~8% in the interim. “So, on capex, the overall plan for the between FY 26, FY27 to FY 29, FY30, we are looking at doing a capex spend of around INR 800 crores plus, which includes a significant chunk of investment on the new Pune plant which we are in the process of setting up.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1289a753-236a-4201-9367-4432f4270674.pdf)*
13. Q1 FY27 (12 August 2026) validates the focused-entity framing: revenue INR 9,707.7 million, up 18.3% YoY, PBT INR 869.2 million at 9.0%, with growth in Wind, General Machinery and Agriculture (Tractors) despite currency and residual demerger costs. “In our 3rd quarter as a focused, independent business, SKF India (Industrial) delivered 18.3% year-on-year Sales growth, while maintaining a healthy 9% PBT (in spite of headwinds from currency and demerger-related expenses).” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** These texts contain no pre-demerger call, so the origin of the idea is not on record here; the earliest document is the Scheme itself (NCLT order 26 September 2025, effective 1 October 2025, listing 5 December 2025). The 4 February 2026 press release, reporting the first post-demerger quarter, carries the only explicit rationale statement (two sector-focused independent organizations, sharper orientation, faster decisions, shareholder value) alongside INR 1,800.8 million of separation costs, and the same Board meeting on 3 February 2026 approved the new Pune factory — converting the rationale into standalone capacity. By the 13 May 2026 Q4/FY26 call the framing had shifted from justification to execution: the ACES strategy 'as we are now a separate listed entity,' INR 800 crore+ capex, re-entry into previously exited wind/railway/tractor business, and a margin path of 13% near term to 15% by FY29-30. The 12 August 2026 Q1 FY27 release continues the 'focused, independent business' framing with 18.3% YoY growth at 9% PBT.

**What management expects from it:** For SKF India (Industrial): sharper market orientation, faster decisions, agility and manufacturing tailored to industrial lot sizes; ~8% growth with PBT recovering to ~13% by end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 (16-18% aspiration); net working capital 19-20% of sales; INR 800 crore+ own capex and a new Pune plant replacing SKF India job work; shareholder value via two independent listed entities.

*Not explained on the calls:* No pre-demerger call rationale; no named requester (investors, lenders, partners); no synergy loss, standalone-cost, tax or valuation quantification; nothing on the automotive entity's economics or arm's-length agreement terms.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders; a more agile, focused industrial entity responding faster to market needs
- *What it reveals:* A clean, growing standalone bearings business: Q1 FY27 revenue +18.3% to Rs 9,707.7mn, underlying PBT 11.5–13.6% once Rs 1,961mn demerger costs are excluded, negligible finance cost, net assets credited to Capital Reserve; management guides ~13% near-term and 15% by FY29-30
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *Read next:* The Scheme of Arrangement's definition of the Demerged Undertaking, and SKF India Limited's post-demerger (automotive) standalone numbers
- *In their words:* “The results come against the backdrop of SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders, marking a pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The business being separated is not a pharma business at all: it is the Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business that grew up inside Arco Lab Private Limited, Strides' wholly-owned Global Capability Centre, covering life-sciences consulting, digital transformation, quality and compliance, drug safety and technology-enabled operational services delivered by 400+ subject-matter experts. Management's account is that this began as a captive serving Strides — its FY26 revenue of ₹1,447 million explicitly 'including revenues for services rendered to Strides', with EBITDA of ₹169 million, 3% of Strides' turnover and ~1% of consolidated net worth — but that 'as demand from external pharmaceutical and life sciences companies grew, the business evolved into an independent platform serving industry-leading customers', which it could not remain inside a generics manufacturer's subsidiary. The filings name four specific problems the carve-out solves: supporting the next phase of growth, serving global customers effectively, building agentic-AI platforms, and enabling access to external capital — so the vehicle was created first (Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232, appointed date April 10, 2025, NCLT Bengaluru approval May 18, 2026, effective June 1, 2026, making Pivot Path a direct wholly-owned subsidiary of Strides) and only then sold down. The sale values Pivot Path at ~₹2,300m post-money: Strides divests a majority for ~₹1,000m (₹750m at initial closing, ₹250m on the first anniversary), Ascent Growth Trust and co-investor Vintage Classic Limited take 65.05%, a 15% ESOP pool is carved for the team, Ascent infuses ₹500m of primary capital, Strides keeps 19.95% and reclassifies Pivot Path as an Associate. Strides frames this as a repeatable playbook rather than a distress exit — 'creating, scaling and unlocking value from high-potential businesses while retaining participation in their future growth' — and says it 'strengthens the Company's balance sheet and provides growth capital for Pivot Path', consistent with the three FY26 priorities Badree repeated on the calls (geographic diversification, profitability, balance sheet strength, with net debt at ₹1,437 crores and net debt/EBITDA 1.55x). The stated precedent is the Softgel/OneSource demerger, which Arun Kumar justified in exactly valuation terms — the softgel business was 'adjusting within the generic space at a suboptimal valuation' until its 'true value' was discovered through OneSource, with ₹78.8 billion distributed to shareholders. No investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for the Pivot Path separation; pricing rests on an independent valuation by a SEBI-registered merchant banker, and the deal is stated not to be a related-party transaction.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The separated unit is Arco Lab's Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business, demerged into Pivot Path Private Limited under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013; on effectiveness Pivot Path became a direct wholly-owned subsidiary of Strides, with the undertaking vesting from the appointed date of April 10, 2025. “The Scheme provides for the demerger of Arco Lab’s Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business (the “Demerged Undertaking”) into Pivot Path, pursuant to Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013 and other applicable provisions of the Act and the Rules framed thereunder (“Scheme”).” — *Scheme*
2. The stated reason for the carve-out is four-fold and explicit: next-phase growth, serving global customers, building agentic-AI platforms, and access to external capital — i.e. things the business could not do while embedded in Strides' Global Capability Centre. “To support its next phase of growth, serve global customers effectively, build agentic-AI platforms, and enable access to external capital, the business was carved out into Pivot Path pursuant to a Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) in May 2026.” — *Scheme*
3. The origin story management gives: a captive capability centre function (life sciences consulting, digital transformation, quality and compliance, technology-enabled operational services) that outgrew its captive role as third-party pharma demand arrived. “As demand from external pharmaceutical and life sciences companies grew, the business evolved into an independent platform serving industry-leading customers.” — *Scheme*
4. Size and profitability disclosed for the carved-out business for FY26 — and the admission that its revenue still includes intra-group work for Strides, which is why standalone turnover contribution is shown as Nil and consolidated contribution as only 3% of Strides' turnover and 1% of net worth. “For FY26, the carved-out business reported revenue of ₹1,447 million (including revenues for services rendered to Strides) and EBITDA of ₹169 million, demonstrating its operating scale and growth trajectory.” — *Scheme*
5. The deal terms: ~₹2,300m post-money valuation, ~₹1,000m to Strides (₹750m at initial closing, ₹250m on the first anniversary), ₹500m primary into the company, and a resultant cap table of Strides 19.95% / investors 65.05% / ESOP pool 15%, with Pivot Path becoming an Associate. “The transaction values Pivot Path at ~₹2,300m on a post-money basis, enables Strides to realise ~₹1,000m while retaining a ~20% stake, and includes a primary capital infusion of ₹500 million to accelerate Pivot Path's next phase of growth.” — *Scheme*
6. The corporate-strategy framing: a repeatable incubate-scale-monetise model in which Strides keeps a minority economic interest, with balance-sheet strengthening named as a direct benefit to the parent. “The transaction reflects Strides' strategy of creating, scaling and unlocking value from high-potential businesses while retaining participation in their future growth.” — *Scheme*
7. Badree's stated timing logic: the business needs a partner with capital and expertise that Strides itself does not bring, and the separation is what lets Pivot Path scale independently while Strides still participates. “As the business enters its next phase, we believe this is the right time to bring in a strategic investment partner with the expertise and capital to accelerate its growth.” — *Scheme*
8. The buyer's rationale is that independence itself is the enabler — combining technology and agentic AI with 400+ subject-matter experts for compliance, digital transformation and drug safety work for global customers. “As an Independent entity, Pivot Path is exceptionally well positioned to combine the power of technology and Agentic-AI with its 400+ subject matter experts in building purpose-built solutions that enable global customers to manage their compliance, digital transformation, and drug safety requirements with greater speed, precision, cost effectiveness and confidence.” — *Scheme*
9. Governance framing: pricing rests on an independent SEBI-registered merchant banker valuation, the buyers (Ascent Growth Trust and BVI-incorporated Vintage Classic Limited) are not promoter/promoter-group/group companies, and the transaction is declared not a related-party transaction and outside Regulation 37A. “The transaction has been undertaken based on an independent valuation conducted by a SEBI-registered merchant banker, reflecting the strength of Pivot Path's differentiated capabilities, established customer relationships and long-term growth potential.” — *Scheme*
10. The template for this separation — never applied to Pivot Path on any call, but stated for the Softgel/OneSource demerger: a niche business trapped inside the generics platform was being valued suboptimally, so carving it out revealed its true value. “And discussing its true value, while it was adjusting within the generic space at a suboptimal valuation, we discovered its true value of a niche business through OneSource.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=eb0f8605-df29-4b18-89a6-1981d2e97582.pdf)*
11. Management quantifies the prior unlock as the proof of its shareholder-value method — ₹78.8 billion distributed via demerger and listing — framing further separations as shareholder-value actions rather than disposals. “And the recent one being we distributed INR 78.8 billion back to shareholders in the form of demerger and listing.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=18a7ad25-fba0-4c37-a54f-e50372724d01.pdf)*
12. The only call reference to Arco Lab, the entity Pivot Path was carved out of: it is described merely as the wholly-owned subsidiary holding the retained OneSource stake, with no hint that a services business inside it was being prepared for separation. “So we retained this in Arco Lab, which is a wholly owned subsidiary of Strides.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=16b39100-202b-45a3-89a5-d7161626f0d6.pdf)*
13. On the Q4 FY26 call held the same day NCLT approved the Scheme, management restated the three priorities the Pivot Path monetisation serves (diversification, profitability, balance sheet strength — net debt ₹1,437 crores, 1.55x) but said nothing about the demerger or any intent to sell the business. “Over the last 3 years, we have been very clear on our priorities, geographical diversification, profitability and balance sheet strength.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=7147ef9f-bea3-419e-a8cf-c18af047bfce.pdf)*
14. Sequencing confirms a two-step design: the Scheme was made effective on June 1, 2026 after the certified NCLT order was filed with the RoC, and the stake sale was approved just 26 days later on June 27, 2026. “Further, pursuant to filing of the certified true copy of the Order with the Registrar of Companies by the participating entities, namely Arco Lab and Pivot Path, the Scheme of Demerger has become effective from June 1, 2026.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** On none of the eight calls (Oct 2024 through May 2026) did management ever mention Pivot Path, Arco Lab's Life Sciences/Digital Innovation business or this Scheme; the only separation discussed was the Softgel-to-OneSource demerger (Oct 2024, Feb 2025, Aug 2025 calls), which established the 'unlock true value outside the generic space' template, and Arco Lab appeared only once, in May 2025, as the wholly-owned subsidiary parked with the retained 1.6% OneSource stake 'for a rainy day'. The Pivot Path track runs entirely through filings: the Scheme was intimated on May 15, 2025 with an appointed date of April 10, 2025, NCLT Bengaluru approved it on May 18, 2026 (the very day of the Q4 FY26 earnings call, which made no reference to it), the order reached the portal May 20 and the certified copy May 25, and the Scheme became effective June 1, 2026. Twenty-six days later, on June 27, 2026, the Board approved the majority-stake sale to the Ascent Capital consortium plus ₹500m primary infusion, with definitive agreements to be executed before June 30 and the share sale to complete by June 30, 2026 and the infusion by July 31, 2026. So the plan visibly changed shape only once: from an internal reorganisation creating a wholly-owned subsidiary into a control sale leaving Strides a 19.95% associate holder.

**What management expects from it:** Pivot Path: ₹500m primary capital, independence to serve global customers, build agentic-AI platforms, scale with a 15% ESOP pool for 400+ experts, and access external capital. Strides: ~₹1,000m cash (₹750m now, ₹250m deferred), a strengthened balance sheet, Associate accounting, continued ~19.95% participation in the upside, and sharper focus on its pharma core.

*Not explained on the calls:* Calls never mentioned Pivot Path, Arco Lab's carve-out or the Scheme; no stated investor, lender or partner request; no margin, valuation-gap or post-deal related-party pricing explanation.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* "To support its next phase of growth, serve global customers effectively, build agentic-AI platforms, and enable access to external capital"; strategy of creating, scaling and unlocking value from high-potential businesses
- *What it reveals:* A profitable services platform hidden inside the GCC: FY26 revenue ₹1,447m, EBITDA ₹169m, only 3% of Strides turnover and 1% of networth, yet valued ~₹2,300m post-money, realising ~₹1,000m cash.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* Definitive agreements and Q1FY27 results: gain on ~₹1,000m sale, ₹250m deferred receivable, Associate reclassification
- *In their words:* “Upon completion of the transaction, Pivot Path shall be reclassified as an Associate Company.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

Management presents the separation as a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232, sanctioned by the NCLT Mumbai Bench amongst Tata Motors Limited (the demerged company, now Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited), TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (the resulting company) and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (amalgamated into the demerged entity), effective 1 October 2025; the resulting company was renamed Tata Motors Limited on 29 October 2025 and its shares listed on BSE/NSE (ticker TMCV) on 12 November 2025, with outstanding PSUs replaced one-for-one under a new scheme covering up to 23,07,647 shares (0.062% dilution). The stated problem the split solves is a reporting and identity one: 'Historically, we reported a CV segment. It was an internal construct that carved out CV operations from within the erstwhile combined entity. That was a practical necessity then' — from Q4 FY26 the company reports standalone financials including the Tata Cummins joint operation as its primary lens, giving 'a cleaner, more complete, and more directly comparable picture'. The separation cost ₹960 crore of one-time demerger expense booked in Q3 FY26 (part of ₹1,500 crore standalone / ₹1,600 crore consolidated exceptionals, alongside ₹603 crore of new labour code and ₹82 crore of Iveco acquisition cost). The pure-play case is argued with numbers: FY26 revenue ₹77,000 crore (vs ₹66,000 crore FY23), EBITDA margin up from 7.8% (FY23) to 13.2% (FY26) — ~550bps of 'structural improvement' — EBITDA doubled from ₹5,100 crore to ₹10,200 crore, PBT before exceptionals ₹8,700 crore, first-ever double-digit EBIT at 11% (the CV segment first crossed it at 10.6% in Q3 FY26), FCF ₹9,200 crore or 12% of revenue, Auto ROCE 72%, cash conversion cycle of negative 31 days, net cash ₹7,500 crore standalone and ₹13,700 crore consolidated, and a maiden final dividend of ₹4/share (~₹1,500 crore outflow). Cyclicality is the second problem: non-cyclical revenue (parts & service, Fleet Edge digital subscriptions, Smart City e-bus operations) is compounding at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR, 'deliberately building this mix', and Q4 working-capital sinks historically concentrated in Q4 have been spread through the year. Third, the standalone CV entity became the acquisition vehicle: its own balance sheet and a committed EUR 3.825 billion bridge from Morgan Stanley and MUFG funded an all-cash voluntary totalitarian tender offer for Iveco Group N.V. at EUR 14.10 (raised to EUR 14.40), valuing Iveco at ~EUR 3.82 billion, creating ~EUR 21 billion (INR 2,28,000 crore+) of combined revenue and ~590k units with Europe ~46%/India ~32%/South America ~8%/RoW ~14% and 'substantially no overlap' — expected to 'drive better operating leverage by spreading its capital investments over larger volumes, generating operating efficiencies and reducing the cash flow volatility inherent in the commercial vehicles sector', plus enhancing Iveco's FPT powertrain business. Structural simplification continues inside the CV entity: TMF Holdings Limited and TMF Business Services Limited (wholly owned subsidiaries) are being amalgamated into it, and Tata Motor Finance had already been folded into Tata Capital (whose October 2025 IPO priced 20–25% below the merger valuation, forcing a ₹2,000 crore mark-to-market loss in Q2 FY26 and a ₹295 crore write-back in Q3).

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. First call of the separated entity: management confirmed the demerger took effect 1 October 2025 and that the CV business was listed as Tata Motors Limited under ticker TMCV on both exchanges, describing it as a commitment delivered. “We successfully completed the demerger with Effective date of 1st October.” — *CALL Nov 2025*
2. Comparatives had to be derived because the resulting company only came into existence in June 2024 — a direct consequence of the scheme structure. “the prior period financials in this presentation, they reflect the impact of the demerger as it has just been effective since the Company’s incorporation that happened in June 2024.” — *CALL Nov 2025*
3. The newly separated CV entity immediately tied up its own acquisition financing for Iveco through a bridge loan, with refinancing options (equity or debt) left open. “On the Iveco acquisition, the regulatory approvals are underway and the initial funding through bridge loan has been secured.” — *CALL Nov 2025*
4. The separation carried an explicit one-time cost of ₹960 crore, booked as an exceptional item in Q3 FY26 within ₹1,500 crore of standalone exceptionals (with ₹603 crore labour code and ₹82 crore Iveco acquisition cost). “Demerger cost has been around ₹960 crore.” — *CALL Feb 2026*
5. Management flagged the demerger and labour-code charges as non-recurring, separating transaction cost from underlying performance. “And both these are going to be one-time for us. We don't expect this on a recurring basis.” — *CALL Feb 2026*
6. The CV business crossed a double-digit EBIT margin for the first time as a standalone reporting unit — the profitability milestone used to validate the standalone case. “The CV segment also achieved the milestone of a double-digit EBIT margin for the first time, which now stands at 10.6%.” — *CALL Feb 2026*
7. The clearest statement of what the separation achieved: a pure-play commercial vehicle company, which management calls a defining shift that changes how the business should be presented. “Demerger being effective from 1st of October 2025, Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company, and this is a defining shift that changes how we think is most appropriate to present our financials.” — *CALL May 2026*
8. The problem the split solves, as stated: the CV business was previously visible only as an internal carve-out construct inside the combined entity. “Historically, we reported a CV segment. It was an internal construct that carved out CV operations from within the erstwhile combined entity. That was a practical necessity then.” — *CALL May 2026*
9. Post-demerger reporting switched to standalone financials including the Tata Cummins joint operation as the primary lens, for transparency and comparability. “This gives you a cleaner, more complete, and more directly comparable picture of the business going forward.” — *CALL May 2026*
10. The margin record cited as structural rather than cyclical: 7.8% to 13.2% EBITDA over three years, with EBITDA doubling from ₹5,100 crore to ₹10,200 crore and FY26 EBIT at 11%. “EBITDA margins have expanded from 7.8% in FY23 to 13.2% in FY26. That's nearly 550 bps of structural improvement over three years.” — *CALL May 2026*
11. Capital-efficiency case for the standalone entity: ₹9,200 crore FCF (12% of revenue), ₹2,800 crore reinvested, Auto ROCE of 72%, negative 31-day cash conversion cycle, net cash ₹7,500 crore standalone and ₹13,700 crore consolidated. “Finally, the Auto ROCE stands at 72% is an industry-leading number, when EBIT doubles, capital discipline holds, returns follow.” — *CALL May 2026*
12. Deliberate de-cyclicalisation of the standalone business via parts & service, Fleet Edge digital and Smart City e-buses, growing far faster than the cyclical truck business. “Over the period, non-cyclical CAGR is running at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR. We've been deliberately building this mix, and this is now showing up meaningfully in the numbers.” — *CALL May 2026*
13. Mechanics of the separation as disclosed in every filing: NCLT Mumbai-sanctioned Composite Scheme of Arrangement amongst Tata Motors Limited, TML Commercial Vehicles Limited and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited, with the resulting company renamed and listed. “As per the Composite Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by the Hon’ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench—amongst Tata Motors Limited, TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (the Company) and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited—the Company’s name was changed to Tata Motors Limited from TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (effective 29 October 2025), and its equity shares are listed on the BSE Ltd and the NSE Ltd.” — *Scheme*
14. Employee incentives were carried across the split one-for-one: outstanding PSUs of the demerged company entitle holders to a matching PSU from the CV entity, implemented via a new scheme for up to 23,07,647 shares (0.062% dilution). “the unexercised performance share units (“PSUs”) (whether vested or unvested) granted to participants under the Demerged Company’s Incentive Scheme(s) and remaining outstanding as on the record date shall entitle such participants to receive one (1) corresponding PSU to be granted by the Resulting Company under a new incentive scheme.” — *Scheme*
15. The separated CV entity's strategic use of its independence — the Iveco combination is justified on scale, no overlap, operating leverage and dampening CV cash-flow volatility; ~EUR 21 billion combined revenue, ~590k units, Europe 46%/India 32%. “The new company will be able to drive better operating leverage by spreading its capital investments over larger volumes, generating operating efficiencies and reducing the cash flow volatility inherent in the commercial vehicles sector.” — *Scheme*
16. Iveco was pursued as an all-cash EUR 14.10 (later EUR 14.40) offer valuing Iveco at ~EUR 3.82 billion, funded by a committed EUR 3.825 billion bridge from Morgan Stanley and MUFG, with Exor (27.06% of shares, 43.19% of votes) irrevocably committed. “TML CV HS signed a debt commitment letter with Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A., Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc. and MUFG Bank, Ltd. for fully committed bridge financing to be used in connection with the Transaction, which was subsequently implemented through a facility agreement entered into by the Offeror for an aggregate amount of up to EUR 3,825,000,000.00.” — *Scheme*
17. Structural simplification continued after the demerger: the CV entity is absorbing its own wholly owned financing subsidiaries TMF Holdings and TMF Business Services under a further NCLT scheme. “The Scheme provides for the merger of Amalgamating Company 1 and Amalgamating Company 2 (being direct and indirect wholly owned subsidiaries of the Company respectively) with the Company.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** In the Nov 2025 call (Q2 FY26, 13 November 2025) management reported the split as done rather than argued for it — demerger effective 1 October, CV listing completed as TMCV 'as committed previously', Iveco approvals underway and the bridge loan secured. In the Feb 2026 call (Q3 FY26, 29 January 2026) the cost showed up as a ₹960 crore one-time demerger exceptional while the CV segment hit a double-digit EBIT margin (10.6%) for the first time and Iveco approvals were guided to end-March. In the May 2026 call (Q4 FY26, 13 May 2026) the framing shifted decisively: 'Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company... a defining shift', the old carved-out CV segment was retired in favour of standalone reporting, three-year pure-play metrics were laid out, and Iveco closure slipped to Q2 FY27 pending French and Spanish financial-regulator approvals. Filings then show execution: offer launched 4 September 2026, 89.42% tendered by 27 October 2026, 96.29% after the reopening on 6 November 2026, triggering the Dutch legal squeeze-out, alongside the TMF Holdings/TMF Business Services amalgamation notices.

**What management expects from it:** Pure-play CV: cleaner, comparable standalone reporting including Tata Cummins joint operations; teens (not mid-teens) EBITDA guidance, double-digit EBIT, capex 2–4% of revenue, FCF ~12% of revenue, 72% ROCE, net cash ₹7,500cr standalone/₹13,700cr consolidated funding a ₹4 dividend and the Iveco bid; with Iveco, ~EUR21bn revenue, operating leverage over larger volumes, less cash-flow volatility. No PV-entity commentary.

*Not explained on the calls:* Why separate at all — no pre-demerger call is in the record: no stated valuation-unlock, synergy or capital-allocation rationale, no investor, lender or partner named as requesting it, no entitlement ratio.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* A high-quality pure-play CV business: FY26 revenue ~Rs. 77,000 crores, EBITDA margin 13.2% (vs 7.8% in FY23), first double-digit EBIT at 11%, FCF Rs. 9,200 crores (12% of revenue), Auto ROCE 72%, net cash Rs. 7,500 crores standalone.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *Read next:* Q1 FY27 results: commodity pass-through after the April 2% price increase, and the Iveco bridge-loan refinancing equity/debt mix.
- *In their words:* “Demerger being effective from 1st of October 2025, Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company, and this is a defining shift that changes how we think is most appropriate to present our financials.”
