The Board also approved acquiring 100% of STPL Trading and Services Private Limited (18,89,47,551 equity shares) for Rs. 530.08 Cr in cash: "The shares are acquired  from various stakeholders  who are related parties." and "The transfer of shares will be done at “arms -length” based on a valuation report." No promoter or management buying, selling or pledging of TVS Motor shares is stated.
- **Insiders, per the checklist read:** Shareholding mirrors parent 1:1; promoters hold 50.27% (23,88,12,786 shares) post-Scheme, public 49.71%. Chairman Sudarshan Venu; TVS Motor's own shares in Resulting Company cancelled · *option pricing date:* 28th October 2026 — valuation report of M/s. Bansi S. Mehta Valuers LLP fixing the 1:1 share entitlement ratio (record date only 'as defined in the Scheme', not stated)

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

TVS Motor is carving its consumer finance and related business undertaking — the lending, investment, leasing and ancillary/support activities it runs directly and through subsidiaries, principally the NBFC TVS Credit Services — out of the listed automotive company into Harita ARC Limited, a shell wholly-owned subsidiary bought from TVS Credit Services for Rs 25,000 on 28th October 2026, with TVS Motor shareholders getting 1 share of the resulting company for every 1 TVS Motor share (47,50,87,114 shares, valuation by Bansi S. Mehta Valuers LLP, fairness opinion by JM Financial), and the resulting company to be listed; the same Composite Scheme also amalgamates the dormant wholly-owned TVS Motor Services Limited (total assets Rs 251.44 Cr, net worth Rs 198.93 Cr, nil turnover) into TVS Motor 'to streamline the group corporate structure', after which it is dissolved without winding up. Management's stated problem is that finance has outgrown its host: the demerged undertaking already turned over Rs 3,921 Cr of TVS Motor's Rs 35,770 Cr consolidated revenue in H1 FY27, and the Financial segment carries Rs 43,003 Cr of assets and Rs 33,288 Cr of liabilities against Automotive's Rs 23,868 Cr, which is why consolidated net debt/equity sits at 2.90x versus 0.37x standalone. The Scheme says the consumer finance business 'needs a separate strategy suited to its industry-specific risks, market dynamics and growth path', that 'the nature of, and competition in, the consumer finance and related business differ from those of the other businesses', and — the capital-structure crux — that 'a financial services company can have a higher leverage (as compared to the Demerged Company) for its growth'. The second stated problem is investor mismatch: a standalone entity 'can attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders having a specific interest in the consumer finance and related business', and the demerger will 'unlock the value of the Demerged Undertaking for the shareholders of the Demerged Company'. Chairman Sudarshan Venu framed it as 15 years of sustained investment reaching scale — TVS Credit plus Home Credit India serving 'more than 45 million customers across 100,000 touchpoints', plus the Varthana education-finance acquisition and the Jana Small Finance Bank stake — so the platform should now allocate capital to its own priorities while TVS Motor 'remain[s] focused on strengthening its leadership in mobility globally'. It follows the August 2026 step in which the group's NBFCs approved merging STPL Trading and Services into Home Credit India Finance (155.79 shares per 200) and then Home Credit India Finance and TVS Housing Finance into TVS Credit Services (9.94 per 180), expressly for 'consolidating the NBFCs within the group in terms of RBI directions'; alongside the demerger the board also bought STPL outright for Rs 530.08 Cr to pick up ~2.4% more of TVS Credit post-merger. No lender, partner or named investor is cited as having asked for the split.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The 28 Oct 2026 Composite Scheme demerges the consumer finance and related business undertaking from TVS Motor into Harita ARC Limited and simultaneously amalgamates wholly-owned TVS Motor Services Limited into TVS Motor. “The Scheme, inter alia, provides for: (i) the amalgamation of the Transferor Company with the Company; and (ii) the demerger of the Demerged Undertaking (as defined in the Scheme) from the Company into the Resulting Company on a going concern basis, in consideration for which the Resulting Company shall issue its shares to the shareholders of the Company in proportion to their shareholding in the Company.” — *Scheme*
2. Stated rationale #1: structural simplification into two independent standalone platforms, each with its own strategy and capital plan. “The demerger will simplify the group structure and create focused businesses, with a clear segregation of the Demerged Undertaking and the Remaining Business.” — *Scheme*
3. Stated rationale #2: the lending business has risk, competitive and growth characteristics unlike the vehicle business, so it needs its own strategy. “The consumer finance and related business needs a separate strategy suited to its industry-specific risks, market dynamics and growth path;” — *Scheme*
4. The capital-structure crux — an NBFC can run far more balance-sheet leverage than a manufacturer; consolidated net debt/equity was 2.90x at 30 Sep 2026 against 0.37x standalone. “a financial services company can have a higher leverage (as compared to the Demerged Company) for its growth .” — *Scheme*
5. Investor/lender mismatch is named explicitly: a pure-play finance entity can draw capital providers who want finance exposure, and this unlocks value for existing holders. “the independent company can attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders having a specific interest in the consumer finance and related business .” — *Scheme*
6. Size of the carve-out: the demerged undertaking produced Rs 3,921 Cr of revenue in the period ended 30 Sep 2026 against TVS Motor's Rs 35,770 Cr consolidated turnover; shareholders get 1:1 shares and the new entity will be listed. “The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the period ended 30th September 2026 was Rs. 3,921 Crore out of the total turnover of Rs. 35,770 Crore of the Company .” — *Scheme*
7. Press release frames the trigger as scale reached after 15 years of investment — TVS Credit plus Home Credit India at 45 million customers and 100,000 touchpoints, plus Varthana and Jana Small Finance Bank — needing a dedicated structure for capital allocation. “The consumer finance and related business have expanded in scale and scope and a dedicated st ructure will provide greater strategic focus, flexibility in capital allocation and the ability to pursue opportunities across the consumer finance and related sector s.” — *Scheme*
8. Chairman Sudarshan Venu's framing: full value realisation for the finance platform while TVS Motor concentrates on global mobility leadership, with shareholders participating in both. “It positions them to realise the full potential of their assets and capabilities while enabling TVS Motor Company to remain focused on strengthening its leadership in mobility globally .” — *Scheme*
9. The precursor step (5 Aug 2026): STPL merges into Home Credit India Finance, then Home Credit India Finance and TVS Housing Finance merge into TVS Credit Services — partly driven by regulator-led NBFC consolidation; TVS Motor separately paid Rs 530.08 Cr for STPL to gain ~2.4% more of TVS Credit. “consolidating the NBFCs within the group in terms of RBI directions.” — *Scheme*
10. The only investor-side prod in three years of calls: an analyst asked about earlier plans to monetise or IPO TVS Credit Services, and the CFO said the board had not taken it up — no mention of a demerger. “And as far as the question is all about IPO, not yet even discussed at the Board level.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=fd52c6c1-59d2-406d-9bf3-2381f22aa01d.pdf)*
11. Scale of the business being separated, as management last described it on a call: book up 19% to Rs 32,053 Cr, PBT Rs 283 Cr for the quarter, ~2.6 crore customers, ~62,000 touchpoints. “The book size of TVS Credit grew by 19%. Now it is at INR 32,053 crores as against INR 26,898 crores last year.” — *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e99280ca-79c3-4fa1-8188-f0f34294abfa.pdf)*
12. FY26 record finance earnings quantified on the call — the profit stream now leaving the listed automotive entity. “PBT has grown by 22%, INR 1,248 crores as against INR 1,027 crores during last year.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d60c3c01-cbb0-4df1-9cba-9e23ccc6fc27.pdf)*
13. TVS Motor was repeatedly injecting equity into the finance arm while it sat inside the parent — Rs 200 Cr in Q3 FY26, and Rs 711 Cr in Q2 FY27 per the quarterly filing — the capital drain the separate structure is meant to re-route. “Now coming back to the second question on INR 900 crores, the delta this quarter has been TVS Credit Services, we have invested about INR200 crores.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=53c3b829-4568-4cca-a559-e584d7253eed.pdf)*

**How it evolved:** Strikingly, the separation is absent from all seven earnings calls in the window (Jan 2025 through Jul 2026): management discussed TVS Credit only as a performance line — book Rs 26,647 Cr and PBT Rs 1,027 Cr in FY25 (28 Apr 2025 call), Rs 30,631 Cr and Rs 1,248 Cr in FY26 (13 May 2026), Rs 32,053 Cr and 2.6 crore customers in Q1 FY27 (21 Jul 2026) — while repeatedly describing fresh equity infusions into it (Rs 200 Cr in Q3 FY26 per the 28 Jan 2026 call, Rs 200 Cr across FY26, Rs 711 Cr in Q2 FY27 per the filing). The only hint of structural intent came from an analyst on the 31 Jul 2025 call asking about monetising or IPO-ing TVS Credit, which CFO Gopala Desikan shut down as 'not yet even discussed at the Board level'. The plan then surfaces entirely in filings: the 5 Aug 2026 NBFC-consolidation scheme (STPL → Home Credit India Finance → TVS Credit Services, citing RBI directions), then the 28 Oct 2026 board approval of the Composite Scheme of Arrangement that demerges the undertaking into Harita ARC Limited 1:1 and folds TVS Motor Services into TVS Motor, with the press release calling the demerger 'the next step in this strategic process'.

**What management expects from it:** For the finance platform: strategic autonomy, sharper capital allocation, freedom to run higher NBFC-style leverage, a dedicated investor/lender/partner base, and value unlocked via a 1:1 listed entity. For TVS Motor: a simplified group structure, operational synergies from absorbing TVS Motor Services, and undiluted focus on automotive/mobility leadership globally. Shareholders participate in both.

*Not explained on the calls:* No call ever discusses the demerger; no margin, ROE, capital-release, cost, tax, debt-allocation or timeline numbers for either entity; no promoter-control or future-stake-sale intent disclosed.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Simplify group structure and create focused standalone platforms; consumer finance needs separate strategy, unlocks value, attracts different investors, and allows higher leverage than the auto company
- *What it reveals:* Financial segment carries Rs 43,003 Cr of the Rs 66,871 Cr consolidated assets vs automotive Rs 23,868 Cr, H1 segment PBT Rs 782 Cr on Rs 3,921 Cr turnover; separation reveals a leveraged NBFC platform (45 million customers) that can gear up independently of the auto balance sheet
- *Parent or spin:* both · *Read next:* The Scheme itself on www.tvsmotor.com — Demerged Undertaking's assets/liabilities, record date, and TVS Credit/Home Credit merger terms
- *In their words:* “The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the period ended 30th September 2026 was Rs. 3,921  Crore out of the total turnover of Rs. 35,770 Crore of the Company .”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

Management presented the separation as a focus-and-investor-base argument, not a rescue: India Glycols was running four structurally different businesses under one listing — Bio-based Specialties & Performance Chemicals (BSPC, including the 49% Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals JV into which IGL sells ethylene oxide), Potable Spirits (country liquor/IMIL plus IMFL, with the Amrut and Bacardi tie-ups), Bio-Fuel/ethanol-ENA sold at government-administered prices to OMCs, and Ennature Biopharma (thiocolchicoside, nicotine, nutraceuticals) with biopolymers. On 4 February 2025 the board approved splitting these into India Glycols (chemicals, glycols, bio-glycols, new specialties, industrial gases, plus the Clariant JV), IGL Spirits (spirits + bio-fuel/ENA) and Ennature Bio Pharma (biopharma + biopolymers), all three to be listed via the NCLT route. CEO Rupark Sarswat said the purpose was to run the companies differently with much more focus and to allow potential investments in different businesses because different investors have different appetites; CFO Anand Singhal listed the benefits as independent growth for each business, reducing the risk of one business affecting the others, unlocking value by drawing focused investors, and clearer focus leading to improved management and resource allocation — while insisting the structure would not unduly increase the cost base. Scale was quantified with 9MFY25 numbers: chemicals Rs 1,079 cr at 13.6% EBITDA margin, IGL Spirits Rs 1,628 cr net at 14.4%, Ennature Bio Pharma Rs 178 cr at 14.9% (against FY24 BSPC Rs 1,626 cr, Bio-Fuel Rs 512 cr, Potable Spirits Rs 5,575 cr gross). Capital allocation was the hard constraint: big capex was frozen until after the demerger, long-term debt was pre-allocated with the SBI-led consortium (about Rs 500 cr chemicals / Rs 700 cr liquor out of Rs 1,200 cr in May 2025, restated to Rs 600 cr / Rs 800 cr out of about Rs 1,400 cr in November 2025), the Rs 467 cr preferential allotment at Rs 915/share in November 2025 went entirely into prepaying debt, and the credit rating was parked on watch-list with no upgrade possible until the demerger completed. Management simultaneously defended keeping bio-fuel with spirits rather than with chemicals, arguing captive multi-feedstock ethanol/ENA gives backward integration, quality control, scale and resilience even if it dilutes percentage margin, and that plant proximity and the EO-to-JV link preserve synergies. By FY26 the residual chemicals business was pitched as under-earning for want of focus and in-house cost streamlining, with the contracted sale of a further 24% of the Clariant JV in FY29 expected to make the chemicals entity debt-free. The scheme was sanctioned by NCLT Allahabad on 17 July 2026, became effective 1 September 2026 (appointed date 1 April 2026), with IGL Spirits and Ennature Bio Pharma listing and trading from 2–4 November 2026.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. Rupark Sarswat first unveiled the three-way restructuring, initially to sit inside the IGL group before listing. “So, essentially what we are trying to do is to restructure these businesses into three separate companies, for the time being within the IGL group.” — *CALL Feb 2025*
2. The core stated reason: different businesses need different strategies and attract different pools of capital. “And also, to allow potential investments in different businesses because different investors tend to have a different focus for investments.” — *CALL Feb 2025*
3. CFO Anand Singhal framed one benefit as ring-fencing contagion between segments (relevant given Ennature's margin collapse and the chemicals/EO price squeeze). “Separating the business will reduce the risk of one business affecting the others.” — *CALL Feb 2025*
4. Anand gave the pro-forma 9MFY25 size and margins of each proposed entity — chemicals Rs 1,079 cr at 13.6%, spirits+biofuel Rs 1,628 cr at 14.4%, Ennature Rs 178 cr at 14.9%. “IGL Spirits, which is proposed to be the other Company which will be having the Liquor business and the Bio-Fuel business, is having 9MFY25 turnover of Rs. 1,628, this is on net basis with 14.4% EBITDA margin.” — *CALL Feb 2025*
5. Anand confirmed the NCLT route, a 12-15 month timetable, 1 April 2026 appointed date and listing of all three entities. “So, this demerger will be effective from 1st April, 26 and all the three companies will be listed on the stock exchange.” — *CALL Feb 2025*
6. Investors pushed on listing of the biggest piece, noting over 75% of the business would sit in IGL Spirits. “Sir, my first question regarding post restructuring, more than 75% of business comes from IGL Spirits. Is there any plan to list that entity?” — *CALL Feb 2025*
7. Lender involvement: working capital and term loan allocation across the three companies had to be negotiated with the SBI-led consortium and was not yet confirmed. “Rohit, regarding the working capital allocation to each Company and the term loan allocation, we are talking to the term lender, mainly the State Bank of India, who is the leader in our consortium banking.” — *CALL Feb 2025*
8. Rupark stressed the split must not create duplicate overheads; corporate resources would stay shared with an allocation mechanism. “The principle of demerger to start with is to continue to run the businesses under one umbrella, but differently as in separately from a strategic perspective, but not unduly increasing the cost base.” — *CALL Feb 2025*
9. Asked by Saket Kapoor whether clubbing government-priced bio-fuel with liquor would dilute the IMFL valuation, Rupark defended it as backward integration, quality control and scale. “Well, percentage margin is one factor, but the overall profitability and resilience of the business also improves.” — *CALL Feb 2025*
10. First debt allocation disclosed: Rs 1,200 cr long-term debt split roughly Rs 500 cr to chemicals and Rs 700 cr to liquor, with annual repayments of Rs 150-160 cr (spirits) and Rs 90 cr (chemicals). “Just to brief you as of now position, we are having about INR 1,200 crores long-term debt in the books of the company, out of which about INR 500 crores will go to the Chemical division and INR 700 crores will go to the liquor division.” — *CALL May 2025*
11. Rupark restated the rationale and the exact clustering — spirits with ethanol/bio-fuel into IGL Spirits, chemicals with the Clariant JV, Ennature with biopolymers. “The idea is that different investors have different appetites for different kind of businesses.” — *CALL Aug 2025*
12. Growth capex was explicitly deferred to the post-demerger entities; FY26 limited to rollover and Rs 40-50 cr maintenance capex. “And after the demerger, the separate companies will think over the CapEx.” — *CALL Aug 2025*
13. Investor pushback: a long-term shareholder challenged unlocking value by demerging a unit whose net margin had fallen from ~33% (2021) to ~2.4%. “We are planning to unlock shareholder value by demerging our business units when there is extreme degrowth in that business.” — *CALL Aug 2025*
14. Entity-level debt restated: of about Rs 1,400 cr long-term debt, Rs 600 cr to India Glycols and Rs 800 cr to IGL Spirits, with the Rs 467 cr raise plus Rs 180 cr scheduled repayment cutting both proportionately. “INR 600 crores in India Glycols and INR 800 crores in IGL Spirits.” — *CALL Nov 2025*
15. The Rs 467 cr preferential issue at Rs 915/share to promoters, friends and relatives was earmarked entirely for debt reduction ahead of the split. “So, this is the update, and the money which whatever we will receive out of this preferential will be utilized for the reduction of the term loan.” — *CALL Nov 2025*
16. Rupark tied the restructuring to the broader strategy of focusing on bio-based ingredients and consumer/lifestyle value capture. “And one of the outcomes of that is in the last few years and now once again, how we've been reorganizing and restructuring our businesses to bring the necessary focus.” — *CALL Feb 2026*
17. Rating agencies had placed IGL on watch-list because of the demerger; no upgrade (and hence no full benefit of the Rs 582 cr debt reduction) until completion. “So, you will not find the rating improvement till our demerger happens.” — *CALL Feb 2026*
18. Capex remained gated on the demerger even after the Rs 467 cr raise and planned FY26 closing term debt of about Rs 1,100 cr. “Apart from this, we are not having any big size capex. And any capex will be undertaken only after the demerger.” — *CALL Feb 2026*
19. Rupark argued the chemicals business (FY26 net revenue Rs 1,203 cr, down 10.4%, EBIT Rs 141 cr, margin 11.7%) is understated and needs in-house cost streamlining and dedicated focus. “Now, there is, if you look at EBITDA without adjusting the other income and probably some streamlining that is required in-house, we will start to see that the quality of the Chemicals business is probably going to be better than this going forward.” — *CALL Jun 2026*
20. Anand said the contracted sale of a further 24% of the Clariant JV in FY29 would fund term-loan repayment and leave the chemicals entity debt-free. “So, in '28-'29, I'm hopeful that the Chemical business will be totally debt-free.” — *CALL Jun 2026*
21. Investors were tracking the NCLT timetable; management expected the sanction order around 21 May/early June 2026, then ROC filing. “21st May, we are hopeful that we will get the order for the demerger of the division.” — *CALL Jun 2026*
22. Plan change: the board on 16 May 2025 dropped the amalgamation of promoter vehicle Kashipur Holdings Limited and pursued the demerger alone, with appointed date 1 April 2026. “The earlier proposal for the amalgamation of KHL into the Company will no longer form part of the Scheme being pursued.” — *Scheme*
23. The 1 September 2026 news release stated the benefit as dedicated focus and better oversight and resource allocation for each of the three companies. “Each company will have a dedicated focus, enabling improved management oversight and more efficient allocation of resources towards growth.” — *Scheme*
24. The release made the capital-allocation argument explicit — each entity sizing its own capital and investment needs. “In addition, each company will be able to manage its capital, investments and resources based on its specific business requirements, thereby enabling more efficient utilisation of capital.” — *Scheme*
25. Share entitlement: 1 IGL Spirits share for every 1 IGL share, and 1 Ennature Bio Pharma share for every 3 IGL shares (6,70,26,765 and 2,23,42,255 shares of Rs 5 allotted on 8 September 2026). “Resulting Company 2 shall issue 1 (One) Equity Share having face value of INR 5 (Indian Rupees Five) each, to the shareholders of Demerged Company holding 1 (One) Equity Share of INR 5 (Indian Rupees Five) each.” — *Scheme*
26. The tax cost-of-acquisition apportionment implies relative weights of IGL Spirits 47.62%, India Glycols 31.77% and Ennature Bio Pharma 20.61%. “Accordingly, for the purpose of determining the Cost of Acquisition of the Equity Shares of the Company and the Resulting Companies following the Demerger, the shareholders may apportion the original Cost of Acquisition of their Equity Shares of India Glycols Limited in the following manner” — *Scheme*
27. Near-unanimous stakeholder approval at the 24 March 2026 court-convened meetings; the secured creditors' meeting was dispensed with on 95.46% consent, and unsecured creditors voted 36/36, 100% by value. “it appearing from the said reports that the Scheme of Arrangement has been approved by the requisite majority of Equity Shareholders (4,42,48,625 votes in favour out of 4,42,48,626, with 1 vote against)” — *Scheme*
28. Completion: ROC filing on 1 September 2026 made the scheme effective, Q1 FY27 pro-forma net revenues being India Glycols Rs 345 cr, IGL Spirits Rs 694 cr and Ennature Bio Pharma Rs 90 cr; both new entities began trading 4 November 2026. “Accordingly, in terms of the provisions of the Clause 24 of the Scheme, the “Effective Date” of the Scheme is 1st September, 2026 and the Scheme contemplating the Demerger has now become effective and the Resulting Companies have ceased to be the subsidiaries of the Company.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** First disclosed on the 6 February 2025 call as a composite scheme that also folded promoter holding company Kashipur Holdings into IGL so promoters would hold IGL directly; by the 21 May 2025 call it was accompanied by a Rs 500 cr/Rs 700 cr debt split, and the board on 16 May 2025 dropped the KHL amalgamation to pursue the demerger alone. The 11 August 2025 and 18 November 2025 calls hardened the mechanics — three named entities, capex deferred to the post-demerger companies, debt restated to Rs 600 cr/Rs 800 cr, and a Rs 467 cr promoter-and-associates preferential issue to cut debt — while an investor on the August call openly questioned demerging a unit in degrowth. The 12 February 2026 call added that the credit rating would stay on watch-list and no sizeable capex would be sanctioned until completion, and the 18 May 2026 call was spent waiting on the NCLT hearing of 21 May. Shareholders (4,42,48,625 of 4,42,48,626 votes) and unsecured creditors (100% by value) approved on 24 March 2026; NCLT sanctioned on 17 July 2026, effective 1 September 2026, record date 2 September 2026, with trading in both new entities from 4 November 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Chemicals: cost streamlining, higher-value performance chemicals, improving EBIT (11.7% FY26), JV stake sale funding a debt-free unit by FY29. IGL Spirits: premiumisation toward ~22% EBIT margins on captive ENA, geographic and CSD expansion. Ennature: branded nutraceuticals margin recovery. All three: dedicated focus, own capital allocation, focused investors, value unlock.

*Not explained on the calls:* Never quantified: value unlock, standalone corporate costs, inter-company ENA/EO transfer pricing, shared Kashipur utilities, debt-covenant consents; no investor, lender or partner was named as having requested it.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* "The demerger will result in the creation of three separate companies, each with a clear business focus," giving each dedicated management oversight and capital, investments and resources managed to its own business requirements.
- *What it reveals:* Tax cost apportionment assigns Ennature 20.61% of value on only ~2% of group revenue (FY26 segment revenue Rs 207.77 crore, EBIT Rs 7.23 crore, 3.5%, down from 20.76 crore EBIT in FY25), with segment assets Rs 426.42 crore versus liabilities Rs 92.49 crore — a depressed-margin, asset-heavy business management says is being rebuilt into branded nutraceuticals.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *Read next:* Ennature Bio Pharma's Information Memorandum (board-approved 8 September 2026) — standalone balance sheet, debt allocation and segment margin trend.
- *In their words:* “Ennature Bio Pharma Limited will house the bio-pharma and bio-polymers businesses.”

- **operating margin** — parent / remaining: Chemicals (Bio-based Specialities and Performance Chemicals, the remaining business): "net revenue of INR1,203 crores in FY26, which is down 10.4%, but our EBIT at INR141 crores is up 12.5% and our EBIT margins are up to 11.7%"; separated business: Potable Spirits FY26 EBIT margin materially higher (EBIT INR285 crores on INR1,331 crores, Q4 EBIT margin 22.1%); Bio-Fuels FY26 EBIT margin 7.8% with EBIT up 103.3%; Ennature Biopharma margins under pressure (Q3 FY26 EBIT margin 4.1%, 9M FY26 2.9%) “As far as the Potable Spirit business is concerned, we posted a top-line of INR1,331 crores in FY26, up 14.4% and an EBIT of INR285 crores, which is up 11.1%.”
- **debt and leverage** — parent / remaining: About INR 600 crores of long-term debt allocated to India Glycols Limited; management expects "the Chemical business will be totally debt-free" in FY28-29 after the planned sale of a further 24% of the joint venture equity; separated business: About INR 800 crores of long-term debt allocated to IGL Spirits Limited; of FY26-27 normal term-loan repayment of INR 268 crores, "in liquor, it is INR168 crores, and INR100 crores in Chemical" “So, in these two companies, India Glycols and IGL Spirits, the segregation what we have done as of date is about INR 600 crores and INR 800 crores. INR 600 crores in India Glycols and INR 800 crores in IGL Spirits.”
- **capex and capital intensity** — parent / remaining: Chemicals capex described as incremental and modular: "we are talking about in the range of maybe INR 10 crores to INR 50 crore kind of CAPEX to start with"; plant shutdown 17th March to 2nd April 2026 for catalyst change reduced production and sales; separated business: Of roughly INR830 crores of FY26 capital expenditure, about INR 400 crores was the two grain distilleries (Gorakhpur and Kashipur) that sit in the Spirits and Biofuel Undertaking “Actually, there are two distilleries largely, which are the main capital expenditure. One is the grain distillery in Gorakhpur, and one is the grain distillery in Kashipur.”
- **tax** — parent / remaining: The Income Tax Department "is permitted to retain recourse for recovery in respect of demand and any other future liabilities of the Demerged Company in respect of the assets sought to be transferred under the Scheme"; counsel noted "the Petitioner Company No.1 which is a demerging company and remains in existence post approval" would be bound by any outstanding demand (Rs.27,890/- outstanding per demand raised on 06th May, 2026); separated business: Tax liabilities, pending appeals and compliances relating to the Biopharma Undertaking and the Spirits and Biofuel Undertaking transfer to the respective Resulting Company from the Appointed Date, 01.04.2026 “The respective Resulting Company shall be responsible for paying any tax liability of the Demerged Company relating to the respective Demerged Undertaking, if any, pending on the Appointed Date, i.e., 01.04.2026 or determined by the Income Tax Department after the Appointed Date, i.e., 01.04.2026.”
- **cash** — parent / remaining: INR 466.99 crore preferential issue proceeds plus internal accruals used to prepay about INR804 crores of debt in Q4 FY26, saving about INR20 crores of interest; other income of the remaining business includes the Clariant joint venture share (INR20.60 crores for the quarter ended 30 June 2026); separated business: not stated “So, this INR804 crores include the long-term debt, the working capital, and the short-term loans resulting in INR20 crores saving in the interest cost, which is already there in the results.”
- **return on capital** — parent / remaining: Consolidated India Glycols Limited before the demerger; management also notes debt-to-equity down from 0.7x in FY23 to 0.5x in FY26 and interest coverage up from 2.3x to 3.0x; separated business: not stated (no separate return-on-capital figures given for the demerged undertakings) “And if you look at ROCE over the last few years, it has gone from 7.7% in FY23 to 11.9% in FY26, and RONW has gone up from 7.7% in FY23 to 11.3% in FY26.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: Segment assets as at 30.06.2026 (standalone): Bio-based Specialities and Performance Chemicals 3,514.26; segment liabilities 577.54 (INR Crores); separated business: Segment assets as at 30.06.2026 (standalone): Potable Spirits 632.16, Bio-Fuel 1,538.06, Ennature Biopharma 417.28; segment liabilities Potable Spirits 385.41, Bio-Fuel 100.20, Ennature Biopharma 107.57 (INR Crores) “Segment assets -Bio-based Specialities and Performance Chemicals 3,514.26 -Potable Spirits 632.16 -Ennature Biopharma 417.28 -Bio- Fuel 1,538.06 -Unallocated 44.35 Total 6,146.11”
- **working capital** — parent / remaining: not stated; separated business: IMFL expansion within the Spirits business is described as working-capital heavy, which is why the company prioritises government-corporation markets where payment is secure “We are very cautious about giving credit. And subsequently, the annual depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores has been eliminated, thereby increasing the profitability."”

**The judge's read of selling pressure:** likely — Only 122 IRSL shares per 1,000 held - small odd-lot stakes; 4,89,82,030 shares spread to O&M holders; different industry (EPC/power evacuation), loss-making, heavily indebted

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The separation is the demerger of Inox Green Energy Services Ltd's (IGESL) power evacuation / substation and common-infrastructure business into Inox Renewable Solutions Ltd (IRSL, formerly Resco Global Wind Services), leaving IGESL a pure-play renewable O&M company and consolidating all evacuation/EPC infrastructure in IRSL, which gets automatically listed. Management's core explanation is historical and structural: when IGESL was spun out of Inox Wind, the EPC business was slump-sold to Resco, but the already-commissioned substations and transmission lines could not be moved because, as Devansh Jain said in Aug 2024, shifting them 'would have entailed taking approval from over 200 customers and then arm twisting us in terms of renegotiating contracts and screwing the entire O&M business'; so IGESL's balance sheet stayed 'unnecessarily inflated' with assets on which it is 'actually the trustee', while all new substations were being built in Resco anyway ('no future CapEx under Inox Green at all', Feb 2024). The financial fix they repeatedly quantified: a gross block of ~INR 1,000 crore (net block ~INR 750 crore, Aug 2024) leaves IGESL, annual depreciation of ~INR 50-55 crore (~INR 13-17 crore a quarter) is eliminated, PBT rises by that amount, and only ~INR 3-5 crore a quarter (~INR 10 crore a year, Feb 2026) of revenue goes out with virtually no cost and no interest moving — Akhil Jindal put the benefit at '~INR 12-odd crore in the bottom line on a quarterly basis' (Nov 2024), turning reported PAT of ~INR 6 crore into ~INR 18-20 crore. They stressed the evacuation assets are not needed for O&M ('not required for O&M services per se... that is required for further providing a turnkey solution'), so IGESL becomes a zero-capex, asset-light annuity business where EBITDA equals PBT and cash PAT, helped by a ~INR 700 crore accumulated tax-loss shield that stays at company level, with 'significant improvement in ROE and ROCE' (Jun 2026). The Scheme's own rationale adds that risks, rewards, financial profile, competition and opportunities are 'separate and distinct' for O&M versus power evacuation, that the evacuation business 'is capable of attracting different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders', that consolidating it into IRSL (which already does the same business) unlocks value and lends enhanced focus, and that the result is two listed entities each free to pursue its own strategy. On the IRSL side, management argued the infrastructure is itself a high-value platform — INR 175 crore raised at a ~INR 7,400 crore valuation (Sep 2025), ~10 GW of 'plug and play' evacuation infra made more valuable by the CERC hybridisation amendment — and that listing it 'will unlock substantial value for both Inox Wind and Inox Green' (Nov 2025). The push came from the promoters/board (valuers appointed Aug-Nov 2024, scheme approved 13 Nov 2024) with investors on calls repeatedly asking about rationalising subsidiaries and value unlocking; Akhil Jindal framed the purpose as giving shareholders optionality — 'a shareholder has got now a choice to hold any part of the business' — and shareholders, warrant holders, secured and unsecured creditors all approved it before NCLT Ahmedabad sanctioned it.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. Pre-demerger baseline: management explained IGESL carries legacy substation gross block (4 GW capacity, 3 GW commissioned) with ~INR 13 crore quarterly depreciation, while all future common-infrastructure capex is being incurred in Resco Global, a 100% subsidiary of Inox Wind. “So, no future CapEx under Inox Green at all. So, whatever is the depreciation which is being incurred on a quarterly basis will continue until and unless our net block gets consumed.” — *[Feb 2024](https://inoxgreen.com/PDF/Transcription%20of%20INOX%20Green%20Energy%20-%20Q3%20FY24%20Earnings%20Conference%20Call.pdf)*
2. Board appointed consultants and registered valuers to evaluate the demerger; Mathusudhana framed it as producing a cleaner, asset-light balance sheet whose main benefit is eliminating depreciation. “The proposed demerger will significantly add value through depreciation elimination.” — *[Aug 2024](https://inoxgreen.com/PDF/MOSL-InoxGreenEnergy-Aug09-2024_IGESL.pdf)*
3. Devansh Jain gave the historical reason the assets were stranded in IGESL: at the time of the EPC slump sale to Resco, only uncommissioned assets moved, and commissioned substations could not be shifted without re-opening contracts with over 200 customers. “We could not shunt it out from this balance sheet into Resco because that would have entailed taking approval from over 200 customers and then arm twisting us in terms of renegotiating contracts and screwing the entire O&M business.” — *[Aug 2024](https://inoxgreen.com/PDF/MOSL-InoxGreenEnergy-Aug09-2024_IGESL.pdf)*
4. He added that IGESL's balance sheet was inflated by assets it merely holds as trustee (net block ~INR 750 crore), and that the remaining business is a zero-capex annuity with no land bank or future evacuation capex. “Inox Green's balance sheet is unnecessarily inflated thanks to these historical substations which are lying on its balance sheet of which we are actually the trustee.” — *[Aug 2024](https://inoxgreen.com/PDF/MOSL-InoxGreenEnergy-Aug09-2024_IGESL.pdf)*
5. Akhil Jindal quantified the P&L effect for Pritesh Chheda: the whole depreciation goes, only INR 3-4 crore of quarterly revenue leaves, and IGESL shareholders receive Resco shares in lieu, with valuation yet to be fixed. “Excluding the substation business, the revenue would be down by around Rs. 3 crores or Rs. 4 crores on a quarterly basis, and the whole depreciation will go away. So, broadly that will add around Rs. 12-odd crore in the bottom line on a quarterly basis.” — *[Nov 2024](https://www.inoxgreen.com/PDF/MOSL-InoxGreenEnergy-Oct25-2024.pdf)*
6. Mathusudhana answered Bhavik Shah's objection that the transferred assets would come back as opex: the evacuation and common infrastructure is not needed to run O&M at all, it belongs to the EPC/turnkey business, so margins are unaffected. “So as far as the power evacuation and the common infrastructure, we have developed is not required for O&M services per se. That is required for further providing a turnkey solution to the customers.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a6149a06-42db-4b82-ae77-0dc15e5abe49.pdf)*
7. Jindal described the post-demerger entity as an asset-light balance sheet with no depreciation, so EBITDA is the benchmark for PAT; the ~INR 700 crore accumulated tax losses stay with IGESL because they sit at company, not asset, level. “So when you're looking into the next year's balance sheet of Inox Green, it would be an asset-light balance sheet. And it would also have no depreciation charges as a continued item. What it means is that our profitability will be far more stronger.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a6149a06-42db-4b82-ae77-0dc15e5abe49.pdf)*
8. Asked by Hansal Thakkar whether the subsidiaries would be rationalised into IWL shareholders' hands, Jindal said the whole intent of separating the businesses was shareholder optionality, and that no further corporate action is needed. “And I think from a shareholder's perspective, a shareholder has got now a choice to hold any part of the business. He can hold the O&M business, he can hold the infrastructure business, he can hold the entire value chain together under Inox Wind.” — *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac349021-05a3-4a4e-84a8-edb5f23d90bd.pdf)*
9. Mathusudhana restated the balance-sheet numbers (INR 1,000 crore gross block off, INR 50-55 crore annual depreciation eliminated, PBT up by that amount, ROE/ROCE up), with exchange no-objections received and the scheme filed at NCLT Ahmedabad. “Once the scheme is approved by the NCLT, the gross block of around INR1,000 crore will be off our balance sheet and subsequently the depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores annually will be eliminated, thereby increasing the PBT by that amount.” — *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac349021-05a3-4a4e-84a8-edb5f23d90bd.pdf)*
10. Sanjeev Agarwal gave the value case for the receiving entity: IRSL had just raised INR 175 crore at a ~INR 7,400 crore valuation, and the new CERC hybridisation rules multiply the value of its site infrastructure (Devansh: ~10 GW of plug-and-play infra). “We have recently raised INR175 crores at Inox Renewable Solutions at a valuation of approximately INR7,400 crores.” — *[Sep 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ac349021-05a3-4a4e-84a8-edb5f23d90bd.pdf)*
11. With shareholder and creditor approval obtained, Devansh Jain framed the separation as a value-unlocking event for both the parent and IGESL, with IRSL listing as Inox Wind's EPC arm. “I believe that the de-merger and subsequent listing of Inox Renewable Solutions will unlock substantial value for both Inox Wind and Inox Green.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=12a9f200-8091-44c1-a30e-eb06b0e51134.pdf)*
12. Answering Prit Nagersheth on how much revenue comes off, management sized the revenue leakage at only ~INR 10 crore against ~INR 50 crore of depreciation removed, i.e. no material impact on the INR 600 crore FY27 EBITDA math. “So post the demerger, as we have clarified on the multiple cores, there would be a very limited amount of revenue in the range of INR 10 odd crore will get out of the balance sheet. And around INR 50 odd crores of depreciation will go out from the balance sheet.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d934a5d2-25cf-4a13-92c1-68d279362ad8.pdf)*
13. Mathusudhana confirmed NCLT Ahmedabad approval and booked the benefits as realised: INR 1,000 crore gross block and INR 50-55 crore annual depreciation eliminated, profitability and returns up; Devansh said remaining steps were administrative, 1-2 months. “It has also led to significant improvement in ROE and ROCE of Inox Green.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78c64939-3c62-49ac-9827-562fd6465a1b.pdf)*
14. Management declined to disclose IRSL's top line or EBITDA profile until the demerger dates are announced, and tied the post-demerger IGESL story to ~INR 600 crore FY27 EBITDA converting almost fully to cash with no depreciation, no finance cost and a INR 700 crore tax shield. “We cannot say at this point in time. I think once that demerged, we'll elucidate more plans. At this point in time, it's part and parcel of Inox Wind.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=78c64939-3c62-49ac-9827-562fd6465a1b.pdf)*
15. The Scheme's stated rationale is segregation of two verticals whose risk-reward and financial profiles differ, consolidation of the evacuation business into IRSL which already runs it, and establishing IGESL as a pure-play O&M player, producing two listed entities. “Further, the Power Evacuation Business is capable of attracting different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.” — *Scheme*
16. Consideration to IGESL shareholders was fixed by registered valuer Finvox Analytics (fairness opinion from Marwadi Chandarana) at 122 IRSL shares per 1,000 IGESL shares; appointed date 1 Oct 2024, NCLT sanction 13 Mar 2026, effective 4 May 2026, record date 1 Aug 2026, 4,89,82,030 IRSL shares allotted 24 Aug 2026. “122 equity shares of Resco of face value of INR 10 each fully paid up to be issued for every 1,000 equity shares of Inox Green of face value of INR 10 each fully paid up” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** On the Feb 2024 call the idea did not exist yet; management only explained that all future common-infra capex would sit in Resco, not Inox Green, while legacy depreciation ran on. By the Aug 2024 and Nov 2024 (Oct 25, 2024) calls the board had appointed consultants and registered valuers to evaluate demerging the power evacuation business, pitched as a 'cleaner and asset-light balance sheet' worth ~INR 12 crore a quarter to the bottom line, and the board approved the Scheme on 13 Nov 2024; in Feb 2025 (Jan 31, 2025) Akhil Jindal said exchange approvals were due in February and NCLT would take 6-9 months, with IGESL holders getting ~20% of the renamed Inox Renewable Solutions. By Sep 2025 (Sep 1, 2025) stock-exchange no-objections were in and the scheme filed at NCLT Ahmedabad (approval expected in 2-3 quarters), IRSL had raised INR 175 crore at a ~INR 7,400 crore valuation, and the CERC hybridisation ruling made its infra far more valuable; Nov 2025 (Nov 14, 2025) reported shareholder and creditor approval, and Feb 2026 (Feb 13, 2026) said hearings were in final stages with listing 2-3 months out. NCLT sanctioned the scheme on 13 Mar 2026, it became effective 4 May 2026, and on the Jun 2026 (May 29, 2026) call management confirmed approval and booked the benefits as done — INR 1,000 crore gross block and INR 50-55 crore depreciation gone, ROE/ROCE improved — while refusing to give IRSL's standalone top line or EBITDA until listing; the record date was 1 Aug 2026 and 4,89,82,030 IRSL shares were allotted on 24 Aug 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Inox Green: asset-light pure-play O&M — Rs 1,000 crore gross block and Rs 50-55 crore depreciation gone, only ~Rs 10 crore revenue lost, EBITDA≈PBT≈cash PAT, better ROE/ROCE. IRSL: separately listed EPC/evacuation arm with its own investors, lenders and ~10 GW plug-and-play infra; IGESL holders get 122 IRSL shares per 1,000.

*Not explained on the calls:* Never quantified IRSL's evacuation revenue/EBITDA, who pays IGESL's common-infrastructure contract revenue post-transfer, lender/customer consent mechanics, or whether IGESL now rents the substations back.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Segregation of distinct business verticals with separate risks, rewards and investors; consolidation of Power Evacuation Business into IRSL to unlock value and lend enhanced focus; establishing IGESL as a pure-play O&M player, creating two listed entities
- *What it reveals:* Removing ~Rs 1,000 crore gross block and Rs 50-55 crore annual depreciation leaves Inox Green a pure-play O&M business with ~50% EBITDA margins, tax shield and FY27 EBITDA guidance above Rs 600 crore; IRSL holds the capital-heavy, leveraged evacuation assets, losses and a Rs 96.8 crore tax demand
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* IRSL listing/trading approval intimation and its standalone financials - secured/unsecured debt and the Rs 96.80 crore AY2023-24 tax demand
- *In their words:* “Such consolidation in a single entity will lend enhanced focus to the Power Evacuation business.”

### 8. The separated business's financial statements

**The business being separated — its own numbers**, entity by entity: its reported statements once it is listed and on file, and the segment numbers the annual reports and presentations carry for it before that.

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

Management is demerging the Sugar Business of Piccadily Agro Industries Ltd. (PAIL) into Piccadily Food & Essentials Limited (PFEL), a wholly owned subsidiary, so that PAIL becomes a pure-play premium alco-bev company; CFO Natwar Aggarwal framed it on the April 29, 2026 call as "we want to be a global alco-bev company and in that pursuit we want to focus on our core brand portfolio," with the scheme Board-approved April 28, 2026, filed with SEBI, KPMG as adviser, and completion envisaged in FY27. The stated intent is to pool human and capital resources behind the Alco-Bev portfolio (Indri single malt, Camikara rum, Cashmir vodka, Whistler blended whisky) and to list sugar — described as a "traditional heritage business" — as a separate entity rather than sell it. The economics behind it are visible in the numbers management cited: Alco-Bev revenue grew 42% to INR 908 crore (from INR 639 crore) with 31.5% EBITDA margins and 45–50% IMFL margins, while sugar was only INR 233.05 crore of turnover (20.53% of the listed entity) and dragged Q4 standalone EBITDA margin down ~300 bps as sugar's quarterly EBITDA margin collapsed from 11% to 2%; the segment tables show the sugar segment result at a loss of INR 904.62 lakh in FY26 versus a loss of INR 327.13 lakh in FY25, with sugar segment assets of INR 10,553.97 lakh against segment liabilities of INR 22,166.79 lakh. Management also repeatedly blamed sugar seasonality for making quarter-to-quarter margins hard to read. The scheme's own rationale (Annexure B) lists focused attention for each core business and the ability to attract required investment, greater business focus and enhanced shareholder value, more efficient use of financial resources, managerial talent, technical skills and marketing resources, value unlock "through price-discovery of the individual entities," the "right operating architecture" with sharper individual strategies and "clear capital allocation," and separately listed companies attracting a specific set of investors with financial flexibility and "stronger capital market outcomes." Mechanically it is a mirror listing: no cash consideration, 1 PFEL share of INR 10 for every 9 PAIL shares (ratio fixed on sugar's turnover and assets), PFEL's pre-scheme capital cancelled, no change in PAIL's shareholding pattern, producing "two listed companies with proportionate shareholding." No investor, lender or business partner is identified anywhere as having demanded the separation — it is presented as a management/Board decision, recommended by the Audit Committee and Independent Directors, alongside the unrelated FY27 agenda of INR 250–300 crore incremental Indri revenue, INR 300–400 crore from the 200 KLPD Chhattisgarh plant, 60–70% growth and brand-side inorganic options.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The CFO announced the demerger of the sugar business into a new entity as a step toward becoming a global alco-bev company focused on the core brand portfolio, filed with SEBI with KPMG as partner and NCLT to follow, targeting completion in FY27. “A couple of announcements also, we want to be a global alco-bev company and in that pursuit we want to focus on our core brand portfolio.” — *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)*
2. Timeline and process: scheme filed with SEBI, NCLT filing after SEBI go-ahead, completion envisaged within FY27. “Once we get go-ahead from SEBI, we will follow the due process of filing it to NCLT and we envisage to complete this process by FY '27 this year.” — *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)*
3. Management restated the demerger purely as a focus measure alongside guidance of 60–70% FY27 growth and 3x–4x revenue in three to four years. “As mentioned earlier, we also in a process of demerger just to focus on the main Alco-Bev business.” — *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)*
4. Asked by Himanshu Shah of Dolat Capital whether sugar would eventually be sold or listed, management said the intent is to pool human and capital resources for Alco-Bev only and to separately list sugar, which it called a traditional heritage business. “Yes, intent is very clear that we want to be a global Alco-Bev company. We want to pool our human and capital resources just for the Alco-Bev business.” — *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)*
5. The separation is explicitly a separate listing of the heritage sugar business, not a divestment, so the company can focus only on the Alco-Bev portfolio. “So sugar business is like a traditional heritage business for us. So we want to separate it and list it as a separate entity than our Alco-Bev company and focus only on the Alco-Bev portfolio.” — *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)*
6. Sugar was the main reason standalone Q4 EBITDA margin fell about 300 basis points, its quarterly EBITDA margin dropping from 11% to 2% — the dilution the demerger removes. “That is one of the major factor is because of sugar drop in business, sugar margins drop, which was 11% EBITDA margin last year and last year same quarter and 2% this year quarter.” — *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)*
7. Management contrasted sugar's drag with Alco-Bev EBITDA margins of about 31.5% (and IMFL margins of 45–50%), which it expects to maintain or improve with premiumisation. “I would like to highlight one more point here that if you look at our Alco-Bev business EBITDA margins, which is in the range of, let's say, current year about 31.5%, which is one of the highest margin in any Alco-Bev competition.” — *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)*
8. Sugar seasonality was also cited as what makes quarter-to-quarter margin comparison unreliable for the consolidated entity. “So as I said, that as you rightly said that overall our EBITDA margins are same on year-over-year basis, but quarterly one factor is a sugar because of seasonality of the sugar business.” — *[May 2026](https://www.piccadily.com/themes/piccadily/pdfs/piccadily_transcript_earnings_call_dated_29_4_26.pdf)*
9. The April 28, 2026 Board outcome states the scheme demerges the Sugar Business into wholly owned subsidiary PFEL under Sections 230–232, creating two listed companies with proportionate shareholding — sugar in PFEL, distillery in PAIL. ““The effectiveness of the Scheme would result in the creation of two listed companies with proportionate shareholding with the Resulting Company housing the Sugar Business and the Company housing the Distillery Business.” — *Scheme*
10. Sugar's scale is disclosed as INR 233.05 crore of FY26 turnover, 20.53% of the listed entity's total turnover. “The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking of the Company for the financial year ended 31% March 2026 is as follows:” — *Scheme*
11. Scheme rationale: separating the undertaking lets each company give focused attention to its core business and attract the investment that business needs. “Demerger of the Demerged Business and Undertaking and transferrmg it to a separate company would enable both the Demergéd Company and. the Resulting Company to provide focused attention for growth of their core businesses and attract required investments for growing that business;” — *Scheme*
12. Scheme rationale: value unlock via separate price discovery for each entity for existing shareholders. “The Scheme would unlock value for the overall-business portfolio through price-discovery of the individual entities for existing shareholders;” — *Scheme*
13. Scheme rationale: the right operating architecture, sharper individual business strategies and clear capital allocation for each company. “The Scheme could lead to the right operating architecture for both companies with sharper focus on, their individual business strategies and clear capital allocation, in alignment with the respective value creation journeys;” — *Scheme*
14. Scheme rationale: two separately listed companies each attract their own investor set, gain financial flexibility and better capital market outcomes. “Separately listed companies to attract specific set of investors for their’ business profile, achieve financial flexibility and consequently, encourage stronger capital market outcomes.” — *Scheme*
15. Scheme rationale: better, more efficient conduct of each business by using its own financial resources, managerial talent, technical skills and marketing resources, and greater business focus enhancing shareholder value. “The Scheme will be conducive to better and more’ efficient and effective conduct of: business. and operations of the respective . companies, by utilizing the financial resources, managerial talents, technical skills and marketing resources and services delivery” — *Scheme*
16. Mirror listing, no cash: one PFEL share of INR 10 for every nine PAIL shares, PFEL's existing capital cancelled, no change in PAIL's shareholding pattern, ratio set on sugar's turnover and assets. “The Share Entitlement Ratio is fixed keeping in view the turnover of Sugar Business Undertaking and assets of the Sugar Business.” — *Scheme*
17. The April 28, 2026 press release frames the end state as a pure-play alco-bev company with sharper focus, better capital allocation and value creation, scheme filed with SEBI and completion expected by end-FY27. “Post-demerger, Piccadily Agro will transition into a pure-play alco-beverage company, enabling sharper strategic focus, improved capital allocation, and enhanced value creation for stakeholders.” — *Scheme*
18. CFO's press-release quote ties the demerger directly to unlocking value in core operations alongside Chhattisgarh monetisation from May 2026. “With the strategic demerger of our sugar division, we are now sharply focused on unlocking value in our core operations.” — *Scheme*
19. On August 17, 2026 the company intimated receipt of no-adverse-observation letters dated August 14, 2026 from BSE and NSE (following SEBI's August 13, 2026 comments), enabling the NCLT filing; the letter is valid six months and PFEL's listing is at the exchange's discretion. “We wish to inform you that the Company has received the No Adverse Observation Letters dated August 14, 2026, in respect of the aforesaid Scheme from the BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited (“Stock Exchanges”).” — *Scheme*
20. SEBI's comments require the company to spell out, to NCLT and shareholders, the need for and rationale of the demerger, cost-benefit analysis, swap-ratio basis, assets and liabilities transferred, risks and the financial implications for promoters and public shareholders — disclosure not yet made in these documents. “Need for the demerger, rationale of the scheme, synergies of business of the entities involved in the scheme, impact of the scheme on the shareholders and cost benefit analysis of the scheme.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** Only one earnings call falls in the window, the FY26 call of April 29, 2026, and the demerger appears there already as a done decision rather than an idea being floated — announced in the CFO's opening remarks the day after the April 28, 2026 Board meeting approved the scheme and filed it with the exchanges/SEBI, with KPMG as partner and FY27 as the completion target. It resurfaced later in the same call only when Himanshu Shah of Dolat Capital pressed on intent (sell or separately list), drawing the explicit answer that sugar would be listed separately, not sold. The filings then track execution rather than rationale: the April 28, 2026 Regulation 30 outcome with the full Annexure B rationale, share entitlement ratio and sugar turnover of INR 233.05 crore (20.53%), the April 28, 2026 press release restating the pure-play framing, and the August 17, 2026 intimation of BSE/NSE no-adverse-observation letters dated August 14, 2026 (SEBI comments dated August 13, 2026) clearing the way for the NCLT petition. Earlier filings in the window (November–December 2025) concern only CCD and warrant conversions and never mention a separation.

**What management expects from it:** Alco-Bev PAIL becomes a pure-play premium spirits company: sharper focus, pooled human and capital resources, better capital allocation, and 31.5% alco-bev / 45–50% IMFL margins no longer diluted by seasonal sugar; 60–70% FY27 growth and 3–4x revenue in 3–4 years. Sugar, housed in PFEL, gets focused attention, its own investor set, price discovery, financial flexibility and ability to attract investment.

*Not explained on the calls:* No sugar standalone P&L/debt split, lender or creditor consents, demerger costs, PFEL management, dividend or sale intent beyond listing; no investor, lender or partner named as requesting it.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Separating the Sugar Business lets both companies give focused attention to core businesses and attract investment, unlocks value through price-discovery of individual entities, and makes PAIL a pure-play alco-bev company.
- *What it reveals:* Parent becomes pure-play alco-bev: FY26 distillery segment result Rs 23,658.72 lakhs vs sugar's Rs 494.79 lakhs on 20.53% of turnover; sugar segment liabilities Rs 22,166.79 lakhs exceed its assets Rs 10,553.97 lakhs, so leverage leaves with the stub.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* Scheme explanatory statement: value of assets and liabilities transferred to PFEL, plus PFEL's abridged prospectus/Information Memorandum.
- *In their words:* “The effectiveness of the Scheme would result in the creation of two listed companies with proportionate shareholding with the Resulting Company housing the Sugar Business and the Company housing the Distillery Business.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

Thomas Cook (India) Ltd (TCIL) is carving out its Resorts and Resort Management business — the six resorts it owns/operates directly under the Nature Trails brand, which it had itself absorbed from Nature Trails Resorts Pvt Ltd by slump sale for Rs 522.5 mn (appointed date 1 March 2025) — and demerging it into its wholly owned subsidiary Sterling Holiday Resorts Ltd (SHRL), which will then be separately listed on BSE and NSE. Management's stated logic is twofold: operationally, the resorts "would reap more benefit from being owned and operated by SHRL in light of their vast expertise in the hospitality industry" (SHRL ran 75+ resorts/3,700+ rooms at scheme date, 78 resorts/~3,800 rooms across 65 destinations by FY26-end, FY26 revenue INR 5,487 mn, EBITDA INR 1,701 mn at 31%, PBT INR 1,142 mn at 21%, 25 straight profitable quarters, debt-free with ~INR 3,400 mn cash); and financially, the split is meant to "unlock value" and "attract differentiated investor cohorts for each business segment," leaving TCIL to "concentrate our resources on our core Travel and Financial Services business." The demerged undertaking is tiny in revenue terms — INR 70 crores for the year ended 31 December 2025, ~0.4% of TCIL standalone turnover — so the driver is structural, not scale: SHRL's board says it "has matured over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity in the fast-growing hospitality industry," with two listed entities each pursuing "growth opportunities that are more aligned with their own industry dynamics." Bolted onto the same composite scheme are three capital-structure fixes aimed squarely at EPS and optics: consolidating four Re 1 shares into one Rs 4 share (47,69,50,562 shares becoming 11,92,37,641) to "better reflect the true market value" and "convey stronger financial stability and valuation metrics"; absorbing three dormant subsidiaries — TC Visa Services (India), Jardin Travel Solutions and Borderless Travel Services — that are "incurring unnecessary compliance and administrative costs"; and cutting face value from Rs 4 to Rs 3 with no payout to "right size the balance sheet and capital structure." Consideration is 81 SHRL shares of Rs 10 for every 100 TCIL shares of Re 1, with no cash; TCIL keeps its existing SHRL shares (~7%), promoters end at 65.55% of SHRL and public at 32.30%. The initiative came from the Board on the recommendation of the Audit Committee and an Independent Directors Committee — no lender, partner or named investor demand is disclosed anywhere in the calls or filings, though analysts had repeatedly pressed management on deployment of the ~INR 780-800 crore net cash pile and on Sterling's EBIT failing to scale with its room additions.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. First earnings-call disclosure of the March 2026 board approval, framed as a strategic divestment of the resort business into Sterling that unlocks shareholder value. “Before we move on to the segmental analysis, I will discuss the strategic divestment announcement that was made in March 2026, where the Board has granted in-principle approval for the demerger of our resort business into Sterling Holiday Resorts.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d884e7c7-ee2e-41fb-b1b5-e6408e592685.pdf)*
2. Iyer's stated benefit for the remaining TCIL: a cleaner capital structure and resources concentrated on Travel and Financial Services (forex, corporate travel, MICE, DMS). “For Thomas Cook (India) Limited, this restructuring allows us to streamline our capital structure and concentrate our resources on our core Travel and Financial Services business.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d884e7c7-ee2e-41fb-b1b5-e6408e592685.pdf)*
3. The face-value consolidation plus absorption of the three dormant subsidiaries is pitched explicitly as an EPS and corporate-structure simplification measure. “The consolidation of our face value per share, along with the merger of the three dormant subsidiaries, further simplifies our corporate structure and improves our Earnings Per Share, directly benefiting our shareholders.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d884e7c7-ee2e-41fb-b1b5-e6408e592685.pdf)*
4. Lalvani places the demerger alongside Sterling's own next phase — brand re-architecture and expansion to 95 resorts/4,500 rooms in 2027 — as process already under way. “In parallel, as you are aware, the demerger process from Thomas Cook has also been initiated.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d884e7c7-ee2e-41fb-b1b5-e6408e592685.pdf)*
5. Nandy gave the only timeline guidance: 12-15 months from board approval, NSE/BSE applications filed and queries being answered, completion expected Q1 FY28. “So when we took the Board approval for this particular demerger project, we said that it will take us 12 to 15 months.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d884e7c7-ee2e-41fb-b1b5-e6408e592685.pdf)*
6. Sterling's readiness argument on the call: FY26 as an inflection year with revenue INR 5,487 mn, EBITDA 31%, PBT margin 21%, 25 consecutive profitable quarters and a debt-free balance sheet with ~INR 3,400 mn cash. “FY '25-'26 marks a defining year for Sterling, a decisive inflection point where scale, profitability and balance sheet strength have expanded simultaneously, not sequentially.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d884e7c7-ee2e-41fb-b1b5-e6408e592685.pdf)*
7. Core operating rationale: the resorts belong with Sterling because Sterling has the hospitality operating expertise, catering to a different demographic with more curated experiences (adventure holidays, educational trips, corporate getaways). “TCIL and SHRL's Management believes that the Resort Business of TCIL would reap more benefit from being owned and operated by SHRL in light of their vast expertise in the hospitality industry.” — *Scheme*
8. Sterling is presented as having outgrown subsidiary status and ready for its own listed existence in a fast-growing sector — the justification for subsequently listing SHRL on BSE and NSE. “Further, SHRL's Management is of the view that SHRL has matured over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity in the fast-growing hospitality industry.” — *Scheme*
9. The value-unlock case is explicitly about attracting different investor bases to travel/financial services versus leisure hospitality, with each entity pursuing sector-specific growth strategies with agility. “Unlock value for the shareholders of TCIL by demerging the Resorts and Resort Management business into SHRL and to attract differentiated investor cohorts for each business segment” — *Scheme*
10. Segregating verticals is expected to improve operating efficiency and profitability at both entities because each faces different industry dynamics. “In this manner, the two listed entities can each pursue growth opportunities that are more aligned with their own industry dynamics, leading to improved operational efficiencies and profitability.” — *Scheme*
11. Scale of what is actually moving: the demerged undertaking's turnover was only INR 70 crores for the year ended 31 December 2025, about 0.4% of TCIL's standalone turnover — six Nature Trails resorts. “The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended 31st December 2025 was INR 70 Crores representing ~0.4% of the total standalone turnover of the Company for the year ended 31st December 2025.” — *Scheme*
12. Consideration is all-paper at 81:100, no cash; TCIL retains its existing SHRL stake, leaving promoters at 65.55% (including 7% held by TCIL) and public at 32.30% of SHRL. “for every 100 (One Hundred only) equity shares of Thomas Cook (India) Limited of face value of INR 1/- each credited as fully paid up, the issue and allotment by Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited of 81 (Eighty One only) equity shares of Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited of face value of INR 10/-each credited as fully paid up ("Share Entitlement Ratio").” — *Scheme*
13. Three dormant shells (TC Visa Services, Jardin Travel Solutions, Borderless Travel Services — FY25 turnover Rs 1.2 cr, nil and nil) are folded into TCIL purely to cut compliance and overhead and free management attention. “TCVSL, JTSL and BTSL are dormant and non-operative companies, incurring unnecessary compliance and administrative costs.” — *Scheme*
14. The Rs 4-to-Rs 3 face-value reduction involves no payout to shareholders and no change in share count; it is a balance-sheet right-sizing aimed at EPS, and is stated not to prejudice creditors. “The Management of TCIL believes that the proposed reduction of share capital is required to right size the balance sheet and capital structure of TCIL such that TCIL has a more efficient capital structure and the shareholders also benefit in terms of improved earnings per share.” — *Scheme*
15. The 4-into-1 share consolidation is justified on ratio optics — making reported per-share metrics reflect intrinsic value and signal financial stability. “The Management of TCIL believes that the proposed consolidation of the face value of its equity shares will result in a significant improvement in certain key financial ratios.” — *Scheme*
16. Six weeks before the announcement, management told investors asking about the ~INR 1,000 crore gross cash pile that no cash-return or acquisition discussions were live — no separation was signalled on this call. “But currently, there are no conversations around either any kind of disbursement of cash to shareholders or for that matter, any acquisition.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=c7f0dda1-3b3e-4381-8413-8467a63a4eec.pdf)*
17. The opposite-direction precursor: in March 2025 TCIL bought the Nature Trails resorts business into itself by slump sale (three resorts near Mumbai, 80-90 rooms, INR 10-15 crores revenue) — the very undertaking now being demerged out to Sterling. “We completed this, the slump sale in March. Now this actually includes 3 resorts close to Bombay.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=450ff761-fa88-4aee-a8d9-dc9675000d91.pdf)*
18. Analyst pressure on Sterling's standalone performance versus listed hospitality peers, which Lalvani answered by citing the completed transformation from vacation-ownership to a hospitality model. “But if you see, if you see the revenue, we are quite underperforming the industry.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=450ff761-fa88-4aee-a8d9-dc9675000d91.pdf)*
19. Standing investor concern the separation does not address: Sterling's EBIT stayed around INR 129 crores for two years despite roughly 1,200-1,300 extra rooms, attributed to membership-revenue sunset, resort ramp-up lags and ROU depreciation. “But our EBIT continues to actually be steady in terms of INR 129 crores over the last 2 years, in fact, a decline from FY '24.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d884e7c7-ee2e-41fb-b1b5-e6408e592685.pdf)*

**How it evolved:** Across the May 2025, Aug 2025, Nov 2025 and Feb 2026 calls there is no hint of a separation: the only structural move discussed is the opposite direction — the March 2025 slump sale pulling Nature Trails' three Mumbai-area resorts (80-90 rooms, INR 10-15 crores revenue) into TCIL — while analysts push on cash use and on why Sterling's EBIT stayed flat at ~INR 129 crores despite adding 1,200-1,300 rooms, and on 6 February 2026 Mahesh Iyer still says "there are no conversations around either any kind of disbursement of cash to shareholders or for that matter, any acquisition." The Board then granted in-principle approval on 20 March 2026 and the full composite scheme (demerger, 4:1 consolidation, merger of three dormant subsidiaries, Rs 4-to-Rs 3 capital reduction) was announced that day. It was discussed on an earnings call for the first time on 13 May 2026, where Iyer framed it as a "strategic divestment"/value unlock, Vikram Lalvani confirmed "the demerger process from Thomas Cook has also been initiated," and Debasis Nandy reaffirmed the original 12-15 month timeline with completion expected by Q1 FY28. Execution then tracked that guidance without the plan itself changing: BSE no-adverse-observation on 31 August 2026, NSE no-objection on 1 September 2026, SHRL's registered office shifted from Tamil Nadu to Maharashtra effective 13 July 2026, and an NCLT Mumbai procedural order dated 4 November 2026 admitting the application and directing TCIL shareholder and unsecured-creditor meetings.

**What management expects from it:** TCIL: streamlined capital structure, resources focused on travel and financial services, improved EPS from the 4:1 consolidation, Rs 4-to-Rs 3 reduction and dormant-subsidiary merger, lower admin cost. SHRL: separate listing on BSE/NSE, own growth path in fast-growing hospitality, hospitality-expert ownership of the resorts. Both: differentiated investor cohorts, sector-aligned strategies, improved operational efficiency and profitability.

*Not explained on the calls:* No valuation methodology or derivation of the 81:100 ratio, no quantified value unlock or SHRL financials post-demerger, no accounting treatment of the capital reduction, no shareholder-vote or listing-date specifics.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Unlock value by separating resorts into SHRL, which has hospitality expertise; SHRL "matured over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity"; attract differentiated investor cohorts.
- *What it reveals:* The demerged undertaking is tiny — INR 70 Crores turnover, ~0.4% of TCIL standalone. The real asset is SHRL itself: 78 resorts, ~3,800 rooms, FY26 revenue INR 5,487 mn, EBITDA 31%, PBT INR 1,142 mn, debt-free, cash ~INR 3,400 mn, 25 straight profitable quarters.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *Read next:* Shareholder meeting notice: SHRL abridged prospectus, valuation report, post-demerger balance sheets of TCIL and SHRL.
- *In their words:* “Accordingly, the Board of TCIL is of the view that for better focus and maximum result, it is better to divest the Resorts and Resort Management Business into SHRL and subsequently list SHRL.”
