**What the documents themselves say about the differences:**

- **other** — parent / remaining: TCIL standalone turnover for the year ended 31st December 2025 is the base; the resort business being separated is a very small fraction of it; separated business: Demerged Undertaking turnover INR 70 Crores, ~0.4% of total standalone turnover; TCIL "owns and/ or operates 6 resorts directly under the brand name Nature Trails" “The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended 31st December 2025 was INR 70 Crores representing ~0.4% of the total standalone turnover of the Company for the year ended 31st December 2025.”
- **growth** — parent / remaining: Group revenue fell 10% in Q4 FY26 to INR 17,707 million; FY26 consolidated income up 3% to INR 83,982 million with EBT 14% lower at INR 3,268 million; separated business: Sterling grew 19% on top line in the quarter and 7% for the full year; Q4 FY26 total revenue INR 1,408 million, up 14%, with room revenue up nearly 40% at INR 672 million “Sterling Resorts also contributed positively to the overall group's performance with 19% increase in top line during the quarter and 7% growth for the full year on the back of a growing resort network.”
- **operating margin** — parent / remaining: FY26 travel segment EBIT down 11% to INR 2,218 million with an EBIT margin of 3.3%; forex FY26 revenue and EBIT flat at INR 3,261 million and INR 1,493 million, EBIT margin 46%; DEI posted EBIT of negative INR 10 crores in Q4 FY26; separated business: Sterling FY26 EBITDA INR 1,701 million at 31% margin and PBT INR 1,142 million at 21% margin; Q4 FY26 EBITDA INR 348 million (up 10%), PBT INR 207 million (up 18%); 25th consecutive profitable quarter “EBITDA stood at INR 1,701 million, and the margins are healthy at 31%. Our profit before tax is at INR 1,142 million with PBT margins of 21%.”
- **debt and leverage** — parent / remaining: Group carries debt — "we have about INR 2,600 crores of cash and equivalents ... INR 1,600 crores of float minus the debt of INR 277 crores", net cash close to INR 730–740 crores (Q4 FY26); ECLGS of about INR 85–90 crores to be repaid over the next two years; separated business: Sterling is debt-free with cash reserves close to INR 3,400 million, grown at a multiyear CAGR of 55% “Our cash reserve stands close to INR 3,400 million, while continuing to maintain a completely debt-free balance sheet.”
- **cash** — parent / remaining: Group net cash moved from INR 405 crores (December '24) to about INR 780 crores (December '25); intended uses are technology capex, paying off long-term loans and inorganic opportunities; separated business: Sterling's operating free cash flow for Q3 FY26 was INR 346 million, up 52% year-on-year; cash and investments INR 3,243 million at December 31, 2025, up 54% over last year “So against the INR 780 crores that I talked about in December '25, the corresponding number for December '24 would have been INR 405 crores after taking out the float money and any debt that we had.”
- **capex and capital intensity** — parent / remaining: Parent's investment is directed at technology — "there will be increasing investment in technology"; capital structure to be "right sized" by reducing face value from Rs. 4 to Rs. 3 per share; separated business: Sterling expands on an asset-right model: 78 resorts/approx. 3,800 rooms across 65 destinations, targeting 95 resorts and 4,500 rooms in 2027, with 62% of rooms P&L led and 38% managed inventory, plus 3 land banks; cost of a typical incremental room approximately INR 12–13 lakhs “Today, 62% of our rooms are P&L led, while 38% of our rooms are managed inventory. As we scale further, we are consciously optimizing our portfolio through a judicious mix of P&L-led growth and an asset-light expansion, which is what we've been saying in an asset-right model.”
- **return on capital** — parent / remaining: Capital reduction is expected to improve the parent's key financial ratios and earnings per share: "a) More efficient capital structure of TCIL b) Improved earnings per share of TCIL"; separated business: Sterling reports growth with rising operating leverage and cash generation rather than stated return-on-capital figures “The Board of TCIL believes that the proposed reduction of share capital is required to right size the balance sheet and capital structure of TCIL such that TCIL has a more efficient capital structure and the shareholders also benefit in terms of improved earnings per share.”
- **tax** — parent / remaining: Parent will move to the new tax regime from FY27 and expects to utilise its entire MAT credit: "effective '26-'27 we'll move into that new regime"; the Scheme is to be implemented under Section 2(19AA), 2(1B) of the Income-tax Act, 1961; separated business: not stated for the separated business “So the government has now mandated that all companies have to move to the new tax regime if they want to utilize the MAT. And therefore, we will also do so. So effective '26-'27 we'll move into that new regime.”
- **working capital** — parent / remaining: TCIL has 1,233 unsecured creditors (Rs. 21,08,90,00,000/-) and 6 secured creditors with aggregate outstanding liability of Rs. 66,94,98,851/-; separated business: SHRL has 1,502 unsecured creditors (14,50,99,123) and no secured creditors “The unsecured creditors of the First, Second, Third, Fourth and Fifth Applicant Companies, as on 30.06.2026, are predominantly trade payables, including amounts payable on demand, which are proposed to be discharged in the ordinary course of business in accordance with the respective working capital cycles.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

HEGAM's separation is the "Composite Scheme of Arrangement" among HEG Advanced Materials Limited (formerly HEG Limited, the Demerged Company), HEG Limited (formerly HEG Graphite Limited, the Resulting Company) and Bhilwara Energy Limited (the Transferor Company): the legacy Graphite Undertaking — the graphite electrodes business, plus the overseas investment and the assets and liabilities of the TAWA power plant — was demerged into the Resulting Company on a going-concern basis with mirror shares issued to HEGAM shareholders, while Bhilwara Energy Limited was simultaneously amalgamated into HEGAM. As the filings present it, the purpose is to put the mature, cyclical electrodes business (FY26 revenue ₹2,568.50 crore, H1 FY27 ₹1,207.36 crore and PAT ₹192.33 crore, carrying ₹4,419.21 crore of segment assets and ₹1,245.85 crore of liabilities) in one listed vehicle, and leave HEGAM as a "technology-led, globally competitive advanced materials platform" spanning anode materials (TACC), graphene (HEG Graphene Materials), battery energy storage (Replus Engitech, 74% held) and green power. The amalgamation of Bhilwara Energy brings 278 MW of debt-free hydro (86 MW MPCL + 192 MW AD Hydro) plus 14 MW of wind into HEGAM, which the CFO says "provides a sound financial foundation for the Group" with "stable cash flows of over ₹300 crore" annually — i.e. the hydro cash flow and the ₹1,322.84 crore cash pile now sit against the heavy new-materials capex rather than against electrodes. The problem it solves is capital allocation and identity: HEGAM's board on 3 November 2026 approved a revised Phase-1 anode cost of ~₹2,350 crore (20,000 MT, COD June 2027, 61% built), a ₹1,606 crore Phase-2 to 44,000 MT by March 2029, a ₹475 crore crucible plant for "backward integration" and cost optimisation, and a ₹500 crore 500 MTPA graphene plant — none of which belong on an electrode balance sheet. The company also altered its main object clause to insert "Anode, Graphene, crucible, advanced carbon materials and other allied material" (CIN changed from L23109MP1972PLC008290 to L35100MP1972PLC008290) and implemented an ESOP of up to 98,93,970 options, so each entity can be objected, incentivised and financed on its own. Leadership was split along the same line: Ravi Jhunjhunwala moved to Chairman, MD & CEO of the demerged HEG Limited (graphite), while Riju Jhunjhunwala leads HEGAM and has now taken the chair of MPCL and AD Hydro. A lender appears in the record on the power side: CYHPL bought Statkraft's 49% of MPCL on 17 November 2025 and intends to merge MPCL and ADHPL into itself "for consolidating the hydro power asstes of the group in the CYHPL in line with undertaking given by CYHPL to ICICI Bank."

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The Scheme's core mechanic: the Graphite Undertaking — including the overseas investment and the TAWA power plant assets and liabilities — goes out to the Resulting Company, and Bhilwara Energy comes in. “the demerger of the Graphite Undertaking including overseas investment and assets and liabilities pertaining to TAWA power plant of the Company into the Resulting Company and amalgamation of the Transferor Company with the Company” — *Scheme*
2. The press release states plainly what moved where on the 1 September 2026 effective date, and that the two sides are now reported separately as continuing and discontinued operations. “Under the Scheme, the graphite electrodes business was transferred to HEG Limited (earlier known as HEG Graphite Limited), and Bhilwara Energy Limited was amalgamated into the Company.” — *Scheme*
3. Riju Jhunjhunwala frames the remaining entity's purpose as a technology-led advanced materials platform across anode, graphene, BESS and green power, with "research to revenue" as the motto. “Q2 FY27 reflects our continued progress towards building HEG Advanced Materials into a technology -led, globally competitive advanced materials platform.” — *Scheme*
4. CFO Neha Rajvanshi explains the financial logic of pulling hydro in: the debt-free green power business funds and underwrites the developmental verticals. “Our Green Power Business, with its differentiated model, profitable operations, debt -free position and stable cash flows, provides a sound financial foundation for the Group.” — *Scheme*
5. The scale of that foundation: 278 MW of hydro in Himachal (86 MW MPCL + 192 MW AD Hydro) plus 14 MW wind, all debt-free, against H1 FY27 cash of ₹1,322.84 crore. “Both operating hydro projects and the wind project are debt -free, and the existing hydro assets generate annually stable cash flows of over ₹300 crore.” — *Scheme*
6. Immediately post-demerger the board sanctioned the capex the new entity exists to carry: Phase-1 20,000 MT anode revised to ~₹2,350 crore (COD June 2027), Phase-2 24,000 MT for ~₹1,606 crore to reach 44,000 MT by March 2029. “Proposal for expansion plan by increasing the capacity from 20,000 MT to 44,000 MT.  The estimated cost is ~ Rs. 1606 crore with target COD by March 2029.” — *Scheme*
7. The ₹475 crore, 80,000-unit crucible plant is justified as backward integration into the anode line rather than as a new market. “The project is expected to strengthen backward integration, optimize procurement costs, and improve operational  efficiencies,  thereby supporting the long-term growth and competitiveness of the subsidiary.” — *Scheme*
8. The ₹500 crore, 500 MTPA graphene plant in HEG Graphene Materials Limited is positioned as a new growth avenue built through a subsidiary. “The proposed project is expected to create a new avenue for business growth through the subsidiary, strengthen the Company's long-term business prospects, and contribute to sustainable  value  creation  for stakeholders” — *Scheme*
9. The legal identity was re-pointed at the new businesses: the object clause was amended to insert anode, graphene, crucible and advanced carbon materials, which changed the CIN from L23109MP1972PLC008290 to L35100MP1972PLC008290. “Alteration of the main object clause of Memorandum of Association (MOA) of the company by inserting the objects relating to Anode, Graphene, crucible, advanced carbon materials and other allied material, subject to the approval of shareholders.” — *Scheme*
10. A lender's requirement drives the parallel power-side restructuring: CYHPL, having bought Statkraft's 49% of MPCL on 17 November 2025, plans to acquire the remaining 51% and merge MPCL and ADHPL into itself. “Theproposed acquisition andmerger isbeing done forconsolidating thehydro power asstes of the group in the CYHPL in line with undertaking given by CYHPL to ICICI Bank.” — *Scheme*
11. Shareholders, not just the board, carried the Scheme — approved at the NCLT-convened meeting of 5 May 2026, sanctioned by NCLT Indore on 13 August 2026, effective 1 September 2026 with 1 April 2024 as appointed date. “The equity shareholders at the NCLT -convened meeting held on May 05, 2026  have passed the resolution with requisite majority approv ing the Scheme .” — *Scheme*
12. Management had been briefing investors on the Scheme well before effectiveness, via a dedicated webinar in January 2026. “Please find below the link for Video Recording of Webinar on Update on Composite Scheme of Arrangement held on 19th January, 2026 at 1600 hrs IST.” — *Scheme*
13. The split is also a leadership and generational split: Ravi Jhunjhunwala took the graphite entity, Riju Jhunjhunwala runs HEGAM and from 3 November 2026 chairs MPCL and AD Hydro. “He was the Chairman, Managing Director & CEO of HEG Limited (now renamed as HEG Advanced Materials Limited ), (until effectiveness of the Composite Scheme of Arrangement) .” — *Scheme*
14. Reporting consequence management flags for investors: the two halves are no longer comparable, and the unlisted Resulting Company's results are being published through HEGAM until its shares list. “Current financial figures are not comparable to previous financial figures owing to demerger of HEG Limited.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** No earnings-call transcripts were supplied, so the sequence can only be traced through filings: by 19 January 2026 the Scheme was already public enough to warrant an investor "Webinar on Update on Composite Scheme of Arrangement," and the 49% MPCL buy-out from Statkraft (SPA 9 September 2025, closed 17 November 2025) had pre-positioned the hydro assets. Shareholders approved it at the NCLT-convened meeting on 5 May 2026 with requisite majority; the NCLT Indore Bench sanctioned it on 13 August 2026; the board fixed 1 September 2026 as Effective Date (Appointed Date backdated to 1 April 2024) and allotted the new shares on 7 September 2026, lifting paid-up capital from ₹38.60 crore to ₹65.96 crore. Only after effectiveness did the plan visibly widen from "separate graphite" to "build out advanced materials": the 3 November 2026 board added Phase-2 anode (44,000 MT), crucibles, graphene, an ESOP and the new object clause, while on 29–30 October 2026 the object-clause CIN change was registered and HEGAM had to publish the unlisted Resulting Company's results on its behalf pending listing.

**What management expects from it:** Graphite stands alone as HEG Limited (FY26 revenue ₹2,568.50 crore), pending listing. HEGAM becomes a focused advanced-materials platform — anode 20,000→44,000 MT, crucibles, 500 MTPA graphene, Replus BESS (1→6 GWh), 278 MW debt-free hydro giving ₹300 crore-plus annual cash flow and ₹1,322.84 crore cash to fund capex — with diversified revenues, ESOP-aligned talent and "multiple avenues for value creation."

*Not explained on the calls:* No earnings-call transcripts were provided, so no Q&A, no Scheme rationale clause, no share-exchange ratio, valuation, debt allocation, target multiples, or named investor/partner demands.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* Graphite carried Rs 4,601.53 cr assets vs Rs 1,357.07 cr liabilities (June 30, 2026) and earned Rs 319.71 cr H1 FY27 PAT; parent keeps debt-free hydro with over Rs 300 cr annual cash flows and Rs 1,322.84 cr cash.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *Read next:* HEG Limited's listing/trading approval intimation, and its standalone balance sheet borrowings of Rs 708.97 cr.
- *In their words:* “Under the Scheme, the graphite electrodes business was transferred to HEG Limited (earlier known as HEG Graphite Limited), and Bhilwara Energy Limited was amalgamated into the Company.”

**What the documents themselves say about the differences:**

- **cash** — parent / remaining: Green power provides stable cash flows: hydro assets generate annually over ₹300 crore; consolidated cash and bank balances of ₹1322.84 crore as on 30 September 2026; separated business: Graphite electrodes described as a mature, cash-generative business; HEG Limited's own cash & cash equivalents were ₹66.67 crore as at 30 September 2026 “The restructuring is designed to unlock long-term value for shareholders by giving investors direct and differentiated exposure to a mature, cash-generative graphite electrode business on the one hand, and a fast-scaling growth platform focused on advanced materials, battery energy solutions and renewable energy on the other.”
- **debt and leverage** — parent / remaining: Hydro and wind assets debt-free; TACC's anode project funded 65:35 debt-equity with a fully guaranteed INR12,030 million term loan and INR4,000 million of OCDs from the parent; separated business: HEG Limited (graphite) shows current borrowings of ₹79.08 crore and total liabilities of ₹1,390.86 crore against total assets of ₹4,698.79 crore as at 30 September 2026 “Both operating hydro projects and the wind project are debt-free, and the existing hydro assets generate annually stable cash flows of over ₹300 crore.”
- **capex and capital intensity** — parent / remaining: Anode Phase-1 revised to ~Rs. 2,350 crore, 20,000 MT to 44,000 MT expansion ~Rs. 1,606 crore, crucible plant ~Rs. 475 crore, graphene 500 MT ~Rs. 500 crore, 200 MWh BESS IPP ₹227.8 crore; separated business: Graphite electrodes: 15,000 TPA capacity addition over 30 months at approx. Rs. 650 Crores, financed by "Internal accruals and debt if required" (Board approval 30 July 2025, pre-demerger) “Board approves expansion of current 20,000 MT capacity anode plant to 44,000 MT at a capex of INR 1606 Cr ( 20,000 MT to come into operation by Jun 2027 and balance 24,000 MT by March 2029 )”
- **operating margin** — parent / remaining: H1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA of ₹438.00 crore and PAT of ₹269.07 crore on revenue from continuing operations of ₹725.80 crore; TACC's anode project expected to earn gross margins ~55% and EBITDA margins ~30%; separated business: HEG Limited (graphite): profit before tax of ₹319.71 crore on revenue from operations of ₹1,421.31 crore for the half year ended 30 September 2026; graphite segment results of INR 149.64 crore on segment revenue of INR 677.77 crore in Q1 FY27 “Ind-Ra believes this is likely to support healthy gross margins and EBITDA margins of around 55% and 30%, respectively, with the project remaining comfortable for debt servicing even at EBITDA margins of about 20% over the loan tenure.”
- **working capital** — parent / remaining: TACC's anode operations expected to be working capital-intensive, with inventory holding of four-to-six months, receivables of two-to-three months and creditors of two-to-three months; separated business: not stated for the graphite business “Consequently , Ind-Ra expects the net working capital-to-revenue ratio to range between 25% and 30% post the commencement of operations.”
- **growth** — parent / remaining: A "fast-scaling green tech growth platform"; global lithium-ion battery production expected to grow from about 2.3 TWh in 2025 to about 8 TWh by 2035, with non-China anode demand set to exceed 1 Mn tons by 2030; separated business: "a mature cash-generating graphite electrode business"; Q1 FY27 graphite segment revenue up 11.3% year-on-year “These businesses have different growth drivers, risk profiles, capital needs and valuation frameworks.”
- **tax** — parent / remaining: Shareholders apportion 27.60% of pre-demerger cost of acquisition to HEG Advanced Materials Limited; separated business: 72.40% of pre-demerger cost of acquisition apportioned to HEG Graphite Limited; GST proceedings for FY 2020-21 proposing recovery of IGST refunds with penalty of ₹282.34 crore were dropped on 15 October 2026 and sit with the Resulting Company “The above-mentioned demerger envisaged under the Scheme satisfies all conditions under Section 2(35) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 ("IT Act") and hence, the demerger is tax neutral in the hands of shareholders of the Demerged Company under the IT Act in view of the exemption granted under Section 70(k) of the IT Act.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: Reported results now split continuing and discontinued operations, and are not comparable with earlier periods; separated business: HEG Limited's comparative figures are extracted from the books of HEG Advanced Materials Limited under common-control accounting “The HEG Composite Scheme became effective on 1 September 2026. Under the Scheme, the graphite electrodes business was transferred to HEG Limited (earlier known as HEG Graphite Limited), and Bhilwara Energy Limited was amalgamated into the Company. The results accordingly present continuing and discontinued operations separately. Current financial figures are not comparable to previous financial figures owing to demerger of HEG Limited.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The separation at issue is the demerger of Lloyds Enterprises Limited's (LEL) Real Estate Business Undertaking into a new, separately listed vehicle, Lloyds Realty Limited (LRL), carried out inside a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232 read with Section 66 of the Companies Act, 2013 that the Board approved on 22 December 2025; the same scheme first merges Lloyds Realty Developers Limited (LRDL, Transferor 1) and Indrajit Properties Private Limited (IPPL, Transferor 2) into LEL, so that all realty assets sit in one place before being carved out into LRL. The only rationale management itself states is in the Chairman's speech at the 40th AGM (9 July 2026): the merger-and-demerger scheme means 'our real estate business will be listed, unlocking its true potential and delivering greater value to shareholders', set against a realty platform spread across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Panvel, Khopoli, Dadar and Thane with 'nearly 14 million square feet of upcoming projects under development' — i.e. a capital-hungry pipeline that needs its own currency and price discovery. For the parallel group merger the Chairman gives the generic benefits: 'enhance operational efficiencies, optimize resource utilization, strengthen the overall business structure, and create sustainable long-term value for shareholders'. The filings show why real estate sat awkwardly inside LEL: for 9M FY26 the Real Estate segment did only ₹53.30 crore of revenue and ₹0.88 crore of segment result (down from ₹11.26 crore) on ₹993.09 crore of segment assets and ₹553.40 crore of segment liabilities, while Steel (₹492.80 crore revenue, ₹255.60 crore result) and Engineering (₹795.75 crore, ₹151.08 crore) carried the group, and subsidiary LRDL itself ran a ₹1.26 crore net loss; consolidated FY26 total income was ~₹2,200 crore against ~₹800 crore standalone, with LEL otherwise functioning as a holding/trading company (stakes of ~4.13% in Lloyds Metals and Energy, ~31% in Geomysore, and material subsidiary Lloyds Engineering Works with a group order book of ~₹8,000 crore and 44% PBT growth). No investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for the separation; the only parties on record demanding anything are the regulators — SEBI, NSE and BSE required LEL to disclose to shareholders the 'Need for the merger/demerger, rationale of the scheme and swap ratio', synergies, minority impact and a cost-benefit analysis, plus lender NOCs and 'Conditions imposed by lenders, if any'. The same unlock-by-listing logic recurs twice more in the group: LEWL's absorption of Lloyds Infra, Metalfab and Techno Industries to end 'silos' and create a ₹6,150 crore-order-book design-to-execution entity, and the SISCOL acquisition (88.12% for ~₹1,073.40 crore), where a DRHP within 30 months is meant to 'facilitate independent price discovery', market visibility and access to capital.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. Board approval on 22 December 2025 of the Composite Scheme: LRDL and IPPL merge into LEL, and LEL's Real Estate Business Undertaking is demerged into Lloyds Realty Limited; filed with BSE and NSE the same day. “The Scheme is filed with Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) & National Stock Exchange (NSE) on December 22, 2025.” — *Scheme*
2. The only explicit purpose management gives for the demerger, in the Chairman's speech at the 40th AGM (9 July 2026): a separate listing of the real estate business to unlock value, against a pipeline of nearly 14 million sq ft across MMR, Panvel, Khopoli, Dadar and Thane. “Importantly, as a result of the merger and demerger scheme approved during the year, our real estate business will be listed, unlocking its true potential and delivering greater value to shareholders.” — *Scheme*
3. For the group merger leg, the Chairman offers only structural benefits, noting approvals from NSE, BSE and SEBI and an application filed with the NCLT. “This strategic merger is expected to enhance operational efficiencies, optimize resource utilization, strengthen the overall business structure, and create sustainable long-term value for shareholders.” — *Scheme*
4. NSE's 15 May 2026 observation letter confirms the demerger is a route to a new listed realty entity, but conditions it on an Information Memorandum, newspaper advertisement, frozen shares until trading permission, and listing within 60 days of the NCLT order. “However, the listing of shares of Lloyds Realty Limited  is at the discretion of the Exchange.” — *Scheme*
5. The parties actually demanding an articulated rationale are the regulators: SEBI and both exchanges ordered LEL to put the need, rationale, swap ratio, synergies, minority impact and cost-benefit analysis in the shareholder explanatory statement. “Need for the merger/demerger, rationale of the scheme and swap ratio, synergies of business of the entities involved in the scheme, impact of the scheme on the minority shareholders and cost benefit analysis of the scheme.” — *Scheme*
6. Lenders are referenced only as a consent/disclosure requirement imposed by SEBI — NOCs from lending banks, FIs and debenture trustees, plus any lender-imposed conditions — not as instigators of the separation. “Conditions imposed by lenders, if any, may be disclosed to the public shareholders along with the impact of same on the scheme.” — *Scheme*
7. The mirror-image transaction at material subsidiary LEWL (announced 29 December 2025) consolidates LICL, Metalfab and Techno Industries into one vertically integrated design-to-execution entity with a ~₹6,150 crore combined order book, ~38.1 crore new shares and equity rising from 147.42 to 185.52 crore shares, appointed date 1 April 2025. “By bringing Lloyds Infra, Metalfab, and Techno Industries under one banner, we are eliminating silos.” — *Scheme*
8. The same unlock-by-separate-listing logic is applied to the June 2026 SISCOL acquisition (88.12% for ~₹1,073.40 crore; FY26 turnover ₹816.87 crore, net profit ₹43.42 crore), with a DRHP promised within 30 months of Stage 1. “The proposed listing of SISCOL is expected to facilitate independent price discovery of its business, enhance its market visibility and access to capital, and unlock value for all its stakeholders, including the Company as a significant shareholder.” — *Scheme*
9. The filings' own numbers show the real-estate leg was the group's weakest earner before separation: 9M FY26 segment revenue of ₹53.30 crore and segment result of ₹0.88 crore (vs ₹11.26 crore a year earlier) on ₹993.09 crore of segment assets and ₹553.40 crore of segment liabilities, with LRDL itself loss-making. “We have not conducted a review of the Subsidiary (Lloyds Realty Developers Limited) included in the unaudited consolidated financial results. whose financial information reflects total revenues of <53.30 and total Net Loss after tax of t1.26. crores.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** No earnings-call transcripts are on file, so the idea is traceable only through filings. It surfaces fully formed on 22 December 2025, when the Board approved the Composite Scheme (LRDL + IPPL into LEL, real-estate undertaking out into LRL) and filed it with BSE and NSE the same day; a week later (29 December 2025) the group announced the separate LEWL merger of LICL, Metalfab and Techno Industries, and the 9 February 2026 results notes restated the Scheme verbatim alongside a ₹500 crore NCD approval, the ₹361 crore Tata Capital/Bajaj Finance/Jio Credit borrowings and the block-deal sale of LEWL shares to Thriveni Earthmovers. On 15–16 May 2026 LEL received NSE's 'No objection' and BSE's 'no adverse observations' (with LRL's listing left to exchange discretion, an Information Memorandum, frozen shares and a 60-day post-NCLT listing timetable), followed on 18–19 May 2026 by exchange NOCs and CCI clearance for the LEWL merger; by the 9 July 2026 AGM the Chairman described the scheme as approved, an NCLT application filed, and the realty business as one that 'will be listed'.

**What management expects from it:** For the realty entity: a separate listing of the ~14 mn sq ft Mumbai-region pipeline, 'unlocking its true potential' and greater shareholder value. For the retained LEL group: enhanced operational efficiencies, optimised resource utilisation, a stronger business structure and sustainable long-term value, leaving a holding/trading company around LEWL (~₹8,000 crore order book, 44% PBT growth), Lloyds Metals, Geomysore and SISCOL.

*Not explained on the calls:* No earnings-call transcripts on file; no swap ratio, valuation, debt or asset split for LRL, no margin or capital targets, no timeline, no named investor or lender demand.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Chairman: "as a result of the merger and demerger scheme approved during the year, our real estate business will be listed, unlocking its true potential and delivering greater value to shareholders"
- *What it reveals:* Real estate segment assets Rs. 993.09 cr vs liabilities Rs. 553.40 cr, 9M FY26 sales Rs. 53.30 cr and segment result Rs. 0.88 cr, yet "nearly 14 million square feet of upcoming projects under development" across MMR, Panvel, Khopoli, Dadar, Thane
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *Read next:* Lloyds Realty Limited's Information Memorandum and the scheme's valuation report — assets, liabilities and debt transferred to LRL
- *In their words:* “Importantly, as a result of the merger and demerger scheme approved during the year, our real estate business will be listed, unlocking its true potential and delivering greater value to shareholders.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

This is not a sale but a three-way split by demerger: a Scheme of Arrangement approved by MSL's board (first on 22 May 2026, then re-approved 7 October 2026 with an Appointed Date of 1 October 2026) carves two 'Demerged Undertakings' out of Maharashtra Seamless into two wholly owned subsidiaries that will themselves be listed on BSE and NSE. Demerged Undertaking 1 — the Mangaon, Maharashtra seamless pipe plant (125,000 MTPA) plus the 10 MW captive solar plant at Beed — goes to MSL Seamless Tubes Limited (MSTL); Demerged Undertaking 2 — the Narketpally, Telangana seamless mill (200,000 MTPA), the Khetusar (20 MW) and Pokhran (5 MW) solar plants in Rajasthan, and the rig Jindal Explorer — goes to United Seamless Limited (USL), i.e. the asset base MSL bought out of IBC as United Seamless Tubulaar for INR477 crores plus INR73 crores of reactivation capex. On FY2025-26 operational turnover the split is Undertaking 1 INR793 crores (16.98%), Undertaking 2 INR693 crores (14.84%) and the residual company (Nagothane pipes, ERW, treasury) INR3,185 crores (68.18%) of INR4,671 crores. The board's stated reasons are that the undertakings have 'distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies used, operational requirements, customer profile and base, market focus, logistics consideration' — specifically three different mill technologies, CPE at Nagothane, MPM at Mangaon and FQM at Telangana, each needing its own modernization and technical expertise — so each should run as a focused, independently reported vertical. It also says manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy have 'different capital intensity and funding requirements', so splitting them allows better assessment of capital needs and more flexibility for expansion; the renewable plants are attached to the mills they can power; and the rig business, long described on calls as outside the core, is segregated because it has 'distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business'. No cash changes hands: shareholders get 1 share of INR5 in each resulting company for every 5 MSL shares, producing the same proportionate holding (promoter ~70.30%, public ~29.70%, 2,67,99,850 shares in each), which the filing calls 'value neutral'; creditor liabilities are neither reduced nor extinguished and travel with each undertaking. Notably, the nine earnings calls supplied — including Feb 2026, three months before the first board approval — contain no mention of a demerger at all; the only antecedents are repeated investor pressure to exit the rig and one shareholder's demand to split the company, and management's standing answer that it would continue 'in the steel pipe segment only' and that exit was 'for the Board to decide'.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. Two undertakings are carved out into two wholly owned subsidiaries, MSL Seamless Tubes Limited and United Seamless Limited, both to be listed, with an Appointed Date of 1 October 2026; the Mangaon 125,000 MTPA mill and the 10 MW Beed captive solar plant form Undertaking 1. “Demerged Undertaking 1: Seamless pipe manufacturing business of the Demerged Company located at Mangaon, Maharashtra (125,000 MTPA), captive solar power plant at Beed, Maharashtra (10 MW), along with the specified assets and liabilities of Demerged Undertaking 1.” — *Scheme*
2. Undertaking 2 bundles the Telangana (Narketpally) 200,000 MTPA mill with the Rajasthan solar plants and the rig Jindal Explorer into United Seamless Limited — effectively re-separating the ex-United Seamless Tubulaar asset base and the rig in one entity. “Demerged Undertaking 2: Seamless pipe manufacturing facility of the Demerged Company located at Narketpally, Telangana (200,000 MTPA), solar power plants at Khetusar (20 MW) & Pokhran (5MW) in Rajasthan, rig Jindal Explorer along with the specified assets and liabilities of Demerged Undertaking 2.” — *Scheme*
3. The headline justification is that one company holds businesses with nothing in common operationally — different geographies, products, technologies, customers and logistics — so each should be managed separately. “The said undertakings having distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies used, operational requirements, customer profile and base, market focus, logistics consideration, commercial considerations and growth opportunities.” — *Scheme*
4. The most concrete operating reason given is that the three mills run on three different pipe-making technologies, each needing its own specialised management and modernization programme — which maps exactly onto the three-way split. “The manufacturing facilities operate on different technological platforms, including CPE technology at Nagothane, MPM technology at Mangaon and FQM technology at Telangana, each requiring specialized operational management, modernization initiatives and technical expertise.” — *Scheme*
5. Capital allocation is cited: pipes, drilling and renewables have different capital intensity, so separation is meant to let each assess and fund its own needs — relevant given the stalled INR852 crore capex plan and the INR350 crore Nagothane hot-mill upgrade never started. “Efficient Capital Allocation: The manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy businesses have different capital intensity and funding requirements.” — *Scheme*
6. The rig is singled out for segregation on the grounds that it is commercially unlike pipe manufacturing — the same objection investors had raised on calls for two years. “Focused Development of Rig Operations: The rig business has distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business.” — *Scheme*
7. The renewable plants are deliberately attached to the mills they sit beside rather than kept central, framed as energy-management efficiency and sustainability support for each business. “The renewable power assets proposed to be transferred along with the respective undertakings are expected to provide better operational alignment, energy management efficiencies and support sustainability initiatives of the corresponding businesses.” — *Scheme*
8. Separate financial and operational reporting per entity is itself presented as a benefit — transparency and performance evaluation — which speaks to the calls where management refused to give product-wise or mill-wise margins. “Improved Transparency and Value Creation: The proposed demerger would result in creation of focused business entities with independent financial and operational reporting, thereby enhancing transparency, improving performance evaluation and facilitating long-term value creation for stakeholders.” — *Scheme*
9. No cash is paid; shareholders receive 1 INR5 share in each resulting company per 5 MSL shares, giving identical proportionate ownership (promoter 70.3008%, public 29.6992%, 2,67,99,850 shares each) and, the board says, value neutrality. “The above share exchange ratios shall ensure same proportionate shareholding structure of Resulting Company 1 and Resulting Company 2 with Demerged Company and hence Scheme shall be value neutral to the Demerged Company's shareholders.” — *Scheme*
10. Lenders are explicitly left untouched: no arrangement or compromise with creditors, liabilities travelling with each undertaking — i.e. the split is not presented as lender-driven or a debt restructuring. “The liabilities towards the creditors of the Demerged Company and/or the Resulting Companies under the Scheme are neither being reduced nor being extinguished and the liabilities pertaining to the respective undertakings shall be assumed and discharged by the respective Resulting Companies in the ordinary course of business.” — *Scheme*
11. The plan was not stable: approved 22 May 2026, pulled back for review on 15 June 2026, and re-approved only on 7 October 2026 with tightened wording ('specified' rather than 'related' assets, 'same proportionate' rather than 'mirror' shareholding) and slightly revised indicative share counts (promoter 70.2784% to 70.3008%). “This is further to the intimation dated 22nd May, 2026, about the approval of the Scheme of Arrangement by the Board of Directors of the Company, we have to inform you that the said Scheme is under further review and would be placed before any subsequent Board Meeting for its approval and would be submitted to Stock Exchanges thereafter.” — *Scheme*
12. The first hint of any separation was about the rig: asked whether MSL would keep two verticals, the Chairman declined to commit, while noting day rates had risen (~$40,000/day, expecting a new contract above $80,000). “Well, we have to take the appropriate decision at the right time.” — *[Feb 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=b72c7b85-4c69-46c2-a090-5ef0d9c829bd.pdf)*
13. An investor asked outright about demerging or selling the rig business post-May 2025; management confirmed intent but no board discussion and no valuation expectation. “It is something which we want to do, but it is subject to Board approval.” — *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=527a8802-c766-46b3-bf40-c501d9bde473.pdf)*
14. After an investor said the rig arrangement (MSL renting the rig to group company Jindal Drilling, which sub-contracts to ONGC) looked out of line with MSL's governance clean-up, management personally agreed and promised a communication once board approvals came. “You are right, and I personally agree with you, but once suitable decisions and Board approvals are received, we will send communication on this.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=daab9f9c-f377-44ab-81ff-c957deffd107.pdf)*
15. Management confirmed a rig exit had been contemplated but that the board had given no update, while re-committing to pipes only — the rig had just been recontracted to Jindal Drilling at ~$35,000/day L1, with MSL to get ~$17,000-18,000/day. “There was a view of getting out of the rig business, but we've not received any update from the Board in the Board meeting, which concluded yesterday.” — *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e6cad32a-cb31-4ae1-8cd1-8c8bd7df377b.pdf)*
16. A five-year shareholder explicitly demanded the company be split so investors could choose the pipe business over the treasury/holding activity, arguing the merged picture was unclear; management offered no response. “Either divide the company in two parts. One should be a holding company, one should be a seamless company.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9f4e9de0-b4a6-4b5e-9282-3cedd1bc0c79.pdf)*
17. Six months before board approval, an analyst asked specifically about getting the Jindal Explorer rig off the books and was told there was no update, with the rig about to start a new ONGC contract. “There is no update on the proposal that you mentioned.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=92cac794-00b8-4e60-be7b-2e45526b6464.pdf)*
18. On the last call before the first board approval, management described the future as cash conservation and opportunistic distressed acquisitions, with no mention of any restructuring, while defending the INR3,500 crore treasury against shareholders noting ~50% of market cap was cash. “We are conserving cash as of now and we are on the lookout for any inorganic opportunity that may arise, but that inorganic opportunity should be at a cost level at which we are comfortable.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f71803d8-c20b-4934-a1c6-184365d050a4.pdf)*
19. The same call set out the economics of the Telangana asset that now forms United Seamless Limited: INR477 crores purchase plus INR73 crores reactivation, INR100-200 crores of EBITDA a year, and ~INR375 crores of tax saved from USTPL's INR1,500 crore-plus accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation. “We acquired it for INR477 crores, and we invested an additional INR73 crores to reactivate the mill.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f71803d8-c20b-4934-a1c6-184365d050a4.pdf)*

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced only as a rig exit: on the Feb 2024 call (30 Jan 2024) Chairman D.P. Jindal said of staying in rigs 'we have to take the appropriate decision at the right time', and on the Nov 2024 call (29 Oct 2024) an investor asked directly about demerging or selling the rig, to which management said it was something 'we want to do, but it is subject to Board approval'. Pressure widened over the next year: on the Feb 2025 call (28 Jan 2025) management personally agreed the rig-to-Jindal-Drilling structure 'doesn't look in line' with its governance clean-up, on the Jun 2025 call (27 May 2025) it confirmed 'there was a view of getting out of the rig business' with no board update, and on the Aug 2025 call (31 July 2025) a shareholder explicitly asked management to 'divide the company in two parts' — a holding company and a seamless company — and got only 'I don't have anything to add'. By the Nov 2025 call (5 Nov 2025) there was still 'no update on the proposal', and the Feb 2026 call (29 Jan 2026) discussed only cash conservation, treasury and a hunt for distressed acquisitions. The actual plan then appeared without any call commentary: board approval 22 May 2026, a 15 June 2026 notice that the Scheme was 'under further review', and a revised, re-approved Scheme on 7 October 2026 that widened it from a rig/holding split into a full three-way break-up of the three mills by technology, with 'related assets and liabilities' tightened to 'specified assets and liabilities' and 'mirror shareholding' restated as 'same proportionate shareholding'.

**What management expects from it:** Per the Scheme only: each mill run as a focused vertical with dedicated management and technology-specific modernization; sharper assessment and deployment of capital across pipes, drilling and renewables, with more flexibility for expansion; solar assets aligned to the mills they serve; the rig managed on its own terms; independent reporting improving transparency and performance evaluation; identical proportionate shareholding, so value-neutral. No margin, cost, ROCE or valuation figures were given.

*Not explained on the calls:* No call ever mentioned it. Silent on where the ~INR3,500 crore treasury, debt, ERW and premium-connections subsidiary sit, on margins, valuation, lost shared overheads, and NCLT timing.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Undertakings have distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies (CPE/MPM/FQM), customers and capital needs; demerger gives focused management, efficient capital allocation, transparency and long-term value creation, with mirror shareholding keeping it value neutral.
- *What it reveals:* Separate reporting prices each plant's economics: UD1 Rs 793 crore turnover (16.98%), UD2 Rs 693 crore (14.84%), remaining Rs 3,185 crore (68.18%). Parent retains Nagothane plus Rs 3,115 crore treasury management said to back ~50% of market cap.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* The full Scheme filed with NCLT: which specified assets, liabilities and the Rs 3,115 crore treasury stay with MSL.
- *In their words:* “The above share exchange ratios shall ensure same proportionate shareholding structure of Resulting Company 1 and Resulting Company 2 with Demerged Company and hence Scheme shall be value neutral to the Demerged Company's shareholders.”

**What the documents themselves say about the differences:**

- **capex and capital intensity** — parent / remaining: Manufacturing business retained at Nagothane; capital expenditure plan of INR852 crores, of which the Telangana finishing line (purchase orders of INR90 crores) and the cold drawn pipes project were started, with other items deferred pending reassessment; separated business: The manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy businesses being transferred are stated to have different capital intensity and funding requirements “Efficient Capital Allocation: The manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy businesses have different capital intensity and funding requirements.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: Nagothane operates on CPE technology; separated business: Mangaon (Demerged Undertaking 1) operates on MPM technology and Telangana (Demerged Undertaking 2) on FQM technology “Technology-Specific Operational Focus: The manufacturing facilities operate on different technological platforms, including CPE technology at Nagothane, MPM technology at Mangaon and FQM technology at Telangana, each requiring specialized operational management, modernization initiatives and technical expertise.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: Pipe manufacturing business; separated business: Rig business (rig Jindal Explorer) transferred with Demerged Undertaking 2, stated to have distinct operational and commercial characteristics “Focused Development of Rig Operations: The rig business has distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business.”
- **cash** — parent / remaining: Treasury of INR 3,115 crores as on 30 September 2025; liquid investments of about INR3,500 crores of which close to INR2,957 crores in mutual funds; total portfolio return in excess of 24% for the nine months ending December 2025; separated business: not stated “The second point is the treasury, which is at INR 3,115 crores as on 30th September '25.”
- **operating margin** — parent / remaining: Q2 FY '26 revenue declined by 5% to INR 1,234 crores, EBITDA declined by 27% to INR 123 crores, PAT declined by 44% to INR 130 crores, EPS INR 10 per share; management expects margins in the range of INR10,000 to INR15,000 per ton; separated business: not stated “We do not give out guidance specifically, but the only thing that I can tell you from some experience is that we don't see margins to decline materially from here. I think it will remain in the range of INR10,000 to INR15,000 per ton.”
- **growth** — parent / remaining: Order book at INR1,302 crores as of 20th January, of which 33% comprises ONGC and Oil India orders; project awards declining; dispatches of 1,03,000 tons in Q2 and 1,01,000 tons in Q3; separated business: not stated “It says that project awards have declined 27% year-on-year and 13% in quarter 2 FY '26.”
- **tax** — parent / remaining: Accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation in excess of INR1,500 crores in United Seamless Tubulaar Private Limited were set off against Maharashtra Seamless profits after the merger; separated business: not stated “Subsequent to merger of that company with Maharashtra Seamless, we were able to set off the profits of Maharashtra Seamless with the unabsorbed depreciation and accumulated losses of United Seamless Tubulaar, thereby saving tax of around INR375 crores.”
- **debt and leverage** — parent / remaining: Credit rating remains at AA+, the highest credit rating the company has received in the past 11 to 12 years; separated business: Liabilities pertaining to the respective undertakings shall be assumed and discharged by the respective Resulting Companies in the ordinary course of business “The liabilities towards the creditors of the Demerged Company and/or the Resulting Companies under the Scheme are neither being reduced nor being extinguished and the liabilities pertaining to the respective undertakings shall be assumed and discharged by the respective Resulting Companies in the ordinary course of business.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: Total renewable energy capacity of 59.5 megawatt, out of which 1 wind and 2 solar plants are in Maharashtra and 2 solar plants are in Rajasthan, earning EBITDA of approximately INR60 crores every year; separated business: Beed solar (10 MW) goes with Demerged Undertaking 1; Khetusar (20 MW) and Pokhran (5 MW) solar plants in Rajasthan go with Demerged Undertaking 2 “We already have 59.5 megawatt of renewable energy capacity, out of which 1 wind and 2 solar plants are in Maharashtra and 2 solar plants are in Rajasthan.”

*Stated figures are the documents' own (a turnover share, or the cost-of-acquisition split the company publishes for tax, which reflects relative value); the segment share is this business's revenue over the parent's sales, and the market-cap share is the entity's value over the entity plus the parent (parent ₹7,649 cr, NSE bhavcopy of 2026-11-13), both computed here.*

**In the documents' words:** “"This strategic move comes as Raymond's Real Estate Business has achieved scale, reporting revenue of INR 1,593 Cr. (43% YoY growth) and EBITDA of INR 370 Cr. in FY24, positioning it well to chart its own growth path as a separate entity." (Press Release, July 4, 2024). The turnover table in the same board disclosure states: "Turnover of Real Estate Business Undertaking as on 31 March 2024 — 1,59,265 [INR in Lakhs]; Percentage to the total turnover of RL as on 31 March 2024 — 24.16%". Apportionment of cost of acquisition of equity shares (May 13, 2025): "Raymond Limited 60.92%" and "Raymond Realty Limited 39.08%".”

**The judge's read of selling pressure:** likely — Realty is a separate industry from lifestyle/engineering and contributed only ~23% of portfolio EBITDA in H1FY27

- **Promoters in the parent, per the documents:** Raymond Limited shareholding pattern in the July 4, 2024 board disclosure: "Promoters 3,26,26,525 — 49.01%" (both pre-Scheme and post-Scheme); "Public 3,39,24,906 — 50.96%"; "Non Promoter – Non Public 22,300 — 0.03%". The Q2/H1 FY2027 group presentation (reporting benchmark 30-Sept-2026) states only a range across the three listed entities: "PROMOTER STEWARDSHIP 48.87% – 59.62% PUBLIC FREE FLOAT 40.36% – 51.10% REPORTING BENCHMARK 30-Sept-2026".
- **What the promoters will hold in the separated entity:** 2024 real estate demerger — mirror shareholding; pre and post shareholding of RRL as disclosed on July 4, 2024: pre-Scheme "Promoters 16,50,000 — 100.00"; post-Scheme "Promoters 3,26,26,525 — 49.01 / Public 3,39,24,906 — 50.96 / Non Promoter – Non Public 22,300 — 0.03"; "Upon the Scheme coming into effect on the Effective Date (as defined under the Scheme), on demerger, RRL shall issue 6,65,73,731 (Six Crores Sixty Five Lakhs Seventy Three Thousand Seven Hundred and Thirty One) Equity Shares of RRL having face value of INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten) each to the equity shareholders of RL." 2024 engineering composite scheme — "Post Scheme, RPAL & MPPL will cease to exist and shareholding in JKTTL & RGCEL will change from 100% to 66.3% as subsidiaries of Raymond Limited."; CARE Ratings (July 4, 2025): "Post the process, MPPL and RPAL will cease to exist, and RL & its promoters will hold 67.40%, MPPL promoters 28.5%, and balance will be with the others and minority shareholders of the new companies." 2023 lifestyle demerger — promoter holding in Raymond Lifestyle Limited not stated (shares issued to all RL shareholders in the ratio 4 RLL shares of INR 2 for every 5 RL shares of INR 10).
- **What a public shareholder receives:** Real estate demerger (2025): "In accordance with provisions of the Scheme, RRL shall issue and allot 1 (One) fully paid-up equity shares of RRL having face value of INR 10/- each for every 1 (One) fully paid up equity shares of INR 10/- each of RL to the shareholders of the Company whose names are recorded in the register of members and / or records of the depository as on the Record Date (i.e., Wednesday, May 14, 2025)." Lifestyle demerger (2024): "Each equity shareholder of Raymond Limited as on the Record Date, will be issued and allotted 4 (four) fully paid-up equity share(s) of INR 2 (Indian Rupees Two) each of Raymond Lifestyle Limited for every 5 (five) fully paid-up equity share(s) of INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten) each of the Raymond Limited." Engineering composite scheme (NCLT order 2025): shareholders of Raymond Limited receive nothing — "No. The shares issued by JKTTL and RGCEL would not be listed on any of the stock exchanges." and "Not applicable, since the Scheme is between subsidiaries and step-down subsidiaries of the Company." Fractional entitlements under the lifestyle scheme: "Fractional entitlement, if any, shall be consolidated and allotted to the Trustee (as defined in the Scheme), who shall hold such shares in trust on behalf of the relevant security holders entitled to such fractional entitlements, for the specific purpose of selling the same in the market and on such sale, distribute to the relevant security holders in proportion to their respective fractional entitlements, the net sale proceeds of such shares (after deduction of applicable taxes and costs incurred and subject to withholding tax, if any)."
- **Management incentives:** not stated in the documents on file.
- **Insider actions around the separation:** not stated in the documents on file.
- **Insiders, per the checklist read:** Promoter stewardship 48.87%–59.62% across the three listed entities; promoter largest shareholder and chairs the Board. Promoter-group JK Investors (Bombay) took 66,57,373 Raymond Ltd warrants at ₹497; Gautam Hari Singhania ultimate beneficial owner · *option pricing date:* not stated

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

No earnings-call transcripts were supplied ("no transcripts on file"), so this reconstruction rests solely on Raymond Limited's filings. Management's own framing, set out in the EGM explanatory statements of May 25, 2026 and September 8, 2026, is that the separation is already executed — "the demerger of its lifestyle and real estate business" — leaving Raymond Limited as "a conglomerate which is in engineering businesses through its subsidiaries," namely JK Maini Precision Technology Limited (precision engineering and auto components) and JK Maini Global Aerospace Limited (aerospace / new-age industrial and technology-led businesses), while Raymond Lifestyle Limited (branded textile, branded apparel, garmenting, high-value shirting, emerging) and Raymond Realty Limited (100-acre Thane land ~₹25,000 cr revenue potential plus asset-light Mumbai JDAs ~₹27,000 cr potential) trade separately. The problem the structure is said to solve is focus and clean capital allocation: the Q2/H1 FY2027 group update (filed November 2, 2026) titles the result "Raymond Portfolio: Pure-Play Platforms" across three listed entities, each with its own ~75%-independent board (vs a ~50% top-100 Indian average), its own ring-fenced audit/pay/risk/related-party committees, its own CARE/CRISIL ratings (RLL AA/A1+, Raymond Realty and TenX A+/A-, JKMPTL A+/A1+, JKMGAL A/A1 within ₹9,476 cr rated debt) and its own balance sheet — group net debt/EBITDA 0.43x on TTM EBITDA of ₹1,738 cr and revenue of ₹13,115 cr, liquidity up from ₹571 cr in FY20 to ₹2,791 cr, and short-term debt cut from 74% of gross debt in 2020 to 38% in 2026 with 4.24-year average maturity. It also de-concentrates earnings: non-lifestyle verticals now generate 49% of YTD EBITDA (388.16 of 792), with engineering Raymond Ltd. posting H1FY27 income of ₹1,311 cr (+17%), EBITDA ₹203 cr (+22%), PBT ₹84 cr (+69%), aerospace & defence revenue ₹262 cr (+56%) and a ₹77 cr net cash surplus, against FY21 engineering revenue of just ₹141 cr and EBITDA of ₹22 cr. The separated, residual listed company is then being funded as an acquisition vehicle described as being "at a pivotal inflection point": ₹330.88 cr of 18-month warrants at ₹497 to promoter-group JK Investors (Bombay) Limited (29.83% to 35.91% diluted; ultimate beneficial owner Gautam Hari Singhania), then ₹214.71 cr at ₹645 to Minerva Ventures Fund (0% to ~4.31%, ultimate beneficial owner Ghanshyam Hurry), with 75% earmarked for Indian and international acquisitions in aerospace, automotive and defence including acquisition-debt repayment or bridge funding, and 25% for general corporate purposes, CARE Ratings appointed monitoring agency. Nobody outside is named as having demanded the separation: no investor campaign, lender covenant or JV partner appears in the texts; the visible external pressure is from the stock exchanges, whose queries forced a June 10, 2026 corrigendum and an October 22, 2026 restatement of the allottee's diluted stake. Running the other way, the January 27, 2026 Scheme folds wholly-owned Everblue Apparel Limited (denim garmenting, ₹10,858 lakh turnover) back into Raymond Limited "to enable simplified structure and greater management focus," so the pattern management describes is separation of the big consumer and property platforms combined with re-absorption of small subsidiaries into the listed engineering holdco.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The May 27, 2026 EGM explanatory statement states the separation is complete and defines what the residual listed company now is — an engineering holdco operating through JKMPTL and JKMGAL. “Raymond Limited ("Company") is a conglomerate which is in engineering businesses through its subsidiaries and has consistently invested in building world-class capabilities across its business verticals.” — *Scheme*
2. The same statement (repeated in the September 11, 2026 notice) gives the explicit cause-and-effect: because lifestyle and real estate were demerged, the remaining entity can pursue a focused multi-sector engineering strategy. “Having undertaken significant restructuring and demerger activities in recent years — including the demerger of its lifestyle and real estate business — Raymond is now positioned to pursue an accelerated, multi-sector growth strategy through its subsidiary companies, including:” — *Scheme*
3. Management frames the moment created by the separation as requiring fresh growth capital, which is what both warrant issues (₹330.88 cr to promoter group JK Investors (Bombay) Limited at ₹497, ₹214.71 cr to Minerva Ventures Fund at ₹645) are for. “The Company is at a pivotal inflection point in its growth trajectory.” — *Scheme*
4. The November 2, 2026 Q2/H1 FY2027 group update brands the outcome of the demergers as three single-focus listed platforms: Raymond Lifestyle Limited, Raymond Realty Limited and Raymond Limited (Aerospace & Defence plus Precision Technology and Auto Components). “Raymond Portfolio: Pure-Play Platforms” — *Scheme*
5. The same update argues the separation de-risks group earnings by removing reliance on the lifestyle business, quantifying the shift precisely for H1FY27. “Non-lifestyle verticals (Realty + Raymond Ltd.) now generate 49% of YTD EBITDA (388.16 of 792), signalling an increasingly balanced, multi-engine growth profile.” — *Scheme*
6. Governance is presented as a deliberate consequence of splitting into three listed vehicles — independent boards and independently chaired audit, pay, risk and related-party committees at each entity, above what LODR requires. “This is not a statutory response to LODR, LODR would allow far less. It is a deliberate architecture.” — *Scheme*
7. Each separated entity carries its own leverage, liquidity and rating profile: group net debt/EBITDA 0.43x, ₹1,738 cr TTM EBITDA, ₹3,382 cr cash, with Raymond Limited at -0.34x and Raymond Realty at 1.70x; the engineering arm reports a ₹77 cr net cash surplus. “Net cash surplus of Rs77 Cr as of September 2026, backing disciplined growth investments.” — *Scheme*
8. Who actually put up money: the promoter group, not an outside activist or lender — the May 2026 issue is justified on promoter conviction and on speed versus a QIP or rights issue, given time-sensitive acquisition targets. “Promoter participation in the fund-raise demonstrates a strong personal commitment and conviction in the Company's strategic direction.” — *Scheme*
9. The stock exchanges, not investors, forced disclosure changes: NSE (June 3, 2026) and BSE (June 8, 2026) queries produced a corrigendum that dropped subsidiary capex/capacity expansion and re-labelled 75% of proceeds as acquisition funding including acquisition-debt repayment. “Funding acquisitions of businesses in India and internationally across targeted growth sectors either directly or through subsidiary entities for organic and inorganic growth including repayment of acquisition debt upto 75% of the aggregate proceeds of the issue; and” — *Scheme*
10. Public institutions were not uniformly convinced by the promoter-funded step: 31.72% of institutional votes polled went against the June 18, 2026 resolution (overall 96.36% in favour), whereas the October 3, 2026 Minerva resolution passed with 99.9978% in favour and institutions 100% in favour. “Whether promoter/promoter group are interested in the agenda/resolution? Yes” — *Scheme*
11. Asked on June 24-25, 2026 about a reported German engineering acquisition (Deharde), the company neither confirmed a target nor denied the programme, pointing back to the stated objects of the warrant issue. “The Company evaluates various strategic opportunities in the ordinary course, for growth and expansion of its business.” — *Scheme*
12. The January 27, 2026 Scheme of Amalgamation runs opposite to the demergers — wholly-owned Everblue Apparel Limited (denim garmenting, ₹10,858 lakh turnover, ₹376 lakh net worth) is absorbed into Raymond Limited with no shares issued, purely for structural simplicity and focus. “To enable simplified structure and greater management focus on the business, it is imperative for the Transferor Company to be merged into the Transferee Company.” — *Scheme*
13. The amalgamation rationale lists the specific benefits claimed from collapsing subsidiaries into the listed holdco, the same vocabulary used for the larger separation. “Simplification of overall group structure by fully integrating EBAL's garmenting operations directly into RL and creating efficiencies through amalgamation;” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** The idea is presented as already settled rather than emerging: by the January 27, 2026 Everblue Apparel amalgamation filing, Raymond Limited is described as holding "investment in Engineering and Aerospace business through its subsidiaries" with standalone turnover of only ₹289 lakh, and the scheme's stated logic is simplification and management focus. The May 25, 2026 board outcome and May 27, 2026 EGM notice first spell out the post-separation rationale — demerger done, engineering holdco now raising ₹330.88 cr of promoter warrants for a multi-sector growth strategy through JKMPTL and JKMGAL — and that framing is repeated verbatim in the September 8/11, 2026 notice for the ₹214.71 cr Minerva Ventures Fund issue. The plan changed under exchange pressure: the June 10, 2026 corrigendum deleted "Capital expenditure and capacity expansion at subsidiary companies" and recast 75% of proceeds as acquisitions "including repayment of acquisition debt," the June 18, 2026 EGM passed with 31.72% of public-institution votes against, and the June 24-25, 2026 rumour verification on a German target (Deharde) was answered as speculative. By the November 2, 2026 Q2/H1 FY2027 group update the separation is marketed as three "Pure-Play Platforms" with per-entity boards, ratings and balance sheets, and the second raise (approved October 3, 2026 with 99.998% in favour) was granted exchange in-principle approval on November 6, 2026.

**What management expects from it:** Three focused listed platforms, each with its own board, ratings and balance sheet. Lifestyle: premiumisation, net cash of ₹69 cr. Realty: ~20% pre-sales growth, 17-19% EBITDA margin, ~20% ROCE, 9-10% PAT margin, debt/equity below 1.0x. Engineering Raymond Ltd.: aerospace scale-up at ~21% segment margins, operating leverage (PBT margin 6.4% vs 4.4%), and warrant capital for acquisitions without pre-funding dilution.

*Not explained on the calls:* No earnings-call transcripts were provided; filings never explain demerger mechanics, ratios, record dates, costs, who requested it, or why garmenting sits under the engineering holdco.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Documents state only that, having undertaken significant restructuring and demerger activities including the demerger of its lifestyle and real estate business, Raymond is positioned to pursue accelerated multi-sector growth through subsidiaries; group presented as pure-play platforms
- *What it reveals:* Realty holds 100-acre Thane land with ~₹25,000 cr revenue potential plus asset-light JDAs ~₹27,000 cr; H1FY27 pre-sales +111% to ₹1,602 cr, EBITDA +30%, but net debt ₹912 cr, D/E 0.8x and PAT down 14%
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* Raymond Realty Limited's own H1FY27 financials — ₹912 cr net debt, 1.70x net debt/EBITDA — against the ₹4,100 cr MMR launch pipeline
- *In their words:* “Having undertaken significant restructuring and demerger activities in recent years — including the demerger of its lifestyle and real estate business — Raymond is now positioned to pursue an accelerated, multi-sector growth strategy through its subsidiary companies”
