### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The business being separated is the Madura Fashion & Lifestyle / western-wear branded-apparel business — Louis Philippe-type premium lifestyle brands plus Reebok, American Eagle, Van Heusen Innerwear and the (exited) Forever 21 — demerged out of ABFRL into a separately listed Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited (ABLBL), leaving in ABFRL the Pantaloons/OWND (ex-Style Up) masstige-value play, the ethnic portfolio (Sabyasachi, Tarun Tahiliani, House of Masaba, Shantnu & Nikhil, Tasva, Jaypore, TCNS/W-Aurelia), luxury (The Collective, Galeries Lafayette) and digital-first TMRW. Management's stated reason is a capital-allocation and focus problem inside one company: ABLBL is a mature, high-margin, cash-generating platform (FY25 normalized revenue INR7,830 crores, EBITDA margin 16.2%, up 100bps; Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 17%, +200bps; brands at 19.3% FY25 margin, retail LTL 9-12%) whose growth lever — an 'aggressive' net 300+ store rollout, 200 of them own-capex — was 'underleveraged in the combined entity', so the demerger was explicitly designed to 'leave that cash for allowing that business to soar' and let it invest through downcycles when franchisees cannot. Conversely the retained ABFRL is a portfolio of loss-making/investment-phase businesses (TCNS, Tasva, Style Up/OWND, Galeries Lafayette, TMRW) that needed a clean, cash-rich balance sheet: ABFRL raised USD 490 million via QIP plus preferential issue (promoters paying a significant premium) to make demerged ABFRL 'debt-free' with gross cash of INR2,350 crores at consolidation, versus ABLBL starting with ~INR700-781 crores net debt to be repaid in 2-3 years. Dikshit framed the underlying problem as too many simultaneous growth bets starving each other of attention — 'Innerwear will get the attention which it would not have got when we had 5 or 6 such growth opportunities in front of us' — i.e. separation is about focus, differentiated capital structures (dividend-paying ABLBL vs. investment-funding ABFRL) and separate value-creation journeys. The same philosophy is applied one level down: TMRW was built as a separate company from 2021 precisely so it would raise its own capital (INR437 crores from ServiceNow Ventures for ~11%, INR440-450 crores equity in FY26, INR500 crores NCDs, ~INR800 crores cash) and eventually have 'its own public market journey'. Mechanically the demerger was Board-approved 19 April 2024, shareholder-approved 21 January 2025, NCLT-sanctioned 27 March 2025, effective 1 May 2025 with an appointed date of 1 April 2024, a 1:1 share entitlement (1,22,02,94,773 ABLBL shares allotted 26 May 2025) and ABLBL listed 23 June 2025; it also reset intercompany accounting, producing a one-off INR97 crore gain from ending inter-division elimination on Madura stock sold through Pantaloons and INR148 crore of depreciation not charged on discontinued operations. Targets attached to the split: ABLBL to 'double in scale' and expand margins over five years and pay dividends at the earliest opportunity; ABFRL to deliver 3x revenue and 2x margin over five years, with most of that margin uplift coming from turning TCNS, Tasva and TMRW from EBITDA-negative to profitable.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. First formal framing of the separation: the western-wear brands business is being carved into a separate listed entity, ABLBL, with NCLT scheduled for the third week of March 2025 and completion expected in 2-3 months. “First, the demerger of western wear brands business into a separate entity, that is Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited, or ABLBL, is progressing well and set for completion within the next 2, 3 months.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)*
2. The USD 490 million QIP plus preferential issue was raised inside the pre-demerger company specifically so the retained ABFRL would emerge debt-free with enough cash to fund its loss-making businesses until self-sustaining. “The fundraise within demerged ABFRL will strengthen its balance sheet by making it debt-free and leaving enough cash in the books to take care of the growth needs of its businesses until they become self-sustainable.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)*
3. Capital structures were deliberately split asymmetrically — debt with the cash-generating lifestyle entity, cash with the investment-phase entity. “We expect ABLBL to start the next year with opening debt of INR700 crores, whereas demerged ABFRL will have a likely cash balance of approximately INR1,300 crores.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)*
4. The sharpest stated rationale: Lifestyle Brands' store-expansion opportunity was under-exploited while inside the combined company, and the demerger was designed to free its own cash for that expansion (300+ stores, ~200 own-capex). “And one of the strategic rationale for the demerger was to leave that cash for allowing that business to soar.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)*
5. A second, cyclical argument: as a standalone entity ABLBL can self-fund store rollout when franchisee partners pull back in weak demand periods. “Lifestyle Brands particularly also will have access to their own cash. So their ability to grow even in downtimes, when franchisees sometimes are not in a position to invest during the low time, the business will be able to sort of short circuit that and invest deeper.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)*
6. The umbrella justification offered to investors was value unlock via two independently capitalised, independently growing entities. “The completion of these steps in the next 2, 3 months will enable us to unlock value through 2 independent entities, both with attractive growth potential and a strong balance sheet through a resilient growth-oriented business model sharpened over time.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=86aee500-e77b-4d18-9566-af83384f5a37.pdf)*
7. Completion announced: demerger done, 1:1 entitlement, ABLBL shares allotted to ABFRL shareholders and listing targeted by end-June 2025. “We successfully completed the demerger, creating two focused fashion power houses, Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited, ABLBL; and Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited, ABFRL, both now set on independent high-growth trajectories.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)*
8. The underlying diagnosis stated plainly in answer to a question on why Innerwear had stagnated at ~INR500 crores since 2016 — one company carrying five or six growth bets could not give each the management attention and capital it needed, hence restructuring into separate entities. “I think as it becomes part of a company which is fundamentally profitable free cash flow generator and it's an important part of its growth journey, Innerwear will get the attention which it would not have got when we had 5 or 6 such growth opportunities in front of us.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)*
9. Same answer gives the structural logic for the split: multiple growth opportunities in one company required separate capitalisation and structure. “ABFRL, the combined ABFRL business had multiple growth opportunities, and we realized at some point of time, that we'll have to capitalize it and structure it differently to pursue independent growth opportunities more aggressively.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)*
10. Both halves were shown as independently healthy at separation — ABLBL Q4 margin +200bps (FY25 normalized revenue INR7,830 crores, 16.2% margin), demerged ABFRL Q4 EBITDA more than doubled to INR199 crores comparable. “Both entities delivered robust profitability, ABLBL clocking 200 basis points margin expansion, while demerged ABFRL more than doubling its EBITDA.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)*
11. ABLBL is positioned as the self-funding, net-debt-INR781-crore, dividend-paying mature platform with a 300+ store FY26 pipeline, to double in scale over five years. “ABLBL shall be a dividend-distributing company at the earliest appropriate opportunity.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)*
12. Retained ABFRL's post-demerger ambition quantified; management added that most of the margin uplift must come from turning TCNS, Tasva and TMRW from EBITDA-negative to profitable. “ABFRL with a sharpened brand portfolio, a comprehensive diversified play across high-growth segments and a gross cash balance of INR2,350 crores is set to unlock the next phase of growth, targeting a 3x revenue scale up and 2x margin expansion over the next 5 years.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)*
13. Accounting consequence of separating the two: the inter-division elimination on Madura brand merchandise sold through Pantaloons ends, producing a one-off INR97 crore inventory write-up gain, alongside INR148 crore of depreciation not charged on discontinued operations. “Reported EBITDA includes gain of INR97 crores on account of discontinuation of interdivision elimination post demerger as company's financials get reset to report on independent and stand-alone basis going forward.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=29b83308-dd71-4b41-9802-e328e83350ee.pdf)*
14. Process closed out and ABLBL separately listed, completing the separation. “On demerger, as previously communicated, all requisite processes have been successfully completed, culminating in the creation of Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=605235b0-2e2b-4b89-9dcf-9a88f5115fa7.pdf)*
15. The same 'separate entity, separate capital' philosophy is applied one level down to TMRW, created as a separate company in 2021 so it would raise external capital (INR437 crores from ServiceNow Ventures for ~11%) and eventually list on its own rather than consume ABFRL's cash. “And over the next 8, 10 years, build a company which can find a very digital native path to this industry, which is fashion industry and have its own public market journey as we go forward from private to public.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=605235b0-2e2b-4b89-9dcf-9a88f5115fa7.pdf)*
16. A year on, the demerger persists only as a comparability adjustment in reported numbers; underlying ABFRL is now at standalone EBITDA breakeven and ex-TMRW consolidated pre-Ind AS loss narrowed to INR33 crores. “It is important to note that last year included a onetime gain of INR97 crores relating to inventory write-up and accounting treatment relating to demerger, which was explained in detail during Q4 results of last year.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=cf16c559-ad8d-4518-802d-9e35cc221c92.pdf)*
17. Leverage guidance is explicitly carried across both the pre-demerger combined company and the post-demerger entities, at 2-3x for any of the group's fashion companies. “We are very far, but that's the guidance we gave 5 years back and 3 years back.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=cf16c559-ad8d-4518-802d-9e35cc221c92.pdf)*
18. The later corporate action runs the other way: wholly-owned Jaypore E-Commerce and TG Apparel & Decor are amalgamated INTO ABFRL (Board 5 Feb 2026, NCLT order 2 July 2026, appointed date 1 April 2026, effective 1 August 2026) with no consideration or share issue, purely to simplify structure and cut administrative cost. “Seamless integration and better financial strength and flexibility for the Amalgamated Company, which would result in maximizing overall shareholder value.” — *Scheme*
19. Stated benefits of that simplification step are legal/operating structure and cost, not value unlock — a contrast with the ABLBL demerger rationale. “Streamlining of business & administrative operations consequently reducing administrative & other operating costs;” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** The demerger was Board-approved on 19 April 2024 and by the Feb 17, 2025 call was 'progressing well', with NCLT listed for the third week of March 2025, the USD 490 million QIP/preferential raise just closed, and guidance that ABLBL would open FY26 with INR700 crores debt while demerged ABFRL held ~INR1,300-1,500 crores cash; in that call the rationale sharpened from generic 'unlock value' into the specific point that Lifestyle Brands' store expansion had been 'underleveraged in the combined entity'. By the May 26, 2025 call it was 'successfully completed' — two 'focused fashion power houses', ABLBL shares allotted 1:1, ABFRL carrying INR2,350 crores gross cash, with the first explicit five-year targets (ABLBL to double in scale and pay dividends; ABFRL 3x revenue, 2x margin) and the clearest statement of cause, that a combined ABFRL with '5 or 6' growth opportunities starved businesses like Innerwear of attention. The Aug 14, 2025 call confirmed completion and listing on 23 June 2025 and extended the same logic to TMRW raising its own external capital, and by the Nov 2025/Feb 2026/May 2026 calls the demerger survives only as an accounting comparability footnote (the INR97 crore base-quarter gain) while the structural work shifts to simplification inside ABFRL — the Feb 5, 2026 Scheme amalgamating wholly-owned Jaypore E-Commerce and TG Apparel & Decor into ABFRL, NCLT-sanctioned 2 July 2026 and effective 1 August 2026.

**What management expects from it:** ABLBL: own cash flows fund 300+ net stores, scale to double and margins expand from 16.2%, INR781 crore net debt repaid in 2-3 years, dividends paid early. Demerged ABFRL: debt-free with INR2,350 crore cash to fund OWND, Tasva, TCNS, luxury and TMRW; 3x revenue and 2x margin in five years, chiefly by turning TCNS, Tasva and TMRW profitable; sharper focus and attention per business.

*Not explained on the calls:* No investor, lender or partner is named as having demanded it; no tax, dis-synergy, cost-allocation, brand-royalty or transition-service detail; no reason given why INR700-781 crore debt stayed with ABLBL.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* The departed MFL business was the profitable half (FY25 discontinued-operations PBT Rs 230.97 crore on revenue Rs 7,618.62 crore), leaving a loss-making, cash-consuming parent: FY26 revenue Rs 8,177 crore, PAT loss Rs 830 crore, FCF positive only by FY29.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *Read next:* Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited's own standalone results — the demerged MFL business's post-listing revenue, margin and debt
- *In their words:* “The Equity Shares of the Resulting Company listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited on June 23, 2025.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The only separation described in these documents is the one that created ABLBL itself: the Madura Fashion and Lifestyle ('MFL') business was demerged out of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited ('ABFRL'), approved by the ABFRL board on April 19, 2024, sanctioned by NCLT on March 27, 2025, effective May 1, 2025, with ABLBL shares issued 1:1 so shareholders hold identical stakes in both companies — ABLBL carries the four Lifestyle/Power brands (Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly, Peter England, plus formats like Peter England Red and the Philippe bridge-to-luxury store) and the Emerging portfolio (Reebok, Van Heusen Innerwear, American Eagle; Forever 21 was closed/restructured with a ₹98.33 crore exceptional charge and ~₹50 crore of EBITDA loss plus ~₹50 crore interest in the FY25 base), while ABFRL retains the newer 'tomorrow' businesses. Management's stated reason is capital allocation, not operations: the mature Madura cash flow had been funding other things. Ashish Dikshit (Q1 FY26, Aug 14, 2025): 'The cash generated by this business in the past has -- was used to actually kick start or acquire multiple new businesses. And the whole purpose of demerger was actually to need the cash for this business to grow faster.' He restated it in Q3 FY26 (Feb 3, 2026) as 'One of the primary reasons for demerger was to create an entity which can reinvest back more aggressively into growth,' quantifying it: the business throws off EBITDA cash of close to ₹900 crore, historical capex was only ₹150–200 crore (₹225 crore in the best years), and FY26 capex was taken 'north of INR300 crores, perhaps INR320 crores, INR330 crores' — which is also why debt fell only modestly. Separation also fixed the funding and payout frame: no equity fundraise in either entity (only the 'tomorrow business' excepted), borrowings split 'based on the allocation formula', a ₹500 crore NCD repaid in January 2026 and refinanced with 'no fresh borrowing', a stated path to debt-free in 2.5–3 years at ₹200–300 crore repayment a year, and, within year one post-demerger, a first dividend of 50 paise per share with a policy of ~15–25% of net profit. Visible results of that reinvestment: 300+ store additions in FY26 to 3,348 stores / 4.9 million sq ft / ~800 towns, FY26 revenue ₹8,396 crore (+7%), EBITDA ₹1,429 crore (+13%, margin 17%, +90bps), normalized PAT ₹209 crore (+61%), net debt ₹726 crore versus ₹781 crore. Nobody in these texts says investors, lenders or brand partners demanded the split; the only external pressure visible is analysts policing the no-fundraise promise and the debt-reduction pace.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The structure: ABFRL's board approved demerging the Madura Fashion and Lifestyle business into ABLBL on a going-concern basis, consideration being ABLBL shares to ABFRL's own shareholders — a pure separation, no cash and no change in ownership. “The Board at its meeting held on April 19, 2024, subject to necessary approvals, considered and approved the demerger of the Madura Fashion and Lifestyle ('MFL') Business under a Scheme of Arrangement between Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited ('Demerged Company') and Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited ('Resulting Company').” — *Scheme*
2. Mirror shareholding and 1:1 ratio: 1,22,02,94,773 shares of ₹10 allotted on May 26, 2025 to ABFRL holders of record May 22, 2025; NCLT sanction March 27, 2025, effective May 1, 2025, listed June 23, 2025. “The Scheme provided that all shareholders of the demerged company will hold Identical shareholdings in both the companies, post the demerger.” — *Scheme*
3. Legacy liabilities travel with the demerged business: GST orders for FY2019-20 to FY2022-23 still issued in ABFRL's name land on ABLBL, including a ₹310.13 crore demand (tax ₹59.07 crore, interest ₹23.81 crore, penalty ₹227.26 crore) dated March 30, 2026, which the company says it will appeal. “Order is in the name of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited (ABFRL). However, it relates to the business of the Company, which got demerged from ABFRL, pursuant to a Scheme of Arrangement effective from May 1, 2025.” — *Scheme*
4. The core rationale, given by MD Ashish Dikshit in answer to Niharika Karnani asking where the cash goes now that it won't be invested into ABFRL: Madura's cash had been bankrolling the group's new business bets, and the demerger exists to keep it inside Madura. “The cash generated by this business in the past has -- was used to actually kick start or acquire multiple new businesses. And the whole purpose of demerger was actually to need the cash for this business to grow faster.” — *CALL Aug 2025*
5. Explicit priority order for the retained cash — growth capex first (including the Lifestyle brands, not just Reebok and Innerwear), debt reduction only after that. “So the first use of cash would be to accelerate the growth in the businesses that we have.” — *CALL Aug 2025*
6. The balance-sheet promise attached to the separation: ₹200-300 crore of debt repayment a year off a ~₹700 crore March-2025 base (which had risen ~₹200 crore in Q1 on festive inventory), reaching debt-free in 2.5-3 years; capex guided at ~₹250 crore for retail, shop-in-shops, warehouse, some manufacturing and technology. “we expect between INR200 crores to INR300 crores reduction each year. And that's why we had indicated an overall debt-free status in two and a half years to three years.” — *CALL Aug 2025*
7. Growth ambitions the separated entity was given: Lifestyle Brands in early double digits off 15% Q1 retail LTL, and the emerging portfolio (Reebok, American Eagle, Van Heusen Innerwear) at 18-20%+, with Reebok already taken from ~₹200 crore/90 stores at acquisition to ~₹500 crore/180+ stores. “We expect the newer business to grow anything between 18 % to 20 %, while Lifestyle Brands business will grow in early double digits.” — *CALL Aug 2025*
8. Reinvestment visibly ahead of deleveraging in the second quarter as a standalone: 75+ new stores, 65 company-owned store renovations in a single quarter (each taking 45-60 days of lost trading), working capital and debt up on early-festive and Bangladesh winterwear inwarding; no restatement of the demerger rationale on this call. “So, just to give you a sense, we did 65 store renovations in just the last quarter.” — *CALL Nov 2025*
9. Dikshit restated the rationale in its sharpest form when asked why net debt had barely moved, and CFO Dharmendra Lodha framed it as the growth-capital rationale 'which we conveyed' at the time of demerger. “One of the primary reasons for demerger was to create an entity which can reinvest back more aggressively into growth.” — *CALL Feb 2026*
10. The numbers behind it: ~₹900 crore EBITDA cash, historical capex of ₹150-200 crore (₹225 crore at best) versus FY26 capex of ₹320-330 crore — with ~80%+ of it going to Lifestyle Brands expansion and renovation — which management says is precisely why debt fell only from ₹1,000 crore (September) to ₹800 crore (December). “This year, our capex will be north of INR300 crores, perhaps INR320 crores, INR330 crores. And that's really why the debt reduction is not very large this year.” — *CALL Feb 2026*
11. The no-fundraise commitment made at demerger was policed by Ambit's Videesha Sheth over a board-approved ₹500 crore NCD issue; management said debt came across on an allocation formula and the NCDs merely refinance a January repayment. “Yeah, you know, at the time of demerger, the company got the borrowings transferred based on the allocation formula.” — *CALL Feb 2026*
12. Portfolio ambition for the separated entity: the emerging brands (Reebok 200+ stores, doubled from 100 at acquisition; Van Heusen Innerwear; American Eagle) to become a quarter of ABLBL, with Lifestyle margins at a four-year-high 20.6% in Q3 and emerging-segment profitability up 790bps. “This portfolio is expected to be one-fourth of overall ABLBL business in next 4 -5 years.” — *CALL Feb 2026*
13. The payout half of the story delivered in year one: a maiden 50 paise per share dividend on top of FY26 revenue of ₹8,396 crore, EBITDA ₹1,429 crore (17%, +90bps), normalized PAT ₹209 crore (+61%), ₹450 crore operating cash flow and net debt down to ₹726 crore. “The Board of the company has also declared a dividend of INR 50 paisa per equity share within the first year of the company post -demerger.” — *CALL May 2026*
14. Dikshit tied dividend and debt-free status back to what was promised 'at the time of formation of company', guiding a 15-25% of net profit payout and debt-free in about three years while explicitly declining to chase zero debt. “As you know, we had announced at the time of formation of company that looking at the predictable, consistent, historical cash flows of the company, we are very confident that this company over a period of time will become a debt -free company and equally will be able to pay dividends as it goes forward.” — *CALL May 2026*
15. Reinvestment sustained rather than wound down: 300+ gross store additions in FY26 to 3,348 stores, FY27 capex of ₹250-300 crore (~₹200 crore into retail expansion and renovation), Reebok at 210+ stores adding 40-50 a year, and Van Heusen Innerwear targeting its first profitable quarter in FY27. “About INR 300 crores. So, we will continue with that kind of momentum. There is still a lot of growth opportunities in the market, so we will continue to drive that.” — *CALL May 2026*

**How it evolved:** The split was board-approved on April 19, 2024, NCLT-sanctioned March 27, 2025, effective May 1, 2025, with shares allotted May 26, 2025 and listing on June 23, 2025; the first post-demerger call (Aug 14, 2025) is where Dikshit framed the 'why' — cash previously used to kick-start/acquire new businesses would now fund this one, with 'first use of cash' for growth and 'only the subsequent part' for debt, ₹250 crore capex guided and debt-free in 2.5–3 years. Nov 5, 2025 added no new rationale, only execution and its cost — 65 store renovations in one quarter, debt up ~₹200 crore on festive inventory. Feb 3, 2026 sharpened it into a number: ~₹900 crore of EBITDA cash, capex lifted from ₹150–225 crore historically to ₹320–330 crore, explicitly explaining the small debt reduction, while Videesha Sheth challenged a ₹500 crore NCD against the no-fundraise commitment (answer: pure refinancing). By May 8, 2026 the emphasis shifted from reinvestment to returns — maiden 50 paise dividend 'within the first year of the company post-demerger', a 15–25% payout band, FY27 capex ~₹300 crore, and debt-free in three years described as achievable but 'not something that we are chasing'.

**What management expects from it:** For ABLBL: retained cash funds its own growth — capex up from ₹150-225 crore to ₹300-330 crore, 300+ stores a year, double-digit revenue growth, 7% steady LTL, Lifestyle margins ~20% improving on rent leverage, emerging brands to one-fourth of sales and rising EBITDA, debt-free in ~3 years, 15-25% dividend payout. For ABFRL: only implied — it keeps the newer 'tomorrow' businesses and the option to raise funds.

*Not explained on the calls:* No one is named as having asked for it — no investor, lender or brand-partner demand; no dis-synergy, separation cost, valuation or re-rating argument; no ABFRL-side rationale; debt allocation formula undisclosed.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Management: "One of the primary reasons for demerger was to create an entity which can reinvest back more aggressively into growth," with growth capital available to it.
- *What it reveals:* A ₹8,396 crore single-segment branded apparel business, FY26 EBITDA ₹1,429 crore (17%), pre-Ind AS PAT ₹313 crore versus reported ₹171 crore; net debt cut to ₹726 crore, first dividend paid, plus inherited ABFRL-era GST demands exceeding ₹310 crore.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *Read next:* Shareholding pattern / FY26 annual report for promoter stake and ESOP grants, and appeals against the ₹310 crore GST demand.
- *In their words:* “One of the primary reasons for demerger was to create an entity which can reinvest back more aggressively into growth.”

**What the documents themselves say about the differences:**

- **capex and capital intensity** — parent / remaining: not stated; separated business: The demerger was intended to create an entity that can reinvest more aggressively into growth; FY26 capex was north of INR300 crores versus a historical INR150-225 crores, with INR250-300 crores planned for FY27, of which about INR200 crores goes into retail expansion. “One of the primary reasons for demerger was to create an entity which can reinvest back more aggressively into growth. Some of those signals are visible here. This year, our capex will be north of INR300 crores , perhaps INR320 crores , INR330 crores . And that's really why the debt reduction is not very large this year.”
- **debt and leverage** — parent / remaining: not stated; separated business: ABLBL net debt INR 726 crores at end-FY26 versus INR 781 crores in March last year; debt equity ratio 0.39 times at December 31, 2025; INR500 crores of NCDs approved to refinance debentures repaid in January 2026; management expects the company to be debt-free in about three years. “Net debt at year -end stood at INR 726 crores versus INR 781 crores in March last year.”
- **cash** — parent / remaining: not stated; separated business: ABLBL generated INR 450 crores of operating cash flow (before capex and security deposit) in FY26, largely used for store expansion; a maiden dividend of 50 paisa per share was declared in the first year post-demerger, with a stated payout range of close to 15% to 25% of net profit. “Through business operations, the company generated operating cash flow (before CAPEX and security deposit) of INR 450 crores. A large share of this cash has gone towards funding aggressive store expansion during the year.”
- **operating margin** — parent / remaining: not stated; separated business: ABLBL FY26 EBITDA INR 1,429 crores, up 13%, with margin improving 90 bps to 17%; Lifestyle Brands FY26 margin 19.6% (up 20 bps) and Emerging Business EBITDA near 4% versus almost breakeven last year; standalone operating margin 7.73% in Q4 CY-quarter ended December 31, 2025 versus 8.42% a year earlier. “ABLBL revenue stood at INR 8,396 crores, up 7% YoY . EBITDA grew 13% to INR 1,429 crores versus INR 1,269 crores in last year, with margin improving by 90 bps to 17%.”
- **growth** — parent / remaining: not stated; separated business: ABLBL Q4 FY26 revenue grew 12% YoY to INR 2,174 crores, Lifestyle Brands 11% and Emerging Business 18%; store network expanded by 300+ in FY26 to 3,348 stores; the business is expected to double in scale with improved profitability over the next five years. “With this diverse portfolio of strong brands and access to free cash flow, the business is poised to pursue an aggressive growth trajectory. It is expected to double in scale with improved profitability over the next five years, reinforc ing its position as one of the largest branded fashion players in the country.”
- **working capital** — parent / remaining: not stated; separated business: Working capital rose about INR 100 crores in FY26 on pre-production of core products in new manufacturing capacity; management expects to release working capital in FY27. Current ratio 1.09 times and long term debt to working capital 0.34 times at December 31, 2025. “I think, fair question. Simple answer, is there juice for improvement on working capital? Answer is yes, and we do plan to do that this year.”
- **tax** — parent / remaining: not stated; separated business: GST orders in the name of ABFRL but relating to the demerged business now fall on ABLBL, including a total demand of Rs. 3,10,13,33,083 (order dated March 30, 2026) and further orders dated March 16 and March 17, 2026; the Company believes the demands are not tenable and intends to appeal. “There is no impact on financials, operations or other activities of the Company. The Company believes that the said demand is n ot tenable as per the law.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

Triveni Engineering & Industries Ltd. (TEIL) put through a single composite scheme of arrangement that does two things: it amalgamates its ~61.77%-owned listed subsidiary Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises Ltd. (SSEL, the Shamli sugar/distillery unit) into TEIL, and it demerges TEIL's Power Transmission Business (PTB — high-speed/turbo gearboxes at Mysuru, plus the incubating defence business) into Triveni Power Transmission Ltd. (TPTL) for separate listing, which management described on the Feb 2026 call as being done 'to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies' and in Feb 2025 as 'value unlocking that the Board of Directors has felt very important.' The problem being solved is that PTB's economics look nothing like the rest of TEIL: PTB ran PBIT margins above 34% in FY25 (PBIT ₹126.8 crore, +18.4%, on turnover up 27%, order booking ₹475+ crore), about 36% in H1 FY26 and 41% in Q2 FY26, against sugar and alcohol businesses whose output and input prices are both administered (SAP up ₹300/tonne in UP, no ethanol price revision for two years, maize at ₹20–26/kg, MSP unrevised), and whose FY25 segment profits fell on a 69bps recovery decline. Investors made exactly this point on the call: Bharat Shah of ASK Investment Managers told management that 'barring the Power Transmission business, which is relatively more robust, predictable economics and predictable outcomes,' the other businesses 'produce a very mercurial kind of an outcome,' and Tarun Sawhney conceded TEIL had not met its return profile on ethanol capital. Separation is also meant to let PTB fund and run its own growth: a board-approved capex of ₹340 crore in three tranches (taking gears capacity from ~₹400 crore to ~₹700 crore of output by September 2026, with just over ₹100 crore sanctioned for the defence facility and ₹231 crore incurred by 31 March 2026, of which ₹78 crore on defence), an export-led order book just under ₹500 crore (+25%), a Swiss subsidiary (Triveni Power Transmission GmbH, acquired 100% by TPTL), aftermarket at ~40% of gears, and a global addressable high-speed/turbo gear market of about $650–700 million. Crucially, TEIL deliberately did not do a clean 100% separation: it retains roughly 30% of TPTL, and Sawhney justified this by the defence business — 'we are incubating a Defence business, which we have large aspirations for,' where establishing pre-qualifications and the ability to bid involves 'balance sheet considerations… from a Group perspective,' plus the precedent of the Triveni Turbine separation, which he called 'actually quite a positive one for the Company.' Post-approval TEIL said ICRA reaffirmed its long-term rating at AA+ Stable, lifting it off watch, and that TPTL goes out 'armed with sufficient cash flows and a balance sheet' to fund its capex and opex.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. First call after the 10 December 2024 board approval; Sawhney introduced the composite scheme — amalgamation of ~61.77%-held SSEL into TEIL and transfer of the PTB undertaking to wholly-owned TPTL — explicitly as a value-unlocking exercise by the Board. “I also wanted to provide an update on the Scheme, as you're all aware, this is in conjunction with value unlocking that the Board of Directors has felt very important.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)*
2. Resham Jain of DSP Asset Managers challenged the structure, arguing TEIL's retained ~30% stake in TPTL would re-import a holdco discount and that a clean separation was needed for value to be unlocked. “It seems that Triveni Engineering will still be holding 30% stake even after demerger. So why such structure, if the value unlocking has to happen, it should have happened in a clean structure where Triveni would not be holding anything otherwise, the same Holdco discount will be applicable to the Power Transmission business once it gets demerged.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)*
3. Sawhney's two reasons for keeping ~30%: the positive precedent of the Triveni Turbine separation, and — decisively — that the incubating defence business needs group balance-sheet backing to win pre-qualifications and be allowed to bid, since defence is co-located with gears in Mysuru. “The second and very, very important is because we are incubating a Defence business, which we have large aspirations for. In establishing pre-qualifications (PQs) and the ability to be able to quote, there are balance sheet considerations that even from a Group perspective that are very, very important to allow us to be in contention.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)*
4. Bharat Shah of ASK Investment Managers made the investor case for separation directly — PTB is the predictable, brick-by-brick business while the regulated sugar/ethanol/water businesses swing unpredictably — and Sawhney conceded the ethanol capital had not met its return profile. “On a shorter-term basis, interplay of the other businesses always produces a very mercurial kind of an outcome, sometimes to delight, but other times to depress.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)*
5. Same call quantified why PTB deserves its own listing: incremental board-approved capex of ₹60 crore taking gears capacity to ₹700 crore by September 2026 from ~₹400 crore, order book at an all-time-high ₹377 crore, and a global high-speed/turbo gear market of about $650–700 million. “The Board meeting of the Directors concluded yesterday had an important announcement of an incremental capex of ₹60 crore for the enhancement of capacity in the Power Transmission business. This will take the gears capacity to ₹700 crore by September 2026.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)*
6. Initial timeline guidance: NCLT sanction expected by the end of calendar 2025. “As far as the Scheme of Arrangement is concerned, we anticipate approval from NCLT by the end of this calendar year.” — *[Feb 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=32ebf539-4c61-4455-9d21-3cc24a97dd7a.pdf)*
7. Q4 FY25 call showed the margin gap the demerger exposes — PTB turnover up 27% with PBIT ₹126.8 crore (+18.4%) and PBIT margins above 34%, record Q4 revenue of almost ₹140 crore and PBIT ₹46.5 crore — while the scheme itself sat pending at SEBI, with separation guided to Q4 FY26. “So we're expecting that by the middle of Q1 of next calendar year, Q4 of this fiscal year, we will have the separation of the PTB business.” — *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=24085d8d-b7bb-42bb-bd4f-8cb00e75ea19.pdf)*
8. Resham Jain asked management to begin disclosing PTB in granular detail — customers, industry mix — precisely because it was about to be separately listed after being buried inside a much larger company; Sawhney accepted. “And since it was a part of a much larger company, the understanding of this business from the very granular perspective was much lower.” — *[Jun 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=24085d8d-b7bb-42bb-bd4f-8cb00e75ea19.pdf)*
9. Q1 FY26: approvals still outstanding, with continuous follow-up at SEBI and stock-exchange queries answered; slippage of about 30 days flagged but Q1-calendar-2026 timing maintained. PTB closing order book was a record ₹423 crore (+38%), with engineering order book just under ₹2,000 crore. “The amalgamation with Sir Shadi Lal and the demerger of the Power Transmission business. We are still awaiting regulatory approvals. We're following up continuously with SEBI.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a50ea3c4-1d70-4e28-a663-9393cce6158b.pdf)*
10. Stock exchanges had cleared the scheme (observation letters of 7 and 11 August 2025) and NCLT stakeholder meetings were set for late November/early December; separately, TPTL bought 100% of Triveni Power Transmission GmbH in Switzerland, building the export engine inside the entity being listed. “The proposed scheme has been approved by the stock exchanges, and the process is obtaining approval of NCLT.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ec578aab-464f-47c2-8bc5-cb3982d61b3e.pdf)*
11. PTB PBIT margins improved more than 400bps YoY on product mix and cost optimisation (about 36% PBIT for H1, 41% in the quarter), and TPTL was equipped with its own CRM, digital-factory/digital-twin and SAP HANA systems ahead of standing alone. “Triveni Power Transmission Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the company, has acquired a 100% stake in Triveni Power Transmission GmbH, a Swiss company.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ec578aab-464f-47c2-8bc5-cb3982d61b3e.pdf)*
12. Shareholders and creditors approved in December 2025 with an NCLT hearing in February; management stated the twin purpose as unlocking value and driving operational efficiencies, and said PTB was being equipped with the systems and skills to run as an independent company. “Lastly, with respect to the proposed scheme of amalgamation of SSEL and the demerger of the Power Transmission business to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies, the scheme has been approved by shareholders of creditors, this was in December of 2025.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2bc4c751-c2b8-4a3a-a75a-a00326d1ee32.pdf)*
13. Sawhney signalled the split was imminent and thanked participants for years of feedback, saying the next call would be with two separate companies; a lot of systems work was underway so TPTL could start at full speed with TEIL-level efficiencies. “I think the next time we speak in all probability, this will be two separate companies.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2bc4c751-c2b8-4a3a-a75a-a00326d1ee32.pdf)*
14. Scheme effective 19 May 2026 after NCLT approval; amalgamation appointed date 1 April 2025 and demerger appointed date 1 April 2026; SSEL record date 3 June 2026, TEIL record date within four weeks, and listing of TPTL anticipated by end-August 2026 with separate board meetings, published results and earnings calls for both entities. “I'm delighted to inform you that the composite scheme of arrangement is effective from the 19th of May, 2026 after the approval of the NCLT.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=113e1acd-25ed-4260-8b7f-62ac04ca5fd6.pdf)*
15. Management argued the separated entity is self-funding: of the ₹340 crore board-approved capex in three tranches (output of about ₹700 crore of gears, excluding defence), ₹231 crore was spent by 31 March 2026 including ₹78 crore on defence, with ₹109 crore left to September 2026 — all fundable by TPTL itself. “Of course, as power transmission migrates into Triveni Power Transmission Limited, the company is armed with sufficient cash flows and a balance sheet to be able to incur all of this CapEx and OpEx and more.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=113e1acd-25ed-4260-8b7f-62ac04ca5fd6.pdf)*
16. A balance-sheet benefit of completion was cited: ICRA reaffirmed TEIL's long-term rating at AA+ Stable and removed the under-watch status that the pending scheme had caused, restoring Triveni's historical highest rating. “I am very proud to announce that post the scheme having been approved, ICRA has reaffirmed our long-term credit rating as AA+ Stable, lifting it from its previous under watch status.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=113e1acd-25ed-4260-8b7f-62ac04ca5fd6.pdf)*
17. Asked about post-demerger margins, CFO Suresh Taneja said PTB's own dynamics support continuation of the roughly 35% PBIT level it had been delivering inside TEIL; Sawhney also guided that exports of original equipment should exceed half of PTB sales in the near future. “As regards to the PTB business, it has got its own dynamics, as a matter of fact. So far, we have been maintaining about 35% PBIT. I think the same trend is expected to continue in future also.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=113e1acd-25ed-4260-8b7f-62ac04ca5fd6.pdf)*
18. Entitlement terms: TEIL shareholders receive 1 TPTL share of ₹2 face value for every 3 TEIL shares of ₹1; SSEL shareholders received 100 TEIL shares of ₹1 for every 137 SSEL shares of ₹10, with 4,308 consolidated fractional shares sold by a trustee and ₹12,24,787 net distributed to 6,064 shareholders by 9 September 2026. “For every 3(three) equity shares of the Demerged Company with a face value of INR 1 each held in the Demerged Company, every equity shareholder of the Demerged Company shall, without any application, act or deed, be entitled to receive 1 (One) equity share of the Resulting Company with a face value of INR 2 each, credited as fully paid up on the same terms and conditions of issue as prevalent in the Demerged Company” — *Scheme*
19. Demerger record date was 22 July 2026 and 7,34,54,338 TPTL shares were allotted to TEIL shareholders on 28 July 2026, at which point TPTL ceased to be a subsidiary and became an associate of TEIL — confirming the deliberately retained residual stake (3,13,00,000 locked-in shares of the 10,47,54,338 total). “Accordingly, the Company ceased to be a subsidiary and become an associate of TEIL.” — *Scheme*
20. TPTL was staffed as a standalone listed company on 28 July 2026: Tarun Sawhney as Vice Chairman & Managing Director, Dhruv M. Sawhney as Non-Executive Chairman, Raman Kumar S. as CFO, Rakesh Kumar Yadav as Company Secretary, EY as internal auditor, with Geeta Bhalla and Suresh Taneja resigning as TPTL directors because of the scheme's implementation. “I Suresh Taneja, hereby tender my resignation from the directorship of the Company with effect from closing of business hours on 28th July, 2026, due implementation of the Composite Scheme of Arrangement and the consequent reconstitution of the Board of Directors of the Company.” — *Scheme*
21. For tax purposes the cost of acquisition was split 86.60% to TEIL and 13.40% to TPTL — the only quantified indication in these documents of the relative value attributed to the demerged power transmission business. “Triveni Engineering & Industries Limited 86.60% 13.40% Triveni Power Transmission Limited” — *Scheme*
22. TPTL's 10,47,54,338 shares received BSE and NSE listing and trading approvals on 8 October 2026 and began trading on 12 October 2026 (BSE 544824, NSE TRIVENIPT) — roughly six weeks later than the end-August listing guided on the June 2026 call. “Accordingly, the equity shares of the Company shall be listed and admitted to dealings on BSE and NSE with effect from October 12, 2026” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** The board approved the composite scheme on 10 December 2024, and the Feb 2025 (5 Feb) call was the first investor call after it — there Sawhney framed it as value unlocking, guided to NCLT approval 'by the end of this calendar year,' and defended the retained ~30% stake against Resham Jain's push for a clean structure; Bharat Shah's 'mercurial' critique of the commodity businesses came on the same call. By Jun 2025 (28 May) the scheme was stuck with SEBI with NCLT next, guidance slipped to 'middle of Q1 of next calendar year, Q4 of this fiscal year,' and Resham Jain asked for granular PTB disclosure ahead of listing, which Sawhney accepted as a 'welcome suggestion'; on Aug 2025 (30 July) approvals were still pending with SEBI and stock-exchange queries, with Sawhney allowing it 'could add another 30-odd days.' Nov 2025 (7 Nov) reported stock-exchange approval (observation letters 7 and 11 August 2025) and NCLT stakeholder meetings set for late November/early December, plus TPTL's 100% acquisition of Swiss step-down subsidiary Triveni Power Transmission GmbH; Feb 2026 (2 Feb) reported shareholder/creditor approval in December 2025, an NCLT hearing in February, systems work to let TPTL 'hit the ground sprinting,' and Sawhney's line that 'the next time we speak in all probability, this will be two separate companies.' On Jun 2026 (4 June) he confirmed the scheme effective 19 May 2026 after NCLT approval (orders 7 and 18 May), appointed dates of 1 April 2025 for the amalgamation and 1 April 2026 for the demerger, the SSEL record date of 3 June 2026, and guided to a TPTL listing 'by the end of August' with separate results and earnings calls for both companies — in the event the demerger record date was 22 July 2026, 7,34,54,338 TPTL shares were allotted on 28 July 2026 (TPTL thereby ceasing to be a subsidiary and becoming an associate), and TPTL listed and began trading only on 12 October 2026.

**What management expects from it:** TPTL: independent listing of a ~35% PBIT, export-led gears and defence business, self-funding its ₹340 crore capex toward ~₹700 crore of gears output, exports above 50%, aftermarket-led margins. TEIL: a cleaner sugar-distillery-water commodity platform with SSEL absorbed, AA+ Stable restored off watch, and cash flows for brownfield/greenfield expansion. Both: unlocked value, operational efficiencies, separate reporting.

*Not explained on the calls:* No valuation basis for the 1:3 ratio, no standalone PTB balance sheet or financials, no quantified dis-synergies, demerger costs, TPTL dividend policy, or why exactly 30% was retained.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Management: “the proposed scheme of amalgamation of SSEL and the demerger of the Power Transmission business to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies”.
- *What it reveals:* PTB was only 4.45% of TEIL turnover but earned ~35-36% PBIT margins; cost-of-acquisition split gives it just 13.40%. Order book just under ₹500 crore (+25%), ₹340 crore capex, new defence facility, Swiss subsidiary, exports targeted above 50%.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *Read next:* TPTL's first standalone quarterly results — whether ~36% PBIT margin holds on the ₹500 crore order book post-capex.
- *In their words:* “For every 3(three) equity shares of the Demerged Company with a face value of INR 1 each held in the Demerged Company, every equity shareholder of the Demerged Company shall, without any application, act or deed, be entitled to receive 1 (One) equity share of the Resulting Company with a face value of INR 2 each, credited as fully paid up on the same terms and conditions of issue as prevalent in the Demerged Company”

**What the documents themselves say about the differences:**

- **operating margin** — parent / remaining: Sugar & allied: FY26 sugar revenues grew ~13% with PBIT of about ₹272 crore; group EBITDA margin rose to 16.9% (~₹624 crore) from ₹533 crore in the previous fiscal year; separated business: Power Transmission has maintained about 35% PBIT margin and is expected to continue at that level; H1 FY26 PBT margins improved by more than 400 basis points and the quarter PBIT margin reached ~41% “As regards to the PTB business, it has got its own dynamics, as a matter of fact. So far, we have been maintaining about 35% PBIT. I think the same trend is expected to continue in future also.”
- **capex and capital intensity** — parent / remaining: Sugar capex limited to lowering cost of production: "the CapEx that are presently being incurred is only to lower the cost of production within sugar", funded by internal accruals with "nothing substantial"; separated business: ₹340 crore board-approved capex for the gearbox business in three tranches, of which ₹231 crore incurred up to March 31, 2026 (₹78 crore for the defence facility) and ~₹109 crore to be incurred in Q1/Q2 FY27, completion by September 2026 “the CapEx that the board of Triveni Engineering has approved in three tranches totals exactly ₹340 crore. For the gearbox business, this represents an output of about ₹700 crore based on the product mix.”
- **debt and leverage** — parent / remaining: Consolidated debt ₹2,148 crore on March 31, 2026 vs ₹1,969 crore on March 31, 2025; long-term debt ₹472 crore vs ₹506 crore; ICRA reaffirmed long-term rating AA+ Stable after the scheme; separated business: TPTL stated to have sufficient cash flows and balance sheet strength to fund all of the approved capex and opex; TPTL had no secured or unsecured creditors (its NCLT creditor meetings were dispensed with) “Of course, as power transmission migrates into Triveni Power Transmission Limited, the company is armed with sufficient cash flows and a balance sheet to be able to incur all of this CapEx and OpEx and more.”
- **growth** — parent / remaining: FY26 consolidated revenues ₹6,291 crore, growth of 10.6%, propelled by stronger sugar and distillery volumes and better sugar realisations; Q4 revenue slightly down from the previous corresponding quarter; separated business: Power Transmission closing order book just under ₹500 crore, 25% higher year on year; exports targeted at more than half of original equipment sales in the near future; enquiry levels up at least 75% year on year “We concluded this year with a very strong order book of just under ₹500 crore, 25% higher than the previous year, providing distinct revenue visibility for the coming quarters.”
- **working capital** — parent / remaining: Short-term borrowings higher due to the increase in cane price; total receivables about ₹500 crore of which water business is ₹125–150 crore; short-term borrowings expected to fall to almost zero by September/October; separated business: not stated “Now as far as the cash credit is concerned, you must realise that there has been an increase in the cane price also. As a result of increase in cane price, you require a higher working capital.”
- **tax** — parent / remaining: 86.60% of the cost of acquisition of equity shares allocated to Triveni Engineering & Industries Limited under Sections 73(1) (Table Serial Nos. 14 and 15) of the Income-Tax Act, 2025; separated business: 13.40% of the cost of acquisition allocated to Triveni Power Transmission Limited “riveni Engineering & Industries Limited 86.60% 13.40% riveni Power Transmission Limited”

**Reading: VERY LIKELY — the piece is under a tenth of the whole; index funds and large holders who receive it without choosing it tend to sell.**

|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| ITC Hotels Limited | Pro forma financials of Hotels Business (excluding ITC Gran… | — | 3.0% (FY2025) | 36,161 | 9.2% | yes |

*Stated figures are the documents' own (a turnover share, or the cost-of-acquisition split the company publishes for tax, which reflects relative value); the segment share is this business's revenue over the parent's sales, and the market-cap share is the entity's value over the entity plus the parent (parent ₹357,120 cr, NSE bhavcopy of 2026-11-13), both computed here.*

**In the documents' words:** “"For example, if 1,000 Ordinary Shares of ITC were purchased at ` 400/- per share by a shareholder, the total cost of acquisition would amount to ` 4,00,000/- before the demerger. Based on the Share Entitlement Ratio, 100 shares of ITCHL would be allotted to the said shareholder. The total cost of acquisition of ` 4,00,000/- would be apportioned in the aforesaid ratio - ` 3,45,960/- (86.49% of ` 4,00,000/-) being the total cost of acquisition of 1,000 ITC shares and ` 54,040/- (13.51% of ` 4,00,000/-) being the total cost of acquisition of 100 shares of ITCHL." (apportionment table: ITC Limited 86.49%, ITC Hotels Limited 13.51% of total cost of acquisition of Ordinary Shares of ITC Limited)”

**The judge's read of selling pressure:** likely — Hotels sits outside ITC's three stated business groups (FMCG, Paperboards/Paper & Packaging, Agri); documents disclose no index or shareholder-base detail.

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

On the documents supplied, the business being separated is ITC's IT services arm, ITC Infotech India Limited (ITCI), a wholly owned subsidiary that is to be carved out of the unlisted group structure and listed on BSE and NSE through a strategic combination with listed Happiest Minds Technologies Limited (31 Aug 2026 filing). The mechanics are two-step: ITCI buys 3,36,61,700 shares (22.106% fully diluted) from promoters Ashok Soota and Ashok Soota Medical Research LLP for ~Rs 1,330 crores cash in two tranches (11.00% at Rs 390/share, 11.106% at Rs 400/share), funded by a Rights Issue of Rs 1,330 crores, after which Happiest Minds amalgamates into ITCI at 25 ITCI shares per 81 Happiest Minds shares (1:3.24) — implying Rs 405/share or Rs 6,167 crores for Happiest Minds and Rs 1,312/share or Rs 11,920 crores for ITCI pre-rights — leaving ITC with ~73.4% and Happiest Minds holders ~26.6%, and ITCI listed. The stated problem it solves is sub-scale: management says '> $1Bn revenue puts provider on the vendor management office radar' and gives the 'Right to Hunt' and 'Right to Win' large deals, so the combination targets US$1 billion revenue by FY28 on a pro-forma basis versus ITCI's FY26 IT services revenue of Rs 4,718 crores (PAT Rs 510 crores adjusted, 18.5% adj. EBITDA margin, 13,000+ employees, 5-yr CAGR 14%) and Happiest Minds' FY26 Rs 2,315.11 crores (FY25 Rs 2,060.84 crores, FY24 Rs 1,624.66 crores, 6,500+ employees, 5-yr CAGR 25%). It also fixes portfolio gaps: Americas mix rises from 27% to 38%, BFSI from 12% to 20%, Build:Run moves to 50:50, and Hi-Tech, EdTech and Healthcare verticals plus 800+ clients and 19,000+ professionals are added, against an industry backdrop of a ~$400 Bn AI-driven TAM by 2030, compression of ~$350 Bn of legacy services, cost-takeout deals at 30-40% savings and vendor consolidation. For ITC shareholders the explicitly stated benefit of separation itself is that it 'Creates a listed IT services platform, enabling independent value discovery and strategic flexibility', alongside ~10% revenue synergies, ~100 bps margin expansion and EPS accretion in the first full year. Nobody is recorded as having demanded it: ITCI's board moved under its own 'Orbit Next' strategy, ITC's board merely 'endorsed' it, and the only external party is the counterparty-seller Ashok Soota, who frames it as Happiest Minds finding 'a welcoming new home'; approvals needed are CCI/anti-trust, stock exchanges/SEBI, shareholders, creditors and NCLT, over ~15 months.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The separation vehicle is disclosed in the 31 August 2026 filing: ITC Infotech acquires 22.106% of Happiest Minds for cash and then amalgamates it, with ITCI's own shares to be listed on both Indian exchanges. “The shares of ITC Infotech are proposed to be listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited.” — *Scheme*
2. Transaction summary states the listing is the consequence of the merger, not an IPO or a demerger to ITC shareholders; ITC retains ~73.4% and Happiest Minds holders get ~26.6%. “Thereafter, Happiest Minds to merge with ITC Infotech pursuant to which ITC Infotech will be listed” — *Scheme*
3. The value-creation case for ITC shareholders names independent price discovery as a benefit of having the IT business separately listed. “Creates a listed IT services platform, enabling independent value discovery and strategic flexibility” — *Scheme*
4. Regulation 30 disclosure frames the deal as the execution of ITCI's existing standalone expansion strategy, aimed at a step change in revenue scale and competitiveness. “ITC Infotech's 'Orbit Next' strategy envisages rapid global expansion through capability led strategic partnerships.” — *Scheme*
5. The industry slide gives the explicit scale threshold problem the separation-and-combination is meant to clear — being below US$1bn keeps ITCI off large buyers' vendor lists. “> $1Bn revenue puts provider on the vendor management  office radar” — *Scheme*
6. Media statement sets the quantified target for the combined, listed entity: US$1 billion revenue by FY28 on a pro-forma basis, AI-first, with 19,000+ professionals. “ITC Infotech (ITCI), a wholly owned subsidiary of ITC Limited and a leading global technology services player, today announced the proposed strategic combination with Happiest Minds Technologies Limited (Happiest Minds) to create a scaled, future-ready, AI-first global technology services enterprise.” — *Scheme*
7. Synergy slide quantifies what the combination is expected to deliver financially: roughly 10% revenue synergies, about 100 bps of margin expansion, and EPS accretion in year one. “Expected to be EPS accretive in first full year of combined entity operations” — *Scheme*
8. ITC's Chairman Sanjiv Puri justifies it on complementarity of capability and culture rather than on any investor, lender or partner demand. “The coming together of our complementary strengths, deep domain expertise and future-ready capabilities will further enhance our ability to deliver cutting-edge solutions across geographies.” — *Scheme*
9. The only external party pressing for a change of ownership is the Happiest Minds promoter selling the 22.106% stake, who wanted a larger home for his company. “We believe that ITC Infotech is the best partner for Happiest Minds to fulfil its destiny and we are pleased that our team will have a welcoming new home .” — *Scheme*
10. ITCI's CEO Manas Chakraborty positions the rationale as capability completeness — full-stack AI-led transformation — rather than financial engineering. “Integrating Happiest Minds' Digital Engineering, Data, AI, and Cybersecurity capabilities with our deep domain expertise, cloud and engineering capabilities will enable us to serve as a full stack AI-led transformation partner.” — *Scheme*
11. At the parent level ITC is simultaneously simplifying in the opposite direction, absorbing wholly owned Sproutlife Foods (Yoga Bar; FY26 turnover Rs 451.71 crores, total assets Rs 150.07 crores) on 2 November 2026. “Result in reduction of the number of operating entities to simplify the corporate holding structure.” — *Scheme*
12. The 1 September 2026 filing shows pre-listing entity cleanup: step-down subsidiaries Blazeclan and Cloudlytics were merged into ITC Infotech with appointed date 1 October 2024. “Accordingly, with effect from 1st September , 2026, BTPL and CTPL stand  dissolved without winding up and have cease d to be subsidiaries of the Company.” — *Scheme*
13. Completion is conditional and long-dated — about 15 months — with CCI, exchange/SEBI, shareholder, creditor and NCLT approvals, and the two firms operating independently until then. “The compani es expect the transaction to be completed within the next                     15 months and will continue to operate independently until all approvals have been obtained.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** No earnings-call transcripts were provided, so the idea is traceable only through filings: ITC had already demerged its Hotels business (visible as discontinued operations with Rs 15,163.06 crores of exceptional items in FY2024-25 and ITC Hotels Limited now an associate), establishing the separation template. The IT separation surfaces fully formed on 31 August 2026, when ITCI's board approved both the 22.106% promoter-stake purchase and the Happiest Minds amalgamation that will list ITCI, endorsed the same day by ITC's board. Housekeeping then followed in the opposite, consolidating direction: on 1 September 2026 step-down subsidiaries Blazeclan Technologies and Cloudlytics were dissolved into ITC Infotech (appointed date 1 October 2024), tidying the entity to be listed, while on 2 November 2026 ITC moved the other way at the parent by absorbing wholly owned Sproutlife Foods (Yoga Bar) to 'reduce the number of operating entities'. The plan's indicative sequencing was set at board approval in Aug'26, Tranche 1 and exchange/SEBI no-objection around Q3FY27-early Q4FY27, shareholder/creditor meetings Mar-Apr'27 and ITCI listing in Q2-Q3 FY28.

**What management expects from it:** ITC Infotech: step change to ~US$1bn revenue by FY28 (from Rs 4,718 crores FY26), Americas mix 27%→38%, BFSI 12%→20%, Build:Run 50:50, ~10% revenue synergies, ~100 bps margin expansion, EPS accretive in year one, 19,000+ people, 800+ clients. ITC: a separately listed IT platform giving independent value discovery and strategic flexibility, while retaining ~73.4%.

*Not explained on the calls:* No earnings-call transcripts supplied; filings never explain ITC's intent for its 73.4% stake, any ITC-shareholder entitlement, carve-out/dis-synergy costs, valuation basis, or the earlier hotels demerger's rationale.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* Separation revealed hotel assets carried far below fair value: FY2025 exceptional items of ₹15,179.43 crores (standalone discontinued operations) and a ₹15,617.37 crores gain on fair valuation of net assets distributed, against only ₹572.52 crores pre-exceptional PBT from hotels; parent retains cash-generative cigarettes.
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *Read next:* The Scheme of Demerger of Hotels business, plus ITC Hotels Limited's own results behind ITC's ₹5,288.24 crores equity-method investment.
- *In their words:* “The Company is currently focused on three business groups : FMCG, Paperboards, Paper & Packaging and Agri Business.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The business being separated is STL's Global Services (system integration / network-deployment) business, demerged out of Sterlite Technologies Limited (STLTECH) into a separate listed entity, STL Networks Limited, rebranded 'Invenia', leaving STL as a pure optical business (optical fibre, fibre cable, specialty cable, optical connectivity) plus the small STL Digital IT-services arm. Management's stated reason was portfolio simplification and focus: Ankit Agarwal said on the May 2025 call that the demerger 'aligns with our goal of portfolio simplification and sets the stage for focused growth in each of the businesses,' and in Jul 2026 placed it in a multi-year clean-up in which STL exited, sold or shut down wireless solutions, OSS/BSS, active components and other businesses to be 'very, very focused on the optical fiber cable connectivity side.' The second reason was capital and working-capital drag: the services business was a project business with large net fund involvement, and on the Jan 2025 call management's stated priority for it was 'select projects intake to improve the profitability and optimize the net fund involvement,' with Tushar Shroff conceding receivables and contract assets in state-government projects like T-Fiber and MahaNet were liquidating slower than planned because they depended on state budgetary allocation. The scale difference management cited: Global Services did INR 289 crores of revenue in Q3 FY25 at only INR 20 crores EBITDA (6.8% margin), versus the optical business at INR 924 crores and INR 119 crores (12.9%); consolidated net debt was INR 2,195 crores at Q3 FY25 and the retained (post-demerger) business reported net debt of about INR 1,350 crores at Q4 FY25, with a stated target of taking net debt/EBITDA from ~3x to 2x. Structurally, management wanted a clean break rather than a carve-out on paper: in Nov 2025 Ajay Jhanjhari said 'the entire thought process of doing demerger is that there should not be any intercompany guarantees because that is a separate company,' and 'No relationship between STL and STL networks from that perspective.' The INR 2,600 crore BharatNet Phase III Jammu & Kashmir package (3-year build plus 10-year maintenance) went with the demerged entity, and STL now supplies cable to it on an arm's-length basis — in Jan 2026 described as 'our group company, Invenia has secured Jammu Kashmir package, where we will be supplying the cable on arm's length basis.' Each entity also got its own leadership and identity: Pankaj Malik as CEO of STL Networks under the Invenia brand, with shareholders receiving a 1:1 share entitlement on holdings as of April 24, 2025. Across the calls, no investor, lender or partner is named as having demanded the separation; the only shareholder pressure visible is generic complaints about poor equity returns and past cash burn (Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26 calls), which management answered by pointing to the business exits, the ~INR 1,000 crore QIP of April 2024, and the demerger as portfolio simplification.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. Completing the demerger of the services business was listed as a formal FY26 strategic priority alongside building value-added services and cutting fund involvement in that business. “Concurrently we will work towards completing the demerger of the services business.” — *[Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=98f6b077-32ee-41f8-b96d-a36366cf2a48.pdf)*
2. CFO Tushar Shroff gave the regulatory timeline — scheme approved by shareholders and creditors on July 10, 2024, petition admitted with NCLT in October 2024, final hearing January 30, 2025 — with listing of the resulting company to follow, and a target of completing the demerger by Q1 FY26. “The final approval is expected in Q4 FY25 after which resulting company is anticipated to be listed on a stock exchanges.” — *[Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=98f6b077-32ee-41f8-b96d-a36366cf2a48.pdf)*
3. The services business was explicitly managed for lower capital absorption, not scale: Q3 FY25 revenue of INR 289 crores produced only INR 20 crores EBITDA (6.8%), and receivables/contract assets in state projects (T-Fiber, MahaNet) were stuck pending state budgetary allocation. “We will continue to build our capability towards value added services and system integration to improve our margins and reduce the fund involvement going forward.” — *[Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=98f6b077-32ee-41f8-b96d-a36366cf2a48.pdf)*
4. Ankit Agarwal announced completion effective March 31, 2025, with the demerged Global Services business operating as STL Networks under the new Invenia brand, Pankaj Malik as CEO, and a 1:1 share entitlement to STL shareholders based on holdings as of April 24, 2025. “This move aligns with our goal of portfolio simplification and sets the stage for focused growth in each of the businesses.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3a33a16d-778d-4047-8e61-79e95df6983b.pdf)*
5. The separation was framed as the last step of a multi-year pruning of the portfolio, after exiting wireless solutions and OSS/BSS, and alongside a ~INR 1,000 crore QIP to repair the balance sheet; the INR 2,600 crore BharatNet J&K package (deployment plus 10 years' maintenance) sat in the demerged entity, not in STL's reported order book. “This is part of the services business, which is now demerged.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=3a33a16d-778d-4047-8e61-79e95df6983b.pdf)*
6. CFO confirmed NCLT final approval was received in February 2025 and that STL Networks was a separate legal entity from March 31, 2025, with share listing still pending regulatory approvals and expected by end-August 2025 (versus the earlier Q1 FY26 / June target). “As of March 31, 2025, STL Networks Limited is now a separate legal entity.” — *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8111472f-4f00-4159-9e5a-70f93bf1b0d8.pdf)*
7. Asked about intercompany loans, advances or guarantees with STL Networks, management said the purpose of the demerger was precisely to have none, while conceding the operational transfer takes about a year to complete. “So, STL networks, the entire thought process of doing demerger is that there should not be any intercompany guarantees because that is a separate company.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=6103688c-1b5b-4922-b304-d2d348f60fea.pdf)*
8. The post-separation relationship is purely commercial: STL supplies optical fibre cable to Invenia's BharatNet Phase III Jammu & Kashmir package on an arm's-length basis, and also holds Manufacturing Authorization Forms with other BharatNet bidders. “And as you know, our group company, Invenia has secured Jammu Kashmir package, where we will be supplying the cable on arm's length basis.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e0a51053-117e-457b-90f3-4487eed18370.pdf)*
9. A year later Ankit cited the demerger, alongside exits from active components and other businesses, as proof of a deliberate narrowing to glass-fibre-cable-connectivity, and ruled out adjacent areas like transceivers and semiconductors. “We've consciously chosen to exit, sell off or shut down many businesses. So -- and we've also demerged our system integration business into a separate entity.” — *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8a08fac5-bc05-4f79-acee-f6a5076525cd.pdf)*
10. The Aug 2026 filing records the legal mechanics: the Scheme of Arrangement was approved by NCLT Mumbai by order dated February 14, 2025, and the Global Services Business demerged into STL Networks Limited from the close of business hours on March 31, 2025, with litigation outcomes of that business (e.g. the Kakinada Smart City writ petition) now accruing to STL Networks. “Please note that pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai, vide order dated February 14, 2025, STL's Global Services Business has been demerged into STL Networks Limited, effective from the close of business hours on March 31, 2025.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** The idea is already in execution by the Jan 23, 2025 call, where it appears as a standing FY26 priority ('work towards completing the demerger of the services business') with the NCLT timeline laid out — scheme approved by shareholders and creditors July 10, 2024, petition admitted October 2024, final hearing January 30, 2025, listing targeted by Q1 FY26. On the May 16, 2025 call Ankit Agarwal declared it done, effective March 31, 2025, named the new entity STL Networks, the new brand Invenia, Pankaj Malik as CEO and the 1:1 share entitlement, and reported the retained business separately at INR 1,350 crores net debt. By Jul 25, 2025 the plan had slipped only on listing (NCLT approval received Feb 2025, shares expected to list 'by the end of August'), and by Nov 6, 2025 the emphasis shifted to completing the operational separation — no intercompany guarantees, a roughly year-long transition to transfer everything. Thereafter it is treated as finished history: Jan 23, 2026 references Invenia only as a BharatNet customer served at arm's length, and Jul 24, 2026 cites 'we've also demerged our system integration business into a separate entity' purely as evidence of focus.

**What management expects from it:** Focused growth in each entity: STL becomes a pure optical manufacturer chasing global top-3, 70-80% utilisation and 20% EBITDA versus ~13-14%, with net debt/EBITDA cut from ~3x to 2x (net debt INR 1,350 crores post-demerger versus INR 2,195 crores consolidated), no intercompany guarantees, and less capital tied up in project/working-capital-heavy services. Invenia gets its own brand, CEO and large-project mandate.

*Not explained on the calls:* No standalone Invenia financials, valuation, debt split, separation costs, or capital allocation given; no investor, lender or partner named as requesting it; listing-date slippage unexplained.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Not stated in the scheme filing; on the Jul 2026 call management said it had "consciously chosen to exit, sell off or shut down many businesses" and demerged system integration to be "very, very focused on the optical fibre cable connectivity side"
- *What it reveals:* Leaves a pure-play optical parent: Q2 FY27 record revenue INR 2,529 Cr, EBITDA INR 846 Cr, PAT INR 517 Cr, order book INR 35,274 Cr, net debt-free, CRISIL AA/Stable. Any Kakinada writ contingent gain now belongs to STL Networks, not STL
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* STL Networks Limited's own August 20, 2026 exchange disclosure and its standalone financials
- *In their words:* “Please note that pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai, vide order dated February 14, 2025, STL's Global Services Business has been demerged into STL Networks Limited, effective from the close of business hours on March 31, 2025.”

For the Transferee Company: "As no new shares are proposed to be issued for the amalgamation of Transferor Company into the Transferee Company, there shall be no change in the shareholding of the Transferee Company after the effectuation of this Scheme."

The entitlement is "1 (One) fully paid-up Equity Share of Rs.2 each of the Resulting Company shall be issued and allotted as fully paid up for every 1 (One) Equity Shares of Re. 2 each fully paid up held in the Demerged Company." For the amalgamation leg no consideration is paid: "There is no cash consideration involved in the Scheme."
