Existing plan in the parent: "During the quarter, the Company had not granted any Employee Stock Options ("ESOPs") under the Refex Employee Stock Option Scheme, 2021 ("ESOP 2021"). However, the Company had allotted 20,057 equity shares of face value of ₹2/-each pursuant to the exercise of vested Employee Stock Options by eligible employees under the said ESOP 2021 on May 01,2026." and "The Company, on November 20, 2025 has made allotment of 2,73,925 equity shares of ₹2/- each, in lieu of exercise of vested Employee Stock Options (ESOPs) under Refex Employee Stock Option Scheme 2021 ("ESOP 2021"), to the eligible employees." No new plan in the resulting company is stated. Warrants are mirrored with a repricing mechanism: "If any share warrants convertible into equity shares of the Demerged Company are outstanding on the Record Date (as defined in the Scheme), upon the Scheme becoming effective and upon vesting of the Demerged Undertaking of the Demerged Company in the Resulting Company, the Resulting Company shall allot share warrants for each warrant outstanding on the Record Date. The adjustments to the issue price of warrants would be based on the net assets (post factoring the impact of merger under Part B of the Scheme), that are transferred to the Resulting Company". Benefit to promoters: "Benefits if any, which may incur to the promoter /promoter group/group companies, will be at par with other public shareholders."
- **Insider actions around the separation:** Promoter warrants lapsed and upfront money forfeited: "On November 07, 2024, the Company had allotted 1,11,70,000 convertible warrants on a preferential basis at an issue price of ₹468/-per warrant (including face value of ₹2/-each) to certain persons belonging to the promoter & promoter group and non-promoter category... As the balance consideration towards the warrants was not received within the stipulated period ending May 06, 2026, the said warrants lapsed upon expiry of the exercise period. Consequently, the upfront amount received on such warrants aggregating to ₹1,30,68,90,000/-has been forfeited by the Company"; management called it deliberate: "It was a deliberate decision. And company has sufficient cash balance and the banking limit and the internal accrual." Earlier promoter subscriptions: "the Company approved the preferential allotment of 1,25,75,000 warrants to Refex Holding Private Limited (formerly Sherisha Technologies Private Limited)(RHPL), Promoter of the Company. Upon exercise of conversion of warrants, the Company allotted 50,00,000 equity shares of ₹2 each to RHPL on July 22, 2024, at an issue price of ₹125 per share... Subsequently, upon exercise of conversion of warrants for the second tranche, the Company allotted the remaining 75,75,000 equity shares on October 3, 2025, at an issue price of ₹125 per share, for an aggregate consideration of ₹94.68 crore". Promoter pledge (Q3 FY26 call): "this catalyst pledge was related to a borrowing at a holdco level and there is a plan over a period of next six months substantial pledge will get reduced. As of now, close to 25%-26% of the promoter holding has been pledged"; on a margin call: "company has taken a steps prepaid you are right the margin call came and we have paid from the own source and we have we have securitized the lender." In the Q4 FY26 call a participant stated "the pledge has only increased to 41%" and management said "We expect some relief would happen in the coming week. And over a period of months, we'll be closing the pledge." Group-level dilution unrelated to the scheme: "the Company diluted its holding of 540 equity shares constituting 0.40% of the total paid up share capital in Venwind Refex Power Limited pursuant to an internal structural realignment."
- **Insiders, per the checklist read:** Directors/KMP have no interest except directorship and shareholding; RIL holds 100% of RML pre-scheme (cancelled); post-scheme promoter and promoter group hold 56.57% of RML, mirroring RIL 1:1. · *option pricing date:* not stated

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The separation is the demerger of Refex's green mobility (electric-vehicle fleet) business out of Refex Industries Ltd (RIL), whose core is Ash & Coal Handling. Management structured it as a composite scheme in two steps: first merge the wholly-owned subsidiary Refex Green Mobility Ltd (RGML) into RIL, then demerge the Mobility Undertaking from RIL into a new, separately listed entity, Refex Mobility Ltd (RML), with mirror shareholding (1 RML share of Rs 2 for every 1 RIL share) and, as Dinesh Agarwal stressed, no valuation exercise required because RGML was a 100% subsidiary. The stated reason is investor fit and value discovery: 'the set of investor for the sustainable and the EV business is a completely different set of investor compared to what is there in the Refex Industries Limited,' so a parallel listing is meant to unlock value; the Scheme adds that the mobility business can attract a different set of investors, lenders and strategic partners, and that its risk, competition, financial profile and return ratios are distinct from ash & coal. The second driver is the drag mobility placed on consolidated results — Q1 FY26 showed standalone PAT of about INR33 crore against consolidated INR20.4 crore, with Green Mobility segment margin at minus 50%, prompting an investor to allege 'a miscalculation in your capital allocation'; management had already exited Bangalore airport B2C services to save INR6.82 crore of annual fixed cost. Post-demerger RIL becomes essentially a single-business company (Anil Jain: '95% business from ash and coal handling only'), while RML carries its own balance sheet — roughly INR220 crore of net assets and, per Jan 2026, 'all the debt etc. will also move to that entity' — and pursues asset-light, clean-fuel, enterprise-led growth toward profitability after crossing about INR100 crore of revenue in three years. Mechanically the appointed date is 1 April 2025, mobility was reported as discontinued operations from FY26, lender NOCs were a gating item, BSE/NSE no-adverse-observation letters came on 16 March 2026, the NCLT application was filed 26 March 2026, and the NCLT-convened shareholder and creditor meetings on 5 August 2026 approved the scheme unanimously (equity shareholders ~99.999% of value in favour).

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. Before any demerger was mentioned, management was already pruning the loss-making B2C part of mobility (Bangalore airport taxis) to cut fixed costs and refocus on B2B/B2B2C. “The withdrawal of service from Bangalore Airport will help us save an annual fixed cost of INR6.82 crores and other variable expenses pertaining to the operation over there.” — *[Apr 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=162e778d-67b5-41c3-a245-daaee5637513.pdf)*
2. An investor confronted management with the gap between standalone PAT (~INR32-33 crore) and consolidated PAT (INR20.4 crore), blaming mobility's minus-50% segment margin; this is the first on-record push to rework the business. “It seems to be there is a miscalculation in your capital allocation, sir. Why don't you focus on coal business and go one by one later on?” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=308de71b-7879-459a-8396-d6990b0a31cb.pdf)*
3. Anil Jain conceded mobility was pulling down consolidated results because EMIs start the day a vehicle is acquired while full utilisation takes 6-9 months, and accepted the need to restructure. “Point well taken, we will try and assess how to rework on these businesses to ensure that we remake them profitable, sir.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=308de71b-7879-459a-8396-d6990b0a31cb.pdf)*
4. First disclosure of the structure on a call: a two-step composite scheme — RGML merges into RIL, then the Mobility Undertaking is demerged into a separately listed Refex Mobility Ltd — framed as unlocking focused value. “On this note, I would like to briefly mention that the de-merger of Refex Green Mobility Limited from Refex Industries Limited is in progress through a
composite scheme comprising two steps.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f2733f9d-0910-4f38-8c2d-f74a1600e438.pdf)*
5. Because RGML is a 100% subsidiary, no valuation was done and shareholders simply get mirror shareholding in the new entity; value is left to the market after listing. BSE/NSE filing done, NCLT next, 6-7 months estimated. “As per the company and the process of merger and demerger process there is no valuations requirement to be done since the company holds 100, it is a 100 subsidiary and a mirror shareholding will happen, all the shareholder of Refex Industries Limited will be same shareholding as per the scheme which has been disclosed there.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f2733f9d-0910-4f38-8c2d-f74a1600e438.pdf)*
6. Lenders were a gating party — final NOCs from lenders were the open item — and management confirmed the demerged entity carries its own debt and operating freedom; INR220 crore of net assets move to Mobility. “Once it is demerged, the Refex Mobility will run as a separate entity where it will have more liberty to do its own business and also it will have its own, all the debt etc. will also move to that entity.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=63755f06-063b-42e8-b635-b18c38eb7a4a.pdf)*
7. Management quantified what leaves the consolidated balance sheet and confirmed RML will be a parallel separate listing rather than a sale. “It is a 100% subsidiary and Refex industry does not own any assets of the Refex Green Mobility. So it is a 100% subsidiary and it will be a parallel separate listing completely.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=63755f06-063b-42e8-b635-b18c38eb7a4a.pdf)*
8. Post-demerger RIL is intended to be effectively a single-business company, with mobility no longer consolidated. “Green mobility will be demerged. So it will be a separate entity. Officially, on a standalone basis, Refex industries will have 100% business, maybe 95% business from ash and coal handling only.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=63755f06-063b-42e8-b635-b18c38eb7a4a.pdf)*
9. The clearest statement of rationale: the EV/sustainability business appeals to a different investor base, and separation is intended to unlock value, with mobility itself on a path to profitability after crossing ~INR100 crore revenue in three years. “The purpose of the demerger is because the set of investor for the sustainable and the EV business is a completely different set of investor compared to what is there in the Refex Industries Limited.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f1aa0b70-a34f-4c91-8973-009a48c493d3.pdf)*
10. Management framed the expected post-separation benefits for each entity — focus, capital allocation and value discovery — and said compliance was complete with only the NCLT court process (75-90 days) pending after BSE and NSE approvals. “We believe this structure will create sharper operational focus, clear capital allocation and stronger long-term value discovery for all the stakeholders.” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=f1aa0b70-a34f-4c91-8973-009a48c493d3.pdf)*
11. The scheme's own rationale rests on the distinct risk/return character of the two businesses and mobility's ability to draw its own investors, lenders and partners, enabling separate capital-market access. “The Green Mobility Business is capable of attracting a different set of investors, lenders, strategic partners and other stakeholders and have significant potential for growth and profitability.” — *Scheme*
12. Shareholders receive a 1:1 mirror entitlement in RML (appointed date 1 April 2025; RIL's existing 50,000 RML shares cancelled), and the August 5, 2026 NCLT-convened meetings approved it with ~99.999% of equity value and unanimous secured/unsecured creditor support. “"1 (One) fully paid-up Equity Share of Rs.2 each of the Resulting Company shall be issued and allotted as fully paid up for every 1 (One) Equity Shares of Re. 2 each fully paid up held in the Demerged Company."” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** Through FY25 (May 2024, Nov 2024, Apr 2025 calls) mobility was presented as a growth vertical to scale to 2,000 then 5,000 EVs, with no separation contemplated; the first visible pressure came on the Aug 13, 2025 call, where an investor attacked the capital allocation given minus-50% mobility margins, and Anil Jain replied 'point well taken, we will try and assess how to rework on these businesses.' The board approved the draft composite scheme on September 22, 2025, and it was first explained to investors on the Nov 6, 2025 call as a two-step merger-then-demerger into a separately listed Refex Mobility Ltd, with a six-to-seven-month timeline and no valuation needed. By Jan 21, 2026 the hold-up was 'final NOCs from the lenders', the net assets moving were quantified at INR220 crore with debt following, and completion was guided to end-April 2026; on May 27, 2026 BSE/NSE approvals were in hand, the NCLT filing done, and 75–90 more days guided. The timeline then slipped: creditor and shareholder meetings were only held August 5, 2026, and the October 28, 2026 press release still shows NCLT hearings pending with the next hearing on 28 October 2026.

**What management expects from it:** RIL becomes a near-pure Ash & Coal Handling play (95-100% of standalone revenue) with sharper focus and clearer capital allocation; RML operates independently, carrying its own debt and ~INR220 crore of net assets, pursuing asset-light clean-fuel and enterprise-led growth toward profitability; the 1:1 mirror listing lets a different investor set value the EV business and unlock shareholder value.

*Not explained on the calls:* No valuation, margin or capital-raise plan for RML; no reason given for the merger-then-demerger structure; no debt split detail; repeated timeline slippage never explained.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Green Mobility's risk, competition, financial profile and return ratios are distinct from Ash & Coal handling; it attracts a different set of investors, so the group plans it as a separate listed entity to unlock value.
- *What it reveals:* Separation leaves parent as high-margin Ash & Coal handling (FY26 PAT ₹247cr, 17% EBITDA, ₹1,721cr orderbook) plus wind; the spin is small and loss-making (segment EBIT −₹38.2cr FY26, ~₹220cr net assets, RGML creditors ₹153cr) but 'progressing steadily towards profitability'.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* Annexure 19 — assets and liabilities demerged into RML; then RML's Information Memorandum and the NCLT sanction order.
- *In their words:* “The Green Mobility Business is capable of attracting a different set of investors, lenders, strategic partners and other stakeholders and have significant potential for growth and profitability.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The business being separated is SBI Funds Management Limited (SBIFM) — SBI Mutual Fund, the bank's asset-management joint venture with Amundi — which SBI is partially separating by listing it, not by demerging it; management repeatedly framed the purpose as "value unlocking" and, in Chairman C.S. Setty's words, "more importantly, value recognition for the industry" (Nov 2025), with SBI General Insurance named alongside AMC as the other listing candidate. The driver management gave was that SBI's own stock does not reflect the conglomerate's worth: Setty called SBI's valuation "a conundrum, considering our return on equity and growth metrics" (Nov 2025, with ROE 19.7%–20.68% and ROA >1% through FY26), and the same theme runs through the hidden-value argument on strategic holdings — of the group's ~7.3% NSE stake he said "the moment NSE gets listed, the whole shareholding by SBI will be available as reserve to us to mark to market" (May 2026). Explicitly NOT a capital-need story at first: in Nov 2025 Setty said "these two companies do not require capital at this juncture. Neither the parent requires because we just raised Rs. 25,000 crores" (the July 2025 QIP, India's largest, 4.5x oversubscribed on a >Rs. 1.1 trillion book, >60% cross-border), which is why timing was left to "respective boards"; by May 2026 the rationale had hardened into a capital one — the listing "will result in capital augmentation, CET-1" on top of CAR already up 115bps to 15.4%. The structure confirms it is monetisation, not a fix for the business: the IPO is a pure offer for sale (no fresh issue), SBI offering 6.3007% and JV partner Amundi India Holding 3.7006%, total up to 10.0013% / 203,709,239 shares at Rs. 1 face value, so no money reaches SBIFM itself. Management stressed that separation does not break the franchise link — SBIFM stays the country's largest AMC inside the "One SBI" cross-sell engine (a special dividend of ~Rs. 2,200 crore came up to the bank in Q3FY26, cross-sell/CVE income targeted at $1 billion, YONO "deep integration with subsidiary production"), and Setty was explicit that "Mutual fund, we are not fully exiting. So we still have potential to monetize further when market improves" (Feb 2026). The push came from the sell side and retail investors — Sushil Choksey (Indus Equity), Manoj Alimchandani and Kunal Shah (Citigroup) raised monetisation/value-unlocking on four of the five calls, Alimchandani even arguing in Feb 2026 that delaying the IPO five years could fetch three times the market cap — rather than from lenders or regulators; the only regulator-linked nudge cited was the SEBI chairman on NSE's listing. No problem with SBIFM's performance was ever offered as a reason: it was described only as "the largest AMC in the country," contributing Rs. 4,969.09 crore of FY26 total income, just 0.70% of group income.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. No separation on the table: subsidiaries framed purely as value creators to be retained, while the bank instead took an enabling resolution to raise Rs. 25,000 crore of its own equity. “Our subsidiaries are consistently performing well and continue to create significant value for all the stakeholders. We will continue to nurture these subsidiaries and maintain leadership position in the respective businesses.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=bba71336-f98b-40e2-8d50-c9435948876b.pdf)*
2. First acknowledgement of listing candidates, asked for by Sushil Choksey (Indus Equity Advisors); Setty explicitly de-prioritised it because the Rs. 25,000 crore QIP had just closed. “No, as we mentioned that we definitely have a couple of candidates for listing, but the timing is not very… there is no sense of urgency there, I believe.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=2fa1b8da-c066-4091-b913-b10127270df1.pdf)*
3. The rationale stated in full for the first time, in answer to Choksey on the group's underperforming consolidated value: SBI AMC and SBI General named, with value unlocking and industry recognition of value as the purpose. “But among these four major subsidiaries, we definitely would be looking at, as I mentioned several times, SBI AMC and SBI General are right candidates for listing in our stable. It also provides some value unlocking and, more importantly, value recognition for the industry.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ad15487a-d1a9-4e33-90e9-624255749750.pdf)*
4. Answering Kunal Shah (Citigroup) on what would trigger the decision, Setty ruled capital need out as a motive for either the subsidiaries or the parent, leaving timing and quantum to the subsidiary boards. “I think we need to just look at, see, one is, as I mentioned earlier also, that these two companies do not require capital at this juncture.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ad15487a-d1a9-4e33-90e9-624255749750.pdf)*
5. The underlying grievance the separation is meant to address — SBI's own market valuation not tracking its ROE and growth — stated in the Chairman's opening remarks; Ashok Ajmera had quantified it as a Rs. 8.82 lakh crore market cap on Rs. 100 trillion of business versus Rs. 15.14 lakh crore for a Rs. 57 trillion peer. “Although the current valuations of SBI are a conundrum, considering our return on equity and growth metrics, we are confident that they will eventually align with our fundamental and operational metrics, the institutionalized nature of our business and our market leadership in the coming years.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=ad15487a-d1a9-4e33-90e9-624255749750.pdf)*
6. Retained-stake logic: asked by Manoj Alimchandani whether delaying the IPO five years could treble the market cap, Setty defended a partial sale that keeps future upside with SBI. “Mutual fund, we are not fully exiting. So we still have potential to monetize further when market improves.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8fabbe0f-593e-4701-b565-d5fce57385a2.pdf)*
7. Why the AMC is worth separating while staying attached: it is already the country's largest AMC, upstreamed a Rs. 2,200 crore special dividend into SBI's Q3FY26 profit, and feeds a cross-sell income stream management targets at $1 billion. “If I have to talk about one-off, I think the one item which is a special dividend we have received, around Rs. 2,200 crores from SBI Mutual Fund.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=8fabbe0f-593e-4701-b565-d5fce57385a2.pdf)*
8. The rationale shifts to capital: with the AMC listing under way, Setty tied it to CET-1 augmentation supporting credit growth (the bank could already fund ~Rs. 12 trillion of growth, CAR 15.4%, up 115bps YoY). “We are also seriously, as you are aware, we have embarked on listing SBI AMC and hopefully in this financial year we will be able to complete, which will result in capital augmentation, CET-1.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9a3280a0-5ce9-445e-a881-6b7c505e9a90.pdf)*
9. Same hidden-value argument applied to the group's ~7.3% NSE holding, which is not marked to market today — listing is the mechanism that converts unrecognised strategic stakes into reported reserves. “But as you mentioned, I think the moment NSE gets listed, the whole shareholding by SBI will be available as reserve to us to mark to market.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=9a3280a0-5ce9-445e-a881-6b7c505e9a90.pdf)*
10. 6 Nov 2025 board approval, restated in the 19 Mar 2026 DRHP filing: a pure offer for sale of up to 10.0013% (203,709,239 shares of Rs. 1 each) — SBI 6.3007% (128,334,397 shares) and JV partner Amundi India Holding 3.7006% (75,374,842 shares). No fresh issue, so no proceeds go to SBIFM. “The IPO comprises an offer for sale of up to 128,334,397 Equity Shares (amounting to 6.3007% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFML) by State Bank of India, and of up to 75,374,842 Equity Shares (amounting to 3.7006% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFML) by Amundi India Holding.” — *Scheme*
11. Plan changed in execution: a pre-IPO secondary placement on 9–10 July 2026 moved 1.4156% of pre-offer capital to 30 investors at the eventual Rs. 574 offer price, raising Rs. 1,655 crore for SBI ahead of the book build. “State Bank of India had entered into share purchase agreements each dated July 9, 2026 to sell, in aggregate, 2,88,32,748 equity shares of SBIFM of face value Rs. 1 (one) each ("Equity Shares"), being equivalent to 1.4156% of pre-Offer share capital of SBIFM, to a total of 30 (thirty) investors at Rs. 574.00 per Equity Share, for an aggregate consideration of Rs. 1,655.00 crores.” — *Scheme*
12. The 11 July 2026 addendum cut SBI's offer-for-sale by exactly the pre-IPO quantum, to 4.8851% (total offer 8.3933%); the offer was priced at Rs. 574 on 16 July with a Rs. 54 employee discount and allotment expected on or about 18 July 2026. “The size of the offer for sale by the State Bank of India in the IPO has been revised from up to 128,334,397 Equity Shares (amounting to 6.3007% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFM) to up to 99,501,649 Equity Shares (amounting to 4.8851% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFM).” — *Scheme*
13. Materiality disclosed for the separated business: SBIFM's FY2026 total income of Rs. 4,969.09 crore is 0.70% of group income and its reserves 0.59% of group reserves — the separation is about price discovery, not size. “Total income: Rs. 4,969.09 crores (0.70% of Total Income of SBI Group)” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** May 2025 had no separation plan at all — only "we will continue to nurture these subsidiaries," while the bank instead took an enabling resolution for Rs. 25,000 crore of its own equity. By Aug 2025 Setty conceded "a couple of candidates for listing, but… there is no sense of urgency," and in Nov 2025 he named them — SBI AMC and SBI General — as the right candidates for "value unlocking" and "value recognition," with boards to set timing; the SBIFM stake-sale approval for 6.3007% followed on 6 Nov 2025 and the DRHP on 19 Mar 2026 (share count restated to 128,334,397 after a bonus issue and ESOP exercises). Feb 2026 added the retained-upside caveat ("we are not fully exiting") and May 2026 re-cast the deal as CET-1 capital augmentation to be completed within FY27. The plan then changed in execution in July 2026: a pre-IPO placement of 28,832,748 shares (1.4156%) to 30 investors at Rs. 574 for Rs. 1,655 crore on 9–10 July cut SBI's offer-for-sale from 6.3007% to 4.8851% (total offer 8.3933%), priced at Rs. 574 with allotment expected 18 July 2026.

**What management expects from it:** For SBIFM: a listed market price that recognises India's largest AMC, with SBI retaining control, banca distribution and future monetisation upside. For SBI: value unlocking and "value recognition," CET-1 capital augmentation supporting 13-15% credit growth, hidden reserves surfaced (as with NSE), and valuation converging on >1% ROA and 15%+ through-cycle ROE. No margin or focus benefit was claimed.

*Not explained on the calls:* No valuation target, expected proceeds, CET-1 basis points, or use of funds; no reason the offer was trimmed; Amundi's motive, SBI General's timeline, and post-listing distribution/royalty terms unexplained.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Value unlocking and value recognition for the industry; listing will result in capital augmentation, CET-1, supporting credit growth; subsidiaries seen creating value for their own shareholders and SBI's
- *What it reveals:* A dominant AMC carried at cost: total income Rs.4,969.09 crores, only 0.70% of SBI Group income, reserves Rs.3,533.09 crores; priced at Rs.574/share. Chairman cites "hidden reserves... in terms of strategic investments" not marked to market, plus Rs.2,200 crores special dividend
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* SBIFM Prospectus dated July 16, 2026 — AUM, PAT and implied valuation at Rs.574 versus SBI's retained stake
- *In their words:* “State Bank of India has been informed that the Offer Price for the Offer has been decided to be Rs. 574.00 per Equity Share.”

**What the documents themselves say about the differences:**

- **other** — parent / remaining: Listing SBI AMC is presented as capital augmentation / CET-1 accretion for the bank, alongside the mark-to-market unlocking if NSE lists; the bank says it can already fund about Rs 12 trillion of credit growth with current capital.; separated business: SBI Funds Management is the vehicle for that unlocking; only a minority stake is sold and SBI is "not fully exiting". “We are also seriously, as you are aware, we have embarked on listing SBI AMC and hopefully in this financial year we will be able to complete, which will result in capital augmentation, CET -1.”
- **growth** — parent / remaining: Bank guidance of 13-15% credit growth for FY27, domestic NIM above 3%, ROA above 1% through the cycles and minimum 15% ROE through cycles (ROE 18.5% at end-Q4FY26, 20.68% at end-Q3FY26).; separated business: The mutual fund business is described as having a large growth runway, with talk of the industry doubling in five years and SBI Mutual Fund as the largest AMC in the country. “I see a great opportunity for mutual fund growth and SBI mutual fund will be playing a very, very large role in this.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: The AMC contributes to the parent through dividends and trail/cross-sell income: a one-off special dividend of about Rs. 2,200 crores from SBI Mutual Fund was a major element of Q3FY26 miscellaneous income (of about Rs. 5,000 crores).; separated business: SBIFM's own Fiscal 2026 total income was Rs. 4,969.09 crores, 0.70% of SBI Group total income; reserves and surplus Rs. 3,533.09 crores, 0.59% of the group's. “If I have to talk about one -off, I think the one item which is a special dividend we have received, around Rs. 2,200 crores from SBI Mutual Fund.”
- **capex and capital intensity** — parent / remaining: The parent raised Rs 25,000 crores of equity by QIP in Q2FY26 (largest ever in India, oversubscribed 4.5 times) and says neither it nor the listing candidates need capital at this juncture; the listings are for value unlocking and recognition, not funding.; separated business: "these two companies do not require capital at this juncture" — i.e. the AMC (and SBI General) are not being listed to raise money for themselves; the 2026 IPO is a pure offer for sale with no fresh issue. “I think we need to just look at, see, one is, as I mentioned earlier also, that these two companies do not require capital at this juncture.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

These texts contain no separation, demerger, spin-off or scheme of arrangement for HDFC Bank, and management never explains one; the question's premise is not supported by the documents supplied. The only business that was partly separated from the Bank is HDB Financial Services Limited (HDBFS), the group's non-deposit-taking NBFC, and that was done by listing it rather than by demerging it: a June 25, 2025 IPO comprising a fresh issue of Rs 2,500.00 crore plus an offer for sale of Rs 10,000.00 crore of the Bank's shares (13,51,35,135 shares of Rs 10 each at Rs 740 per share), after which the Bank still held 74.1%. Management gave no reason for the listing at all — no regulatory mandate, no capital need, no valuation argument, no investor or lender demand was cited; Sashidhar Jagdishan only reported that 'we carried out the HDB Financial Services listing process, wherein the bank also diluted some stake' and thanked IPO investors. The only strategic point made about HDBFS was in answer to Pranav Gundlapalle (Jul 2025), who asked about customer conflict between the two entities: management said HDBFS serves a segment 'a notch or two below' the Bank, with 'zero or very minimal overlap' expected to persist, i.e. the two are kept distinct by customer segment and pricing, not separated to fix a problem. Financially the event was treated as a one-off gain — Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone and Rs 7,000.27 crore consolidated (before tax, net of IPO expenses) — which Srinivasan Vaidyanathan later flagged (Jul 2026) as a base-effect distortion making reported PAT growth 5% versus 9.8% adjusted. Every other corporate action in these texts runs the other way: deepening the 2023 HDFC Limited merger (Apr 2026: e-HDFC home-loan customers' liability penetration up from 36% to ~50%, their CASA balances up from about Rs 50,000 crore to Rs 86,000 crore, 98% of new home loans opening a liability account, 23% carrying active Bank credit cards) and the Apr 16, 2026 board approval to invest up to Rs 1,000 crore in HDFC Life's preferential issue. The closest thing to a forward-looking separation hint is Jagdishan's unprompted remark on surplus capital (Oct 2025): if options arise 'to sort of delight shareholders, we would be more than happy to do so' — unspecified, with no business named.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The only partial separation disclosed in any call: HDBFS was listed and the Bank sold down part of its holding, reported as a completed process with no stated rationale. “During the quarter, we carried out the HDB Financial Services listing process, wherein the bank also diluted some stake, and which eventually culminated in the stocks being listed on 2nd of July.” — *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d1268138-e288-4335-9764-7a944dfa3570.pdf)*
2. Asked by Pranav Gundlapalle (Bernstein) whether the Bank and HDBFS would end up chasing the same customers, Jagdishan said HDBFS sits a notch or two below the Bank's segment on customer profile and pricing. “HDB, we have maintained this. I think the segment that they cater to is about a notch or two below that of HDFC Bank.” — *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d1268138-e288-4335-9764-7a944dfa3570.pdf)*
3. Management framed the two entities as permanently distinct by segmentation rather than as a business being carved out to solve a conflict. “There is zero or very minimal overlap at this juncture that will continue to stay for a long period of time.” — *[Jul 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d1268138-e288-4335-9764-7a944dfa3570.pdf)*
4. On the capital question (CET1 near 20%, draft RWA relief, ECL), Jagdishan said capital will be consumed once FY27 growth exceeds system growth, but left unnamed shareholder-friendly options open — the only forward-looking hint of any corporate action. “Having said that, if there are any opportunities that may arise in terms of other options that are available to sort of delight shareholders, we would be more than happy to do so.” — *Oct 2025*
5. The Jan 17, 2026 filing quantifies the HDBFS sell-down: fresh issue of Rs 2,500 crore plus Rs 10,000 crore offer for sale by the Bank, 13,51,35,135 shares at Rs 740, producing a Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone gain (Rs 7,000.27 crore consolidated) with the Bank retaining 74.1%. “On June 25, 2025, the Bank's subsidiary company, HDB Financial Services Limited ("HDBFS") launched its initial public offering ("IPO"), comprised of a fresh issuance of equity shares aggregating to 2,500.00 crore and an offer for sale ("OFS") of equity shares by the Bank, aggregating to 10,000.00 crore.” — *Scheme*
6. Six weeks before the Apr 2026 call the Board moved in the opposite direction, approving fresh capital into a subsidiary rather than any separation, subject to RBI approval. “the Board of Directors of the Bank, at its meeting held today i.e. on April 16, 2026, approved investment of an amount not exceeding Rs. 1,000 crore (Rupees One thousand crore only) in the preferential issue of equity shares to be made by HDFC Life Insurance Company Limited, a subsidiary of the Bank” — *Scheme*
7. Kaizad Bharucha's merger-synergy update shows integration, not separation: e-HDFC mortgage customers' liability penetration up from 36% to ~50%, their CASA from about Rs 50,000 crore to Rs 86,000 crore, 60-65% paying EMIs from in-house accounts, 23% holding active Bank credit cards. “Net of attritions, net of acquisitions over this journey, this 36% has come as high as 50% within the last 2.5 years.” — *[Apr 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=a77abbbb-954a-4221-8240-67bf0da6ba1c.pdf)*
8. The HDBFS transaction appears only as a prior-year one-timer distorting the growth base, with adjusted PAT growth of 9.8% versus 5% reported — the last mention of it in any call. “But last year included certain one-timers like HDB gains and then we had a floating provision counter-cyclical buffer that we added and some contingent provision and so on.” — *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=509cc499-6cb1-4d9f-8de9-9c7de6c70eef.pdf)*
9. At the special call on Atanu Chakraborty's resignation, the only structural change hinted at was an internal reorganisation of responsibilities, explicitly not a business separation and with nothing decided. “Yes, as I said, as we move forward, we will sort of re-examine our organization structure and with the consent and the advice of the board, we will announce it at the appropriate time.” — *[Mar 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=56739132-e21e-4503-aeb6-85f4f53c1244.pdf)*

**How it evolved:** Jul 19, 2025: the HDB Financial Services IPO and the Bank's stake dilution are reported as completed (listed Jul 2, 2025), with no rationale, and management answers only the question of bank-versus-HDBFS customer overlap. Oct 18, 2025: asked by Chintan (Autonomous) what the Bank will do with excess CET1, Jagdishan leaves the door open to unnamed 'other options... to delight shareholders' while stressing capital will be consumed once growth accelerates from FY27. Jan 17, 2026 filings quantify the transaction (Rs 10,000 crore OFS, Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone gain, 74.1% residual stake); Apr 16, 2026 the Board instead commits up to Rs 1,000 crore of fresh capital to subsidiary HDFC Life. Jul 18, 2026: the HDB gain is referred to only retrospectively, as a prior-year one-timer depressing headline PAT growth to 5% versus 9.8% adjusted — the idea never develops into any separation plan.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing was said about a separation, because none was announced. For the one partial carve-out, the HDBFS listing, management claimed no margin, capital, valuation or focus benefit; it cited only a Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone one-time gain (later called a base-effect distortion) and segment distinctness — HDBFS one to two notches below the Bank, with minimal customer overlap.

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything: no separation, demerger or scheme exists here. No reason, regulator, lender or investor demand, valuation case, timeline or margin/capital effect for the HDBFS listing is given.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* Sale of 13,51,35,135 shares at Rs 740 raised Rs 10,000 crore, netting Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone gain (Rs 7,000.27 crore consolidated) — implying carrying value far below market; HDBFSL loan book Rs 1,146 billion, Stage 3 2.81%, CAR 21.8%.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* HDBFS's own standalone financials and shareholding pattern — the Bank's residual 74.1% stake and its carrying value.
- *In their words:* “On June 25, 2025, the Bank's subsidiary company, HDB Financial Services Limited ("HDBFS") launched its initial public offering ("IPO"), comprised of a fresh issuance of equity shares aggregating to ₹ 2,500.00 crore and an offer for sale ("OFS") of equity shares by the Bank, aggregating to ₹ 10,000.00 crore.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The business being separated is Linjemontage i Grästorp AB (LMG), KPIL's Swedish power-grid EPC subsidiary held through Kalpataru Power Transmission Sweden AB (KPTS) — separated not by demerger but by an offer-for-sale IPO on Nasdaq Stockholm (listed 25 September 2026), in which KPTS sold down from 96.12% to 66.45% rather than giving LMG new capital. The trigger management cited on the calls was value crystallisation and cash: LMG had compounded from ~INR1,000 crores revenue in FY24 to INR1,800+ crores in FY25 (PBT INR21 crores to INR70+ crores) to ~INR3,000 crores in FY26 with EBITDA ~INR200 crores and PBT ~INR170 crores (both up over 100%), i.e. SEK1.3bn to SEK3.2bn net sales at a 56.6% CAGR with adjusted EBITA margin rising from 4.4% to 7.6%, net cash of SEK172.1m, ROCE of 48.1% and an order book of SEK4,349m — yet it was only ~11.14% of KPIL's consolidated revenue and ~4.5% of consolidated net worth. Mohnot repeatedly placed the Sweden 'fundraise' inside the same bucket as the noncore exits (Vindhyachal road asset sold January 2026 for ~INR799 crores EV / INR600+ crores net, Indore real estate, Shree Shubham Logistics), i.e. as a source of 'further cash flows' to cut leverage and fund the INR800-900 crores/year capex programme and lift ROCE; the IPO delivered KPTS gross proceeds of ~SEK711.45m at SEK46/share, valuing LMG at SEK2,356.6m (~INR2,324 crores). The second problem it solves is that LMG's economics are structurally different from KPIL's: management argued a 6%-7% PBT in a 'mature market' is fine there because 'the ROCE numbers are very, very high and they are cash positive always' — a profile the consolidated KPIL multiple was not reflecting. LMG's own filings justify the separation on strategic grounds: visibility, credibility and brand recognition with customers, partners and employees, transparency, a platform for long-term value creation, a broadened shareholder base, and support for its ambition to lead Nordic power-infrastructure EPC in a Swedish serviceable market growing from ~SEK19bn (2025) to ~SEK31bn (2030) at 11% CAGR (transmission 17%), with ~80% of Sweden's transmission grid over 40 years old and Statnett planning NOK150-200bn of 2025-2034 investment. Pressure came from investors and analysts, not lenders: Carnelian and DAM Capital pushed management on why a T&D business sitting inside a T&D company needed its own listing, while cornerstone demand from Tredje AP-fonden and Unionen (SEK290m) anchored the book; LMG's management/employee shareholders (991,950 shares) sold mainly to repay the financing they had used to buy their shares. KPIL stressed continuity, not exit: KPTS 'indicated an intention to remain a long-term major shareholder', is locked up for 360 days, and LMG remains a step-down subsidiary.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. Baseline: no separation plan existed; LMG was simply presented as a record performer, with revenue doubling and an all-time-high order book of INR3,143 crores. “LMG's order book is at a all time high of INR3,143 crores.” — *[Feb 2025](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q3_FY25_Transcript.pdf)*
2. First disclosure of the separation idea — the Board approved bankers and intermediaries to study fundraising options at Linjemontage, mentioned in the same breath as LMG's PBT rising from ~INR21 crores to ~INR70+ crores. “the Board has also approved appointment of bankers as well as intermediaries to look at fund options, fundraising options in Sweden Linjemontage in the last Board meeting, which we have declared to everyone.” — *[May 2025](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q4_FY25_Transcript.pdf)*
3. Formalised as a disclosed 'strategic overview' with an IPO explicitly named as one of the options, and merchant bankers and advisers appointed; LMG had already begun preparatory steps. “We have initiated a strategic overview on LMG where various options are being evaluated, including options related to IPO, subject to market conditions.” — *[Aug 2025](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q1FY26_transcript.pdf)*
4. An investor (Mihir Manohar, Carnelian Capital) pressed on exactly the question management never answered — why carve out a T&D business that already sits inside a T&D company; Mohnot declined to comment. “I just wanted to understand the thought process because I mean, it is also T&D business similarly sitting in KPIL.” — *[Aug 2025](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q1FY26_transcript.pdf)*
5. Management explained LMG's different economic profile — lower PBT than KPIL's core but very high ROCE and permanently cash positive — the implicit valuation argument for separating it, with bankers still mandated and the path undecided. “As far as margins are concerned, I think that those are mature markets where a PBT of 6% to 7% is very reasonably good because the ROCE numbers are very, very high and they are cash positive always.” — *[Oct 2025](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q2_FY26_Transcript.pdf)*
6. The Sweden transaction was placed squarely in the monetisation/debt-reduction bucket alongside transmission assets, the last road asset and Shree Shubham Logistics, with cash expected in FY26-27. “We do not know which options and what timing it exactly is, but we have appointed bankers to look at exploring fund option raising at Sweden also, which I'm expecting in FY26-27 should give us further cash flows.” — *[Feb 2026](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPIL_Q3_FY26_Earnings_Call_Transcript-5th_feb_2026.pdf)*
7. Final pre-IPO framing: a 'strategic investment' into the Swedish subsidiary grouped with remaining divestments as free-cash-flow events to strengthen the balance sheet, set against INR800+ crores of annual capex and net debt already down 50% to INR915 crores. “We also have some events of free cash flows coming in next year, whether it is through a few more divestments which are left, which might happen either next year or a year after that or whether it is through some strategic investment coming into our Swedish subsidiary in whatever form it comes.” — *[May 2026](https://kalpataruprojects.com/api/view-file/KPILQ4_FY26_Earnings_Call_Transcript_final.pdf)*
8. The 9 September 2026 filing/press release gives the official rationale — standalone visibility, credibility, brand and Nordic leadership ambition — and discloses LMG's scale: SEK3,225m FY26 revenue (~11.14% of KPIL consolidated revenue) but only SEK334m net worth (~4.5% of KPIL's). “The Listing is expected to enhance the Company's visibility, credibility and brand recognition among customers, partners and employees, and to support Linjemontage's long-term ambition to strengthen its position in the Nordics as one of the leading EPC providers within power infrastructure.” — *Scheme*
9. Transparency, long-term value creation and a diversified shareholder base are the stated second leg, with KPTS committing to stay a long-term major shareholder (360-day lock-up) and LMG remaining a step-down subsidiary. “Becoming a publicly listed company will also provide greater transparency and a platform for long-term value creation, while diversifying the shareholder base.” — *Scheme*
10. Structurally this is a pure sell-down, not a capital raise for LMG: 14,311,620 base shares plus a 2,146,743-share greenshoe at SEK46, ~32.1% of LMG, giving KPTS gross proceeds of ~SEK711.45m at a SEK2,356.6m (~INR2,324 crores) valuation and taking KPTS from 96.12% to 66.45% after the partial greenshoe exercise of 1,877,911 shares. “The Offering consists only of existing shares and the Company will therefore not receive any proceeds from the Offering.” — *Scheme*
11. Demand was investor-led: Tredje AP-fonden and Unionen cornerstoned SEK290m, while LMG's own management/director/employee holders sold 991,950 shares chiefly to repay the borrowings used to buy them. “All individual Selling Shareholders other than Kalpataru Sweden are selling shares in the Offering primarily to repay financing arrangements relating to their respective acquisitions of shares in the Company.” — *Scheme*
12. LMG's standalone financial targets quantify what separation is meant to unlock — revenue above SEK5bn, adjusted EBITA margin above 8% (from 7.6%), net debt/adj EBITDA below 1.0x and a 25% dividend payout — in a market growing 11% CAGR to SEK31bn by 2030. “Profitability : Linjemontage aims to reach an adjusted EBITA margin exceeding 8 per cent in the medium term.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced on the 19 May 2025 Q4 FY25 call, where Mohnot disclosed that the Board had approved appointing bankers and intermediaries to examine 'fundraising options' at Linjemontage — framed alongside the noncore clean-up (VEPL, Indore, Shubham); the 14 Feb 2025 call had contained no such plan, only LMG's record order book of INR3,143 crores. By 8 August 2025 (Q1 FY26) it had hardened into a disclosed 'strategic overview… including options related to IPO, subject to market conditions', and management refused to explain the logic when Carnelian asked why a T&D business inside a T&D company needed a separate listing, even withdrawing LMG margin guidance because the process had started. On 31 October 2025 Mohnot said the path was still undecided but expected 'some light' on valuation in FY26-27, and on 5 February 2026 he said the Sweden mandate was 'progressing well' and should throw off cash in FY26-27; by 15 May 2026 he described it only as 'some strategic investment coming into our Swedish subsidiary in whatever form it comes'. The form was fixed in the filings: KPTS board approval on 9 September 2026, prospectus and SEK46 price on 16 September, listing and ~32.1% offer on 25 September, and partial greenshoe exercise on 23-24 October 2026 leaving KPIL at 66.45%.

**What management expects from it:** For LMG: standalone visibility, credibility and brand with customers and employees; transparency; a growth platform and broadened shareholder base; revenue above SEK5bn, adjusted EBITA margin above 8%, net debt/EBITDA under 1.0x, 25% payout. For KPIL: ~SEK711m cash to cut debt and fund capex, value crystallised at SEK2.36bn, retained 66.45% control, higher ROCE and a cleaner noncore-free core EPC portfolio.

*Not explained on the calls:* Calls never explained why a listing over a trade sale, the valuation sought, use of proceeds, dilution to consolidated EPS, or minority/governance terms; management explicitly refused to give the rationale.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Board and majority shareholder Kalpataru Sweden consider the listing a strategic next step: enhancing visibility, credibility and brand recognition, greater transparency, a platform for long-term value creation, while diversifying the shareholder base
- *What it reveals:* A high-return asset-light business priced publicly: FY25/26 net sales SEK 3,225m, adjusted EBITA SEK 245m (7.6%), R.O.C.E. 48.1%, net cash SEK 172.1m, order book SEK 4,349m, valued at SEK 2,356,557,000 — yet only ~11.14% of KPIL revenue and ~4.5% of its net worth
- *Parent or spin:* — · *Read next:* LMG's prospectus on linjemontage.com (Q1 26/27 figures, Selling Shareholders) and LMG's traded price versus the SEK 46 offer
- *In their words:* “Linjemontage's Board of Directors and its majority shareholder, Kalpataru Sweden, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Kalpataru Projects International Limited ("Kalpataru India"), consider the Listing to be a strategic next step in Linjemontage's development.”

**What the documents themselves say about the differences:**

- **growth** — parent / remaining: KPIL consol revenue grew 22% Y-o-Y in FY26 to INR 27,143 crores (standalone 23%); FY27 guidance "around 15% plus top line growth"; separated business: LMG net sales grew from ~SEK 1.3 billion (FY 2023/2024) to SEK 3.2 billion (FY 2025/2026), a CAGR of 56.6 per cent; Q1 26/27 net sales fell 5.8%; target of more than SEK 5 billion revenue in the medium term “The Company has demonstrated strong financial performance, with net sales growing from approximately SEK 1.3 billion in the financial year 2023/2024 to SEK 3.2 billion in the financial year 2025/2026, representing a CAGR of 56.6 per cent.”
- **operating margin** — parent / remaining: KPIL consol PBT margin expanded 120 bps to 4.9% in FY26 and consol/standalone EBITDA margins were 8.3% and 8.4% for 9M FY26; FY27 guidance of 75 bps consol PBT margin expansion; separated business: LMG adjusted EBITA margin 7.6% in FY 25/26 (4.4% in FY 24/25, 10.8% in Q1 26/27); on the FY26 call LMG EBITDA was ~6.7%–6.8% and PBT ~5.6%–5.7%; target of adjusted EBITA margin exceeding 8 per cent in the medium term “For the financial year ended 31 March 2026, Linjemontage's net sales amounted to SEK 3,225 million, with an adjusted EBITA of SEK 245 million, corresponding to an adjusted EBITA margin of 7.6 per cent.”
- **debt and leverage** — parent / remaining: KPIL cut consol net debt by over 50% to INR 915 crores in FY26, with consol and standalone net debt to equity at "a multiyear historic low of 0.1x" and finance cost to sales down 80 bps to 1.8%; separated business: LMG is in net cash: net cash SEK 172.1 million at Q1 26/27 (SEK 164.7 million at FY 25/26); "they hardly have interest cost"; target net debt to adjusted EBITDA below 1.0x “Linjemontage benefits from a strong balance sheet with a net cash position of SEK 172.1 million, providing financial flexibility to invest in organic and inorganic growth initiatives or return capital to shareholders through dividends.”
- **return on capital** — parent / remaining: KPIL consol ROCE improved to exceed 21% in FY26, with ROCE up more than 500 basis points over the last 5 years; separated business: LMG R.O.C.E. of 48.1% in FY 25/26 (33.9% in FY 24/25; 41.7% in Q1 26/27), attributed to its asset-light model “The adjusted EBITA margin has increased to approximately 7.6 per cent in the financial year 2025/2026, while the Company's asset-light business model contributed to a R.O.C.E. of 48.1 per cent.”
- **working capital** — parent / remaining: KPIL optimised its consol working capital cycle to 75 days in FY26 (standalone 90 days), with INR ~1,600 crores of Water receivables outstanding; separated business: LMG operates with low net working capital relative to sales and consistently generates solid operating cash flows “The Company operates with low net working capital relative to sales and minimal capital expenditure requirements as a percentage of sales, consistently generating solid operating cash flows.”
- **capex and capital intensity** — parent / remaining: KPIL invested nearly INR 900 crores of capex in FY26 (nearly INR 3,000 crores over 5 years) and budgets INR 800-plus crores for FY27 on plants, shuttering, equipment and TBMs; separated business: LMG's business model is asset-light and scalable with minimal capex requirements as a percentage of sales “What makes this balance sheet performance truly remarkable is that we delivered it while continuing to invest nearly INR 900 crores in capex and pursued a strong top line growth of 22% in FY26.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: No dividend policy for KPIL is stated in these documents; KPIL consol PAT INR 1,031 crores and consol EPS INR 61 per share in FY26; separated business: LMG has adopted a stated dividend policy of distributing 25 per cent of net profit after tax as annual dividends over time “Dividend policy: Linjemontage intends to distribute 25 per cent of its net profit after tax as annual dividends over time, subject to the Company's financial position, investment needs and general economic conditions.”
- **tax** — parent / remaining: KPIL expects a tax rate of 26% to 28% standalone and 28% to 30% consolidated; separated business: not stated “Standalone, 26% to 28%, consol 28% to 30%.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The business being separated is Reliance's FMCG/consumer-brands arm, Reliance Consumer Products Ltd (RCPL) — Campa, Independence, Good Life, Ravalgaon/Toffeeman/Lotus, Velvette, Glimmer, Enzo, SIL, Maliban, Alan's, plus acquisitions Udhaiyam, Manna, Sosyo, Goodness Group and the Toni & Guy/Brylcreem/Badedas/Matey brands — which was carved out of Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd (RRVL) under a composite scheme effective 1 December 2025: the 'Consumer Brands Business Undertaking' was demerged from RRVL into Tira Beauty Ltd (renamed RCPL), the old RCPL was dissolved, RRVL shareholders received 1 new RCPL share for every 2 RRVL shares, and the new entity became an 83.56% direct subsidiary of RIL rather than a retail subsidiary. The only rationale management actually articulates is in the Chairman's 16 January 2026 statement: the consumer products vertical is 'progressing on its accelerated growth trajectory with a focused organizational structure' — i.e. a dedicated, directly-held vehicle for a business scaling far faster than retail (Q3 FY26 Rs 5,000 crore, +60% Y-o-Y; 9M FY26 Rs 15,000 crore; FY26 Rs 22,000 crore, 2x Y-o-Y; Q4 FY26 Rs 7,350 crore; Q1 FY27 Rs 8,600 crore, 2x; Campa Rs 4,700 crore and India's 4th largest CSD brand; Independence Rs 2,600 crore; beverages over Rs 6,000 crore; 3rd largest packaged water player; 5,000+ distributors, 3 million outlets, 40 export markets; target Rs 1 lakh crore by FY2030). The problem it visibly solves, though never stated as the reason, is mixing an only-breakeven, capex-hungry FMCG build-out (12 plants, integrated food parks, Kurnool and 'one of the largest beverage plants in Asia', edible-oil facility in West Bengal) into Reliance Retail's P&L: on every call since, management has had to strip RCPL out to show the underlying retail trend — Q3 FY26 8.1% reported, Q4 FY26 11% reported vs ~14% adjusted, Q1 FY27 7.4% reported vs 11.6% adjusted — while Ketan Mody confirms RCPL itself is only 'breakeven on EBITDA terms'. Two parallel separations run alongside it: the Jio Platforms IPO (DRHP 19 June 2026 for a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares of Rs 10, SEBI observation 28 August 2026, RHP 14 October 2026, priced at Rs 1,119 on 24 October 2026, with Rs 500 crore reserved for employees and Rs 2,500 crore for individual/HUF RIL shareholders), and the carve-out of AI/data-centre activity into 'Reliance Intelligence'/RIL so that JPL stays asset-light — capex at RIL or Reliance Intelligence, service provision and products accessed by Jio under long-term leases. No investor, lender or partner is recorded as having asked for any of this; analysts' only questions on the demerger were for like-for-like revenue and EBITDA adjustments, and management expressly deferred the EBITDA impact to the next quarter.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The 1 Dec 2025 composite scheme demerged the Consumer Brands Business Undertaking from RRVL into Tira Beauty Ltd (renamed RCPL), dissolved the old RCPL, and paid RRVL shareholders 1 new RCPL share for every 2 RRVL shares. “in terms of the Scheme, as consideration for the demerger of the Consumer Brands Business Undertaking from RRVL to New RCPL, New RCPL will allot 1 (one) fully paid-up equity share of Rs. 10 (Rupees ten only) each for every 2 (two) fully paid-up equity shares of Rs. 10 (Rupees ten only) each of RRVL, to the shareholders of RRVL.” — *Scheme*
2. The structural outcome: FMCG stops being a retail subsidiary and becomes a business RIL owns directly at 83.56%, with the pre-scheme RRVL-held capital of the new entity cancelled. “Accordingly, New RCPL will become 83.56% direct subsidiary of the Company.” — *Scheme*
3. The only stated rationale anywhere in these documents: the Chairman frames the demerger as giving the consumer products vertical a focused organisational structure to support accelerated growth. “The demerger of consumer products business came into effect this quarter. With a broad and diverse product basket ranging from classic Indian brands to new age labels, the consumer products vertical is progressing on its accelerated growth trajectory with a focused organizational structure.” — *FILING 2026-01-16*
4. CFO V Srikanth confirmed the 1 December effective date and sized the separated business at over Rs 5,000 crore of quarterly turnover, growing 60% Y-o-Y — the growth differential versus retail's 8%. “On the FMCG side, the demerger happened on 1st December. And we are at more than 5,000 Crores of turnover, and this is 60% up on a year-on-year basis.” — *CALL Jan 2026*
5. Ketan Mody opened RCPL's first post-demerger section by stating the new ownership line (direct subsidiary of RIL, not of Reliance Retail), with 9M revenue of Rs 15,000 crore and four brands above Rs 1,000 crore. “So RCPL became the direct subsidiary of RIL from 1st December 2025.” — *CALL Jan 2026*
6. Asked by CLSA and Investec to quantify the EBITDA that left Reliance Retail with the demerger, Dinesh Taluja declined to give the number — the separation's margin arithmetic was never explained on the call. “We will have to wait for the next quarter.” — *CALL Jan 2026*
7. From Q4 FY26 the demerger became a permanent adjustment in retail's reported growth: 11% reported, ~14% ex-RCPL for the quarter and 12% for the year. “Now, if you recollect, RCPL business was demerged out in the last quarter adjusted for that, the growth is almost 14%, for the full year the growth is 12% and if you exclude RCPL demerger the growth would be even higher.” — *CALL Apr 2026*
8. RCPL began reporting through its own CFO with full-year scale figures — Rs 22,000 crore FY26 revenue (2x), Campa Rs 4,700 crore as India's 4th largest CSD brand, Independence Rs 2,600 crore, 12 plants, 5,000 distributors, 3 million outlets, 40 countries. “From an FMCG business perspective, we closed our revenue of Rs.22,000 Crores in 2026 and for the Q4 alone, we delivered a revenue of Rs.7350 Crores, both these are two times growth on the similar period for the last year.” — *CALL Apr 2026*
9. A full year of the demerger now creates a ~4 percentage point gap between retail's reported and underlying growth, the clearest evidence of the optics the separation changes. “In terms of topline growth, as you would recollect, RCPL business was demerged out on 1st of December. So Q1 had the full revenue. Adjusted for that, the underlying revenue growth is 11.6%. On a reported basis, the growth is 7.4%.” — *CALL Jul 2026*
10. The separated entity's own target is Rs 1 lakh crore of revenue by FY2030, with Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 8,600 crore (2x) — but it is still only at EBITDA breakeven, with margins to come from scale and supply chain. “So, like we have announced, the target continues to kind of grow leadership in all categories and we have anyway announced the target is to kind of take this to Rs.1 lakh Crores on FY2030.” — *CALL Jul 2026*
11. Ketan Mody conceded RCPL earns essentially nothing today — i.e. a breakeven, market-share-focused business was removed from a retail P&L running at ~8% EBITDA margin. “EBITDA, I would put it across since the concentration there, yes, we are breakeven on EBITDA terms, but EBITDA will improve as a scale and all the supply chain is kind of put it across but yes, right now the concentration more on the market share” — *CALL Jul 2026*
12. Baseline before the separation: the same brands (Campa, Independence, Maliban, Ravalgaon) were reported as one line inside Reliance Retail, with no mention of any demerger or separate entity. “Consumer brands business continues to scale up very nicely. We are expanding our distribution network. The general trade revenues are growing at 250% plus on Y-o-Y basis.” — *CALL Oct 2024*
13. A second, explicitly-reasoned separation: AI/data-centre capex is placed in RIL / Reliance Intelligence while Jio buys capacity under long-term leases, keeping JPL asset-light ahead of its IPO. “Capex will be RIL or Reliance Intelligence. Service provision will be done by JPL; it will be asset-light service. Products will be developed by Reliance Intelligence, AI products and capex will be incurred there.” — *CALL Jan 2026*
14. Management clarified that the gigawatt-scale AI data centres (including the 168 MW Meta project at Jamnagar) sit outside Jio Platforms in the already-created intelligence entity. “So firstly, I would like to clarify that the AI data centers are not being done in Jio Platforms Limited. They are going to be part of the intelligence business, so RIL or the intelligence entity that has already been created.” — *CALL Apr 2026*
15. The Jio Platforms IPO (fresh issue of up to 27 crore Rs 10 shares) carved out reservations specifically for RIL's own individual shareholders and for employees — a partial separation that hands RIL holders direct access to the asset. “The IPO includes reservation of equity shares of JPL (i) for a value not exceeding Rs. 500 crore for subscription by the Eligible Employees (as defined in the RHP) ; and (ii) for a value not exceeding Rs.2,500 crore for subscription by the Eligible RIL Shareholders” — *FILING 2026-10-14*
16. The JPL listing was priced on 24 October 2026 after a 21–23 October book-build, putting an external price on the separated digital business. “JPL has today finalised the Issue Price (including the anchor investor issue price)  at ₹1,119  per Equity Share of face value of  ₹10 each  and has  also filed the Prospectus dated October 24, 2026  with the Registrar of Companies, Gujarat at Ahmedabad .” — *FILING 2026-10-24*
17. Context for separating consumer assets: S&P's upgrade to A- was credited to the rising share of less-cyclical consumer earnings, and RIL cited access to A-rated capital pools and tighter spreads. “They have focused on the fact that higher portion of our earnings are coming from less cyclical businesses, especially the consumer side.” — *CALL Jan 2026*

**How it evolved:** On the Oct 2024 call the consumer-brands business was still just a bullet inside Dinesh Taluja's retail section (general-trade revenue '250% plus' Y-o-Y) with no hint of separation. The 1 Dec 2025 scheme filings made it real — RCPL demerged out of RRVL into a directly held 83.56% RIL subsidiary — and on the 16 Jan 2026 call (Q3 FY26) RCPL got its own speaker (Ketan Mody), its own Rs 5,000 crore quarter, and the Chairman's 'focused organizational structure' line, while analysts (Investec's Harit Kapoor, CLSA's Vikash Jain) could only extract 'we will have to wait for the next quarter' on the margin impact. By 24 Apr 2026 RCPL presented through its own CFO (Ashutosh Goyal, FY26 Rs 22,000 crore) and retail growth was being quoted both reported and ex-demerger; by 17 Jul 2026 an RCPL Executive Director gave a Rs 1 lakh crore FY2030 ambition and admitted EBITDA breakeven. Over the same window the separation theme widened: AI data centres were explicitly moved out of JPL into Reliance Intelligence (Jan/Apr 2026 calls) and the JPL IPO moved from 'imminent' (Apr 2026) to DRHP (19 Jun 2026) to pricing at Rs 1,119 (24 Oct 2026).

**What management expects from it:** RCPL: a focused structure for accelerated growth to Rs 1 lakh crore by FY2030, with EBITDA rising from breakeven as capacity, food parks and supply chain scale. Retail: cleaner double-digit underlying growth plus ~8% margins, free to fund hyperlocal/digital commerce and double EBITDA in three years. RIL shareholders: direct 83.56%-held ownership and 1-for-2 shares; Jio stays asset-light with capex in Reliance Intelligence.

*Not explained on the calls:* No stated reason for separating rather than retaining RCPL, no RCPL margin, capex, funding or listing plan, no EBITDA quantification, no synergy loss, tax or governance discussion.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Management says the demerger gives the consumer products vertical a 'focused organizational structure' on an 'accelerated growth trajectory'; no other reason is stated in the filings.
- *What it reveals:* A fast-scaling FMCG business previously buried in Retail: FY26 revenue Rs.22,000 crore (2x Y-o-Y), Q1 FY27 Rs.8,600 crore, Campa Rs.4,700 crore, Independence Rs.2,600 crore — but only 'breakeven on EBITDA terms', with a Rs.1 lakh crore FY2030 target.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* RCPL standalone EBITDA split that Dinesh Taluja deferred ('we will have to wait for the next quarter') and the composite scheme document
- *In their words:* “Further, in terms of the Scheme, as consideration for the demerger of the Consumer Brands Business Undertaking from RRVL to New RCPL, New RCPL will allot 1 (one) fully paid-up equity share of Rs. 10 (Rupees ten only) each for every 2 (two) fully paid-up equity shares of Rs. 10 (Rupees ten only) each of RRVL, to the shareholders of RRVL.”
