### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

There is no separation, demerger or spin-off of a business by ICICI Bank in these texts — the question's premise is not supported by the transcripts or the filing, and the dominant direction of travel is the opposite: consolidation of group entities into the Bank. The nearest things management actually described are four entity-level reorganizations. (1) Pension funds: the Board on July 19, 2025 approved acquiring 100% of ICICI Prudential Pension Funds Management Company Limited from ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, moving it from a step-down subsidiary of ICICI Life to a direct wholly owned subsidiary of the Bank; the share purchase agreement was executed January 12, 2026, and on the Jan 2026 media call Sandeep Batra said the rationale was that 'the synergy with the Bank will be better and the business will be able to expand in a much better fashion,' i.e. 'synergising with the banking set of customers'; ICICI Life booked a Rs. 1.1 billion gain on the sale, which was part of why its FY2026 PAT rose 34.6% to Rs. 16.00 billion (25.0% excluding the sale). (2) ICICI Venture's private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business was approved in principle on May 8, 2025 for transfer to ICICI Prudential AMC, completed with ICICI Prudential AMC managing the transferred funds effective April 1, 2026; the stated purpose was 'offering of an integrated full range of investment asset classes, including private equity,' while ICICI Venture keeps only 'certain advisory activities' and 'certain residual funds' — ICICI Venture's PAT jumped to Rs. 1.5 billion in FY2026 from Rs. 0.2 billion in FY2025. (3) A small divestment of the Bank's entire stake in the NIIT Institute of Finance and Banking JV (set up around 2006), which Batra on Apr 2025 called 'a very small amount' done to 'rationalise and simplify our own portfolio where we want to remain focused on.' (4) Closure of the Offshore Banking Unit in the SEEPZ, Mumbai, for which RBI gave a no-objection letter in May 2026 (a prior OBU closure had already pushed Rs. 3.40 billion of negative foreign currency translation reserve into the Q4-FY2024 P&L). Against these, the Bank was pulling businesses in, not pushing them out: ICICI Securities was delisted on March 24, 2025 and became wholly owned (56 million ICICI Bank shares issued at a 67:100 swap, which Anindya Banerjee cited as the main reason net worth rose about Rs. 20,000 crore sequentially, 'while it's capital neutral'); the Bank bought ~2% more of ICICI Prudential AMC and ~2% more of ICICI Life, explicitly 'towards maintaining the Bank's majority shareholding' against stock-based compensation dilution; it infused Rs. 5.0 billion (including Rs. 500 crore in Q3-FY2026) into ICICI Home Finance, which Batra justified as meeting 'the regulatory requirement and expansion that is required from their business point of view'; and it acquired the remaining equity of I-Process Services. The only genuine ownership separations described are at the partner/JV level, not the Bank's: ICICI Prudential AMC listed on BSE and NSE effective December 19, 2025 following Prudential Corporation Holdings' February 2025 announcement of a 'potential listing and partial divestment of its stake,' and after PCHL agreed on May 17, 2026 to buy 75% of Bharti Life, ICICI Life applied to IRDAI to reclassify PCHL from 'promoter' to 'investor' and to rename itself 'ICICI Life Insurance Limited' (IRDAI approved the name change August 7, 2026).

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. Batra confirmed the Bank had taken over the pension fund business from ICICI Life, explaining it was a step-down subsidiary and that the decision had been disclosed about two quarters earlier. “It was a step-down subsidiary. We explained this, I think, about two quarters back when we made the decision.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.icici.bank.in/content/dam/icicibank/india/managed-assets/docs/about-us/2026/transcript-earnings-call-jan2026.pdf)*
2. The stated rationale for moving the pension fund manager under the Bank was synergy with the Bank's customer base and faster expansion, not value unlocking or capital release. “We do believe that the synergy with the Bank will be better and the business will be able to expand in a much better fashion.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.icici.bank.in/content/dam/icicibank/india/managed-assets/docs/about-us/2026/transcript-earnings-call-jan2026.pdf)*
3. Asked directly whether the pension business had been acquired from the subsidiary, Batra confirmed it in one word; no numbers, consideration or targets were given on the call. “Yes, we have.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.icici.bank.in/content/dam/icicibank/india/managed-assets/docs/about-us/2026/transcript-earnings-call-jan2026.pdf)*
4. The only outright exit discussed on any call — the entire stake in the NIIT Institute of Finance and Banking JV set up around 2006 — was framed as immaterial portfolio simplification, with no consideration disclosed. “And over the period, we are just wanting to rationalise and simplify our own portfolio where we want to remain focused on.” — *[Apr 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1a691340-05c5-4029-a15f-cdd78f457400.pdf)*
5. The one real carve-out of a business line in the texts: ICICI Venture's private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business was approved for transfer to ICICI Prudential AMC on May 8, 2025, with ICICI Prudential AMC managing those funds from April 1, 2026. “On May 8, 2025, ICICI Venture Funds Management Company Limited's Board of Directors and ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited's Board of Directors, in their respective meetings, approved, in principle, a proposal to transfer the private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business of ICICI Venture Funds Management Company Limited to ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited.” — *Scheme*
6. The purpose of that transfer was to give ICICI Prudential AMC a complete asset-class platform, leaving ICICI Venture with only advisory work and residual funds. “The transaction enabled the offering of an integrated full range of investment asset classes, including private equity, by ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited.” — *Scheme*
7. The pension transaction was a Board-approved intra-group purchase to convert a step-down subsidiary into a direct wholly owned subsidiary, conditional on RBI and PFRDA approvals; the SPA was executed January 12, 2026. “The Board at its meeting held on July 19, 2025 approved the acquisition of 100% shareholding in ICICI Prudential Pension Funds Management Company Limited from ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited to make ICICI PFM a wholly owned subsidiary of the Bank, subject to the Reserve Bank of India, PFRDA and other necessary approvals.” — *Scheme*
8. The seller side quantified it: ICICI Life's FY2026 PAT of Rs. 16.00 billion (up 34.6%) included a Rs. 1.1 billion gain on selling the pension subsidiary; growth was 25.0% excluding it. “The profit after tax of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited grew by 34.6% year-on-year from Rs. 11.9 billion in fiscal 2025 to Rs. 16.0 billion in fiscal 2026, primarily driven by higher investment income from Shareholders' funds, which includes a gain of Rs. 1.1 billion realized from sale of 100% equity shareholding in ICICI PFM.” — *Scheme*
9. Direction of travel was consolidation, not separation: ICICI Securities was delisted and absorbed as a wholly owned subsidiary on March 24, 2025, with Bank shares issued to its public shareholders at a 67:100 swap. “Pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement amongst ICICI Bank Limited and ICICI Securities Limited and their respective shareholders, ICICI Securities Limited has been delisted from stock exchanges on March 24, 2025 and became a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Bank.” — *[Apr 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1a691340-05c5-4029-a15f-cdd78f457400.pdf)*
10. Banerjee attributed the ~Rs. 20,000 crore sequential jump in net worth to the shares issued to ICICI Securities' minority holders, describing it as capital neutral rather than value creating. “So, we would have issued shares to the minority shareholders of ISec that would have, while it's capital neutral, it would have increased the net-worth by a substantial amount.” — *[Apr 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1a691340-05c5-4029-a15f-cdd78f457400.pdf)*
11. Stake increases in the listed subsidiaries were defensive against stock-compensation dilution, not steps toward separation: ~2% more of ICICI Prudential AMC and ~2% of ICICI Life (taking it to ~52.8%). “This purchase was primarily for the purposes of maintaining the Bank's majority shareholding in ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited were it to grant stock-based compensation.” — *Scheme*
12. The only partner-level separation: Prudential Corporation Holdings signalled a partial exit from the AMC, which listed on December 19, 2025, and after agreeing to buy 75% of Bharti Life it is being reclassified from promoter to investor in ICICI Life, which is renaming itself. “Consequently, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited has applied to IRDAI for the reclassification of PCHL from 'promoter' to 'investor', along with a proposal to change the name of the company from 'ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited' to 'ICICI Life Insurance Limited'.” — *Scheme*
13. Capital was being pushed into subsidiaries rather than freed from them — Rs. 500 crore into ICICI Home Finance in Q3-FY2026 (Rs. 5.0 billion in FY2026), with Batra committing to fund it further. “We are happy to infuse the capital to meet the regulatory requirement and expansion that is required from their business point of view.” — *[Jan 2026](https://www.icici.bank.in/content/dam/icicibank/india/managed-assets/docs/about-us/2026/transcript-earnings-call-jan2026.pdf)*
14. The only operational unit being shut is an offshore branch, not a business: RBI issued a no-objection letter in May 2026 for closing the SEEPZ Mumbai Offshore Banking Unit. “In May 2026, the Bank received the no-objection letter from the Reserve Bank of India to close the Offshore Banking Unit located in the Santacruz Electronic Exports Promotion Zone, Mumbai.” — *Scheme*
15. The most recent call contains no mention of any separation, demerger, carve-out or subsidiary restructuring — management's framing of strategy is entirely about growing PBT excluding treasury within one integrated bank. “At ICICI Bank, our strategic focus continues to be on growing profit before tax excluding treasury through the 360-degree customer centric approach and by serving opportunities across ecosystems and micro-markets.” — *[Apr 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=50d0e36c-8e96-4fde-9d2e-d33a9443ec34.pdf)*

**How it evolved:** No separation idea ever surfaces as such: on Apr 2025 (call of April 19, 2025) the only disposal discussed is the small NIIT Institute JV stake sale, framed as portfolio simplification, in the same quarter ICICI Securities was delisted into the Bank (March 24, 2025). The ICICI Venture PE/VC/real-estate fund management transfer was approved in principle on May 8, 2025 and the pension-fund acquisition on July 19, 2025 — the same day as the Jul 2025 call, where neither was mentioned and no analyst asked. By Jan 2026 (call of January 17, 2026) Batra confirmed the pension step-down subsidiary had been brought under the Bank, noting 'we explained this, I think, about two quarters back when we made the decision,' and the Oct 2025 transcript is unreadable so any interim discussion is unverifiable; the Apr 2026 call (April 18, 2026) contains no mention of any of it, and only the September 18, 2026 Annual Securities Report records the ICICI Venture transfer as effective April 1, 2026 and the PCHL promoter-to-investor reclassification.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing was said about a separation, because none was announced. For the moves that were made: the pension business gains Bank-customer synergies and faster expansion; ICICI Prudential AMC gains a full asset-class platform including private equity; ICICI Venture keeps only advisory and residual funds; ICICI Life booked a Rs. 1.1 billion gain. No margin, capital-release, valuation-unlock or focus claims were offered.

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything a separation thesis needs: no demerger exists. No consideration for NIIT or ICICI Venture's transfer, no pension AUM/economics, no lender, investor or partner demands, no analyst questions, and Oct 2025's transcript is unreadable.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* not stated; documents only record that JV partner PCHL announced a potential listing and partial divestment of its stake, subject to market conditions, requisite approvals and other considerations
- *What it reveals:* A listed price for a fee business earning Rs 33.0 billion PAT in fiscal 2026 vs Rs 26.5 billion in fiscal 2025, now also holding ICICI Venture's private equity, venture capital and real estate fund management business
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* Slides 33 to 35 of the Q4-FY2026 investor presentation for ICICI AMC's standalone financials versus the Bank's 53.0% stake
- *In their words:* “Effective December 19, 2025, ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited is listed on Bombay Stock Exchange and National Stock Exchange.”

- **What the promoters will hold in the separated entity:** 2025 AVTL IPO: "Further to our intimations dated December 11, 2024, and January 10, 2025, and as approved by the shareholders of the Company, pursuant to the IPO, AVTL will cease to be a subsidiary of the Company resulting in the dilution of the Company's shareholding in AVTL to less than fifty percent (50%)."; "Pursuant to the aforesaid Issue, AVTL will ceases to be subsidiary of the Company resulting in the dilution of the Company's shareholding in the Material Subsidiary to less than fifty percent (50%). However, no change in the AVTL's management of its business is intended or expected pursuant to the Issue. The Company will continue to have management control over AVTL and further the accounts of the AVTL will continue to be consolidated with the Company." BRSR FY2024-25 shows "Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited# Subsidiary 50.10" % of shares held by listed entity; on the Q2 FY26 call (November 7, 2025) management said "we are also a 44% shareholder of AVTL". 2025-26 Hindustan Aegis LPG transfer: "this transaction is not going to affect us by in spite of diluting 51%, we indirectly continue to hold 34%." Nothing is stated about promoter (Chandaria family) holdings in any entity.
- **What a public shareholder receives:** not stated in the documents on file.
- **Management incentives:** not stated in the documents on file.
- **Insider actions around the separation:** No promoter or management buying, selling or pledging is stated. Related disclosures: "The trading window for dealing in the securities of the Company, which was closed for Company’s Director/designated persons associated with the Company from Tuesday, April 1, 2025 continues to remain closed till the conclusion of 48 hours after the declaration of audited financial results (standalone and consolidated) approved by the Board of Directors of the Company." (May 29, 2025); "None of the Directors/Key Managerial Personnel of the Company/their relatives are in any way, concerned or interested, financially or otherwise in the Special Resolution set out except to the extent to their shareholding in the Company, if any." (Postal Ballot Notice, December 10, 2024); and, at the subsidiary level, "Itochu Corporation has acquired a 10% stake in Aegis Terminal Pipavav Limited coming in as a strategic partner with an intention to raise that to 25% stake over the next 3 years."
- **Insiders, per the checklist read:** Promoter Raj Chandaria is Chairman & MD; parent holds "44% shareholder of AVTL", earns ~25% margin developing assets billed to AVTL; Itochu took 10% of ATPL, intending 25% · *option pricing date:* not stated

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

Across these texts Aegis is not demerging a division to its own shareholders — one filing states plainly "Yes, transaction is outside the Scheme of Arrangement" — it is carving its port terminalling business out of Aegis Logistics Ltd (ALL) into the Royal Vopak joint venture Aegis Vopak Terminals Ltd (AVTL), IPO-ing it, and then migrating terminal assets into AVTL and its subsidiaries by slump sale; ALL retains Mumbai Liquid, Mumbai LPG, LPG/ammonia Distribution, Infrastructure Development (EPC), Sourcing and treasury. Management's stated reason is capital: the group is funding roughly USD 1.2 billion of gross capex (about INR 10,000 crores) by FY27 and a USD 5 billion pipeline to 2030 (including a non-binding INR 20,000 crore Vadhavan MoU, INR 1,675 crores at JNPA/J2, INR 525 crores per ammonia terminal), and Murad Moledina said the AVTL IPO's "primary objective was to reduce debt and strengthen the balance sheet enabling us to seize future growth opportunities and continue our GATI strategy" — GATI being Gateway Access to India. The dilution problem is answered two ways: in Nov 2024 he argued equity infused into the JV "will be value accrued into the holdco because we are eliminating interest cost which is a very high cost for infrastructure companies," so rising minority interest is offset by interest savings; post-listing he called it EPS accretive because reinvested proceeds more than compensate for profit shared with minorities. The split is engineered so cash returns to the parent: ALL (or a 100% subsidiary) builds the assets and bills AVTL at arm's length with a ~20–25% margin — 30% on signing the framework agreement (INR 500 crores of the INR 1,675 crore J2 project) and 70% on completion — so "we recover back whatever we have spent and the margin remains in cash," eliminated on consolidation but real at the standalone level, while ALL also keeps 44.71% of AVTL and management control, so AVTL is still consolidated line by line. Partner structure, not lender pressure, shapes it: Vopak dilutes equally alongside ALL; SEBI rules legally oblige a Phase-II equity infusion within three years; Itochu has taken 10% of Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) Ltd with intent to reach 25%; L&T (Kandla green ammonia) and Hindustan Zinc (15-year ammonia take-or-pay) sit on the project side. Consolidation of stragglers followed — Haldia's Hindustan Aegis LPG (25,000 MT, HPCL contract to 2038) moved 75% into AVTL, with 51% sold by Aegis Gas for INR 701.6 crores, and the Pipavav ammonia terminal transferred to ATPL for INR 525 crores — and performance has been strong throughout: FY26 revenue INR 8,333 crores (+23%), normalised EBITDA INR 1,599 crores (+36%), PAT INR 1,107 crores (+41%), EPS 25.59, cash and investments ~INR 5,939 crores versus INR 150 crores in FY22, consolidated debt-to-equity 0.04 and no net debt.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. Investor Anil Sarin explicitly lobbied against separately listing AVTL, saying minority holders would be confused about which entity to own and that capital should instead be raised in the listed Holdco; management called the discussion premature. “it would be so much better if you retain that in the consolidated hold and raise money in the Holdco.” — *[Aug 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d5eeb379-e933-48d9-aeb1-921a678ebcb6.pdf)*
2. Asked directly about press reports of an AVTL IPO, the CFO would not confirm it, framing it only as one of several ways to fund the capex programme. “As far as the second news item is concerned, I can tell you, we always explore many possibilities of funding our capex program and nothing finalized as of now.” — *[Aug 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d5eeb379-e933-48d9-aeb1-921a678ebcb6.pdf)*
3. On the day after the DRHP was filed, the CFO gave the core defence of the structure: equity raised in the subsidiary repays infrastructure debt, so interest savings offset the increase in minority interest and the holdco is left unaffected. “We have already said earlier that the equity infusion into the JV will be value accrued into the holdco because we are eliminating interest cost which is a very high cost for infrastructure companies.” — *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=65eba500-2091-45e4-803b-b6b3d3bd1264.pdf)*
4. The Chairman stated the stated use of IPO proceeds — debt reduction plus general corporate purposes — while an investor asked whether the listed parent would simply become a holdco since the bulk of the business was moving into the JV. “The capital raise in AVTL will help the company reduce a certain portion of the outstanding debt and also some portion helped fund other general corporate purposes.” — *[Nov 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=65eba500-2091-45e4-803b-b6b3d3bd1264.pdf)*
5. Post-listing (AVTL listed June 2025, ALL holding 44.71% with management control, so still consolidated line by line), the CFO gave the formal rationale and said reinvested proceeds would more than compensate for profit now shared with minorities. “The primary objective was to reduce debt and strengthen the balance sheet enabling us to seize future growth opportunities and continue our GATI strategy.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=33def260-c9ef-4d18-85ef-3a82fdb609f4.pdf)*
6. The Chairman tied the separation to a regulatory obligation: a second equity infusion into AVTL is mandated within three years under SEBI rules, which he said largely funds the USD 1.2 billion-to-USD 5 billion capex plan at 0.6x gearing capped at 3.5x EBITDA. “With the recently concluded Phase-I equity infusion by way of the IPO and as you know we are legally obliged to have a Phase-II equity infusion within the next 3 years under the SEBI regulations, the Capex therefore will be largely funded.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=33def260-c9ef-4d18-85ef-3a82fdb609f4.pdf)*
7. The allocation rule between parent and AVTL was stated: standard port terminals go into AVTL under the GATI strategy, while other assets (e.g. the INR 250 crore Mumbai liquid expansion) stay in the parent, decided case by case on where value is maximised and whether partners are involved. “But yes, most of the standard port terminals will be housed under the strategy GATI in Aegis Vopak, for sure.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=33def260-c9ef-4d18-85ef-3a82fdb609f4.pdf)*
8. Explaining the Haldia/Hindustan Aegis consolidation into AVTL, the CFO quantified the trade: holding drops from 51% to an indirect 34%, but roughly INR 700 crores of cash more than offsets the 17 points, and it lifts the subsidiary's EPS. “The 17% that drops is compensated by the surplus INR 700 crores, whatever is going to come in our hands.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=06b0ba8f-8eb6-42e0-98c0-4cb53ff2ae90.pdf)*
9. The cash mechanics of the two-entity structure were spelled out for a shareholder worried that the USD 5 billion capex benefits only AVTL: the parent builds at ~25% margin, is reimbursed in full plus margin, and also earns via its AVTL stake. “So, for AVTL, if we develop, then obviously, AVTL pays for the entire amount, including our margin. So, we recover back whatever we have spent and the margin remains in cash.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=06b0ba8f-8eb6-42e0-98c0-4cb53ff2ae90.pdf)*
10. Asked what is left in Aegis Logistics outside AVTL, the CFO enumerated the retained perimeter — and added that ammonia distribution is being added to it alongside LPG. “So we have Mumbai Liquid. We have Mumbai LPG. We have Distribution. We have Infrastructure Development. We have Sourcing and we have treasury.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=1b37f48b-924c-4da8-a968-b646d3dc0653.pdf)*
11. The steady-state operating model was confirmed: capex is incurred and the asset built at Aegis Logistics standalone (or a 100% subsidiary), billed as EPC, then transferred to Aegis Vopak, with consolidation capitalised at ALL's billed cost. “So, we will be doing capex at the Aegis level, the Aegis Logistics. And then after creating the asset, will we then transfer it to Aegis Vopak, am I right?” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=d2ebd557-5ec3-4cb1-b90f-9d56e37dbbde.pdf)*
12. The Aug 24, 2026 Business Transfer Agreement transferred the 36,000 MT Pipavav ammonia terminal to Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) Limited by slump sale for INR 525 crores, and states the transaction sits outside any Scheme of Arrangement and is a related-party transaction at arm's length. “The Transfer of storage terminal for Ammonia to ATPL will consolidate the terminalling services under the Group, enabling operational synergy.” — *Scheme*
13. The Oct 29, 2025 board approval priced the Haldia step: 6,21,146 shares (51%) of Hindustan Aegis LPG sold by wholly-owned Aegis Gas (LPG) Pvt Ltd to AVTL, an entity contributing 2.49% of turnover and 10.07% of net worth in FY25. “The consideration to be received by AGPL against the sale of 6,21,146 Equity shares held by AGPL in HALPG from AVTL is  INR.7,01,60,71,920/-” — *Scheme*
14. A year after the AVTL IPO the parent itself moved to raise capital: the Sep 28, 2026 board approved raising borrowing limits to INR 6,000 crores and a fundraise of up to INR 6,000 crores via equity, FCCB/ADR/GDR, debentures or QIP, subject to shareholder special resolution. “raising of funds for an amount aggregating up to Rs. 6,000 Crores, for cash, in one or more tranches” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** The idea surfaced only as press speculation: on the Aug 2024 call (Jul 31, 2024) Murad Moledina refused to engage on an AVTL fundraise news item — "nothing finalized as of now" — and Anil Sarin used that call to lobby against it on behalf of minority holders, asking that capital instead be raised in the Holdco; the Nov 2024 call (Nov 19, 2024) opened by disclosing the DRHP had been filed the previous day, with Moledina declining detail ("We are not at liberty to talk as of now") beyond saying proceeds would repay debt and that dilution would be shared equally by both partners and done in two phases. By the Aug 2025 call (Aug 8, 2025) AVTL was listed (June 2025, INR 2,800 crores raised, ALL at 44.71%) and the rationale was given formally — debt reduction, GATI, EPS accretion, Phase-II infusion legally due within three years — plus the first slump sales (Sea Lord's Mangalore terminal, business transfer agreements of Jun 19, 2025) and the rule that "most of the standard port terminals will be housed under the strategy GATI in Aegis Vopak." Thereafter it became mechanical: Nov 2025 (Nov 7) and the Oct 28–29, 2025 filings moved Hindustan Aegis LPG and Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) into AVTL (INR 701.6 crores for 51%; ALL retaining 34% indirectly, offset by ~INR 700 crores cash), Feb 2026 (Jan 30, 2026) defined the parent's remaining six businesses, the Mar 26 / Aug 24, 2026 filings assigned and executed the INR 525 crore ammonia BTA to ATPL, and the Jun 2026 call (Jun 9, 2026) plus the Sep 28, 2026 board approval of INR 6,000 crores of borrowing limits and INR 6,000 crores of fundraising confirmed the steady state: ALL builds and funds, AVTL owns.

**What management expects from it:** AVTL: debt repaid, balance sheet strengthened, ~25% EBITDA on matured assets, terminals consolidated for operational synergy, partner capital from Vopak and Itochu. Aegis Logistics: upfront 20–25% EPC margin returned in cash, 44.71% of AVTL plus management control and line-by-line consolidation, high-return distribution/sourcing/treasury retained, EPS accretion, 0.6x gearing, and funding for USD 5 billion of capex to 2030.

*Not explained on the calls:* No stated valuation of retained versus transferred businesses, no answer to the which-entity-to-own dilution objection, no Phase-II infusion size, terms or timing, no lender rationale.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Terminals housed in AVTL: transfer of the Ammonia terminal "will consolidate the terminalling services under the Group, enabling operational synergy"; AVTL's listing raised INR 2,800 crore primary capital
- *What it reveals:* Parent keeps Mumbai liquid/LPG, distribution, sourcing, infrastructure development, treasury, INR 5,939 crore cash and no net debt, plus 44% of listed AVTL and a 25% EPC margin on terminals built for it
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* AVTL standalone results and shareholding — value of parent's 44% stake plus INR 5,939 crore cash versus parent market cap
- *In their words:* “This year also marked a significant achievement for one of our subsidiaries, Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited (AVTL), with successfully listing of its equity shares on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited with effect from June 2, 2025, raised INR 2,800 crore through a primary issuance.”

- **other** — parent / remaining: Business left in Aegis Logistics outside AVTL: Mumbai liquid, Mumbai LPG, distribution, infrastructure development, sourcing and treasury, plus the new ammonia distribution.; separated business: AVTL houses the terminalling assets; "if it is a terminal, yes, every chance that it will be housed in AVTL." “So we have Mumbai Liquid. We have Mumbai LPG. We have Distribution. We have Infrastructure Development. We have Sourcing and we have treasury.”
- **operating margin** — parent / remaining: FY26 group: LPG segment revenue INR7,689 crores with EBITDA INR1,131 crores (up 68%); distribution margin around INR7,000 per ton versus INR4,000-odd in the previous year.; separated business: Liquid (terminalling) segment delivered FY26 revenue of INR644 crores with EBITDA of INR472 crores, down 5%; Q3 FY26 liquid segment EBITDA margin expanded by 674 bps to 77%. “Liquid business delivered revenue of INR644 crores broadly stable year-on-year with EBITDA of INR472 crores, down 5%, reflecting phasing of capacity additions.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

On the documentary record available, Edelweiss is not executing a demerger scheme but a sequence of subsidiary-level separations that convert a holding-company conglomerate into separately capitalised, separately owned businesses — described in its own press release as "seven independent and well-governed businesses" each with "dedicated management teams and strong boards." The clearest stated reason is the Alternative Asset Management arm, EAAA India Alternatives: management said the IPO was "the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform," i.e. separating the fastest-growing, fee-income business (FPAUM INR 41,920 Cr, +33% YoY; nine-month fund raise INR 7,576 Cr, +67% YoY; total income Rs 963.76 Cr in FY26 versus Rs 584.25 Cr in FY24; net worth Rs 1,075.54 Cr) from the credit-heavy parent so it can be valued and institutionalised on its own. Critically, the EAAA listing was a pure offer for sale by holdco subsidiary ESIPL (originally up to Rs 15,000 mn, cut to Rs 12,000 mn in the RHP, finally Rs 1,200 Cr gross / Rs 1,120.63 Cr net at Rs 1,665 per share) — no primary money went to EAAA, so the cash accrues to the Edelweiss holding structure, which fits the stated priority of "focused reduction in corporate net debt" (down 15% to INR 6,520 Cr over two years, with consolidated net debt INR 11,390 Cr and a 3.46x debt-equity ratio). The second separation is Housing Finance: Nido Home Finance was handed to a strategic majority investor, CA Sardo Investments (The Carlyle Group) with Salisbury Investments (Aditya Puri's family vehicle), investing ~INR 2,100 Cr — Rs 580.68 Cr of secondary for 45% plus Rs 1,446.14 Cr of primary equity and warrants at INR 193 — taking them to 58.26% immediately and 72.70% fully diluted within 18 months, so Nido "ceased to be a subsidiary" and Edelweiss fell to 38.91% (25.46% diluted). Here the separation solves a growth-capital problem Edelweiss itself was not funding: a business contributing only 5.47% of consolidated income (Rs 520.63 Cr) but consuming 13.99% of net worth (Rs 828.2 Cr) was recapitalised with third-party primary money, with Edelweiss retaining upside via a minority stake and "an additional payment based upon returns realized by CA Sardo Investments." The same template was applied to the Mutual Fund arm, where a 15% sale of Edelweiss Asset Management and Edelweiss Trusteeship to WestBridge moved both into joint control, crystallising a Rs 2,440 Cr unrealised and Rs 281 Cr realised gain (and a Rs 389 Cr deferred tax charge) — evidence that the separations are also being used to mark up carrying value and lift reported net worth/PAT (nine-month PAT Rs 549 Cr, +45% YoY). Taken together, the stated logic is: each business reaches scale, then gets its own owner, its own capital and its own valuation, while the parent de-levers.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The EAAA IPO is explicitly positioned as the first step in separating the alternatives business into a self-standing institutional platform, announced alongside the DRHP filing in January 2026. “We are pleased to share that we have filed EAAA’s DRHP for IPO in January and are on track for the listing, marking the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform.” — *Scheme*
2. The structural end-state management describes for the group is a set of separately governed operating companies rather than an integrated financial conglomerate. “Edelweiss is a diversified financial services company with seven independent and well-governed businesses.” — *Scheme*
3. The separations sit directly under the stated priority of de-levering the holding company, with corporate net debt the metric management tracks. “Corporate net debt continues to be on path to reduction, with a 15% decline to INR 6,520 Cr over the last two years” — *Scheme*
4. Housing Finance was separated by bringing in Carlyle and Aditya Puri's family vehicle as strategic majority owners with roughly INR 2,100 crores of new money. “has entered into definitive agreements (the Agreements) with CA Sardo Investments (an affiliate of The Carlyle Group (NASDAQ: CG)) and Salisbury Investments Private Limited (an investment vehicle of Aditya Puri and his family) (collectively Buyers) for the Buyers to invest approximately INR 2,100 crores to acquire a strategic majority stake in Nido.” — *Scheme*
5. The Nido deal is a true deconsolidation, not a minority stake sale — Edelweiss gives up control of the housing finance book. “Consequent to the transaction, Nido will cease to be a subsidiary of the Company.” — *Scheme*
6. Nido was absorbing far more of the group's capital than it contributed in income — 13.99% of net worth for 5.47% of income — which the recapitalisation by third parties addresses. “Income 520.63 5.47% Net Worth 828.2 13.99%” — *Scheme*
7. Most of the Carlyle money is primary capital into Nido's balance sheet rather than cash out to Edelweiss: Rs 580.68 Cr secondary versus Rs 1,446.14 Cr of fresh equity and warrants. “Further, in accordance with the Agreements, Nido has also issued 2,59,06,736 equity shares and 5,18,13,472 warrants, to the Buyers, for an aggregate amount of INR 14,46,13,99,102.56.” — *Scheme*
8. Edelweiss retains economic upside in the separated housing business through a retained minority stake and a contingent payment linked to Carlyle's realised returns. “Pursuant to the Agreements and subject to applicable laws, the Sellers (Edelweiss) may also receive an additional payment based upon returns realized by CA Sardo Investments from its investment in Nido.” — *Scheme*
9. Control of Nido passes progressively to the buyers — 58.26% on closing rising to 72.70% fully diluted — while Edelweiss falls to 25.46%. “the Buyers now hold 58.26% shareholding of Nido which would be increased to 72.70% within 18 months, on a fully diluted basis post conversion of the warrants.” — *Scheme*
10. The Mutual Fund business was separated on the same template, with a 15% strategic sale converting EAML and ETCL into jointly controlled entities. “Additionally, the WestBridge investment in Mutual Fund received its final approval from the regulators, and the deal has been consummated this quarter.” — *Scheme*
11. That Mutual Fund separation crystallised very large accounting gains — Rs 2,440 Cr unrealised plus Rs 281 Cr realised — showing the separations also re-rate carrying values inside the consolidated accounts. “Pursuant to the terms of the SHA, the Group now has joint control for both of these Entities with the new investor, and consequently, in accordance with Ind AS 110 and Ind AS 28, these entities are now classified as jointly controlled entities under Ind AS accounting principles.” — *Scheme*
12. The EAAA listing raised no primary capital for EAAA itself; proceeds went to the holding-company subsidiary ESIPL, consistent with using separation to fund parent de-leveraging. “The IPO comprises an offer for sale (“OFS”) for an amount not exceeding Rs. 12,000 million, which is proposed to be undertaken by Edelweiss Securities & Investments Private Limited (“ESIPL”), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.” — *Scheme*
13. The alternatives business being separated had tripled income over three years, supporting the argument that it deserves its own valuation. “FY 2025-26: Rs 963.76 crores FY 2024-25: Rs 786.54 crores. FY 2023-24: Rs 584.25 crores.” — *Scheme*
14. On completion Edelweiss kept overwhelming ownership of EAAA — 83.88% across subsidiaries — so this is a listing and institutionalisation step, not an exit. “Consequently, the Company, through all its subsidiaries, hold 54,233,039 equity shares of EAAA representing 83.88% of the total paid-up equity share capital of EAAA.” — *Scheme*
15. The separations are set against an insurance drag and a credit book being wound down, including a Rs 920 Cr discretionary overlay on discontinued security receipts and a 34% YoY cut in the wholesale book. “the Group has recognised a discretionary management overlay provision of 920 crores on its discontinued Security Receipts (Purchased or Originated Credit-Impaired (POCI) loans) in the consolidated financial results as at 31 December 2025.” — *Scheme*

**How it evolved:** This cannot be traced call by call: all ten earnings-call transcripts supplied (Nov 2023, May/Aug/Oct/Nov 2024, May/Aug/Nov 2025, Feb 2026, Apr 2026) contained no extractable text, so no dated management commentary is available. From the filings, the sequence is: EAAA's DRHP filed 19–20 January 2026 (OFS up to Rs 15,000 mn by ESIPL); on 10 February 2026 the Q3FY26 release framed it as "the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform" and the same day the Carlyle/Salisbury definitive agreements for a majority of Nido were announced, with WestBridge's Mutual Fund investment consummated in that quarter; SEBI observations came 23 April 2026, the Nido transaction closed 25 September 2026 (versus a 31 July 2026 expectation), and the EAAA IPO was repriced down to Rs 12,000 mn in the RHP of 19 October 2026 before listing on 2 November 2026 at Rs 1,665. So the plan visibly scaled down in size (Rs 1,500 Cr to Rs 1,200 Cr) and slipped in timing, while widening from one business to three.

**What management expects from it:** EAAA becomes a listed, "standalone institutionalized platform" with its own valuation; Nido gets Carlyle/Puri growth capital and majority ownership while Edelweiss keeps 25–39% plus a returns-linked earn-out; Mutual Fund gains a strategic partner and a Rs 2,440 Cr value mark; the parent frees capital (Rs 1,120.63 Cr net OFS proceeds) to push corporate net debt below INR 6,520 Cr.

*Not explained on the calls:* All ten earnings-call transcripts were unextractable, so management's spoken rationale, investor/lender demands, use of proceeds, valuation targets, and any formal demerger scheme are absent.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* "marking the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform"; IPO comprised an offer for sale by Edelweiss Securities & Investments Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary
- *What it reveals:* IPO price Rs 1,665 values EAAA's ~6.47 crore shares near Rs 10,700 crore versus EFSL net worth of Rs 5,866 crore; Alternatives segment earned PBT Rs 241.40 crore on Rs 989.53 crore capital employed; FPAUM Rs 41,920 crore, up 33% YoY.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* EAAA's Red Herring Prospectus dated October 19, 2026 — fee-earning AUM, fee rates and the Rs 963.76 crore FY26 income mix
- *In their words:* “We are pleased to share that we have filed EAAA's DRHP for IPO in January and are on track for the listing, marking the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The business being separated is the steel business undertaking of Bhushan Power and Steel Limited (BPSL) — the ~4.5 MTPA integrated plant at Jharsuguda/Sambalpur, Odisha, which JSW acquired out of IBC in 2021 at 2.75 MTPA and then expanded to 4.5 MTPA. The mechanics, approved by the Board on December 3, 2025, were a slump sale of BPSL's steel undertaking on a going-concern basis to JSW Sambalpur Steel Limited for Rs. 24,483 crores cash (subject to closing adjustments), with JFE Steel Corporation of Japan subscribing 50% of JSW Sambalpur's holding company JSW Kalinga Steel Limited for Rs. 15,750 crores in two equal tranches of Rs. 7,875 crores — giving a 50:50 JV at an equity value of Rs. 31,500 crores and enterprise value of Rs. 53,000 crores. Management's stated problem was funding growth without stressing the balance sheet: JSW had a 50 MTPA India target by FY31 (raised in May 2026 to 62 MTPA by FY32, plus 16 MTPA across the JFE and POSCO JVs, ~78-80 MTPA in all), and the transaction was 'aimed at securing the Company's growth in a financially prudent manner to enable it to pursue its aspirations across business cycles,' producing a Rs. 32,000 crore cash inflow and ~Rs. 37,000 crores of deleveraging. The second stated problem was capability: BPSL 'has significant growth potential' and the JV would 'enable acceleration of its capacity with best-in-class technology and enable production of high-end value-added steel products,' building on JFE's partnership with JSW since 2009. A third, separate problem was structure — BPSL sat under Piombino Steel Limited, 82.65% JSW Steel and 17.35% JSW Shipping & Logistics (a promoter group entity) — so a parallel scheme amalgamated Piombino into JSW Steel (10 JSW shares of Re. 1 for every 156 Piombino shares of Rs. 10) so JSW could 'directly hold the investment in BPSL,' giving 'a platform to facilitate any transactions and investments related to BPSL's business, thereby enhancing strategic focus without minority shareholders' involvement,' plus 'additional cash to pursue its growth aspirations in a financially prudent manner' and fewer entities/compliances. By May 14, 2026 management reported the JV entity formed by end-March, JFE's first tranche in, ~Rs. 30,000 crores of the Rs. 37,000 crore deleveraging done, net debt Rs. 54,000 crores, leverage down to 1.81x and gearing 0.51x, a credit-rating outlook uplift, a Rs. 18,051 crore exceptional gain on the slump sale (largely sheltered by BPSL's carry-forward losses and unabsorbed depreciation), and BPSL deconsolidated into equity accounting. No text in the filings or the one readable call says investors, lenders or partners demanded the separation; JFE is the counterparty and already had a nominee, Mr. Hiroyuki Ogawa, on JSW Steel's board.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. Board approval of December 3, 2025 set out the structure: slump sale of BPSL's steel undertaking to JSW Sambalpur for Rs. 24,483 crores cash, with JFE buying 50% of JSW Kalinga for Rs. 15,750 crores in two equal tranches. “Transfer of BPSL Steel business undertaking, by way of slump sale on a going concern basis to JSW Sambalpur Steel Limited (“JSW Sambalpur”) for a cash consideration of Rs 24,483 crores, subject to customary closing adjustments as agreed in the transaction documents.” — *Scheme*
2. The stated justification to shareholders was funding a 50 MTPA-by-FY31 growth plan without balance-sheet strain, across cycles. “The present transaction is aimed at securing the Company’s growth in a financially prudent manner to enable it to pursue its aspirations across business cycles.” — *Scheme*
3. The second rationale was technology and product mix: JFE, a partner since 2009, would accelerate BPSL's capacity and push it into high-end value-added steel. “JFE has been a long-term strategic partner of JSW Steel since 2009. The BPSL Steel business has significant growth potential and this joint venture will enable acceleration of its capacity with best-in-class technology and enable production of high-end value-added steel products” — *Scheme*
4. Q3 FY26 press release quantified the deal: 50% of BPSL steel at Rs. 31,500 crore equity value and Rs. 53,000 crore EV, with Rs. 32,000 crores of cash in and Rs. 37,000 crores of deleveraging. “With this transaction, JFE will take a 50% stake in the BPSL Steel business at an equity value of Rs. 31,500 crores and enterprise value of Rs. 53,000 crores. This transaction will enable a cash inflow of Rs. 32,000 crores, and a substantial deleveraging of Rs. 37,000 crores for JSW Steel.” — *Scheme*
5. Accounting treatment: BPSL's steel assets and liabilities were moved to held-for-sale under Ind AS 105 at December 31, 2025, but the company insisted it was not a discontinued operation. “The Group has also assessed and concluded that transfer of BPSL’s steel business undertaking does not qualify as “discontinued operation” as it is not a separate major line of business and forms part of overall steel operations of the Group.” — *Scheme*
6. A Rs. 1,439 crore deferred tax asset was recognised on BPSL's brought-forward unabsorbed depreciation because capital gains on the slump sale made recovery probable. “Further, based on the reassessment of unrecognised deferred tax assets, the Group has recognised deferred tax assets (net) amounting to Rs. 1,439 crores as it is probable that carried forward unabsorbed depreciation will be recovered against the likely capital gains on the above mentioned transaction .” — *Scheme*
7. The parallel Piombino Steel merger was justified as removing the 17.35% promoter-group minority above BPSL so JSW Steel could hold and transact on BPSL directly, and would hand JSW extra cash. “The merger ensures better alignment of the Transferee Company’s long-term strategic interests by enabling it to directly hold the investment in Bhushan Power and Steel Limited (‘BPSL’). This consolidation provides a platform to facilitate any transactions and investments related to BPSL’s business, thereby enhancing strategic focus without minority shareholders' involvement;” — *Scheme*
8. Acharya opened FY26 by framing the BPSL carve-out as the year's defining strategic step and the source of structural deleveraging, with ~Rs. 30,000 of the Rs. 37,000 crores done by March-end. “This transaction entails a deleveraging of approximately Rs.37,000 crores for JSW Steel, out of which about Rs.30,000 crores has been completed at March end.” — *CALL May 2026*
9. Balance-sheet outcome cited: leverage 1.81x, gearing 0.51x, net debt ~Rs. 54,000 crores, rating outlook uplift, plus a further Rs. 7,900 crores of deleveraging from JFE's second tranche by end-June. “The second tranche of equity investment in JFE is expected by end -June, which will dr ive further deleveraging of Rs.7,900 crores approximately.” — *CALL May 2026*
10. Asked by Amit Murarka (Axis Capital) whether multiple simultaneous projects were the new normal, Acharya said the JV's purpose was dual: faster growth plus deleveraging, run as two balance sheets. “So , as we had given you an indication earlier that the idea of the JV was to strategically grow faster in the country, while it helped us to deleverage as well.” — *CALL May 2026*
11. The separation was booked as a Rs. 18,051 crore exceptional gain on the slump sale, inside a Q4 exceptional gain of Rs. 17,888 crores; normalised PAT was Rs. 3,475 crores. “This incl udes a gain of Rs.18,051 crores on slump sale of BPSL steel undertaking and Rs.163 crores exceptional charge on implementation of new labor code.” — *CALL May 2026*
12. Swayam Saurabh told Indrajit Agarwal (CLSA) that BPSL's carry-forward losses and unabsorbed depreciation made the tax cost of the transaction negligible, including in JSW's own books. “So BPSL has had carry forward losses, unabsorbed depreciation. So , the effective tax on this transaction is significantly lower.” — *CALL May 2026*
13. Ashwin Bajaj clarified the reporting consequence: BPSL leaves revenue and EBITDA entirely and appears only as income from associates and joint ventures. “BPSL has been deconsolidated at March - end. And the n umbers for BPSL will not be part of financials of EBITDA. It would be equity accounting, and there is a line in the P&L, which says income from associates and joint ventures.” — *CALL May 2026*
14. The carve-out also carried a raw-material asset into the JV: the 2 MTPA Netrabanda iron ore mine was commissioned in Q4 inside BPSL and now sits with the joint venture. “The 2 mill ion tonnes iron ore mine at Netrabanda, which is now with the joint venture is now part of BPSL is being commissioned in the Quarter 4, increasing the ir on ore availability for the joint venture.” — *CALL May 2026*
15. Management used the freed balance sheet to raise targets to 62 MTPA by FY32 for JSW Steel alone plus 16 MTPA across the JFE and POSCO JVs, and to tighten leverage caps from 3.75x to 3.00x and gearing from 1.75x to 1.25x. “So , we'll have a double engine of growth, one which JSW Steel will grow on and the other which the joint venture will grow on.” — *CALL May 2026*
16. Sumangal Nevatia (Kotak) pressed on why a second partner (POSCO) was needed given the already-strong post-JFE balance sheet; Acharya cited technology access plus POSCO's wish to backward-integrate its 2 MTPA Maharashtra cold-rolling plant. “I just want to understand better what is the rationale and wha t value does the new JV par tner brings given that we already have a very strong balance sheet after the JFE deal.” — *CALL May 2026*

**How it evolved:** Nine of the ten supplied transcripts (Jan 2024 through Jan 2026) contain no extractable text, so the call-by-call germination of the idea cannot be traced from these materials; the paper trail starts with the Board approval and signed JV/business-transfer/share-subscription agreements on December 3, 2025, alongside the separate Piombino merger scheme approved the same day. CCI cleared it on January 20, 2026, and the Q3 FY26 results of January 23, 2026 first quantified it (equity value Rs. 31,500 crores, EV Rs. 53,000 crores, Rs. 32,000 crore inflow, Rs. 37,000 crore deleveraging), classified the undertaking as held for sale under Ind AS 105, booked a Rs. 1,439 crore deferred tax asset against likely capital gains, and explicitly concluded it was not a 'discontinued operation.' The slump sale completed on March 27, 2026, and on the May 14, 2026 call management reframed it as the foundation of a 'double engine of growth' — JSW Steel to 62 MTPA by FY32 with 16 MTPA more in the JFE and POSCO JVs — while tightening its own leverage caps (3.75x to 3.00x) and gearing caps (1.75x to 1.25x). The Piombino amalgamation then ran its course: shareholder meeting August 21, 2026 (94.86% of valid votes, 97.20% of public votes), NCLT sanction October 16, 2026, effective October 31, 2026 from an appointed date of January 1, 2026.

**What management expects from it:** For JSW Steel: Rs. 32,000 crore inflow, ~Rs. 37,000 crore deleveraging, leverage 1.81x and gearing 0.51x, rating uplift, tighter caps (3.00x/1.25x), funding 62 MTPA by FY32 and a Rs. 2,26,000 crore capex programme. For the BPSL JV: faster capacity growth to ~10 MTPA with JFE's best-in-class technology, high-end value-added products, Netrabanda iron ore, equity-accounted. Piombino merger: direct BPSL ownership, extra cash, fewer entities, lower overheads.

*Not explained on the calls:* No BPSL-specific margin, ROCE or valuation basis; no stated originator or investor/lender pressure; no dividend or exit path; nine transcripts unreadable, so pre-Dec-2025 discussion is absent.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* Platform turned profitable for the first time in Q4 FY26; steel volumes +50% YoY, GMV Rs 6,200 crores (+57% YoY). Yet FY26 share of profit was (Rs 90 crores) and investment is 0.06% of consolidated net worth.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* The JOPL IPO price and offer details, to be determined in due course by the competent body.
- *In their words:* “The price and other details of the proposed IPO will be determined in due course by the competent body, in compliance with applicable law including the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, as amended.”

### 5. Why the demerger — point by point

The business being separated is Amber's Electronics / EMS arm, housed in IL JIN Electronics (India) Ltd — PCB assembly (~INR2,281cr of FY26 revenue), bare PCB through Ascent Circuits (98.5% owned), Shogini Technoarts (80%) and the Ascent-K/Korea Circuit HDI JV (~INR600cr), plus Power-One Microsystems (60%, power electronics, ~15% EBITDA) and 50.4% of Israel-listed Unitronics (industrial automation, 24-25% EBITDA) — leaving Amber with the RAC/consumer-durables division (INR8,383cr FY26) and Sidwal railway/defence (INR535cr). The stated driver is funding: essentially all of the group's capex sits in electronics, with more than INR4,500cr of ECMS investment approvals (Ascent multilayer INR991cr, Ascent-K HDI INR3,200cr, Shogini INR500cr), asset turns of only 0.75-1.1x, and the 48% MeitY plus 42% UP incentives arriving 5-6 years after the spend, so FY27 capex of INR1,800-2,000cr (INR1,100-1,200cr cash) and ~INR1,400-1,500cr in FY28 must be pre-funded against a board policy never to exceed 2x debt/EBITDA and Jasbir Singh's pledge to be net-debt-free. Management said investors asked for it: private equity funds were 'chasing to invest in the electronic division', and instead of loading Amber's balance sheet they raised INR1,750cr inside ILJIN (mostly CCPS, including ChrysCapital's INR1,100cr) while Amber separately did a INR1,000cr QIP. Separation also gives electronics its own margin and valuation identity — 2.8% EBITDA when ILJIN was bought in 2018 on INR300cr revenue, 6.9% FY25, 8.8% FY26, 10.8% in Q4 FY26, 26% ROCE, guidance of 40% FY27 growth at 9.5-10% and a $1bn revenue target at 11.5-12% EBITDA — against a weather-driven RAC business that saw quarters of -30% to -35% and nine bad seasons in 25 years. The outside CCPS holders also need a price: conversion happens 'based on the future multiple and valuation' (auditors provisioned up to ~30% dilution in NCI), which a listing supplies; and their presence already constrains group structuring, since management could not say whether the new Oppo mobile-phone business would sit in ILJIN 'because we have other shareholders also in the IL JIN cap table'. It is being done as a listing of the subsidiary, not a demerger: in April 2026 Amber put another INR296.02cr into an INR328.12cr ILJIN rights issue (89.58% to 89.72%); in July 2026 ILJIN split shares from Rs10 to Rs5, raised authorised capital to Rs250cr, issued a 25:1 bonus, converted from private to public limited, shifted its registered office from Pune to Greater Noida and resolved to explore fund-raising 'including... public issue'; the DRHP was filed on 7 November 2026. In parallel Amber is cleaning up the rest of the portfolio — merging wholly-owned AmberPR Technoplast into itself for compliance/cost reduction and peer benchmarking, and selling Sidwal's entire 49% Shivaliks (Titagarh Firema) JV for a nominal Rs1,09,798.85 after INR112cr of FY26 impairment/JV losses, 'to curtail future losses'.

**Point by point, with the source:**

1. The capex need that later drives the separation starts here: the Korea Circuit HDI/substrate JV is on hold pending the ECMS scheme, with a likely Rs1,000cr-plus minimum investment and 70-75% of it only reimbursed later by MeitY and the states. “So, on Korea Circuit we are waiting for Government to finalize the incentive scheme.” — *[Jan 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=813804ee-c3a7-4425-bb42-2057de6be8b1.pdf)*
2. With an INR3,000cr PCB application planned and subsidies spread over 5-6 years, management says the Electronics division is itself seeking third-party funding — the first hint of capital being raised at the subsidiary rather than at Amber. “So we are already in touch with various institutions for that.” — *[May 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=069162e3-fda9-42bb-9c69-0db5b0c2a202.pdf)*
3. Two funding routes are named — an INR2,500cr QIP enabling resolution at Amber and private equity money targeted specifically at the electronics arm; the same call sets the constraint that drives it, a board cap of 2x debt/EBITDA and a goal to be net-debt-free by FY27. “Second direction is a lot of private equity funds who are chasing to invest in the electronic division.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=445f7c35-5bf5-4f56-9d6f-e16495c40233.pdf)*
4. The separated entity is given its own standalone ambition and margin identity — $1bn revenue in three years at 11.5-12% EBITDA, versus ILJIN's 2.8% EBITDA on INR300cr when acquired in 2018. “With all the add -ups, we intend to take Electronics division to $1 billion by next 3 years with target EBITDA of 11.5% to 12% range.” — *[Aug 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=445f7c35-5bf5-4f56-9d6f-e16495c40233.pdf)*
5. The raise happens at two levels simultaneously: INR1,750cr into ILJIN (mostly CCPS; INR370cr in September, INR280cr in October, ChrysCapital's INR1,100cr pending CCI) and a separate INR1,000cr QIP at Amber used mainly to cut debt. “We secured funding of INR1,750 crores from marquee investors.” — *[Nov 2025](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=0bcb53ba-69d0-4386-9199-d20b4b029d9c.pdf)*
6. ILJIN's raise closes in full and Amber's stake stays at 90% only because the instrument is CCPS; the same call adds the ECMS approvals (Ascent-K HDI, Shogini) and 116 acres at Jewar that the money has to fund. “On the balance sheet front, ILJIN Electronics has successfully concluded fundraise with the entire INR1,750 crores received from marquee investors.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=99744db3-5ae9-451c-8d73-b33d28177128.pdf)*
7. The outside investors' economics depend on a valuation event: no dilution has occurred yet because CCPS convert off a future multiple, with auditors provisioning roughly 30% maximum dilution in non-controlling interest. FY27 capex is guided at INR1,800-2,000cr (INR1,100-1,200cr cash), net debt INR511cr rising to INR700-800cr. “It will happen in future based on the future multiple and valuation.” — *[May 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=469945ff-af54-4664-8bd7-ed051c694aff.pdf)*
8. The ILJIN cap table already limits group structuring — management cannot say whether the new Oppo mobile-phone business (8m units year one, 13-15m year two, sub-INR50cr capex, 1.5-2% industry EBITDA) will sit inside ILJIN or directly under Amber. “But we will not be able to define it right now because we have other shareholders also in the IL JIN cap table .” — *[Jun 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=e758d7f3-9942-4baf-b20b-0e80b2d6971a.pdf)*
9. April 2026: Amber pre-funds ILJIN again, subscribing INR296.02cr of a INR328.12cr rights issue (12,46,430 shares), taking its holding from 89.58% to 89.72% — capital in before the listing, not a stake sale. “Further, pursuant to the allotment of equity shares under the rights issue by IL JIN on 21st April 2026, which has resulted in an investment of Rs. 296.02 Crore, Amber Enterprises India Limited (“Amber” or “the Company”) has subscribed to and been allotted 12,46,430 equity shares.” — *Scheme*
10. July 2026: ILJIN is mechanically prepared for listing — Rs10 to Rs5 share split, authorised capital to Rs250cr, 25:1 bonus, conversion from private to public limited, registered office moved Pune to Greater Noida, and a board resolution to explore fund-raising modes including a public issue. “Evaluation and exploration of various fund-raising options to support its future growth initiatives.” — *Scheme*
11. 7 November 2026: the separation becomes a formal partial listing of the electronics arm — a DRHP for ILJIN's IPO filed with SEBI, BSE and NSE, Amber retaining ~90% pre-offer. “IL JIN Electronics (India) Limited (formerly known as IL JIN Electronics (India) Private Limited), a material subsidiary of the Company, has ﬁled the Draft Red Herring Prospectus dated 6th November 2026 (“DRHP”), on 7th November 2026 with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited in connection with its proposed Initial Public Oﬀer (“IPO”).” — *Scheme*
12. The rest of the group is being simplified in the opposite direction: wholly-owned AmberPR Technoplast (cross-flow fans) is merged into Amber — no shares issued, NCLT dispensed with meetings, appointed date moved to 1 April 2026 — for compliance savings, scale synergies and cleaner peer comparison. “more absolute and profound comparison with industry peers ie. benchmarking business performance with industry; and” — *Scheme*
13. Portfolio pruning runs alongside: the 49% Shivaliks/Titagarh Firema stake is impaired (INR94cr in Q3, INR112cr FY26 including JV losses) and then sold in March 2026 to JP Fincap for a nominal Rs1,09,798.85, ending Italy export ambitions while keeping the Titagarh commercial relationship worth ~INR700cr of visibility. “And to curtail future losses, on etime exceptional impairment loss has been recognized during this quarter.” — *[Feb 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=99744db3-5ae9-451c-8d73-b33d28177128.pdf)*

**How it evolved:** The capex trigger appears first on the Jan 2025 call (Korea Circuit JV awaiting the ECMS scheme, Rs1,000cr+ threshold) and on 19 May 2025, when the funding answer is still vague — 'in touch with various institutions' — alongside an INR3,000cr application plan. By 30 July 2025 it has split into two named routes, an INR2,500cr QIP enabling resolution at Amber and 'private equity funds who are chasing to invest in the electronic division', with the $1bn/11.5-12% electronics ambition and a net-debt-free pledge framing why outside money must sit at ILJIN; on 7 Nov 2025 the INR1,750cr ILJIN raise (CCPS, ChrysCapital INR1,100cr pending CCI) and Amber's INR1,000cr QIP are both announced, and 10 Feb 2026 confirms the full INR1,750cr received with Amber still at 90% until CCPS convert. From there it becomes an exit path for those investors: 18 May 2026 ties conversion to 'future multiple and valuation' (~30% assumed dilution), 20 June 2026 shows the ILJIN cap table already constraining where new businesses can be placed, and the filings then execute mechanically — Mar/Apr 2026 rights issue, 11 July 2026 split, 25:1 bonus, public-limited conversion, registered office to Greater Noida and a 'public issue' resolution, and the DRHP on 7 Nov 2026 — none of it ever discussed on an earnings call.

**What management expects from it:** Electronics: self-funded ECMS PCB capex, $1bn revenue in ~3 years, margins from 2.8% (2018) toward 11.5-12%, double digits from FY27, ~26% ROCE, stickier high-entry-barrier industrial/defence mix. Amber: retains ~89.7%, frees cash for consumer durables and railway (30-35% growth, 16-17% margins), stays under 2x debt/EBITDA near net-debt-free; CCPS dilution finally priced off a market valuation.

*Not explained on the calls:* Calls never discuss the IPO itself: offer size, fresh issue versus OFS, use of proceeds, valuation, Amber's post-listing stake, CCPS conversion terms, or why listing rather than demerger.

- *Stated reason, in one line:* Not stated for the IPO itself; IL JIN's board approved "evaluation and exploration of various fund-raising options to support its future growth initiatives", including a public issue
- *What it reveals:* Electronics division FY26 revenue Rs 3,268 crore (+49%), operating EBITDA Rs 287 crore (+89%), guided ~40% FY27 growth at 9.5-10% margins; IL JIN raised Rs 1,750 crore from marquee investors; bought 2018 as a Rs 300-crore, 3%-EBITDA company
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *Read next:* The DRHP dated 6th November 2026: IL JIN standalone financials, fresh-issue versus offer-for-sale split, and CCPS conversion terms
- *In their words:* “The IPO will be subject to receipt of the required regulatory approvals.”

### 8. The separated business's financial statements

**The business being separated — its own numbers**, entity by entity: its reported statements once it is listed and on file, and the segment numbers the annual reports and presentations carry for it before that.

**Electronics Division (reported as "Electronics manufacturing services (EMS)" up to FY2024; key subsidiary IL JIN Electronics (India) Private Limited, with Ascent Circuits, Power-One Micro Systems, Unitronics, Shogini Technoarts — PCB-Assembly & Box Build, Bare PCB, Power Electronics, Industrial Automation) → IL JIN Electronics (India) Limited** · unit ₹ lakh · Annual figures from the consolidated segment note: segment revenue is gross and includes inter-segment (group inter-segment eliminations are shown only in total, not per segment); operating_profit = 'Segment Results (Profit before interest, depreciation and amortisation and tax)', i.e. segment EBITDA, not EBIT/PBT. Segment PAT, capex and depreciation are not disclosed per segment — finance cost, other income, depreciation/amortisation and tax are managed group-wide and not allocated. Normally, this sector operates on a net-working capital days of almost 4, 5 days, maximum 10 days.”
- **debt and leverage** — parent / remaining: "On the balance sheet front, net debt stood at INR511 crores as of March '26 against INR780 crores in March '25." Expected to rise to around INR700 crores to INR800 crores by FY27 year-end; separated business: IL JIN raised INR1,750 crores, predominantly compulsorily convertible preference shares with a small portion of equity, from marquee investors, part kept "in the war chest for the future expansion" “On the balance sheet front, ILJIN Electronics has successfully concluded fundraise with the entire INR1,750 crores received from marquee investors.”
- **capex and capital intensity** — parent / remaining: Overall FY26 capex around INR1,070 crores, of which capitalized capex only INR550 crores; FY27 overall capex INR1,800 crores to INR2,000 crores with cash outflow of around INR1,100 crores to INR1,200 crores; Railway capex only around INR50 crores to INR60 crores; separated business: The electronics/PCB businesses are the asset-heavy part: Ascent around INR1,200-odd crores in FY27, Ascent-K Circuits first phase INR1,200 crores (total INR3,200 crores), Shogini INR500 crores application with INR55 crores to INR60 crores in the coming year; ECMS approvals of more than INR4,500 crores total investment “See Dhruv, I'll add to what Sudhir has answered. These are all asset-heavy businesses where the capex is going, largely the printed circuit boards. This is exactly like OSAT and ATMP business where asset turns are about 0.8 to 1x.”
- **return on capital** — parent / remaining: not stated as a parent-level figure; on the component side "if we talk about the component side where our goal is the PCB, we work in the range of 15% to 16%"; separated business: The new high-volume mobile phone assembly business is said to be ROCE accretive on a stand-alone basis “And -- but we see a very, very good ROCEs. Generally, these are very ROCE accretive. If you take this on a stand-alone basis, I mean, the ROCEs will be more than 30%, 35%.”
- **other** — parent / remaining: Consumer Durable is a pass-through, quarterly-lag business with fixed margin per unit: "we have a fixed price margin per unit. So overall, fixed margin will remain same in terms of value"; Indian Railway contracts are fixed price contracts; separated business: The bare PCB business is a Tier 2 supplier with a longer pass-through lag; mobile phone assembly runs at industry EBITDA of 1.5% to 2% “But in the PCB business, we are Tier 2. We don't supply directly to Maruti or Hyundai, we supply to Tier 1 guys, and that's where the inventory has to be taken care at 2 levels. And hence, the lag in the PCB business to increase the cost is about 2 quarters.”
- **tax** — parent / remaining: Under the AmberPR scheme the authorized share capital of the Transferor Company transfers to Amber "without any liability for payment of any additional fees ... or stamp duty"; the scheme was certified as complying with accounting standards under section 133; separated business: The Ever/IL JIN scheme "complies with the relevant provisions of section 2(1B) and section 47 of the Income-tax Act, 1961", with pooling of interest accounting under Ind AS 103 “In respect of the aforesaid observation, it is submitted that in terms of clause 20 of the Scheme and upon the scheme becoming effective, the Transferee Company shall be accounted as per the "polling of Interest" method provided under Indian Accounting standard (Ind-As)-103 for "Business Combination" prescribed under section 133 of the Act.”
